children.text: 1. Ajātaśatru
children.translated_text: 1. <s>Ajātaśatru</s>

children.text: mahānti pāpāny abhibhūya yasmād ajātaśatrur guṇavān babhūva |
children.translated_text: Because <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having overcome great sins, became virtuous

children.text: upetya sadbhiḥ saha saṃprayogam ato niṣevyā guṇavanta eva || GoAś_1 ||
children.translated_text: by entering into association with good people — therefore, the virtuous alone are to be sought out. // GoAś 1 //

children.text: aho vibhūtir guṇavistarāṇāṃ guṇābdhikair yat saha saṃprayujya |
children.translated_text: Ah, what a glory of the expansion of virtues! That, by associating with those who are oceans of virtue,

children.text: guṇair abhūtair viguṇo 'bhyupeti guṇaprasiddhiṃ guṇabhūṣaneṣu || GoAś_2 ||
children.translated_text: one who is devoid of qualities attains renown for virtues that did not [previously] exist, adorned by [the virtues of others]. // GoAś 2 //

children.text: abhūtasaṃbhāvanayā tayā tu hato 'py asau kālavaśena bhūpaḥ |
children.translated_text: Yet even that king, slain by that groundless expectation [of virtue], by the power of time,

children.text: tuṣāradagdhadrumavad vasante guṇaprabhāvojjvalatām upaiti || GoAś_3 ||
children.translated_text: like a frost-burnt tree in spring, attains the brilliance of the glory of virtue. // GoAś 3 //

children.text: svabhāvasaṃsiddhir iyaṃ tathā hi janasya sadvṛttiniratyayasya |
children.translated_text: For this is indeed the natural accomplishment of a person whose conduct is unfailingly righteous:

children.text: vijihmabhāveṣv api yat prayāti guṇaprasiddheḥ khalu hetubhāvam || GoAś_4 ||
children.translated_text: that even in crooked circumstances, he becomes the cause of the renown of virtue. // GoAś 4 //

children.text: bravīmy ato 'haṃ narake 'pi vāso varaṃ sphuradvahniśikhākarāle |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: better even a dwelling in hell, terrible with flickering tongues of fire,

children.text: na caiva sanmitranirākṛtasya sureśvarāṇāṃ sukhasaṃpado 'pi || GoAś_5 ||
children.translated_text: than the pleasures and riches of the lords of the gods for one who has rejected a good friend. // GoAś 5 //

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate
children.translated_text: As the story goes —

children.text: rājā kilājātaśatrur vanadviradavaropagrahanimittaṃ svanagarād abhiniḥsṛtya dadarśa mahāntaṃ kuñjaravaraṃ vanābhimukham abhidravantam | dṛṣṭvā ca punas tam eva hastinam anujagāma | sa ca dantī
children.translated_text: King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, it is said, having set out from his city for the purpose of capturing a wild elephant, saw a great and excellent elephant running toward the forest. Having seen it, he followed that very elephant. And that tusker,

children.text: smṛtvā sarāṃsi kamalotpalamaṇḍitāni kādambapakṣapavanoddhataśīkarāṇi |
children.translated_text: remembering the lakes adorned with lotuses and blue lilies, sprinkled with spray raised by the wings of <s>kādamba</s> (grey geese),

children.text: udbhinnakomalakaserulatāvanāni vegān mahīdharavanābhimukho jagāma || GoAś_6 ||
children.translated_text: with groves of tender, sprouting <s>kaseru</s> (bulrush) creepers — rushed swiftly toward the mountain forest. // GoAś 6 //

children.text: utkaṇṭhitaḥ kisalayojjvalapādapānāṃ vaiḍūryanīlaharitodgataśādvalānām |
children.translated_text: Longing for the forests with trees resplendent with fresh shoots, with dark-green meadows rising like beryl-blue [carpets],

children.text: uddhūtaśīkarakaro dvirado vanānāṃ tūrṇaṃ yayau pavananunna ivāmbugarbhaḥ || GoAś_7 ||
children.translated_text: the elephant, raising its trunk-hand of spray, went quickly — like a cloud driven by the wind. // GoAś 7 //

children.text: atha sa mahīpatiḥ pavanapaṭujavātiśayaturagavarādhirūḍho dūrād apasṛtabalasahāyo na cireṇa khadirabadarabilveṅgudādikaṇṭakadrumavanagahanāṃ śaravaṇakāśakuśavaṃśajālajaṭiladuḥsaṃcārapradeśāṃ jīrṇaśīrṇavikṣiptāsthikaṅkālaśakaladhavalabhūmibhāgāṃ pratibhayagambhīraśvabhraprapātasthalasthāṇuvalmīkadurnirgamapraveśām aṭavīṃ prapede | sa ca gajādhipatis tasya rājño darśanam apajagāma |
children.translated_text: Then that king, mounted on his excellent steed exceedingly swift as the wind, his military escort having fallen far behind, soon entered a wilderness dense with thorny trees such as <s>khadira</s> (acacia), <s>badara</s> (jujube), <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple), and <s>iṅguda</s>, entangled with thickets of reeds, <s>kāśa</s> grass, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and bamboo groves making passage difficult, with stretches of ground whitened by scattered fragments of old, crumbling skeletal bones, with terrifying deep chasms, precipices, tree stumps, and anthills making entry and exit perilous. And that lord of elephants disappeared from the king's sight.

children.text: rājāsau vihataparākramāvakāśo grīṣmoṣmaklamaśithilākulaprayatnaḥ |
children.translated_text: That king, his opportunity for valor thwarted, his efforts weakened and confused by the oppressive heat of summer,

children.text: bhūreṇuvyatikaradhūsarāgrakeśaḥ saṃmohaṃ samupajagāma sādhvasena || GoAś_8 ||
children.translated_text: his hair at the tips turned grey with the mingling of earth-dust, fell into a swoon from terror. // GoAś 8 //

children.text: tasmin khaḍgaviṣāṇakoṭikaṣṇa – – ⏑ – – ⏑ –
children.translated_text: In that [forest], scored by the tips of sword[-like horns] and tusks — [lacuna]

children.text: siṃhavyāghravarāha – ⏑ mahiṣavyālāvakīrṇe vane |
children.translated_text: in a forest strewn with lions, tigers, boars, [lacuna] buffaloes, and serpents,

children.text: ekākī sa nṛpo bhraman ravikarajvālāpratāpāturas
children.translated_text: that king, wandering alone, tormented by the burning rays of the sun,

children.text: tṛṣṇārtaḥ padavīṃ dadarśa sahasā śailendrasaṃprāpikām || GoAś_9 ||
children.translated_text: afflicted by thirst, suddenly espied a path leading to the king of mountains. // GoAś 9 //

children.text: tāṃ ca muhūrtam anugacchan dadarśa dūrād eva nīlavipulasnigdhapalāśanicitaviṭapataruvaragahanam acalasānupradeśam | dṛṣṭvā + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + yanaḥ(?) provāca ||
children.translated_text: Following it for a short while, he saw from afar a mountain-slope region dense with fine, large, luxuriant, blue-green leafy trees. Seeing it [lacuna] he spoke:

children.text: asmin nūnaṃ pradeśe navanalinavanacchannatoyaṃ saro vā
children.translated_text: Surely in this place there is a lake with water hidden by fresh lotuses and water-lilies,

children.text: dhārā śailodarād vā patati maṇidalasvacchaśobhā jalasya |
children.translated_text: or a cascade falls from the mountain's interior, with waters lovely as a crystal surface;

children.text: vṛkṣās tatsaṃnikarṣād upacitavipulaśyāmaśākhāpraśākhā
children.translated_text: from its proximity, these trees have grown with abundant, expansive, dark-green branches and sub-branches —

children.text: yenaite śailam etaṃ jagad iva sakalaṃ sajjanāḥ śobhayanti || GoAś_10 ||
children.translated_text: whereby these [trees], like good people, adorn this mountain and the entire world. // GoAś 10 //

children.text: dūratvād
a
children.translated_text: [lacuna]
[lacuna — metrical fragment]

children.text: – – – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ bhāraguravo jīmūtapuñjā iva |
children.translated_text: [lacuna] heavy-laden like masses of clouds,

children.text: ete vṛddhim upāgatāḥ khalu parām āsādya toyāśayaṃ
children.translated_text: these [trees] have grown to supreme height, having reached a reservoir of water —

children.text: sanmitraṃ samupetya sādhava iva pradhvasyamānārayaḥ || GoAś_11 ||
children.translated_text: like good people who, having found a good friend, grow while their enemies are destroyed. // GoAś 11 //
From a distance,

children.text: tad ito gacchāmīti saṃpradhāryopetya ca taṃ pradeśaṃ samantato vilokayan dadarśānyatamasmin taruvaragahanavivare + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + kopahārābhidarśane vipulaśilātalābhoganiṣaṇṇakṛtāhāraprayojanam upaśamanibhṛtendriyapracārasaumyavapuṣaṃ śākyabhikṣuṃ dṛṣṭvā samāśvāsaprāptaḥ prahlādita iva viśrānta iva ca vājinam ekānte nibadhya sapraśrayamaḥdhuro + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + kta iva ca vikacakamalavanareṇupiñjarasurabhiśiśirasamīraṇena taṃ bhikṣum abravīt | bhadanta salilāśayapradeśam upadeṣṭum arhatīti | tena copadiṣṭam | atha sa rājā tam upadiṣṭaṃ salilāśayam upagamya vigatapipāsāklamapari + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + ||
children.translated_text: Having resolved 'I shall go from here,' and approaching that place and looking around on all sides, he saw in a certain opening among the dense grove of fine trees [lacuna] a <s>Śākya</s> monk seated on a broad, flat rock-surface, having completed his meal, with senses quiet and restrained, of tranquil appearance. Seeing him, as if having found reassurance, as if refreshed, as if rested, he tied his horse to one side and humbly bowing [lacuna] [he was] as if [cooled] by a gentle, cool breeze fragrant with the pollen of blossoming lotus groves, and he addressed that monk: 'Reverend sir, please be so kind as to direct me to a body of water.' And he was so directed. Then that king, having approached the indicated body of water, freed from the distress of thirst and fatigue [lacuna]

children.text: – – ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – mayūkhaiḥ prasvedavārikaṇikārdralalāṭabhittiḥ |
children.translated_text: [lacuna] with rays; the wall of his forehead moist with drops of perspiration,

children.text: pītvāpi vāri kamalotpalanālaśītaṃ tīvraklamāturamanā na dhṛtiṃ jagāma || GoAś_12 ||
children.translated_text: even after drinking water cool as lotus and lily stalks, his mind tormented by intense exhaustion, he could not find composure. // GoAś 12 //

children.text: atha sa bhikṣuḥ sāndrakaruṇāmṛtarasārdraśītalena cakṣuṣā taṃ rājānam abhisamīkṣyābravīt | klībasattvam iva vyā + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
pra
children.translated_text: [lacuna]

children.text: vādo lokavṛttātivṛttaprabhāveṣv apy upalakṣyate | na khalu sukhocitāḥ paraduḥkhāni jānantīti | nanu bhadantāvaiṣi ||
children.translated_text: this saying is observed even in those whose power surpasses worldly ways. For surely, those accustomed to comfort do not know the sufferings of others. Do you not know this, Reverend Sir?
Then that monk, regarding the king with an eye moist and cool with the nectar of intense compassion, spoke: 'A weakness of spirit, as it were [lacuna]'

children.text: dagdhāpi bhū ravikaraiḥ sphuṭadīptimadbhir dandahyate gataghṛṇena davānalena |
children.translated_text: The earth, though scorched by the rays of the sun blazing with dazzling brilliance, is burnt again by the pitiless forest fire;

children.text: bhartuḥ pravāsavirahe vaniteva duḥkhais ta – ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ – – || GoAś_13 ||
children.translated_text: like a woman in the sorrow of her husband's absence — [lacuna]. // GoAś 13 //

children.text: – – ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ – – ḥ saṃtāpitā ravikaraiḥ sutarāṃ pracaṇḍaiḥ |
children.translated_text: [lacuna] scorched exceedingly by the fierce rays of the sun,

children.text: kalyāṇamitravikalās tu vicāraśūnyā rāgātmakā iva narāḥ pramadāvilāsaiḥ || GoAś_14 ||
children.translated_text: bereft of virtuous friends and devoid of discrimination — [the creatures are] like passion-natured men [distracted] by the wiles of women. // GoAś 14 //

children.text: gharmāturo bhayam anāgatam apradhārya cchāyāṃ samāśrayati bhogiphaṇasya bhekaḥ |
children.translated_text: A frog, tormented by heat, without considering the danger yet to come, takes shelter in the shadow of a serpent's hood;

children.text: āpātamātrasukha – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ – – – – ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ – m iva rājalakṣmīm || GoAś_15 ||
children.translated_text: [so too one grasps at] pleasure that is momentary — [lacuna] as if [grasping] royal fortune. // GoAś 15 //

children.text: saṃśuṣkasālatarukoṭarasaṃnilīno vyarthaṃ virauti pariśuṣkagalaḥ kapotaḥ |
children.translated_text: A pigeon, concealed in the hollow of a withered <s>sāla</s> tree, coos in vain, its throat parched;

children.text: ajñānagahvaraniruddha ivātmavādī bālaḥ punarbhavatṛṣāviṣamūrchitātmā || GoAś_16 ||
children.translated_text: like a self-absorbed child, as if trapped in the cave of ignorance, his mind stupefied by the poison of craving for rebirth. // GoAś 16 //

children.text: ete gajā ravikarotkaratāpiteṣu naiva sthaleṣu na jaleṣu dhṛtiṃ labhante |
children.translated_text: These elephants, on grounds scorched by the fierce rays of the sun, find steadiness neither on land nor in water;

children.text: grāmeṣu puṣpavikaceṣu ca kānaneṣu pāriplavālpamatayo yatayo yathaiva || GoAś_17 ||
children.translated_text: just as ascetics of fickle, shallow intellect [find no peace] in villages or in forests blossoming with flowers. // GoAś 17 //

children.text: ambv eva (?) palvalajalaṃ kṣayam abhyupaiti saṃśuṣkaśaivalarajo'ruṇapaṅkaleśam |
children.translated_text: The water of the pool dwindles — with its remnant of dried algae, reddish with dust and traces of mud;

children.text: mandāgamasya sadasīva vijṛmbhamāṇaṃ vākkauśalaṃ svamatiśaktinirākṛtasya || GoAś_18 ||
children.translated_text: like the eloquence flourishing in the assembly of one of feeble learning, whose ability of mind is negated. // GoAś 18 //

children.text: ete khagā vanatarūn parivarjayanti saṃśīrṇaparṇanicayordhvaviśuṣkaśākhān |
children.translated_text: These birds abandon the forest trees whose heaped leaves have crumbled, whose upper branches are withered —

children.text: vismṛtya pūrvaparibhogasukhāny anāryā veśyā viluptadhanasāram ivālpasattvam || GoAś_19 ||
children.translated_text: forgetting the pleasures of former enjoyment — like ignoble courtesans [abandoning] a man of little substance whose wealth has been plundered. // GoAś 19 //

children.text: dāvāgnibhasmaparuṣaiḥ pavanair udastam etad bhramaty avirataṃ taruparṇacakram |
children.translated_text: Driven by winds harsh with the dust of forest-fire ash, this wheel of tree-leaves whirls ceaselessly —

children.text: utpīḍyamānam aniśaṃ niravagraheṇa saṃsāracakram iva karmasamīraṇena || GoAś_20 ||
children.translated_text: like the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>, perpetually crushed by the unrestrained wind of <s>karma</s>. // GoAś 20 //

children.text: paryanteṣu sphuṭitaśakalacchedasaṃparkarūkṣas
children.translated_text: At the edges, rough with broken, cracking fragments,

children.text: toyābhyāśe srutajalatayā na dravo nātiśuṣkaḥ |
children.translated_text: near the water, neither liquid nor fully dry due to the oozing moisture,

children.text: kiṃciccheṣākaluṣasalilāplāvito madhyabhāge
children.translated_text: in the middle portion, flooded with some remaining turbid water,

children.text: paṅkaḥ śoṣaṃ sphuritaśapharījālagarbhaḥ prayāti || GoAś_21 ||
children.translated_text: the mud, carrying a mass of quivering fish in its depths, dries up. // GoAś 21 //

children.text: kiṃciccheṣavivarṇaparṇaśabalā mūle kaṭhorāruṇā
children.translated_text: Speckled with a few remaining discolored leaves, hard and reddish at the root,

children.text: mandaśyāmapalāśasaṃcayavatī madhye samārdracchaviḥ |
children.translated_text: with a gathering of faintly green foliage in the middle, with a still-moist hue,

children.text: gharmaśyāmavibhugnapallavadalā prānte latā nartakī
children.translated_text: with heat-darkened, curling leaf-tips at the edges — the dancer-creeper

children.text: mlāniṃ yāty aniśaṃ kalāv iva yuge satpauruṣī dharmatā || GoAś_22 ||
children.translated_text: withers ceaselessly, as does the virtue of manly righteousness with each passing age. // GoAś 22 //

children.text: chattrair vyabhraśaśāṅkamaṇḍalasitai ratnaprabhābhāsvarair
children.translated_text: With parasols white as the disc of the moon in a cloudless sky, radiant with the glow of gems,

children.text: vikṣiptāḥ kiraṇā yad asya bahuśo niryāṇakāle mama |
children.translated_text: the rays that were cast about abundantly for me at the time of my going forth —

children.text: tad vairaṃ hṛdayena saṃcitam ayaṃ nūnaṃ vahaty aṃśumān
children.translated_text: surely this sun carries in his heart a grudge stored up [against me],

children.text: yasyāgnir dahatīva durjanavacas tīkṣṇair mayūkhāṅkuraiḥ || GoAś_23 ||
children.translated_text: for he burns like fire with his fierce ray-sprouts, like the harsh words of a wicked person. // GoAś 23 //

children.text: atha sa bhikṣuḥ kathāntaravivakṣayā smitam āviścakāra | + + + + + + + + + + + + + sa rājā samantato nirīkṣyānyam anīkṣamāṇo mām evādhikṛtya pravrajitena smitam ādarśitam iti viniścitya kutūhalākrāntamatis tam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then that monk, wishing to begin another conversation, smiled. [lacuna] That king, looking all around and seeing no one else, and concluding 'The renunciant has smiled directed at me alone,' his mind seized by curiosity, addressed him:

children.text: vinayadhīram idaṃ ca vapus tava smitam idaṃ ca bhadanta vidhāryate |
children.translated_text: 'Your appearance is steady with humility, and this smile of yours, Reverend Sir, is observed;

children.text: calati buddhir iyaṃ pavanāhatā vanalateva kim atra nu kāraṇam || GoAś_24 ||
children.translated_text: this mind of mine wavers like a forest creeper struck by the wind — what is the reason here?' // GoAś 24 //

children.text: + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + | atha sa pārthivaḥ sutarām upajātavimarśasaṃbhramodbhrāntamānasaḥ punar api taṃ bhikṣuṃ smitaprayojanaṃ paryapṛcchat | sa ca bhikṣus tadupakārakāmatayaiva rājñaḥ provāca ||
children.translated_text: [lacuna] Then that prince, his mind all the more agitated with arising doubt and confusion, again asked the monk the purpose of his smile. And that monk, out of a desire to help the king, spoke:

children.text:
sūryātapo dahati vatsa śarīrakaṃ te tasmāt sukhocitam idaṃ tu roganīḍam |

children.text: bhitāpitānām || GoAś_25 ||
children.translated_text: of those who are tormented.' // GoAś 25 //
'The heat of the sun burns your body, my child — therefore this abode accustomed to comfort is but a nest of disease.

children.text: vastrātapatratarumandiracandanāmbuhārādayas tadupaghātanimittabhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Garments, parasols, trees, mansions, sandalwood, water, and necklaces — these are the remedies for that [present heat];

children.text: duḥkhaṃ tv anāgatam avīcisamudbhavaṃ te nāśaṃ prayāsyati narādhipa kair upāyaiḥ || GoAś_26 ||
children.translated_text: but the suffering yet to come, arising from <s>Avīci</s> [hell], O lord of men — by what means will you avert it?' // GoAś 26 //

children.text: prāṇoparodhasamakālam avaśyabhāvi yat prāpsyasi tvam akṛta

children.translated_text: kinds;'

children.translated_text: 'when the suffering, even for a moment,'

[lacuna — metrical fragment]

children.text: tava tadgajabhayā
children.translated_text: 'your [flight from] that elephant-terror'

children.text: ⏑ ⏑ – kṣaṇena || GoAś_27 ||
children.translated_text: 'in an instant.' // GoAś 27 //
'That which you will inevitably undergo at the very moment of the cessation of life-breath — the [suffering] of one who has not recognized [the truth], of manifold

children.text: karmendhanaḥ sphurati tatra (?) sadā hutāśo durvṛttaśoṇitavasāsavapānaśauṇḍaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'There the fire, fueled by <s>karma</s>, blazes constantly, intoxicated by drinking the blood, fat, and marrow of the wicked;

children.text: yo bāndhavān iva pariṣvajate pragāḍhaṃ jvālābhujair aviralaiḥ svakṛtāparādhān || GoAś_28 ||
children.translated_text: with its dense flame-arms, it closely embraces — like kinsmen — those who have committed their own offenses. // GoAś 28 //

children.text:
vīciṃ vadanti vivaraṃ na ca tatra kā cid duḥkhasya vīcir api tiryag upary adho vā |
yasmād avīcir iti tena ca saṃprasiddhaḥ śīrṇas ta
noti bha
children.translated_text: [lacuna — fragment]

children.text: vano narakāntareṣu || GoAś_29 ||
children.translated_text: in the intermediate hells.' // GoAś 29 //

'They call it <s>Avīci</s> — the gap-less — and there is no gap whatsoever of suffering, neither sideways nor above nor below; therefore it is well known as <s>Avīci</s> (without intervals); crumbling [lacuna]

children.text: yatra tvayātithijanapraṇayo niṣevyo jvālāsakhīśatapariṣvajanocitena |
children.translated_text: 'Where you must cultivate hospitality to guests, [you who are] accustomed to the embrace of hundreds of flame-companions —

children.text: sa tvaṃ vyathām upagato raviraśmitapto hārād bibheṣi na tu ghoraviṣād bhujaṅgat || GoAś_30 ||
children.translated_text: yet you, afflicted by the sun's rays, have come to distress; you do not fear the necklace but the terrible poison of the serpent.' // GoAś 30 //

children.text: yasyotsaṅge kṣititalarajodhūsaras tvaṃ niṣaṇṇa
children.translated_text: '[Your father,] on whose lap you sat, grey with the dust of the earth's surface,
[lacuna — metrical fragment]

children.text: premṇā yenākaruṇahṛdayo vardhitaḥ pālitaś ca
children.translated_text: by whom, with love, you — hard-hearted one — were raised and protected,

children.text: taṃ tvaṃ hatvā yadi na patitas tatkṣaṇaṃ citram etat || GoAś_31 ||
children.translated_text: that you, having slain him, did not fall [into hell] at that very instant — this is astonishing.' // GoAś 31 //

children.text: bālye lālāsalilamalinaṃ pāṇinā vaktrapadmaṃ
children.translated_text: 'In childhood, the lotus-face soiled with saliva-water,

children.text: yenāmṛṣṭaṃ vikacakamalacchedatāmrodareṇa |
children.translated_text: [which] he wiped with a hand whose palm was copper-red like a freshly plucked lotus petal,

children.text: tvāṃ kṛtvāṅke kṛpaṇa bhavataḥ kuñcitāḥ kākapakṣā
children.translated_text: placing you — wretched one — on his lap, your locks of hair curled [at the temples] —
who [lacuna].' // GoAś 32 //

children.text: sa tvaṃ hatvā pitaram api te dhārmikaṃ dharmarājaṃ
children.translated_text: 'You, having slain even your father, the righteous <s>Dharmarāja</s>,

children.text: kāmāsvādavyasanamadirāpānavikṣiptacittaḥ |
children.translated_text: your mind scattered by the intoxicating liquor of addiction to sensual pleasures,

children.text: svasthāvasthaś carasi narakadvāraśālāṃ praviṣṭo
children.translated_text: you roam about at ease, having entered the antechamber of hell —

children.text: jvālāhastair narakaśikhinaḥ spraṣṭum icchanti hi tvām || GoAś_33 ||
children.translated_text: the fire-hands of the hell-fire desire to touch you.' // GoAś 33 //

children.text: jvaladanalaśīkhāvalīpiṅgalāntaḥsthalaṃ sarvatas tuṅganiḥsaṅganiśchidralohādrijālāvṛtacchinnasaṃbhinnasaṃvignasaṃkūjitotkṛṣṭaniṣpiṣṭaniṣpīḍitotkṣiptavikṣiptaluptāvaluptāśrayaprāṇisaṃghākulabhīṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Terrifying within, with rows of blazing fire-tongues making it tawny on all sides, surrounded by towering, seamless, unbroken iron mountains — with beings cut, pierced, terrified, wailing, screaming, crushed, squeezed, tossed, flung, and robbed of shelter, all in tumult —

children.text: kṛpaṇa
ka
children.translated_text: [lacuna — fragment]

children.text: narakaṃ padā yāsyasi prerito dāruṇaiḥ karmavātair anekograduḥkhaprakarṣātisaṃtāpito dīnakaṇṭho ⏑ – ūrdhvabāhur jvalacchūlacakrāsikuntaprahāravraṇodvāntaraktokṣitas tatra cākāmakaḥ saṃvasan |
children.translated_text: You shall go to hell on foot, driven by the fierce winds of karma; tormented by the extremity of suffering in countless harsh [births], with a pitiable voice, arms raised upward, your body drenched in blood gushing from wounds struck by blazing spears, discuses, swords, and lances — and there you shall dwell against your will.
O wretched one,

children.text: jvaladanalakamaṇḍalākoṭarastabdhanetraiḥ sphuratkopasaṃdaṣṭadantacchadair udyatāgrāyudhair antakājñākarais tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti nistarjito bhītabhīto diśaḥ prekṣamāṇaḥ sthito 'smīti kṛcchrād abhivyāharan kām avasthām abhiprāpsyasi tvaṃ dhṛto duṣkṛtaiḥ karmabhir
children.translated_text: Threatened with "Stop! Stop!" by the servants of <s>Antaka</s> (Death) — whose eyes are fixed [with rage] as if encircled by blazing fire, whose lip-coverings are bitten with quivering fury, who hold weapons raised and ready, who carry out <s>Yama</s>'s commands — terrified, looking in all directions, barely able to utter "I am standing still" — what state will you reach, held captive by your own evil deeds?

children.text: yadi samanuvicārayet tad bhavān nūnam – – ⏑ – – ⏑ pādopamāḥ syur nidāghe 'titīvrā amī bhūpate na tv anabhyāhatā yānti saṃvegam ajñā janāḥ prāyaśo duḥkhayantrāntarasthās tu śocanti moghaṃ pralāpārtiśokābhibhūtā bhṛśam || GoAś_34 ||
children.translated_text: If you would reflect upon this [carefully] ... these [sufferings] in the hot season would be exceedingly fierce, O lord of the earth; but the ignorant do not feel alarm unless struck [directly]. Mostly, people caught in the machinery of suffering lament in vain, completely overwhelmed by futile prattle, pain, and grief. // GoAś 34 //

children.text: api ca he putraka ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, O son —

children.text: kāntākarāgravidhṛtāni madhūni pītvā niśvāsasaṃcitadalotpalacandrikāṇi |
children.translated_text: Having drunk the honeys held in the lovely fingertips of your beloved,

children.text: saṃdaṃśayantravivṛtāsyapuṭāntarālas tāmraṃ kathaṃ kathaya pāsyasi vahnivarṇam || GoAś_35 ||
children.translated_text: fragrant with the moonlight of blue lotuses gathered by her sighs — how, tell me, will you drink the molten copper, fire-colored, [poured] into your forcibly opened mouth held agape by pincers? // GoAś 35 //

children.text: snātvā tvaṃ gṛhadīrghikāmbhasi hasatpadmotpalālaṃkṛte
children.translated_text: Having bathed in the pool of your mansion, adorned with laughing lotuses and water-lilies,

children.text: tīrāntānatapuṣpapādapalatācchāyāsamāliṅgite |
children.translated_text: embraced by the shade of flowering tree-creepers bending at the bank —

children.text: klinnasvinnanarāsthipañjaravasāniryāsaparyākule
children.translated_text: fallen into the boiling waters of the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> (river of hell), filled with the oozing fat, marrow, and bones of cooked, sweating human bodies,

children.text: tapte vaitaraṇījale nipatito duḥkhāt kadā mokṣyase || GoAś_36 ||
children.translated_text: when will you be freed from suffering? // GoAś 36 //

children.text: prāsāde śaradabhraśubhraśikhare puṣpāvalīmaṇḍite
children.translated_text: In a palace with peaks white as autumn clouds, adorned with garlands of flowers,

children.text: vīṇāveṇumṛdaṅgagītamadhure saṃprāpya citraṃ sukham |
children.translated_text: sweetened by the music of <s>vīṇā</s>, flute, and <s>mṛdaṅga</s> — having obtained such marvellous happiness,

children.text: nityaṃ prajvalitasphuṭānalaśikhāsaṃtānajālākulaṃ
children.translated_text: then reaching <s>Avīci</s> (the deepest hell), thronged with networks of ever-blazing, crackling fire-flames,

children.text: prāpyāvīcim anekaduḥkhavihataḥ kiṃ nāma kartā bhavān || GoAś_37 ||
children.translated_text: struck by manifold sufferings — what will you do then? // GoAś 37 //

children.text: lajjāmātravibhūṣaṇāṃ savinayāṃ cārūpacārāṃ priyāṃ
children.translated_text: Having seen your beloved, whose only ornament is modesty, gentle in manner, charming in conduct,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā prītivijṛmbhamāṇanayano viśrambhaniryantraṇām |
children.translated_text: your eyes blossoming with delight, unrestrained in her trust —

children.text: krodhaprajvalitākṣikośaviṣamabhrūbhaṅgaraudrānanān
children.translated_text: and then beholding the servants of Death (<s>Antaka</s>) face to face, with eyes blazing with wrath, with terrible furrowed brows,

children.text: ālokyāntakakiṃkarān abhimukhān saṃmoham āyāsyase || GoAś_38 ||
children.translated_text: you will fall into a swoon. // GoAś 38 //

children.text: śrīmaccāmaracārubhāsuranarair nānāvidhair vājibhiḥ
children.translated_text: With splendid men radiant [as attendants] bearing beautiful <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks), with various steeds,

children.text: kāliṅgaiś ca vicitritottarakuthair gandhopavāhyair gajaiḥ |
children.translated_text: with elephants from <s>Kaliṅga</s>, adorned with variegated saddle-cloths, wafting fragrance —

children.text: tīvrakrodhaviṣais tṛ – ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ – – – ⏑ – – ⏑ –
children.translated_text: [yet then] with serpents of fierce, poisonous wrath ...

children.text: – – – ⏑ ⏑ ke viśīrṇacaraṇo voḍhāsi dīptān rathān || GoAś_39 ||
children.translated_text: ... with feet shattered, you shall be made to pull blazing chariots. // GoAś 39 //

children.text: dhṛtaś cūḍāpīḍo bakulakusumāmodasubhagas
children.translated_text: That topknot-ornament of <s>bakula</s> (Mimusops) flowers, delightful with fragrance,

children.text: tvayā mūrdhnā yena sphuṭamaṇikarālaṃ ca mukuṭam |
children.translated_text: which you wore upon your head, and the diadem fearsome with gleaming jewels —

children.text: sphuradvahnijvālāvalayakapilaṃ cakram aśivaṃ
children.translated_text: with that very head you shall bear the inauspicious wheel (of torture),

children.text: vahan mūrdhnā tena tvam anubhavitā cāpalaphalam || GoAś_40 ||
children.translated_text: tawny with encircling rings of flashing fire-flames — thus you shall experience the fruit of fickleness. // GoAś 40 //

children.text: kiṃ ca bhūyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: kaler ājñābhaṅgo bhavati sucirāj janmasamaye
children.translated_text: When transgression of the command of <s>Kali</s> (the dark age) occurs, at the time of birth,

children.text: muner yasya prāṇipriyahitasamādhānaviduṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: of the sage who was skilled in securing the welfare of all living beings —

children.text: jagannāthe tasmin bhagavati bhavopadravahare
children.translated_text: when that <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), lord of the world, remover of the calamities of existence,

children.text: praduṣṭānāṃ kā vā bhavatu gatir anyā param ataḥ || GoAś_41 ||
children.translated_text: is offended — what other refuge can there be for the corrupt beyond this? // GoAś 41 //

children.text:
unmīlitā iva diśo daśa yasya dīptaiḥ
kīrtyaṃśubhir ghanatamaḥpaṭalāvanaddhāḥ |
tasmin pradoṣam upagacchati yas tapasvī
svair eva karma
children.translated_text: by one's own deeds

children.text: bhir asau prahataḥ kṣatātmā || GoAś_42 ||
children.translated_text: is that self-injured one struck down. // GoAś 42 //
He whose brilliant rays of fame illuminated, as it were, the ten directions, shrouded as they were by dense curtains of darkness — when one transgresses against that ascetic,

children.text: yo māteva piteva bāndhava iva prāṇiṣv anukrośavān
children.translated_text: He who, like a mother, like a father, like a kinsman, is compassionate toward all beings,

children.text: ātmasnehaparāṅmukhena manasā janmāṭavīgahvare |
children.translated_text: with a mind turned away from self-love, in the dense jungle of birth-and-death —

children.text: prajñāvīryakṛpābhyupāyasacivaḥ kleśair anākampitaḥ
children.translated_text: attended by the ministers of wisdom, heroism, compassion, and skillful means, unshaken by afflictions,

children.text: prāpto bodhim anuttarāṃ sa bhagavān kāṃ satkriyāṃ nārhati || GoAś_43 ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Bhagavān</s> who attained the supreme <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening) — what honor does he not deserve? // GoAś 43 //

children.text: jagaddhitādhānavidhānadīkṣāṃ babhāra śāstā bhṛśadurvahāṃ yaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Śāstā</s> (Teacher), who bore the consecration of the vow to establish the welfare of the world, exceedingly difficult to bear —

children.text: manaḥprasādāyatane 'pi tasmin kathaṃ nu cittāni vidūṣayanti || GoAś_44 ||
children.translated_text: how can they defile their minds even toward him, who is the abode of mental serenity? // GoAś 44 //

children.text: asajjanasamāgamasya kaṭukāvasānaṃ phalaṃ
children.translated_text: The bitter fruit that is the consequence of association with the wicked,

children.text: narendra samupasthitaṃ tad adhunā tavāpāyikam |
children.translated_text: O lord of men, has now arrived for you — that which leads to ruin;

children.text: idaṃ samanucintya sādhujanasaṃgamaḥ sevyatāṃ
children.translated_text: reflecting on this, one should cultivate the company of the virtuous,

children.text: tatas tava bhaviṣyati vyasanapañjarān nirgamaḥ || GoAś_45 ||
children.translated_text: and then there shall be for you an escape from the cage of calamity. // GoAś 45 //

children.text: evaṃ gate 'pi kriyatām prayatnaḥ pāpaprahāṇe kuśalodaye ca |
children.translated_text: Even so, let effort be made in the abandonment of sin and the arising of virtue;

children.text: apy eva nāma vyasanāmburāśeḥ syāt te 'vasānaṃ naralokapāla || GoAś_46 ||
children.translated_text: perhaps then, O protector of men, there may be an end to the ocean of calamity for you. // GoAś 46 //

children.text: anekarūpavyasanopamṛṣṭāṃ samudravelājalalolaśīlām |
children.translated_text: Embracing the royal fortune that is beset by manifold calamities,

children.text: narendralakṣmīm upaguhya pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā duḥkhaśatāvasānam || GoAś_47 ||
children.translated_text: restless as the waves at the ocean's shore —

children.text: bahuprakārātyayadāruṇeṣu vicāryamāṇālpasukhodayeṣu |
children.translated_text: sin has been committed by you, ending in a hundred sufferings. // GoAś 47 //

children.text: viṣajya kāmeṣu manas tvayātmā svayaṃ kṛto durgatiduḥkhasākṣī || GoAś_48 ||
children.translated_text: Attaching your mind to sensual pleasures — which, when examined, yield but little happiness amid their manifold terrible dangers —

children.text: abhisandhikṛtasya karmaṇo na hi nāśaṃ pravadanti sūrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: you have made yourself a witness to the suffering of evil destinies. // GoAś 48 //

children.text: api kalpasahasrakoṭibhiḥ phaladaṃ tan niyamena jāyate || GoAś_49 ||
children.translated_text: Of an intentionally performed deed, the wise do not proclaim destruction;

children.text: ata eva jagau jagadvaro jagadālokakaraḥ kṛpāmayaḥ |
children.translated_text: even after billions of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), it inevitably becomes fruit-bearing. // GoAś 49 //

children.text: bhagavān bhavabhoganiḥspṛhaḥ sa hi karmasvakatāṃ śarīriṇām || GoAś_50 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the best in the world, the illuminator of the world, full of compassion,

children.text: salilānalarājataskarair dhanam atraiva vilupyate nṛṇām |
children.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s>, free from desire for the enjoyments of existence — he has declared that beings are the owners of their own <s>karma</s>. // GoAś 50 //

children.text: prabhavanti tu tena karmaṇā svam ataḥ karma nṛṇāṃ śubhāśubham || GoAś_51 ||
children.translated_text: By water, fire, kings, and thieves, wealth is plundered right here in this world;

children.text: parivartati niścalekṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇamātrapratibaddhajīvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: but through that very <s>karma</s> they prosper — therefore one's own <s>karma</s>, good and bad, is [the true wealth] of people. // GoAś 51 //

children.text: maraṇābhimukho yadā naro nanu karmaiva tadā parāyaṇam || GoAś_52 ||
children.translated_text: When a person with fixed gaze, with life bound to a mere instant,

children.text: svajano janavan nivartane gṛhavittādyaparair vilupyate |
sva
children.translated_text: One's kin turn back like mere people at the departure; home, wealth, and the rest are plundered by others;

children.text: kṛtaṃ tv anuyāti dehināṃ bhavasaṃkrāntyanukūlavartinām || GoAś_53 ||
children.translated_text: but one's own
faces death — then truly <s>karma</s> alone is the [final] refuge. // GoAś 52 //

children.text: api ca he mahārāja ||
children.translated_text: self-made [<s>karma</s>] follows the embodied beings who travel in conformity with the transmigration of existences. // GoAś 53 //

children.text:
maraṇavaśagatasya jantor vivṛddholbaṇaśvāsaśuṣkauṣṭhakaṇṭhasya
hikkāpraveśānubandhād vinirdhūyamānorasaḥ
kalavikalapadākṣare bhāṣite vihvale cakṣuṣi cchidyamāneṣu
marmasv anāmantrya roṣād iva prasthi
tair vā
children.translated_text: For a creature fallen into the power of death, whose throat and lips are parched from violent, labored breathing, whose chest heaves from the onset of hiccups, whose speech is faltering with broken, feeble syllables, whose vision is blurred, whose vital points are being severed, [abandoned] as if in anger by the departing

children.text:
yubhiḥ |
mahati śithilatāṃ gate sandhisaṃghātayantre rujātīkṣṇasūcī-
children.translated_text: life-breaths,

children.text: nipātāntare kvāpi gantuṃ kṛtābhyudyame jīvite
children.translated_text: when the great machine of joint-ligaments has become loose, when amidst the piercing of exceedingly sharp needles of pain, life makes its effort to depart to some unknown place —

children.text: timiragahanasaṃkaṭaṃ nirjanaṃ mārgam ākrāmato nāsti puṇyād
children.translated_text: as one treads the dark, dense, narrow, lonely path, there is no friend other than merit (<s>puṇya</s>);

children.text: ṛte kaś cid anyaḥ sakhā tat prayatnaṃ kuru śreyasi || GoAś_54 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, make effort toward the good. // GoAś 54 //
Moreover, O great king —

children.text: api ca mahārāja ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, O great king —

children.text: avaśyaṃ tyaktavyaḥ paramadayito bāndhavajanaḥ
children.translated_text: The most beloved circle of kinfolk must inevitably be abandoned;

children.text: praveṣṭavyaṃ ghoraṃ sabhayam asahāyena gahanam |
children.translated_text: the terrible, fearful wilderness must be entered, unaccompanied;

children.text: pravāse vastavyaṃ suciram api cāsaṃstutajane
children.translated_text: one must dwell for a long time in exile among unknown people —

children.text: tad asmāt kartavyaṃ bahukuśalapātheyam asakṛt || GoAś_55 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, provisions of abundant merit should be gathered again and again. // GoAś 55 //

children.text: atha sa rājā tena bhikṣuṇā tathā saṃvejito yathā kṣaṇenopalabdhakuśalamūlopacayābhilāṣas tīvrabhayaviṣādavyākulamānasaś ca provāca ||
children.translated_text: Then that king, so deeply stirred by the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), having in an instant developed a desire to accumulate roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), and with a mind agitated by intense fear and dismay, spoke thus:

children.text: tad
children.translated_text: "Then

children.text: adhunā karavāṇi bhadanta he vada vadāsti dayā yadi te mayi |
children.translated_text: now let me act, O venerable one — speak, speak, if you have compassion for me!

children.text: nipatitaṃ mahati vyasanārṇave kṛpaṇakaṃ kṛpayoddhara māṃ yate || GoAś_56 ||
children.translated_text: Lift up this wretched one, fallen into the great ocean of calamity, with your compassion, O ascetic! // GoAś 56 //

children.text: jaladamārutacandanaśītalair api vayaṃ vacanais tava tāpitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even by your words, cool as rain-clouds, wind, and sandalwood, we are scorched,

children.text: svakṛtaduṣkṛtaśaṅkuśatakṣatā viṣayalaulyaparājitamānasāḥ || GoAś_57 ||
children.translated_text: wounded by hundreds of thorns of our own evil deeds, our minds defeated by the fickleness of sensual pleasures. // GoAś 57 //

children.text: vipariṇāmakaṭūni mayā purā viṣayasaṅgasukhāny akṛtātmanām |
children.translated_text: The pleasures of sensual attachment, bitter in their final transformation — I, with uncontrolled mind,

children.text: samupaguhya kṛtaṃ bahu duṣkṛtaṃ dahati yan mama saṃprati mānasam || GoAś_58 ||
children.translated_text: embracing them, have committed much evil, which now burns my heart. // GoAś 58 //

children.text: dhig avaraṃ viṣamaṃ viṣayāśrayaṃ sukham anāryaniṣevitam adhruvam |
children.translated_text: Shame upon the base, crooked, sense-dependent happiness — frequented by the ignoble, impermanent —

children.text: yad upagamya narā viṣayadviṣām iha bhavanti sadā karuṇāspadam || GoAś_59 ||
children.translated_text: for, having resorted to it, people in this world forever become objects of pity, enemies of sensual pleasures. // GoAś 59 //

children.text: avinayo 'nugato mṛditaṃ yaśo na gaṇitaṃ kulam āyatir u
jjhitā |
children.translated_text: [...continued]

children.text: ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ – kaluṣaṃ vivṛto 'nayo viṣayalaulya
children.translated_text: ... defilement is laid bare, ruin exposed

children.text: tayā
children.translated_text: through the fickleness

children.text: ⏑ ⏑ yāgayā || GoAś_60 ||
children.translated_text: of sensual indulgence. // GoAś 60 //
Indiscipline has followed me; fame has been crushed; family has been disregarded; the future has been abandoned;

children.text: asadṛśajanasaṅgābhyāsa
do
children.translated_text: [continued]

children.translated_text: so that I have become pitiable among those rich in virtues. // GoAś 61 //
Through the fault of habitual association with unworthy people,

The virtuous, of naturally beautiful conduct, were not heeded — [they who were] the cause of words sweet as honey for the well-regarded; since I, dwelling within the thicket of misconduct,

children.text: viṣayasukhalavāśāpāśam āmucya citte tṛṇalavam iva jīrṇaṃ projjhya sadvṛttavantam |
children.translated_text: Having released from the heart the noose-trap of the craving for sensual pleasure, discarding it like a withered blade of grass, [I shall follow] the one of good conduct; [yet] of deeds bitter in their ripening, by oneself alone

children.translated_text: have been accumulated heaps as lofty as mountains. // GoAś 63 //

children.text: diksaṃmoham upāgato 'ham adhunā gacchāmi kāṃ vā diśaṃ
children.translated_text: I am now bewildered as to direction — to which quarter shall I go?

children.text: majjāmīva bhadanta śokasarasi vyā – ⏑ – – ⏑ – – /
children.translated_text: O venerable one, I sink as if into a lake of grief ...

children.text: śailo 'yaṃ sphuṭatīva pāpacaritaṃ mām adya saṃdhārayan
children.translated_text: This mountain seems to split asunder, bearing me of sinful conduct today;

children.text: yuṣmatpādasamāśrayāt tu śatadhā na tv eva yāti dhruvam || GoAś_65 ||
children.translated_text: but through taking refuge at your feet, it shall certainly not break into a hundred pieces. // GoAś 65 //"

children.text: atha sa mahātmā taṃ rājānaṃ saṃvignamānasam avetya pātram ayaṃ śreyasa iti vinirdhāryovāca | tena hi mahārāja tam eva bhagavantaṃ vinipāta ... janāvalambavatsalam apā ... tyaktasakalasattvadhātum akhilajagaddhitādhānāmlānaprayogam aparimitaviśuddhodārātiśayaguṇagaṇaratnādhivāsaṃ mahākāruṇikaṃ sarvajñaṃ sarvadarśanaṃ śākyamuniṃ śaraṇam upaihi | tata eva te duḥkhaparaṃparāparyanto bhaviṣyati + + + + + + + + + + |
children.translated_text: Then that great soul, perceiving the king's mind to be deeply stirred, determining "this one is a fit vessel for the good," spoke: "Therefore, O great king, take refuge in that very <s>Bhagavān</s> — tender toward those who [face] downfall ... compassionate toward [all] beings ... who has relinquished the entire realm of sentient beings [from suffering], whose unwearied efforts [are directed toward] establishing the welfare of the whole world, whose abode is adorned with the jewels of immeasurable, pure, exalted, and supreme qualities — the greatly compassionate, all-knowing, all-seeing <s>Śākyamuni</s>. From that alone shall there be an end to the succession of your sufferings ..."

children.text: sukṣetre bījam uptaṃ bhavati bahuphalaṃ tiktam āsyapriyaṃ
children.translated_text: A seed sown in good soil becomes abundantly fruitful, whether bitter or pleasing to the taste —

children.text: vā kṣetrasyāsau svabhāvo bhavati samaguṇaḥ sarvasasyaprasūtau |
children.translated_text: for it is the nature of the field to be equal in producing all crops;

children.text: evaṃ kārāpakārā bhagavati tanavo 'py āhitāḥ pāpakāle
children.translated_text: thus, even slight acts of service or disservice toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, committed in a time of sin,

children.text: paryantaṃ nāpnuvanti vyuparatasakalakleśasaṃtānakāle || GoAś_66 ||
children.translated_text: do not reach their end [even] when the succession of all afflictions has ceased. // GoAś 66 //

children.text: atha sa bhūpatiḥ pravijṛmbhamāṇakuśalamūlopacayābhilāṣamṛduhṛdayatayā buddhe bhagavati samutpannapremagauravaprasādabahumānaḥ sapratyayāśrusalilabāṣpāviladīnamṛdumukulitanayanayugalavadanas taṃ bhikṣum udīkṣamāṇo bāṣpagaṇḍūṣoparudhyamānakaṣāyakaṇṭho dharaṇitalapratiṣṭhitajānumaṇḍalaḥ kṛtakarapuṭa ity uvāca ||
children.translated_text: Then that king, his heart softened by the blossoming desire to accumulate roots of merit, having developed toward the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> love, reverence, serenity, and high esteem — with eyes gently half-closed, moist with tears of conviction, with face dimmed — gazing at that <s>bhikṣu</s>, his throat choked by a mouthful of tears, with knees placed on the ground, palms joined together, spoke thus:

children.text: eṣo 'haṃ tam ṛṣiṃ vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ prāṇair api prāṇinām
children.translated_text: "I go for refuge to that sage — who, even at the cost of life, is the sole kinsman of living beings,

children.text: ekaṃ bāndhavam ekam eva suhṛdaṃ śāstāram ekaṃ param |
children.translated_text: the one friend, the one supreme Teacher,

children.text: trāṇaṃ traibhuvanārtigahvaradarīvyāvartināṃ prāṇinām
children.translated_text: the protector of beings caught in the whirlpool of the cave of suffering in the three worlds,

children.text: ācāryaṃ paramārthatattvaviṣaye bhūtārthanāthaṃ vibhum || GoAś_67 ||
children.translated_text: the master in the domain of ultimate truth, the lord of beings in their true reality, the all-pervading one. // GoAś 67 //

children.text: punaḥ punar anuttaraṃ puruṣadamyasatsārathiṃ
children.translated_text: Again and again I go for refuge to the supreme, the best charioteer for those who are to be tamed,

children.text: prayāmi śaraṇaṃ śaraṇyatamam apy ahaṃ – ⏑ – |
children.translated_text: the most worthy of refuge ...

children.text: acintyacaritaṃ tam eva bhagavantam adya kṛta-
children.translated_text: to that very <s>Bhagavān</s> of inconceivable conduct, today —

children.text: prapañcaviṣabījanirmalaniruttarādhyāśayam || GoAś_68 ||
children.translated_text: whose intention is pure, stainless, unsurpassed, having destroyed the seeds of the poison of worldly proliferation. // GoAś 68 //

children.text: apy asthitishitimatāṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye
children.translated_text: I take refuge also in the shelter of those who are firmly established,

children.text: lokopakārakaraṇaikarasasvabhāvam |
children.translated_text: whose very nature is the single passion of benefiting the world —

children.text: buddhaṃ tam eva śatadhā ca sahasradhā cā-
children.translated_text: in that <s>Buddha</s>, a hundredfold and a thousandfold,

children.text: – – ⏑ – ⏑ makarālayakarṇadhāram || GoAś_69 ||
children.translated_text: ... the helmsman [who steers across] the abode of sea-monsters (the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>). // GoAś 69 //

children.text: manye pūtam ivātmabhāvam adhunā śāstuḥ praṇāmodbhavaiḥ
children.translated_text: I feel my being purified, as it were, by the sacred waters born of bowing to the <s>Śāstā</s> (Teacher),

children.text: puṇyāmbhobhir akhaṇḍamaṇḍalaśaśijyotsnāvalīnirmalaiḥ |
children.translated_text: spotless as moonbeams of a full moon —

children.text: ko vā taṃ praṇipatya sāndrakaruṇāprahlāditādhyāśayaṃ
children.translated_text: and who, having bowed to him whose inner disposition is gladdened by intense compassion,

children.text: tīvrāpāyavatīṃ viṣādamakarāṃ tīrṇo na duḥkhāpagām || GoAś_70 ||
children.translated_text: with terrible calamities, with crocodiles of despair — he has not crossed the river of suffering. [GoAś 70]

children.text: yatraiko 'py akṛtadhiyo manaḥpradoṣaḥ saṃsāraṃ vyasanaśatais tanoti kṛtsnam |
children.translated_text: Where even a single defilement of the mind of the unwise extends the entire cycle of existence (<s>saṃsāra</s>) with hundreds of miseries,

children.text: tatraikaḥ katham api cetasaḥ prasādo nocchindyād vyasanasahasratantujālam || GoAś_71 ||
children.translated_text: how could a single serenity of mind there not sever the web woven of thousands of miseries? [GoAś 71]

children.text: yaṃ gatvā śaraṇam ahaṃ jagatpradīpaṃ sarvāsaccaritavirodhinīṃ prapannaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having taken refuge in him, the lamp of the world, I have entered upon the path of the noble ones, which opposes all wicked conduct,

children.text: āryāṇāṃ nayapadavīṃ samantabhadrāṃ taṃ vande kṛpaṇajanādhikānukampam || GoAś_72 ||
children.translated_text: universally auspicious — I bow to him, who has the highest compassion for wretched beings. [GoAś 72]

children.text: ity uktvā vyasanaparāṅmukhaḥ sa rājā saṃbuddhe bhagavati niścalaprasādaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that king, turned away from misery, with unwavering devotion to the blessed <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One),

children.text: taṃ bhikṣuṃ kṣititalalagnamaulimūrdhnā vanditvā svapuravaronmukho jagāma || GoAś_73 ||
children.translated_text: having bowed to that monk with his crown touching the ground, departed toward his excellent city. [GoAś 73]

The king obtained such faith in the <s>Saṃbuddha</s> that it reduced to a mere remnant the mountain-mass of karmic obstructions. The sin that is committed against a <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), that, through those

children.text: apy eva krakacair niśātadaśanacchedāvalīdanturais
children.translated_text: Even if [one were cut] by saws with rows of sharp-toothed cuts, jagged,

children.text: tasyājñā pravicāryamānatanubhiḥ kāryaiva śāstur bhavet |
children.translated_text: the command of the Teacher must indeed be carried out by those whose bodies are being examined [by pain].

children.text: yasmāt tadvimukhā viśanti narakān jvālāvalīdāruṇān
children.translated_text: Because those who turn away from him enter terrible hells blazing with rows of flames,

children.text: tasyājñāpravaṇai ⏑ – natasukhaṃ saṃprāpyate śāśvatam || GoAś_75 ||
children.translated_text: while by those devoted to his command, ⏑ – eternal happiness is attained. [GoAś 75]

children.text: svābhiprāyam ato bravīmi sakalaṃ saṃsāram apy utsahe
children.translated_text: Therefore I speak my own conviction: I am prepared to dwell even in the entire cycle of existence,

children.text: vastuṃ bhīmabhayānake 'pi narake loke jinālaṃkṛte |
children.translated_text: even in a terrifying, fearsome hell, in a world adorned by the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: na tv evaikam api kṣaṇaṃ surapure saṃbuddhaśūnye jagaty
children.translated_text: but not for even a single moment in the city of the gods, in a world devoid of the <s>Saṃbuddha</s>,

children.text: udvṛttakṣatavṛttarākṣasagaṇavyāluptapuṇyotsave || GoAś_76 ||
children.translated_text: where hordes of demons with unrestrained, wound-inflicting conduct have plundered the festival of merit. [GoAś 76]

children.text: tad yāvan na patati sarva eva loko durdṛṣṭimatavitate pramādakūpe |
children.translated_text: Therefore, before the entire world falls into the well of heedlessness, spread over by the net of wrong views,

children.text: sarvajñapravacanabhāskare gate 'staṃ tat tāvad vacanarasāyanaṃ niṣevyam || GoAś_77 ||
children.translated_text: before the sun of the Omniscient One's teaching has set — until then, the elixir of [his] words must be consumed. [GoAś 77]

children.text: sarvajñe paramagurau niveśya bhaktiṃ śrotavyaṃ vacanam ṛṣeḥ samantaśobhi |
children.translated_text: Having placed devotion in the Omniscient One, the supreme teacher, one should hear the word of the sage, radiant on all sides,

children.text: nikṣipya vyasanamayīṃ kukāryacintāṃ nāto 'nyat param adhikaṃ yato 'sti kṛtyam || GoAś_78 ||
children.translated_text: casting aside the thought of wicked deeds, full of misery — for there is no higher and greater duty than this. [GoAś 78]

children.text: śravaṇakarakaiḥ ko 'rthas teṣāṃ asacchru ⏑ – ⏑ –
children.translated_text: What use are ears for those who hear [only] what is false ⏑ – ⏑ –

children.text: 2. Bhavalubdhaka
children.translated_text: 2. <s>Bhavalubdhaka</s> (The Existence-Hunter)

children.text: āpāyānām avicchinnaprāyasaṃsāravartmanām |
children.translated_text: On the paths of worldly existence, which are mostly uninterrupted series of calamities,

children.text: karmakleśavaśāvaśyā duḥkhamayyaḥ pravṛttayaḥ || GoBhl_1 ||
children.translated_text: the activities, full of suffering, are compelled by the power of <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśa</s> (defilements). [GoBhl 1]

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate |
children.translated_text: As the story is heard:

children.text: dvau bhikṣū srotāpannau babhūvatus tābhyām ekenāśeṣasaṃyojanopakṣayād arhattvam adhigatam | taddvitīyas tanmātrasaṃtuṣṭa evāsīt | sa tenārhatocyate sma | bhadramukha śeṣakleśaviṣopaśamāya yatnam ārabhasveti | duḥkhaikarasā bhavā duṣṭapāpasiddhyupāyāni śreyāṃsi kṣaṇalavapariṇāmāviśvasanīyaṃ jīvitam apariniṣpannaprakṛtayo māyopamās tattvavirodhinaḥ kāmāḥ sabhayāḥ savairāḥ sopāyāsāḥ pāpakriyām evāṅgīkṛtya pravṛttāḥ paribhavāyatanam akṛtabuddhīnāṃ kṛtātmanām apy avahāsyatām āvahanti | leśenāpy anugamyamānā mahad duḥkham ākarṣanti | naitān anupatan kaś cid akṣato 'nupahato vā | hrīmanto 'py ebhir āviṣṭāḥ paśusahadharmatāṃ pratipadyante | naite tulayanti vayasāṃ pariṇāmavaikṛtam | yatijanam apy ete pragalbhā vyāmohayanty eva | śreyaso vadhakāḥ pratyamitrāś cāmī vyatītya vinayaniyamaśrībharām āryamaryādām anāryakam evodbhāvayanti | samuditakāntiśobham api kṣaṇena malinayanti puruṣasya śīlasauṣṭhavam | vipātite ca śīle sarvaviṣayāya dvārabhūte hatopaniṣatsamādhir nālaṃ prajñāsaṃpade | sakala eva ca saṃsāra eṣāṃ durantarāyāṇāṃ paryeṣaṇābhir atītaḥ | ye ca śvasūkarādīnām api sādhāraṇā ratiprasaṅgadohadāḥ kas tān sādhujano manasāpi prārthayet | sa tam arhantam abravīt | bhadramukha
children.translated_text: There were two monks who had attained the state of <s>srotāpanna</s> (stream-enterer). One of them, by the complete destruction of all fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), had attained <s>arhatva</s> (the state of an arhat). The second was content with just that [stream-entry]. The [arhat] said to him: "Good sir, you should exert yourself for the pacification of the remaining poison of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>!" Worldly existences (<s>bhava</s>) have suffering as their sole essence; the means to welfare are accomplished through evil and sin; life is not to be trusted, being subject to momentary, slight transformation; sense-pleasures (<s>kāma</s>) are of unfulfilled nature, like illusions, opposed to truth, accompanied by fear, hostility, and distress, proceeding only by embracing sinful action, a ground for contempt by the unwise, bringing ridicule even upon the self-controlled; even when followed to a slight degree, they drag one into great suffering. No one who follows them remains unharmed or unwounded. Even the modest, when possessed by them, attain the condition of animals. They do not weigh the deterioration wrought by the passage of age. These bold [desires] delude even ascetics. These killers of welfare, these enemies, having transgressed the noble boundary adorned with the glory of discipline and restraint, produce only ignobility. They instantly sully the beauty of a man's character, even when it shines with radiant splendor. And when character has fallen — it being the gateway to all [sense] domains — meditation whose foundation is the secret teaching is destroyed, and is insufficient for the attainment of wisdom. The entire cycle of existence has been spent in the pursuit of these [desires], whose dangers are endless. And those cravings for the excitement of pleasure that are common even to dogs and pigs — what virtuous person would desire them even in thought?" He said to the arhat: "Good sir,

children.text: bhavā duḥkhātmakāḥ santi śreyo durabhisaṃbhavam |
children.translated_text: worldly existences are indeed of the nature of suffering; welfare is hard to attain;

children.text: jīvitaṃ calam atyantaṃ kāmā doṣaśatākarāḥ || GoBhl_2 ||
children.translated_text: life is extremely unstable; and sense-pleasures are the abode of hundreds of faults. [GoBhl 2]

children.text: apāyā mama saṃkṣīṇāḥ kiñciccheṣo bhavārṇavaḥ |
children.translated_text: My [rebirths in] the lower realms have been exhausted; only a little of the ocean of existence remains.

children.text: anubhūya sukhaṃ divyaṃ nirvāsyāmi niyogataḥ || GoBhl_3 ||
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed divine happiness, I shall attain final release (<s>nirvāṇa</s>) in due course. [GoBhl 3]

children.text: api cākṛtapuṇyānāṃ bhavebhyo jāyate bhayam |
children.translated_text: Moreover, for those who have not accumulated merit, fear arises from [worldly] existences.

children.text: puṇyasambhārayuktānām utsavātiśayo bhavaḥ || GoBhl_4 ||
children.translated_text: For those endowed with a store of merit, existence is a supreme festival. [GoBhl 4]

children.text: nānāvipattigahaneṣv anayaprapāteṣv andhān ivāśu pithite pathi saṃnipātya |
children.translated_text: In the dense thickets of manifold calamities, at the precipices of misfortune, as if thrusting the blind onto a path quickly blocked,

children.text: āryān api pratibhayena pathā harantaḥ prakhyāpayanty aśucayo viṣayāḥ svaśaktim || GoBhl_5 ||
children.translated_text: even carrying the noble along a frightening road — the impure sense-objects proclaim their own power. [GoBhl 5]

children.text: atha so 'rhan mandasaṃvegāpanno 'yam āyuṣmān iti viditvā tam āha |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>arhat</s>, knowing "this venerable one is of sluggish spiritual urgency," said to him:

children.text: āyuṣman sapratidvandvāḥ parīttāsvādadūṣitāḥ |
children.translated_text: "Venerable one, existences are beset with adversaries, corrupted by paltry enjoyments,

children.text: bhavā niśitanistriṃśadhārāsaṃpātadāruṇāḥ || GoBhl_6 ||
children.translated_text: as terrible as the striking of the edge of a sharpened sword. [GoBhl 6]

children.text: nopādānakṣamās tāta bhavāḥ kruddhā ivoragāḥ |
children.translated_text: Existences are not fit for grasping, dear one — like angry serpents,

children.text: viṣāgnikavalālokakarālamukhaśaktayaḥ || GoBhl_7 ||
children.translated_text: whose powers are terrifying: jaws [gaping like] the sight of a morsel of poison-fire. [GoBhl 7]

children.text: dagdhapravṛttyupādānavāsanāmalamānasaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By the Lords of the world, whose minds are purified of the stains of residual impressions of burnt-out activity and grasping —

children.text: pravṛttayo jagannāthaiḥ sarvā eva vivarjitāḥ || GoBhl_8 ||
children.translated_text: all activities whatsoever have been abandoned. [GoBhl 8]

children.text: bhavān pariharanty ārād ātmakāmāḥ parīkṣakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who love the self and are discerning avoid existences from afar —

children.text: paricchannataṭāgādhāñ śvabhrāpātabhayaṃkarān || GoBhl_9 ||
children.translated_text: [existences] with concealed banks, fathomless, frightening with the danger of falling into pits. [GoBhl 9]

children.text: ratīnāṃ sopatāpānāṃ mukhe sa parivartate |
children.translated_text: He revolves in the mouth of pleasures accompanied by distress —

children.text: abhinandaty anādeyān kṣaṇikān api yo bhavān || GoBhl_10 ||
children.translated_text: he who delights in existences that are unacceptable, even though momentary. [GoBhl 10]

children.text: vicchinnāśeṣasaṃskārapravāhapratisaṃdhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatas</s> declare that rebirth (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>), in which the stream of all residual impressions has been severed,

children.text: pratisaṃdhim upāyāsamūlam āhus tathāgatāḥ || GoBhl_11 ||
children.translated_text: [that very] rebirth-linking is rooted in distress. [GoBhl 11]

children.text: visaṃvādinya evaitā gatayo mahatām api |
children.translated_text: These destinies are indeed deceitful, even for the great,

children.text: vividhānarthanārācasaṃnipātakhalūrikāḥ || GoBhl_12 ||
children.translated_text: like a threshing floor struck by a hail of arrows of manifold misfortune. [GoBhl 12]

children.text: ādīptaḥ sarva evāyaṃ saṃsāraviṣapādapaḥ |
children.translated_text: This entire tree of the poison of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) is ablaze

children.text: viṣvagvikāsiduḥkhāgner jvālāmālākadambakaiḥ || GoBhl_13 ||
children.translated_text: with clusters of garlands of flames from the fire of suffering spreading in all directions. [GoBhl 13]

children.text: bhavopabhogaspṛhalālasāḥ svayaṃ praviśya saṃmohatamisradurdinān |
children.translated_text: Those who yearn with craving for the enjoyments of existence, having entered of their own accord the stormy gloom of delusion,

children.text: caranti mattā iva bhagnalocanā ghanāndhakāre viparītabuddhayaḥ || GoBhl_14 ||
children.translated_text: wander like drunkards with impaired vision, in dense darkness, with perverted understanding. [GoBhl 14]

children.text: hitodyatānām avakīrya bhāratīṃ nipātarūkṣāṃ pariṇāmapeśalām |
children.translated_text: Scattering the speech of those intent upon their welfare — speech that is harsh at the fall but elegant in its result —

children.text: anarthapaṅkaughanimagnaśaktayo bhavanti niśvāsaparāyaṇā narāḥ || GoBhl_15 ||
children.translated_text: their powers submerged in a flood of the mire of misfortune, men become devoted [only] to sighing. [GoBhl 15]

children.text: latāṃ dvirephā iva puṣpahāsinīm upāsate ye tu satāṃ sarasvatīm |
children.translated_text: But those who attend upon the speech of the virtuous, blooming with flowers like a creeper [attended by] bees,

children.text: akāryanirmokam apāsya te kaler mukhaṃ na paśyanti punar vibhīṣaṇam || GoBhl_16 ||
children.translated_text: having cast off the fetters of wicked deeds — they no longer see the terrifying face of the Age of Strife (<s>Kali</s>). [GoBhl 16]

children.text: sa tam arhantam abravīt | niruttarāṇy amūni vo vacanakusumāni | kiṃ tu
children.translated_text: He said to the <s>arhat</s>: "These flower-words of yours are unanswerable. However —

children.text: āpāyikāni vyasanāni yāni mayānubhūtāny atidāruṇāni |
children.translated_text: the miseries of the lower realms that I have experienced were extremely terrible.

children.text: teṣāṃ pratīkāranimittabhūtaṃ sukhaṃ bhadantānubhavāmi tāvat || GoBhl_17 ||
children.translated_text: The happiness [I now seek] is the very cause of their remedy — let me enjoy it, Venerable Sir. [GoBhl 17]

children.text: atha sa mahātmā tena tasya vacasā sutarām upajanitasaṃvego 'bravīt |
children.translated_text: Then that great soul, his spiritual urgency intensified all the more by those words, said to the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>):

children.text: na varṇayanti kṣaṇikām apīśvarā bhavābhinirvṛttim avandhyavādinaḥ |
children.translated_text: The masters of non-futile speech do not praise even a momentary accomplishment in worldly existence.

children.text: tathā hy ayaṃ skandhakadambakodbhavaḥ samudbhavo naikavidhasya pāpmanaḥ || GoBhl_18 ||
children.translated_text: For this arising from the cluster of aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) is the origin of manifold sin. [GoBhl 18]

children.text: bhavaprabandhapraṇayo manasvino jagaddhitādhānaparasya yujyate |
children.translated_text: Affection for the continuity of existence is fitting for the noble-minded one whose purpose is the establishment of the world's welfare.

children.text: anuttarajñānanibaddhacetasāṃ bhavodbhavo bhāvasukhād api priyaḥ || GoBhl_19 ||
children.translated_text: For those whose minds are bound to the highest knowledge, birth in existence is dearer than even the happiness of [cessation of] becoming. [GoBhl 19]

children.text: punarbhavāsvādalavākulāśayaḥ pravṛttim anvicchati yas tu mohanāt |
children.translated_text: But he who, out of delusion, with a mind disturbed by a taste of the flavor of rebirth, seeks continued activity —

children.text: mudhā sa sarvāyatanopatāpinīṃ vipattim anvicchati sarvatomukhīm || GoBhl_20 ||
children.translated_text: that person vainly seeks calamity on all sides, tormenting all sense-bases. [GoBhl 20]

children.text: bhavāḥ saśokāḥ sabhayāḥ savigrahā vivarjitāḥ sadbhir udāramānasaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Existences — with sorrow, with fear, with conflict — have been abandoned by the noble, the magnanimous,

children.text: narair maruddhūtaśikhā viṣadrumā bhujaṅgamādhiṣṭhitakoṭarā iva || GoBhl_21 ||
children.translated_text: like poison-trees whose flames are fanned by the wind, whose hollows are inhabited by serpents. [GoBhl 21]

children.text: bhavāvaśiṣṭāḥ kila sapta jātayo bhayaṃ na te yena punarbhavāśrayam |
children.translated_text: You have only seven more births remaining in existence — is there no fear in you regarding rebirth?

children.text: bhavānuṣaṅgo 'py aśucer vivṛjyate narair vidagdhābharaṇānulepanaiḥ || GoBhl_22 ||
children.translated_text: Even the taint of attachment to existence is avoided by men who are accomplished in refined adornment and anointing [of wisdom]. [GoBhl 22]

children.text: kṛtaṃ tvayāpāyikaduḥkhalaṅghanaṃ pravṛttim anvicchasi yena janmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: You have accomplished the crossing beyond the suffering of the lower realms, yet you seek continued birth.

children.text: jijīviṣus tīvraviṣābhidūṣitaṃ praṇītam apy annam upādadīta kaḥ || GoBhl_23 ||
children.translated_text: Desiring to live, who would take up food, however well-prepared, that is contaminated with virulent poison? [GoBhl 23]

children.text: api ca he bhavābhinandin
children.translated_text: Moreover, O delighter in existence —

children.text: krimer ivāvaskarakardamāntar vivartamānasya yathākathaṃ cit |
children.translated_text: Like a worm somehow turning about in the mud and filth of a refuse heap,

children.text: narasya mātur jaṭharāntarāle kiṃ garbhavāso na mahān apāyaḥ || GoBhl_24 ||
children.translated_text: is not the dwelling of a person in the interior of a mother's womb a great calamity? [GoBhl 24]

children.text: kaḍevarāvaskaranirjhareṇa subaddhasāsṛṅmaladurdinena |
children.translated_text: For a person being born, in a stormy [deluge] of blood and impurity bound to the stream flowing from the body's refuse —

children.text: prajāyamānasya narasya duḥkham apāyaduḥkhair api kiṃ na tulyam || GoBhl_25 ||
children.translated_text: is the suffering not equal to the sufferings of the lower realms? [GoBhl 25]

children.text: davānalapluṣṭapalāśarūkṣaṃ vahan jarājarjaram asthiyantram |
children.translated_text: Carrying the skeletal mechanism, withered by old age, dry like leaves scorched by a forest fire,

children.text: kathaṃ cid āyāsanipītaharṣo na kiṃ samo 'pāyaśatair manuṣyaḥ || GoBhl_26 ||
children.translated_text: with joy somehow sipped away by exertion — is a human being not equal to a hundred lower-realm [sufferings]? [GoBhl 26]

children.text: vidāhibhir niṣpratikāraghoraiḥ kṛtāntabāṇair iva saṃpatadbhiḥ |
children.translated_text: With burning diseases, terrible and without remedy, falling like the arrows of Death (<s>Kṛtānta</s>),

children.text: vibhidyamānasvaviṣātmabhāvo gadair ihaivānubhavaty apāyān || GoBhl_27 ||
children.translated_text: one whose very nature is being split by the poison of one's own being — one experiences the lower realms right here. [GoBhl 27]

children.text: pratyāvṛttasitākṣikośavikṛtavyāghrānano bhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Terrifying, with a face like a tiger's, the white of the rolled-back eyes distorted,

children.text: śastreṇeva vidāryamāṇakaraṇo marmacchidā vāyunā |
children.translated_text: with faculties being torn apart as if by a weapon, by the wind that pierces the vital points,

children.text: bandhūnāṃ purataḥ kṛtāntamakareṇākramya nighno yadā
children.translated_text: when one is seized by the crocodile of Death before one's kinsmen, crushed

children.text: kruddheneva vitīryate 'dhikataraṃ kiṃ nāma duḥkhaṃ tataḥ || GoBhl_28 ||
children.translated_text: as if assailed by an enraged [beast] — what suffering could be greater than that? [GoBhl 28]

children.text: kiṃ cāyuṣman
children.translated_text: Moreover, Venerable One —

children.text: karmāvedhasamuddhatasphuṭaśikhijvālāvalīpiṅgalo
children.translated_text: Even the terrible <s>Avīci</s> [hell], tawny with garlands of flames whose crests blaze forth, stirred up by the piercing of <s>karma</s>,

children.text: naivāvīcir api vyathām upaharaty āryasya tāṃ dāruṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: does not inflict upon the noble one that terrible [pain]

children.text: dhīdaurbalyakarāḥ samādhividhurāḥ sadvṛttavelābhido
children.translated_text: which the mental fevers — causing weakness of intellect, devoid of meditation, breaching the bounds of good conduct —

children.text: yāṃ kurvanti manojvarāḥ paricayāḥ sphītāvalepā malāḥ || GoBhl_29 ||
children.translated_text: [which] the familiar [defilements], swollen with arrogance, the impurities, inflict. [GoBhl 29]

children.text: atha sa viṣayadaurātmyam ivodbhāvayaṃs taṃ maharṣim abravīt |
children.translated_text: Then he, as if manifesting the wickedness of sense-objects, said to that great sage:

children.text: viṣayāsaṅginī buddhir duḥkhena prativāryate |
children.translated_text: "The mind attached to sense-objects is restrained only with difficulty,

children.text: gaṅgeva kūlatoyormiparyastataṭapādapā || GoBhl_30 ||
children.translated_text: like the <s>Gaṅgā</s> whose bank-trees are toppled by the waves of the flooding shore. [GoBhl 30]

children.text: anye 'pi bahavaḥ śaikṣā bhavasaṃbhogalālasāḥ |
children.translated_text: Many other learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) too, craving the enjoyments of existence,

children.text: tarpayantīndriyagrāmaṃ viṣayair aviṣādinaḥ || GoBhl_31 ||
children.translated_text: satisfy the host of senses with sense-objects, without being disheartened." [GoBhl 31]

children.text: sa cārhaṃs tais tadvacobhiḥ sutarām udvejitapratibhayas taṃ śaikṣam avocat |
children.translated_text: And the <s>arhat</s>, all the more alarmed and frightened by those words, said to the learner:

children.text: pratisaṃkhyānamahatām akṛcchraś cittanigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: "For the great ones who practice analytical meditation (<s>pratisaṃkhyāna</s>), mental restraint is effortless.

children.text: na cānuvartanīyās te viṣayair ye parājitāḥ || GoBhl_32 ||
children.translated_text: And those who are conquered by sense-objects should not be followed. [GoBhl 32]

children.text: mayaiva viṣayoddāmaṃ nanu ceto nivāritam |
children.translated_text: "Has not the mind, unrestrained toward sense-objects, been restrained by me

children.text: anyaiś ca vratibhir vīrais tat kasmān nānuvartase || GoBhl_33 ||
children.translated_text: and by other heroic ascetics? Why then do you not follow [our example]? [GoBhl 33]

children.text: viṣayeṣu yadi pramādam eṣe tvam anāryācariteṣu hanta naṣṭam |
children.translated_text: If you seek heedlessness in sense-objects, in those practices unworthy of the noble — alas, you are lost!

children.text: atha te virajanti naiva cetas tava ko 'rtho vada tair anarthabhūtaiḥ || GoBhl_34 ||
children.translated_text: But if they do not delight your mind, then tell me, what use are they to you, being sources of harm? [GoBhl 34]

children.text: viṣayeṣu pariplutendriyāṇāṃ svamanovibhramamātrabhadrakeṣu |
children.translated_text: For those whose senses are flooded by sense-objects, which are auspicious only through the delusion of one's own mind,

children.text: nikaṭe nivasanti sarvaduḥkhāny aparijñātanipātadāruṇāni || GoBhl_35 ||
children.translated_text: all sufferings dwell nearby, terrible with falls that go unrecognized. [GoBhl 35]

children.text: viṣayāpacayānupātinīnām aparimlānasukhāmṛtapradānām |
children.translated_text: A man, misled by the faults of attachment to pleasures that follow the decline of sense-objects

children.text: chalitaḥ puruṣaḥ prasaṅgadoṣair na ca saṃvetti nirāmiṣaṃ ratīnām || GoBhl_36 ||
children.translated_text: yet bestow unfading nectar of happiness — does not know the pleasures that are free of bait. [GoBhl 36]

children.text: paribhūtir upāntike narāṇāṃ bhavasaṃbhogaviṣaktamānasānām |
children.translated_text: Humiliation is near at hand for men whose minds are attached to the enjoyments of existence.

children.text: viṣayapratikuñcitaṃ ca ceto vinipātāyatanāni cāvṛtāni || GoBhl_37 ||
children.translated_text: and the mind, recoiled from sense-objects, and the abodes of downfall are concealed. || GoBhl 37 ||

children.text: pariṇāmaratām aśāntarūpāṃ viparītālpasukhānurāgaramyām |
children.translated_text: Disdaining the wretched pleasure of desire — delighting in transformations of restless form, charming with attachment to reversed and meager joys —

children.text: paribhūya manasvino ramante kṛpaṇāṃ kāmaratiṃ tapovaneṣu || GoBhl_38 ||
children.translated_text: the wise rejoice in the forests of austerity. || GoBhl 38 ||

children.text: vinigṛhya manaḥ pramādadolācalam adhyātmarativyapāśrayeṇa |
children.translated_text: Having restrained the mind, wavering on the swing of heedlessness, by reliance on the joy of inner contemplation,

children.text: anirākṛtayogino ramante bahurūpair atimānuṣair vihāraiḥ || GoBhl_39 ||
children.translated_text: yogins of unbroken practice delight in manifold superhuman pleasures. || GoBhl 39 ||

children.text: vitathābhiniveṣamātraramyāḥ puruṣasyopanamanti nāma kāmāḥ |
children.translated_text: Desires, charming only by the force of false attachment, approach a person —

children.text: gaticakracaravrataṃ narāṇāṃ viṣayā eva samādiśanty anāryāḥ || GoBhl_40 ||
children.translated_text: they are ignoble sense-objects that dictate the vow of wandering in the wheel of destinies for people. || GoBhl 40 ||

children.text: vyasanopanipātalakṣyavṛkṣe jagati kleśapiśācikābhibhūte |
children.translated_text: In this world — a tree marked as the target for the fall of calamities, overwhelmed by the goblins of affliction —

children.text: udayā na tu sarvadā bhavanti prakṛtisvāsthyakṛtāṃ tathāgatānām || GoBhl_41 ||
children.translated_text: the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s> who produce natural well-being does not always occur. || GoBhl 41 ||

children.text: tad ayaṃ samayaḥ kathaṃ cid eva pratilabdhaḥ kuśalaprayogayogyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore this occasion, somehow obtained, is fit for the application of merit;

children.text: pratipattividhau bhavān pramāṇaṃ śakunānāṃ hi vanaṃ virāvamātram || GoBhl_42 ||
children.translated_text: you are the authority in the matter of practice — for birds, the forest is merely a sound. || GoBhl 42 ||

children.text: sa tam arhantam abravīt |
children.translated_text: He said to that <s>Arhat</s>:

children.text: śaknuyāṃ sugatau bhogaspṛhāṃ yady apy upekṣitum |
children.translated_text: Even if I could disregard the craving for pleasures toward the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One),

children.text: brūyāḥ pravadatāṃ śreṣṭha naiva māṃ tvaṃ punaḥ punaḥ || GoBhl_43 ||
children.translated_text: O best of speakers, do not tell me again and again. || GoBhl 43 ||

children.text: yatas tu māṃ haraty eṣā kāmatṛṣṇā niśācarī |
children.translated_text: But since this nocturnal thirst of desire carries me away,

children.text: tenātivelakṛpayā tvaṃ māṃ kutsayase vibho || GoBhl_44 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O Lord, out of exceedingly great compassion you reprove me. || GoBhl 44 ||

children.text: sa taṃ mahātmā punar api sānukrośapeśalair vacobhiḥ saṃvejayann abravīt |
children.translated_text: That great soul, once more stirring him with words gentle with compassion, said:

children.text: khinnā vayaṃ rudhirabindum upādadānāḥ sāṃkleśikeṣu sabhayeṣu bhaveṣu vatsa |
children.translated_text: We are weary, child, from gathering drops of blood in afflicted, fearful existences,

children.text: āyāsinīṃ ca kaṭasīm abhivardhayanto naikāntarāyavivaśāḥ svaparābhavāya || GoBhl_45 ||
children.translated_text: and from nurturing this tormenting body-frame, helpless before countless obstacles, for the ruin of self and others. || GoBhl 45 ||

children.text: krūraiḥ parasparavirodhibhir apraśāntair dhātūragaiḥ prakupitair iva kṛṣṇasarpaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With cruel, mutually hostile, unpeaceful bodily elements, like enraged black serpents gone mad with <s>dhattūra</s> (poison),

children.text: ātudyamānavapuṣām aparāyaṇānāṃ kalpāyutāny abhigatāni ca no mahātman || GoBhl_46 ||
children.translated_text: our bodies pierced, without refuge — ten thousand <s>kalpas</s> (eons) have we passed, O great soul. || GoBhl 46 ||

children.text: pratyarthikair iva samudyatamaṇḍalāgraiḥ skandhair hatā vayam akāraṇabaddhavairaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Struck by the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), like enemies with upraised circles of weapons, bound in enmity without cause,

children.text: āyāsitāś ca viṣayair viṣakumbhakalpais tac chidyatāṃ bhavasukhavyasanānurāgaḥ || GoBhl_47 ||
children.translated_text: and tormented by sense-objects like poison-pots — therefore let the attachment to the addiction to worldly happiness be severed! || GoBhl 47 ||

children.text: sa tam arhantam āha |
children.translated_text: He said to that <s>Arhat</s>:

children.text: nopacchetsyāmi yady atra janmani skandhasaṃtatim |
children.translated_text: If in this birth I shall not cut off the continuity of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates),

children.text: upapadyoddhariṣyāmi tvadvākyena jitādhinā || GoBhl_48 ||
children.translated_text: then in a future birth I shall arise and rescue myself, my will conquered by your words. || GoBhl 48 ||

children.text: sa taṃ pratyāha | yady apy etad evaṃ tathāpi
children.translated_text: He replied to him: Even if that be so, still —

children.text: sakṛn martavye tvaṃ punar api ca mṛtyuṃ mṛgayase
children.translated_text: When one must die but once, you seek death again and again;

children.text: sphuṭaṃ dṛṣṭvālokaṃ tamasi vipule majjasi punaḥ |
children.translated_text: having clearly seen the light, you plunge once more into vast darkness;

children.text: śivaṃ labdhvā mārgaṃ kusṛtim upayāsi pratibhayāṃ
children.translated_text: having found the auspicious path, you take to the terrifying wrong road —

children.text: bhavān yas tvaṃ vāñchasy amṛtapuram utsṛjya sulabham || GoBhl_49 ||
children.translated_text: you who desire the easily-attainable city of immortality yet abandon it! || GoBhl 49 ||

children.text: samuttīryāgādhāt krimikulacalatpaṅkakalilāt
children.translated_text: Having crossed over the fathomless [ocean] — turbid with mud stirring with masses of worms —

children.text: kathaṃ vijñābālāt pipatiṣasi tasmin punar api |
children.translated_text: how is it, O wise fool, that you wish to fall into it again?

children.text: vimukto rogebhyaḥ punar api ca rogāya yatase
children.translated_text: Freed from diseases, you again strive for disease;

children.text: bhavebhyo duḥkhebhyaḥ spṛhayasi punar yas tvam aghṛṇaḥ || GoBhl_50 ||
children.translated_text: you who, merciless, desire once more the painful existences! || GoBhl 50 ||

children.text: a
nā
śān asvantān sulabhavinipātapratibhayān
children.translated_text: ... fearful, easily leading to downfall,

children.text: sa

vairān sodvegān saparibhavasaṃtāpavirasān |
parityajyāyuṣman vyasanaviśikhāpātavihatān
children.translated_text: with enmities, with anxieties, repugnant with the heat of humiliation — having abandoned these, struck by the arrows of calamity,

children.text: bhavān samyagmārgaṃ bhavabhayaharaṃ bhāvaya sadā || GoBhl_51 ||
children.translated_text: O long-lived one, ever contemplate the true path that removes the fear of existence! || GoBhl 51 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭasaṃsāraduḥkho 'pi so 'bhyāsād rāgapāpmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Though he had seen the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>, still, due to habitual practice of the sin of passion,

children.text: tam uvāca mahātmānam ārujann iva vākśaraiḥ || GoBhl_52 ||
children.translated_text: he spoke to that great soul, as if wounding him with the arrows of his words: || GoBhl 52 ||

children.text: bhramanti te bahūn kalpān bodhisattvā bhavādhvani |
