children.translated_text: Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> wander for many <s>kalpas</s> on the road of existence;

children.text: sudāntāḥ saptajanmāni bhramatāṃ kīdṛśī vyathā || GoBhl_53 ||
children.translated_text: for the well-tamed, only seven births [remain] — what pain is there for those who still wander? || GoBhl 53 ||

children.text: sa bhikṣus tena vākyena pratodeneva vikṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: That monk, wounded as if by a goad by those words,

children.text: tam abravīd bhavāsvādakārpaṇyopahatāśayam || GoBhl_54 ||
children.translated_text: spoke to him whose mind was corrupted by the wretchedness of relishing existence: || GoBhl 54 ||

children.text: na tena viditā bhikṣo yā vyathā bhramatāṃ bhave |
children.translated_text: You do not know, O monk, the pain of those who wander in existence;

children.text: avajñāya vaco 'smākaṃ punar apy avabhotsyase || GoBhl_55 ||
children.translated_text: disregarding our words, you will understand again [through suffering]. || GoBhl 55 ||

children.text: punaś ca tvāṃ bravīmi |
children.translated_text: And again I say to you:

children.text: ye janmaivādhimuktāḥ śamasukhamahatīṃ nirvṛtiṃ śuddhasattvā
children.translated_text: Those of pure nature who from birth itself are devoted to the great bliss of tranquility and <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation),

children.text: yeṣāṃ kleśāvaśeṣo 'py upaśamitabalo yo 'py upādānam eva |
children.translated_text: those in whom even the residue of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), though its power is pacified, is itself the basis of clinging (<s>upādāna</s>),

children.text: ātmatvenābhyupetā jagad idam akhilaṃ ye kṛpākrāntacittās
children.translated_text: those whose minds are seized by compassion and who regard this entire world as their own self —

children.text: teṣāṃ ślāghyā pravṛttir gatiṣu na tu bhavāsvādaparyastabuddhiḥ || GoBhl_56 ||
children.translated_text: their activity in the [various] destinies is praiseworthy, but not the intellect overwhelmed by relishing existence. || GoBhl 56 ||

children.text: spṛśyante sattvavanto na viṣayarajasā ye viviktāśayatvād
children.translated_text: Those strong-natured ones who are untouched by the dust of sense-objects due to their detached disposition,

children.text: duḥkhair naiva vyathante kṣitidharaguravo ye parārthe carantaḥ |
children.translated_text: who are not afflicted by sufferings, being heavy as mountains, acting for the benefit of others,

children.text: te janmopādadānāḥ parapuraparikhāsetavo bodhisattvāḥ
children.translated_text: those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who take birth as if building bridges to breach the moats of others' fortresses —

children.text: śobhante na kṣamaṃ tu kṣaṇam api gatiṣu sthātum ātmaṃbharīṇām || GoBhl_57 ||
children.translated_text: they shine; but it is not proper for the self-seeking to remain even a moment in the [lower] destinies. || GoBhl 57 ||

children.text: yeṣāṃ sarve prayogāḥ śaśina iva kalāḥ sarvasattvopajīvyā
children.translated_text: Those whose every endeavor, like the digits of the moon, nourishes all beings,

children.text: ye lokān pānti kṛtsnān pitara iva sutān duḥkhapātālamagnān |
children.translated_text: who protect all the worlds like fathers [protecting] sons plunged into the abyss of suffering,

children.text: teṣāṃ janmopadeśaḥ sucaritamahatām utsavaḥ śrīviśeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: for them of great merit, the teaching of [successive] births is a festival, a special glory;

children.text: svārthodyogānurāgād anupatati bhavān mṛtyave kevalaṃ tu || GoBhl_58 ||
children.translated_text: but you, from love of self-seeking, merely follow death. || GoBhl 58 ||

children.text: yeṣām utpādakāle sucaritakiraṇair likhyamānaṃ samantād
children.translated_text: Those at whose arising, the darkness of the mind — though swollen with the familiarity of its own hidden recesses —

children.text: dhvāntaṃ cetaḥ svaraṅgāvivaraparicayasphītam apy astam eti |
children.translated_text: is everywhere inscribed [and dispelled] by the rays of good conduct, and sets;

children.text: unmajjantīva lokāḥ pratibhayamahato duḥkhapaṅkaughamadhyāt
children.translated_text: worlds emerge as if from the midst of the flood of the terrifying great mire of suffering —

children.text: teṣām evānurūpā parahitaviduṣāṃ janmasaṃtānalīlā || GoBhl_59 ||
children.translated_text: for those who know the welfare of others, the play of the continuity of births is fitting. || GoBhl 59 ||

children.text: kiṃ bahunā
children.translated_text: In short:

children.text: sarveṣv ācāryavaryā niyamagurudharā dharmayānāgradhairyāḥ
children.translated_text: The best of teachers in all [matters], bearers of the weighty discipline of restraint, foremost in steadfastness on the vehicle of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: kāruṇyocchrītavīryā rajanikaranibhā bhāskarābhāś ca dīptyā |
children.translated_text: with heroism raised high by compassion, resembling the moon in luster and the sun in radiance,

children.text: janmāṭavyānuyātrā namucividaraṇā jñānadīpolkadhārāḥ
children.translated_text: accompanied through the forest of births, cleaving <s>Namuci</s> (Māra), bearing the torch of the lamp of knowledge,

children.text: sarvajñatvābhiṣekāḥ puruṣavarayugāḥ sarvadā bodhisattvāḥ || GoBhl_60 ||
children.translated_text: consecrated to omniscience — <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are always the noblest pair of men. || GoBhl 60 ||

children.text: evam apy asāv ucyamānaḥ kuśaladharmasādhanodyogavidhura eva vyāhārṣīt |
children.translated_text: Even when thus addressed, he, utterly lacking in zeal for the practice of wholesome <s>dharma</s>, declared:

children.text: samudāgamavaiguṇyavirūkṣakṣāmacetasām |
children.translated_text: For embodied beings whose minds are barren and withered from the deficiency of their accumulations,

children.text: kuśalapratyayā bāhyāḥ kiṃ kariṣyanti dehinām || GoBhl_61 ||
children.translated_text: what can external conditions of merit accomplish? || GoBhl 61 ||

children.text: prakṣālayanti munayo na jalena pāpaṃ hastena nāpy apaharanti janasya duḥkham |
children.translated_text: Sages do not wash away sin with water, nor do they remove the suffering of people with their hands;

children.text: saṃcārayanty adhigamaṃ na paratra ca svaṃ dharmān vadanti tu sukhapratipattisādhyān || GoBhl_62 ||
children.translated_text: they do not transfer their own realization to others — but they teach the <s>dharmas</s> that are the means to the attainment of happiness. || GoBhl 62 ||

children.text: atha sa krameṇa kālagato bharukacche proṣitabhartṛkāyā nāryāḥ kukṣau janma pratisaṃdadhe | kālāntareṇa ca garbhād abhiniṣkrāntaḥ | mātā cainam abhivīkṣya putrasneham anādṛtyāpavādabhayāśaṅkinī kim api kim api tapasvinī vilalāpa | anunīyamānāpi ca samānasukhaduḥkhābhiḥ sakhībhir asahamānā tanayaviyogavyasanaṃ tam atimanoharātmabhāvaṃ bālakam aṅke kṛtvā bāṣpavegoparudhyamānaskhalitavacasā niyatam īdṛśaṃ kiṃ cid avocat |
children.translated_text: Then, in due course, that one died and took rebirth in the womb of a woman in <s>Bharukaccha</s> (Broach) whose husband was away on a journey. In time he was born from the womb. The mother, seeing him, disregarding motherly affection and fearing public censure, wailed wretchedly about one thing and another. Even though consoled by her companions who shared her joys and sorrows, unable to bear the calamity of separation from her son, taking the infant — who was of exceedingly lovely form — in her lap, with words faltering and choked by a surge of tears, she certainly said something like this:

children.text: jāte putre bhavanti pramuditahṛdayā mātaro jīvaloke
children.translated_text: When a son is born, mothers in this living world become joyful at heart,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vaṃśasya lakṣmīm anuparatarasām unmiṣantīṃ samantāt |
children.translated_text: seeing the glory of the family, unceasing and blossoming all around;

children.text: ānandāndolitānāṃ bhavati sa divaso bāndhavānām adīrgho
children.translated_text: that day seems short to the relatives swaying with joy —

children.text: jātaḥ śokāya tu tvaṃ mama tanaya kathaṃ mandabhāgyodayāyāḥ || GoBhl_63 ||
children.translated_text: but you, my son, were born for the sorrow of me, wretched in destiny. || GoBhl 63 ||

children.text: durvṛttāyā mama tad adhunā karmaṇā preritas tvaṃ
children.translated_text: Driven now by the deed of me, a woman of ill conduct,

children.text: bhuṅkṣvāsahyaṃ vyasanam athavā svasya duśceṣṭitasya |
children.translated_text: you suffer this unbearable misfortune — or rather, [the fruit] of your own misdeeds;

children.text: ete 'nye ca vyasananivahā mūrdhni teṣāṃ sphuranti
children.translated_text: these and other heaps of calamity hover over the heads of those

children.text: tyaktvā lajjāṃ sujanadayitāṃ ye pramādaṃ bhajante || GoBhl_64 ||
children.translated_text: who, casting aside modesty beloved of the virtuous, embrace heedlessness. || GoBhl 64 ||

children.text: khādyamānaparikomalacchavis tīkṣṇatuṇḍanakharaiḥ patatribhiḥ |
children.translated_text: With your tender skin being pecked by birds with sharp beaks and claws,

children.text: putra durnayaphalāni bhokṣyase mātur adya parimāṇavartakaḥ || GoBhl_65 ||
children.translated_text: you shall taste the fruits of misconduct, my son — you who today depend upon your mother for sustenance. || GoBhl 65 ||

children.text: dhig dhig astu pariṇāmadāruṇāṃ saṅgināṃ ratim apūrvavāhinīm |
children.translated_text: Shame, shame upon the pleasure of the passionate, ever-novel yet terrible in its consequences!

children.text: adhyavasyati yayābhibhūtadhīr īdṛśāny api jano hatatrapaḥ || GoBhl_66 ||
children.translated_text: Overpowered by it, a person of lost shame dares even such things as these. || GoBhl 66 ||

children.text: kaṣṭam āyataviṣādabhīṣaṇe saṃkaṭe mama vivartate manaḥ |
children.translated_text: Alas, my mind reels in this dreadful strait, terrible with prolonged despair,

children.text: yatra lokaravabhītayā mayā putraka tvam aṭavīṃ nipātyase || GoBhl_67 ||
children.translated_text: where, frightened of the censure of the world, I must cast you, dear child, into the wilderness. || GoBhl 67 ||

children.text: dāruṇaṃ bata bidher viceṣṭitaṃ duṣkaraṃ khalu mayā samīhitam |
children.translated_text: Cruel indeed is the working of fate; unbearable is what I am about to do;

children.text: kiṃ karomi śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi kaṃ putra śokaśaratāḍitāśayā || GoBhl_68 ||
children.translated_text: what shall I do? To whom shall I go for refuge, my son? — I whose heart is pierced by the arrows of grief. || GoBhl 68 ||

children.text: hā hatāsmi vighṛṇena cetasā kāmadohadapathānupātinā |
children.translated_text: Alas, I am slain by a merciless heart that follows the path of the longings of desire;

children.text: yat suduṣkaram idaṃ kariṣyate vaiśasaṃ vihatalajjayā mayā || GoBhl_69 ||
children.translated_text: for this most difficult cruelty shall be performed by me, whose modesty is destroyed. || GoBhl 69 ||

children.text: bhūr iyaṃ kim iti nāvadīryate nārakaḥ kva nu sa havyavāhanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Why does this earth not split open? Where is that infernal fire

children.text: yo na nirdahati pāpakāriṇīṃ kakṣamuṣṭim iva māṃ hatatrapām || GoBhl_70 ||
children.translated_text: that does not burn me, the sinful one, shameless, like a handful of dry grass? || GoBhl 70 ||

children.text: vitataśikhikalāpodbhāsurālokajālaṃ nipatati mama vajraṃ sāṃprataṃ kiṃ tu mūrdhni |
children.translated_text: Is a thunderbolt with its spread of blazing peacock-plume flames now falling upon my head?

children.text: sutam akaruṇacittā yāham evaṃ tyajāmi stanarasaparibhogaklībavaktrāravindam || GoBhl_71 ||
children.translated_text: For I, hard-hearted, am about to abandon my son — whose lotus-face is softened by the enjoyment of breast-milk. || GoBhl 71 ||

children.text: ity evam anyathā ca tasyā vilapantyāḥ kiṃciccheṣā rajanī babhūva | sā paricārikām abravīt | jñāyatāṃ tāvad bhadre kim avaśeṣaṃ niśāyā iti | sābravīt | svāmini saṃprati hi
children.translated_text: Thus and otherwise as she lamented, only a small portion of the night remained. She said to her maidservant: 'Find out, dear one, how much of the night remains.' She replied: 'Mistress, now —

children.text: aruṇakiraṇamālāpāṭalopāntalekhaṃ praviralataratāraṃ khaṃ parāvṛttacandram |
children.translated_text: the sky, its inner rim reddened by garlands of dawn-rays, with stars grown sparse and thin, the moon having turned away,

children.text: pulinam iva payodher vidrumakṣodatāmraṃ parimukulapalāśasvasthasaṃsuptahaṃsam || GoBhl_72 ||
children.translated_text: like a beach of the ocean, coppery with crushed coral, with lotuses half-closed and geese peacefully asleep — || GoBhl 72 ||

children.text: sā provāca |
children.translated_text: She said:

children.text: imaṃ hṛdayasaṃtāpaṃ dīrghakālānuṣaṅginam |
children.translated_text: This burning of my heart, companion of long duration,

children.text: durjātaṃ mama mandāyā gaccha cchoraya bālakam || GoBhl_73 ||
children.translated_text: go — take away and abandon this ill-born child of wretched me. || GoBhl 73 ||

children.text: ity uktvā sā bāṣpavegoparudhyamānahṛdayā pṛthivyāṃ sahasā nipapāta | paraṃ ca saṃmoham upajagāma |
children.translated_text: Having said this, her heart choked by a surge of tears, she fell suddenly to the ground and was overcome by a deep swoon.

children.text: sā tatheti pratiśrutya tam ādāya tapasvinam |
children.translated_text: Having agreed 'So be it,' taking that pitiable one,

children.text: upahāram ivāpūrvaṃ vicikṣepa mahāpathe || GoBhl_74 ||
children.translated_text: she cast him on the highway like an unprecedented offering. || GoBhl 74 ||

children.text: putrakrauryaṃ vivṛtam aśivaṃ janmaduḥkhopataptaṃ
children.translated_text: The cruelty toward the son revealed, inauspicious, burning with the suffering of birth;

children.text: bhartṛsnehaḥ ciraparicayād baddhamūlo na dṛṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: the love for the husband, deep-rooted from long familiarity, was not considered;

children.text: dagdhaṃ vaṃśadvayam api mayā durnayāṅgāravarṣair
children.translated_text: both families were burned by me with showers of sparks from misconduct —

children.text: hā kāmānāṃ prakṛtir asatī sarvaduḥkhaprasūtiḥ || GoBhl_75 ||
children.translated_text: alas, the nature of desires is wicked, the source of all suffering! || GoBhl 75 ||

children.text: nāsau rurāvāmuṣitasmṛtitvāc cukopa mātre na ca tattvadarśī |
children.translated_text: He did not cry, for his memory was not lost; nor did he, the seer of truth, grow angry at his mother;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu tām ātmagatām avasthāṃ svam eva cittaṃ vinininda bālaḥ || GoBhl_76 ||
children.translated_text: but seeing this condition that had befallen himself, the child reproached only his own mind: || GoBhl 76 ||

children.text: nāyaṃ jananyā mama kāmacāro na cānimittaṃ vyasanaṃ mamedam |
children.translated_text: This is not the willful doing of my mother, nor is this misfortune of mine without cause;

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtāni vyasanāny amūni tvayaiva me citta vimuñca dainyam || GoBhl_77 ||
children.translated_text: these calamities are self-created — O my mind, it is you yourself; let go of wretchedness! || GoBhl 77 ||

children.text: anārya tāṃ cittakale pratārya pragāḍhaduḥkhodayadāruṇeṣu |
children.translated_text: O ignoble [mind], having deceived her in the sport of thought, in the existential enjoyments that are terrible with the arising of deep suffering,

children.text: bhavopabhogeṣv adhunā viṣādaṃ kim eva mohād asamīkṣyakārin || GoBhl_78 ||
children.translated_text: why now this despair, O deluded one who acts without foresight? || GoBhl 78 ||

children.text: hitaiṣiṇas tasya vaco 'vadhīrya tvam ajña nirdagdhapunarbhavasya |
children.translated_text: Having disregarded the words of that well-wisher whose future existences are burned away,

children.text: bibheṣi duḥkhād adhunā kim evaṃ svakarmanirmāṇam idaṃ tavaiva || GoBhl_79 ||
children.translated_text: why do you now fear suffering, O fool? This is the very creation of your own <s>karma</s>. || GoBhl 79 ||

children.text: na pūjayanti pratipattibhir ye giro gurūṇām anukampakānām |
children.translated_text: Those who do not honor with practice the words of compassionate teachers —

children.text: imāni cānyāni ca te labhante viṣādanīnāṃ vipadāṃ śatāni || GoBhl_80 ||
children.translated_text: they obtain these and hundreds of other sorrowful calamities. || GoBhl 80 ||

children.text: yathā yathā tīvradvandvopanipātajāni duḥkhāny anubhavati sma tathā tathā sutarām upajāyamānasaṃvegaḥ sāśrukaṇṭha eva śuśoca viklavātmā tapasvī |
children.translated_text: As he experienced sufferings born of the onset of intense pairs of opposites, so much the more did his sense of urgency arise; the wretched one, with tears in his throat, grieved in utter distress:

children.text: praviralatṛṇacchannaśvabhraprapātabhayaṃkarān
children.translated_text: Fearsome with chasms thinly covered by sparse grass —

children.text: mama gurur asau tyaktvā yāto bhavābdhikadurbhavān |
children.translated_text: my teacher, having left, departed from these wretched states of the ocean of existence;

children.text: tanusukhalavakliṣṭātmāno vayaṃ tu hatatrapā
children.translated_text: but we, shameless, our souls afflicted by the paltry pleasures of trifling joys,

children.text: bhavajalanidher dṛṣṭvāpy antaṃ punar nidhanaṃ gatāḥ || GoBhl_81 ||
children.translated_text: though having seen the far shore of the ocean of existence, they have again perished. // GoBhl 81 //

children.text: matihutabhujā dagdhvā skandhapravṛttiviṣadrumaṃ
children.translated_text: Having burned the poison-tree of attachment to the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) with the fire of wisdom,

children.text: sthitiṣu vaśitāṃ saṃprāpyāpi prakāśayaśotsavāḥ |
children.translated_text: having attained mastery over [all] states of existence, resplendent in the festival of fame,

children.text: sakalabhuvanaśreyaḥ kṛtvā gatāḥ sugatāḥ śamaṃ
children.translated_text: having accomplished the welfare of all worlds, the <s>Sugatas</s> (Buddhas) have gone to peace —

children.text: viṣayakṛpaṇāḥ kaṣṭaṃ naṣṭā vayaṃ bhavalubdhakāḥ || GoBhl_82 ||
children.translated_text: alas, wretched in sense-objects, we are lost, hunters of existence (<s>bhavalubdhaka</s>)! // GoBhl 82 //

children.text: sthānāsthānavivekayogaviduṣā sthānena saṃvarṇitā
children.translated_text: The cessation of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), though momentary, described in its proper place

children.text: skandhānāṃ kṣaṇikāpy anuttaragirā nirvṛttir āyāsinī |
children.translated_text: by one skilled in the practice of discerning the appropriate and inappropriate, with the unsurpassed word, [is yet] painful;

children.text: sthāne prajvalitāṃs tarūn iva khagās tyaktvā bhavān bhaṅgurān
children.translated_text: rightly do the masters of mind, the <s>yogins</s>, abandon these fragile existences like birds leaving burning trees,

children.text: nirvānti jvalanā ivāmbuvihatāś citteśvarā yoginaḥ || GoBhl_83 ||
children.translated_text: and are extinguished like fires struck by water. // GoBhl 83 //

children.text: kṛtvābhiyogam api cāgamagahvareṣu svairapracāram anugṛhya mano manuṣyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Though people make effort in the depths of scriptural tradition and indulge the mind in free wandering,

children.text: alpaśrutā iti jagaty upayānti saṃkhyāṃ cetovinigrahaphalaṃ śrutam āhur āryāḥ || GoBhl_84 ||
children.translated_text: they are counted in the world as 'of little learning' — the noble ones say that the fruit of learning is the restraint of the mind. // GoBhl 84 //

children.text: sa sūcikāgrair iva tudyamānaḥ pipīlikair bhugnakarāladaṃṣṭraiḥ |
children.translated_text: He, pricked as if by needle-points by ants with curved and terrible mandibles,

children.text: mahīrajodhūsarakomalāṅgo muhur muhuḥ saṃparivartate sma || GoBhl_85 ||
children.translated_text: his soft body grey with the dust of the earth, rolled over again and again. // GoBhl 85 //

children.text: sa makṣikāṇāṃ nayutaiḥ parīto mṛduḥ prayatnākulapāṇipādaḥ |
children.translated_text: He, surrounded by tens of thousands of flies, gentle, with hands and feet restless from distress,

children.text: viceṣṭamānaḥ karuṇaṃ kathaṃ cid bhavān jagarhe manasānutāpī || GoBhl_86 ||
children.translated_text: writhing pitifully, somehow the noble one, remorseful in mind, reproached [his past conduct]. // GoBhl 86 //

children.text: krūrārāvaiḥ purabalibhujāṃ maṇḍalaiḥ saṃpatadbhir
children.translated_text: With the fierce cries of circling carrion-birds of the city, swooping down,

children.text: vyādhūtāsyo vipadam aśivāṃ yo 'svatantraḥ prapede |
children.translated_text: his face shaken about, he — powerless — fell into inauspicious calamity;

children.text: gomāyūnāṃ viṣamavirutair agnimālākarālair
children.translated_text: by the discordant howling of jackals, fierce as garlands of flame,

children.text: āryasyāpi prakṛtimṛdukaṃ tasya cetaś cakampe || GoBhl_87 ||
children.translated_text: even the heart of the noble one, naturally tender, trembled. // GoBhl 87 //

children.text: kravyāśināṃ paravadhapraṇayapragalbhaiḥ pūgair asau parivṛto vigatāsukalpaḥ |
children.translated_text: Surrounded by flocks of flesh-eaters, bold in their eagerness for another's death, he was nearly lifeless;

children.text: prākhyāpayat sa bhavabhogalavābhilāṣaduḥkhāni tasya ca vaco vigatasravasya || GoBhl_88 ||
children.translated_text: he proclaimed the sufferings of desire for the enjoyment of existence — and his voice, from which tears had ceased [to flow], [spoke clearly]. // GoBhl 88 //

children.text: tasya tathā kṛcchragatasya puradvāri parivartamānasya gavāṃ nirgacchantīnāṃ puraḥsaro vṛṣabhas tam āyuṣmantaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidhiyogasāmarthyāt pitevopagu tāvad avatasthe yāvad atikrāntaḥ sarvo gaugaṇaḥ | so 'titīvravedanāturatanur alpasthāmatayā kaṇṭhagataprāṇaḥ punar api mayā vyasanam evānubhavanīyaṃ maraṇād ūrdhvam ity abhiviṣādo 'pi mṛtyur eva tatkāladuḥkhapratīkāram ākārayatu | vanavihagapakṣapātoddhṛtadharaṇitalarajo'vakīrṇadeho nirākrando mandam aparispandakaracaraṇavadanakamala idānīṃ na bhaviṣyāmīti buddham eva bhagavantaṃ namaskartum ārabdhaḥ | tadbhāgyaśeṣopakṛṣṭā iva copāsakā buddhadharmasaṃghānuvādāśrayāḥ saṃkathāḥ kathayantas taṃ pradeśam upajagmuḥ | sa tān avalokya pratyujjīvita iva mṛdusphuṭakalena vacasā kamalapalāśakomalaṃ pāṇim abhiprasāryābravīt | bho bhoḥ satpuruṣā muhūrtakaṃ tāvad asmadanukampayāvatiṣṭhadhvam iti | atha te sahasā tacchabdaśravaṇasaṃbhrāntāḥ kim idaṃ kathaṃ cety utpannavimarśāḥ sthitā vayaṃ bhadramukhete taṃ mahāsattvam āśvāsayāṃ babhūvuḥ | kautūhalākulasamāsāś ca punar evam ūcuḥ |
children.translated_text: As he, in such dire straits, lay rolling at the city gate, a bull, the leader of cows going out, seeing that venerable one, by the power of destined connection, stood over him like a father until the entire herd had passed. He, with body tormented by exceedingly sharp pain, his life-breath at his throat from weakness, [thought]: 'Even after death, I shall have to experience misfortune again' — though despairing thus, [he thought] 'let death itself bring remedy for this present suffering.' His body scattered with dust raised by the wing-beats of forest birds, without crying out, with hands, feet, and lotus-face barely moving, [thinking] 'now I shall cease to be,' he began to bow to the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>. And, as if drawn by the remainder of his merit, lay-devotees (<s>upāsaka</s>) came to that place, speaking conversations based on the recitation of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>. Seeing them, as if revived from death, with a voice of soft, clear tone, extending his lotus-soft hand, he said: 'O good people, please stay a moment out of compassion for me.' Then they, suddenly startled by hearing that voice, wondering 'What is this? How?' — stood with curiosity aroused, [saying] 'We are here, O fair-faced one,' and comforted that great being. And, filled with curiosity, they spoke again thus:

children.text: avasthāṃś ca vayaś cedaṃ vāksauṣṭhavam idaṃ ca te |
children.translated_text: Seeing your condition and this age of yours,

children.text: matvā calati no buddhiḥ kautūhalasamākulā || GoBhl_89 ||
children.translated_text: and this eloquence of speech — our mind wavers, filled with curiosity. // GoBhl 89 //

children.text: tat saumya vada ko nāma tvaṃ devo 'py atha dānavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, gentle one, tell us: who are you — a god or a demon?

children.text: kathaṃ cemāṃ daśāṃ prāptaḥ sajjanāyāsakāriṇīm || GoBhl_90 ||
children.translated_text: And how have you reached this state that causes grief to good people? // GoBhl 90 //

children.text: sa tān āha |
children.translated_text: He said to them:

children.text: mānuṣo 'smi mahāsattvā nāhaṃ devo na dānavaḥ |
children.translated_text: I am a human being, O great ones; I am neither a god nor a demon.

children.text: bhavasaṃbhogatarṣeṇa prāptas tv aham imāṃ daśām || GoBhl_91 ||
children.translated_text: But through thirst for the enjoyments of existence, I have reached this state. // GoBhl 91 //

children.text: atha te tadvacaḥ śrutvā saṃvignoddhatamānasāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then they, having heard his words, with minds agitated and aroused,

children.text: anukampāmṛtasnigdhaṃ pratyabhāṣanta taṃ punaḥ || GoBhl_92 ||
children.translated_text: addressed him again, [their speech] tender with the nectar of compassion: // GoBhl 92 //

children.text: upāsakā vayaṃ sādho nityaṃ kiṃkuśalaiṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: We are lay-devotees (<s>upāsaka</s>), O virtuous one, always seeking what is wholesome;

children.text: vistaraṃ śrotum icchāmaḥ sa cet khedaṃ na manyase || GoBhl_93 ||
children.translated_text: we wish to hear the full account, if you do not consider it too wearisome. // GoBhl 93 //

children.text: sa tān ity avadad yūyaṃ dharmabhrātara eva me |
children.translated_text: He said to them: 'You are indeed my brothers in the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: duḥkhāni tāvad vāryantāṃ paścād vakṣyāmi vistaram || GoBhl_94 ||
children.translated_text: first let my sufferings be relieved, then I shall tell [you] in full.' // GoBhl 94 //

children.text: tatheti ca pratiśrutya gṛhītvā pāṇibhiḥ śanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having agreed, they gently took him by the hands,

children.text: pramṛjyāstīrya vastrāṇi svāni teṣu nyaveśayan || GoBhl_95 ||
children.translated_text: wiped [his body], spread out their own garments, and seated him upon them. // GoBhl 95 //

children.text: prasvasthakāyaḥ sa samāhitātmā catvāri satyāni yathekṣitāni |
children.translated_text: His body at ease, his mind composed, that good man, examining

children.text: parīkṣamāṇo na cireṇa sādhur malān yathāsthūlamayāṃś cakāra || GoBhl_96 ||
children.translated_text: the Four Noble Truths as they had been perceived, quickly eliminated the impurities, gross as they were. // GoBhl 96 //

children.text: ⏑ anuśayaviśeṣaṃ bhāvanāmārgaheyaṃ ⏑ ravir iva niśāntadhvāntam ullikhya bhābhiḥ |
children.translated_text: [Eliminating] the particular latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) to be abandoned on the path of meditation, [erasing them] with radiance like the sun dispelling the darkness at night's end,

children.text: svatanum atanupuṇyāpyāyitāntarviśeṣāṃ apahṛtagurubhārāyāsalaghvīṃ babhāra || GoBhl_97 ||
children.translated_text: he bore his own body — lightened by removal of its heavy burden of weariness, its inner distinction nourished by abundant merit — [lightly]. // GoBhl 97 //

children.text: atha sa mahātmā kṛtakaraṇīyaḥ kṣaṇam apy avasthāṃ tāṃ parityajya sabahumānaḥ kevalaṃ teṣām upāsakānāṃ kṛtajñatām anurakṣan paryaṅkaṃ gaganatale baddhvā taiḥ sabahumānam udīkṣyamāṇo vistareṇa tebhyo yathāvṛttaṃ vyāhṛtya punar api tān ābabhāṣe |
children.translated_text: Then that great soul, his task accomplished, without remaining even a moment in that state, with reverence, solely to preserve his gratitude toward those lay-devotees, having formed a cross-legged posture in the sky, gazed upon reverently by them, narrated to them in full what had happened, and then addressed them again:

children.text: abhinandati yo janma sa duḥkham abhinandati |
children.translated_text: He who welcomes birth welcomes suffering;

children.text: duḥkhābhinandī duḥkhebhyo na jātu parimucyate || GoBhl_98 ||
children.translated_text: and he who welcomes suffering is never freed from sufferings. // GoBhl 98 //

children.text: pakvagaṇḍāyamānasya yaḥ kāyasyāsya saṃbhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: The arising of this body, which swells with ripening [of karma],

children.text: ītyupāyāsaduḥkhānām utpādaḥ sa vidāhinām || GoBhl_99 ||
children.translated_text: is the production of burning afflictions, distresses, and sufferings. // GoBhl 99 //

children.text: saṃsārāvacaraṃ kṛtsnaṃ sukham ekaghanīkṛtam |
children.translated_text: All the happiness found in the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>, even if compressed into a single mass,

children.text: narāṇāṃ janmaduḥkhena kṣaṇikenābhibhūyate || GoBhl_100 ||
children.translated_text: is overwhelmed by the momentary suffering of [a single] birth for human beings. // GoBhl 100 //

children.text: viṣopadigdhā niśitā ivāyasāḥ śikhā ivāgneḥ prabalānilākulāḥ |
children.translated_text: Like sharpened iron blades smeared with poison, like flames of fire agitated by powerful wind,

children.text: sabhīmanādā iva cāśmavṛṣṭayaḥ pravṛttayo duṣprasahāḥ śarīriṇām || GoBhl_101 ||
children.translated_text: like hailstorms with terrible roaring — the activities (<s>pravṛtti</s>) of embodied beings are unbearable. // GoBhl 101 //

children.text: bhavaprabandhavyasanānuṣaṅginī matir viparyāsatamo'vaguṇṭhitā |
children.translated_text: The mind, following the misfortunes of the continuous chain of existence, veiled by the darkness of delusion,

children.text: paraṃ samutkṣipya nipātayaty adho vipattipātālatale duruttare || GoBhl_102 ||
children.translated_text: lifts one up high only to cast [one] down into the abyss of calamity, impossible to climb out of. // GoBhl 102 //

children.text: taḍillatānāṃ sphuṭanānukāriṇīm anekarūpavyasanānubandhinīm |
children.translated_text: For a person who takes up this [existence] — resembling the flashing of lightning,

children.text: upādadānasya na jātv imāṃ śivaṃ narasya saṃskāravikārasaṃkulām || GoBhl_103 ||
children.translated_text: attended by manifold misfortunes — there is never well-being, turbulent as it is with the transformations of <s>saṃskāras</s> (mental formations). // GoBhl 103 //

children.text: svayaṃ samutthāpya vikalpavāsanān samīraṇoddhūtaśikhān bhavānalān |
children.translated_text: Having themselves raised up the conceptual tendencies (<s>vikalpavāsanā</s>) — fires of existence with flames fanned by the wind —

children.text: janāḥ saroṣā iva nirdahanty amī svam indriyagrāmam anarthapaṇḍitāḥ || GoBhl_104 ||
children.translated_text: these people, as if angry, burn their own aggregate of sense-faculties, scholars of misfortune that they are! // GoBhl 104 //

children.text: svabhāvaduḥkhān prakṛtiprabhaṅgurān asārakān phenalavān ivāmbhasaḥ |
children.translated_text: These [existences], inherently painful, by nature fragile, insubstantial — like foam-bubbles on water —

children.text: arīn imān ātmasamudbhavān bhavān sukhābhimānāś chalitāḥ śarīriṇaḥ || GoBhl_105 ||
children.translated_text: these enemies of one's own making — embodied beings, deceived by the conceit of happiness, [regard them as] existences. // GoBhl 105 //

children.text: niśamya ko nāma viḍambanām imāṃ pumān madīyāṃ śravaṇopatāpinīm |
children.translated_text: Having heard this mockery of mine, painful to the ears,

children.text: ratiṃ prakuryād apariplutendriyo vicitrasaṃkleśasamudbhave bhave || GoBhl_106 ||
children.translated_text: what person with unagitated senses would take delight in existence, the source of manifold afflictions? // GoBhl 106 //

children.text: ta eva santaḥ sukham adhyupāsate sanātanaṃ śāntam atītamānuṣam |
children.translated_text: Those same saints enjoy the happiness that is eternal, peaceful, beyond the human —

children.text: bhavopabhogapraṇayānupātinī matir na yeṣāṃ pariśuddhakarmaṇām || GoBhl_107 ||
children.translated_text: they whose minds, of purified deeds, do not follow the attraction of enjoying existence. // GoBhl 107 //

children.text: hatāvalepāḥ pariśuddhavṛttayaḥ sthitās ta evopari sarvasaṃpadām |
children.translated_text: With pride destroyed and conduct purified, they stand above all prosperity —

children.text: na bhāvanāṃ ye ślathayanti sādhavaḥ pravṛttyupādānaviṣopaśāntaye || GoBhl_108 ||
children.translated_text: those saints who do not slacken their meditation for the pacification of the poison of attachment to activity. // GoBhl 108 //

children.text: prakhyāpya doṣakaṇikān vibhavān bhavānāṃ nānāvidhavyasanasaṃkaṭasaṃbhavānām |
children.translated_text: Having proclaimed the particle-like defects and the fortunes of existences born from manifold calamities and straits,

children.text: saṃvejya parṣadam ṛṣiḥ sa upāsakānāṃ sadyo yayau praśamam agnir ivāmbuṣiktaḥ || GoBhl_109 ||
children.translated_text: that sage, having stirred the assembly of lay-devotees [to spiritual urgency], immediately went to peace, like a fire drenched with water. // GoBhl 109 //

children.text: iti bhavalubdhakāvadānam ||
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the story of the Hunter of Existence (<s>Bhavalubdhakāvadāna</s>).

children.text: 4. Kapīśvarajātakam = GoKī
children.translated_text: 4. <s>Kapīśvarajātakam</s> (The Story of the Monkey-King)

children.text: abhyasyanti tathā tathāgatasutās tyāgaṃ yathā svān api
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Tathāgata</s> practice generosity (<s>tyāga</s>) in such a way that

children.text: prāṇān prāṇikṛte tyajanti kṛpayā rogān ivāyāsinaḥ |
children.translated_text: out of compassion they give up even their own lives for the sake of living beings, as if discarding diseases that cause suffering;

children.text: kṣudrāḥ pāpavidhau tathā tv abhiratiṃ badhnanti niḥsādhvasā
children.translated_text: whereas the base, fearless in their delight in sinful deeds,

children.text: bhūtvā duścaritaikatānamanaso gacchanty adhastād yathā || GoKī_1 ||
children.translated_text: with minds single-pointedly devoted to evil conduct, descend downward. // GoKī 1 //

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate
children.translated_text: This is what is heard in tradition:

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ kilānyatamasmin vividhavarṇagandharasasaṃpannaphalabhārāvanatadrumopagūḍhe vikacasurabhikusumavallīvirājitaparyante marakatamaṇiprabhāharitaśādvalakuthāstīrṇaviṣamabhūmibhāge kamalakuvalayākaronmīlitavimalajalāśayaparigrahe mahaty araṇye vānarādhipatir babhūva ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in a certain great forest where trees heavy with fruits of various colors, fragrances, and flavors bent low, where the borders were adorned with blooming fragrant flower-vines, where uneven ground was carpeted with lawns green as the luster of emerald gems, and which possessed clear pools with lotuses and blue water-lilies opening — was the lord of monkeys.

children.text: mahākṛpāsvīkṛtamānasatvān nītvāpi puṇyāni paraṃ prakarṣam |
children.translated_text: Though he had taken his mind-essence to great compassion and had carried his merits to the highest degree,

children.text: gatiṃ tiraścām adhamāṃ prapede sādhuḥ sa kenāpi tu kāraṇena || GoKī_2 ||
children.translated_text: that good being, for some reason, attained the lowest destiny of animals. // GoKī 2 //

children.text: śubhāśubhaiḥ karmabhir āryakarmā krīḍann ivāsau bhavaraṅgamadhye |
children.translated_text: That one of noble deeds, playing as it were in the arena of existence with good and bad <s>karmas</s>,

children.text: nidarśayām āsa vicitrarūpām upāyapūrvām upapattimāyām || GoKī_3 ||
children.translated_text: displayed a birth-illusion of varied forms, preceded by skillful means (<s>upāya</s>). // GoKī 3 //

children.text: kṛtvāpy asau durgatisaṃnirodham apāyahetoś ciravipravāsāt |
children.translated_text: Though he had blocked the path to lower destinies and had long been exiled from the causes of misfortune,

children.text: saṃmohatāmisramayīṃ prapede tiryagvipattiṃ karuṇāparītaḥ || GoKī_4 ||
children.translated_text: encompassed by compassion, he entered the darkness-like calamity of animal birth. // GoKī 4 //

children.text: pravartate karmavaśena loko nirāśrayo 'yaṃ gaticakramadhye |
children.translated_text: The world revolves by the power of <s>karma</s>, without refuge, in the midst of the wheel of destinies;

children.text: babhūva tasya tv anavadyabuddheḥ śubhāśubhe karmaṇi kāmakāraḥ || GoKī_5 ||
children.translated_text: but for him of faultless wisdom, there was free will in both good and bad <s>karma</s>. // GoKī 5 //

children.text: mahātmā kāyamātreṇa vinipātaṃ gato 'py asau |
children.translated_text: That great soul, though fallen in body alone into degradation,

children.text: avipannaguṇābhyāsapeśalādhyāśayo babhau || GoKī_6 ||
children.translated_text: shone with a disposition made beautiful by the unimpaired practice of virtues. // GoKī 6 //

children.text: anāryaiś caritair dūrān niśamyaiva vivarjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Shunning from afar ignoble conduct merely upon hearing of it,

children.text: āryām udbhāvayām āsa paddhatiṃ sa śivodayām || GoKī_7 ||
children.translated_text: he manifested a noble path, auspicious in its arising. // GoKī 7 //

children.text: ātmasaṃjñāviparyāsaprahāṇād eva so 'tyajat |
children.translated_text: Solely through the abandonment of the delusion of self-perception (<s>ātmasaṃjñāviparyāsa</s>),

children.text: svasukhāsaṅginīṃ caryām anāryajanavartinīm || GoKī_8 ||
children.translated_text: he relinquished the conduct clinging to personal happiness, followed by ignoble folk. // GoKī 8 //

children.text: vṛttaśobhāṃ samālokya tasya jātivirodhinīm |
children.translated_text: Seeing the splendor of his conduct, contrary to his [animal] birth,

children.text: munayo 'py abhavann ātmany avajñāśithilādarāḥ || GoKī_9 ||
children.translated_text: even sages became slack in their self-regard, humbled with self-deprecation. // GoKī 9 //

children.text: sa tatra mātaram andhāṃ vṛddhāṃ ca paricaran vivekakāmatayā ca svayūtham apahāya teṣu teṣu puṣpaphalasamṛddheṣu vanāntareṣv anutkaṇṭhitamanā vijahāra |
children.translated_text: There he lived, attending to his blind and aged mother, and out of desire for solitude, having left his troop, he wandered contentedly in various forest regions rich with flowers and fruits.

children.text: aṃsena tāṃ pariharan viṣameṣu deśeṣv amlāyinīṃ srajam ivādhipatiḥ kapīnām |
children.translated_text: The lord of monkeys, carrying her on his shoulder through rough terrain like a wilting garland,

children.text: ānṛṇyam apratisamaṃ sa jagāma mātur garbhādidhāraṇapariśramakheditāyāḥ || GoKī_10 ||
children.translated_text: attained an incomparable freedom from debt toward his mother, wearied by the toil of bearing [him] from the womb onward. // GoKī 10 //

children.text: pākopapāditarasaiḥ sa phalaprakārair niṣprāṇakaiś ca madhubhiḥ kusumādhivāsaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With varieties of fruits whose juices were brought to ripeness by nature, with lifeless honeys perfumed by flowers,

children.text: toyaiś ca phullakamalotpalinīmanojñais tāṃ mātaraṃ paricacāra viśuddhasattvaḥ || GoKī_11 ||
children.translated_text: and with waters delightful from pools of blooming lotuses and water-lilies — he of pure nature attended to that mother. // GoKī 11 //

children.text: tayā karuṇayā cāsāv anubaddhaḥ kapīśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Bound by that compassion, the monkey-king

children.text: vijahāra vivikteṣu parvateṣu vaneṣu ca || GoKī_12 ||
children.translated_text: dwelt in secluded mountains and forests. // GoKī 12 //

children.text: atha kadā cid anyatamo vyādho dhanvī pṛṣṭhāvāpī pragāḍhāvabaddhaparikaro mālutāvatānasaṃyatākulakeśabhārabhāsuraḥ śvāpadān abhidravaṃs taṃ deśam abhijagāma |
children.translated_text: Then one day, a certain hunter, carrying a bow and a quiver on his back, with his gear tightly fastened, his mass of tangled hair restrained by a band of bark, brilliant [in appearance], chasing wild animals, came to that region.

children.text: krodhāraktavilocanaṃ giriśilāśyāmāyatoraḥsthalaṃ
children.translated_text: With eyes red with anger, his broad chest dark like mountain-rock,

children.text: vallīkuṇḍalakāvabaddhakapilavyādhūtakeśāśivam |
children.translated_text: inauspicious with tawny disheveled hair bound by vine-earrings,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā mṛtyum ivāpatantam atha taṃ tadgocarāḥ prāṇino
children.translated_text: seeing him descending like Death itself, the creatures in that territory

children.text: yātāḥ kvāpi vilaṅghya kaṇṭakalatānaddhān prapātān api || GoKī_13 ||
children.translated_text: fled somewhere, leaping over even precipices entangled with thorny vines. // GoKī 13 //

children.text: atha sa durātmā viphalaprayāsatayā sutarāṃ krodhāgninā pradīptamānasaḥ saśiraḥprakampaṃ niśvasya ca palāśikayāvagṛhya lalāṭapuṭaprasvedasalilaṃ tam evānukampamānaṃ taṃ vānarādhipatiṃ dadarśa pādapaikadeśāvasthitam | dṛṣṭvā ca bhṛśataraṃ krodhavahninā prajajvāla |
children.translated_text: Then that wicked one, his mind blazing all the more with the fire of anger due to his fruitless efforts, sighing with his head shaking, wiping the sweat from his forehead with a leaf-cup, spotted that very monkey-king — who was full of compassion — stationed on a part of a tree. And seeing him, he blazed even more fiercely with the fire of anger.

children.text: aśaknuvanto balinaḥ prabādhituṃ khalāḥ svadaurātmyavirūkṣadṛṣṭayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The wicked, unable to injure the powerful, with eyes harsh from their own evil nature,

children.text: akāraṇakrodhaviṣāśivāśivā bhavanti sādhuṣv apakāradāruṇāḥ || GoKī_14 ||
children.translated_text: venomous with causeless anger like <s>Aśiva</s> (malignant spirits), become cruel in harming the virtuous. // GoKī 14 //

children.text: atha sa durātmā dhanuṣi niśitaṃ sāyakaṃ saṃdhāya vegena bodhisattvam abhidudrāva | sa ca mahātmā lobhanīyataraṃ vapur avetya mayi ca nāsyāyaṃ nirbandha iti | śakto 'pi pratyavasthātum apagatasaṃrambhamānasaḥ khaga iva mahatā javena tadbāṇapatham aticakrāma |
children.translated_text: Then that evil-souled one, having fitted a sharp arrow to his bow, rushed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with force. And the great-souled one, recognizing his body to be even more desirable [as a target], and [thinking] 'his hostility is not directed at me [personally]' — though capable of resisting, his mind free from agitation, like a bird he passed beyond the range of that arrow with great speed.

children.text: muṣṭiprahāreṇa sa śailaśṛṅgaṃ śakto 'pi saṃcūrṇayituṃ mahātmā |
children.translated_text: Though the great-souled one was capable of crushing a mountain peak with a blow of his fist,

children.text: jālmaṃ tam eva tv anukampamānas tadbāṇasaṃpātapathād vyatītaḥ || GoKī_15 ||
children.translated_text: yet, feeling compassion even for that wretch, he passed beyond the range of his arrow. // GoKī 15 //

children.text: sa ca puruṣādhamas tīvratarasaṃrambhamanyuvegākulīkṛtāśayas tāṃ bodhisattvajananīṃ pratyākṛṣṭatīkṣṇabāṇāśanir abhisasāda |
children.translated_text: And that vilest of men, his mind overwhelmed by an even more intense rush of furious rage, advanced upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother, the thunder of his drawn sharp arrow [ready to strike].

children.text: abhyāsayogāt kaṭhinīkṛtāni manāṃsy anāryaiś caritaprasaṅgaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Minds hardened by the practice of ignoble conduct,

children.text: pāpakriyāyām avicārya kāryaṃ caranti lokasya niraṅkuśāni || GoKī_16 ||
children.translated_text: act without considering consequences in sinful deeds — unbridled in the world. // GoKī 16 //

children.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ purāyaṃ me mātaraṃ vyāpādayatīty avigaṇitasvaprāṇātyayaḥ sasaṃbhramadrutataragatir abhigamya taṃ vyādhaṃ sānunayapraśamamadhuram ity abravīt |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, [thinking] 'before he kills my mother!' — disregarding the risk to his own life, with hurried, swift pace, approached that hunter and spoke soothingly, gently, sweetly:

children.text: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha mahāsattva mā vadhīr jananīṃ mama |
children.translated_text: 'Stop, stop, O great-souled one! Do not kill my mother!

children.text: kas tavemāṃ guṇo hatvā vṛddhāṃ proṣitalocanām || GoKī_17 ||
children.translated_text: What merit is there for you in killing this old one, whose eyes have dimmed? // GoKī 17 //

children.text: tavāpi nūnam āyuṣman mātā hṛdayavallabhā |
children.translated_text: Surely you too, O long-lived one, have a mother dear to your heart;

children.text: ātmasnehānumānena mā vyātsīr mama mātaram || GoKī_18 ||
children.translated_text: by the inference of your own self-love, do not slay my mother! // GoKī 18 //

children.text: phalamūlajalāhārāṃ vasantīṃ vijane vane |
children.translated_text: She who lives in the desolate forest, subsisting on fruits, roots, and water —

children.text: vyāpādayitum ambāṃ me sādhos tava na yujyate || GoKī_19 ||
children.translated_text: it is not fitting for you, a noble one, to destroy my mother! // GoKī 19 //

children.text: spṛṣṭadṛṣṭāpacāre 'pi puruṣās tuṅgamānasāḥ |
children.translated_text: Men of lofty spirit, even when offenses of sight and touch have been committed,

children.text: praharanti na śauṭīrād dainyopahatacetasi || GoKī_20 ||
children.translated_text: do not, out of mere bravado, strike one whose mind is afflicted with wretchedness. // GoKī 20 //

children.text: purātanair eva hatāṃ karmabhiḥ paruṣair imām |
children.translated_text: She is already slain by her former harsh <s>karmas</s>;

children.text: ghnato niraparādhāṃ te kathaṃ notpadyate dayā || GoKī_21 ||
children.translated_text: as you kill this innocent one, how does compassion not arise in you? // GoKī 21 //

children.text: api cedaṃ mṛgendrāsṛkkalaṅkitamukhaṃ śaram |
children.translated_text: And this arrow, its mouth stained with the blood of the lord of beasts —

children.text: na lajjase kathaṃ nāma muñcañ chākhāmṛgītanau || GoKī_22 ||
children.translated_text: how are you not ashamed to release it upon the body of a female monkey? // GoKī 22 //

children.text: sphītāvalepau karimastakeṣu bhujāv imau jyākaṭhinaprakoṣṭhau |
children.translated_text: These arms of yours, with wrists hardened by the bowstring, [fit] for the heads of great elephants —

children.text: niyujyamānau kṛpaṇāśrayeṣu daurbhāgyam udbhāvayataḥ sphuṭaṃ te || GoKī_23 ||
children.translated_text: being employed against wretched beings, they clearly display your misfortune. // GoKī 23 //

children.text: amuktapūrvo hariṇāṅganāsv apy akṣūṇalakṣas tava kaṅkapattraḥ |
children.translated_text: This barbed arrow of yours, never before released even upon doe-eyed deer, of unerring aim —

children.text: śilīmukho 'yaṃ pratikuñjarīva niyujyamānaḥ kapidurgatāyām || GoKī_24 ||
children.translated_text: this shaft is being employed upon a miserable she-monkey, as if upon a rival she-elephant. // GoKī 24 //

children.text: abhyarthyamānā ripuṇāpi dhīrā bāṣpāmbuviṣyandivilocanena |
children.translated_text: Even the steadfast, when entreated by an enemy with eyes flowing with tears,

children.text: bhavanti tatkālavinīyamānakrodhoparāgādhikaramyaśobhāḥ || GoKī_25 ||
children.translated_text: become of an even more beautiful splendor, their anger at that moment being overcome. // GoKī 25 //

children.text: tasmād udvīkṣasva paraṃ ca lokam imāṃ ca vṛddhām aparāyaṇāṃ tvam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, look to the other world and to this aged one who has no other refuge;

children.text: mā gā vaśaṃ roṣaniśācarasya lokadvayānarthaśatāvahasya || GoKī_26 ||
children.translated_text: do not fall under the sway of anger — that night-demon — which brings hundreds of calamities in both worlds.' // GoKī 26 //

children.text: evam apy asāv ucyamānaḥ krauryābhyāsakaṭhorahṛdayapāṣāṇas tad bodhisattvavacanam ākarṇyaivāvadhīrayām āsa |
children.translated_text: Even though addressed thus, that one, his heart a stone hardened by the habit of cruelty, hearing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s words, simply disregarded them.

children.text: pāpaprasaṅgaparuṣīkṛtamānaseṣu vyarthā giro guṇijanābhihitā bhavanti |
children.translated_text: Words spoken by the virtuous are fruitless upon those whose minds are roughened by the course of sin —

children.text: viprasrutā jaladharebhya ivāmbudhārā vajrāgnidagdhaśikhareṣu mahīruheṣu || GoKī_27 ||
children.translated_text: like streams of water from rain-clouds upon trees whose peaks have been burnt by lightning-fire. // GoKī 27 //

children.text: atha vānareśvaras tam anāryakarmāṇam anunayavidhuram avagamya cintām āpede |
children.translated_text: Then the lord of monkeys, understanding that ignoble-acting one to be beyond persuasion, fell into thought:

children.text: mātary ayaṃ yadi mama praharaty anāryaḥ saṃpaśyato mama vadhaḥ sakalaḥ sa eva |
children.translated_text: 'If this ignoble one strikes my mother before my eyes, that is completely the same as my own death;

children.text: tyaktvā svajīvitam ataḥ paripālayāmi vṛddhām imāṃ kumudinīdhavalāṃ ca kīrtim || GoKī_28 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, giving up my own life, I shall protect this aged one and my spotless reputation, white as a bed of <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotuses). // GoKī 28 //

children.text: kāmaṃ mṛte mayi mariṣyati viklaveyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Granted, if I die, this helpless one will die too,

children.text: hā putraketi kṛpaṇā karuṇaṃ rudantī |
children.translated_text: crying piteously 'Alas, my son!' — the wretched one.

children.text: yuktas tathāpi mama pūrvataraṃ vināśo
children.translated_text: Even so, it is proper that I perish first;

children.text: draṣṭuṃ guruvyasanam asti na me prabhutvam || GoKī_29 ||
children.translated_text: I do not have the power to witness the calamity of [my] elder. // GoKī 29 //

children.text: jātaś ca nāma na vinakṣyati vety ayuktam utpāda eva niyamena nipātahetuḥ |
children.translated_text: 'It is unreasonable [to say] that one born will not perish; birth itself is inevitably the cause of downfall;

children.text: tulye ca nāma maraṇavyasanopatāpe mṛtyur varaṃ parahitāvahitāśayasya || GoKī_30 ||
children.translated_text: and when the calamity of death is equal in either case, death is preferable for one whose intention is devoted to the welfare of others. // GoKī 30 //

children.text: tadgarbhasaṃdhāraṇasaṃbhṛtasya snehānubaddhasya pariśramasya |
children.translated_text: 'Of the toil she endured in bearing me in her womb, bound by love —

children.text: asyāḥ krameṇaiva mamābhyupeto nirveśakālātiśayotsavo 'yam || GoKī_31 ||
children.translated_text: for her, by this very [sacrifice] of mine, has come this supreme festival of the time of repayment. // GoKī 31 //

children.text: duḥkhaṃ tu nirgārayatīva ceto mamaikam evāvinivāryavīryam |
children.translated_text: 'Yet one thing alone, of irresistible force, wrings my heart with grief:

children.text: ambā mṛtaṃ māṃ yad iyaṃ viditvā duḥkhena saṃtyakṣyati jīvalokam || GoKī_32 ||
children.translated_text: that this mother, learning of my death, will in sorrow abandon the world of the living. // GoKī 32 //

children.text: arthāya netravyasanaṃ tu jātam asyā na māṃ drakṣyati māryamāṇam |
children.translated_text: 'Yet her eye-affliction has arisen for a purpose — she will not see me being slain

children.text: yad asya tīkṣṇena durādhareṇa vyādhaprayuktena śilīmukhena || GoKī_33 ||
children.translated_text: by this sharp, irresistible arrow discharged by the hunter. // GoKī 33 //

children.text: kṛtvā ca yat pāpam ayaṃ tapasvī duḥkhāni saṃprāpsyati dāruṇāni |
children.translated_text: 'And that this wretched one, having committed this sin, will suffer terrible agonies —

children.text: etan mano nirdahatīva mahyaṃ prāṇoparodhaṃ svam acintayitvā || GoKī_34 ||
children.translated_text: this burns my mind like fire, without a thought for my own cessation of life. // GoKī 34 //

children.text: dhig astu saṃkleśapiśācavaiśasaṃ pṛthagjanatvaṃ dhig anarthapaṇḍitam |
children.translated_text: 'Fie upon the state of an ordinary being (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), that butchery of the demon of defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>), fie upon that which is expert only in calamity —

children.text: vipattipātālatale duruttare vṛthaiva yal lokam imaṃ vimuñcati || GoKī_35 ||
children.translated_text: which casts this world in vain into the abyss of misfortune, difficult to surmount! // GoKī 35 //

children.text: atha sa prakṛtiśuddhasattvas tadavastho 'py anabhijātaviṣādadainyasaṃbhramamanās taṃ vyādham abravīt |
children.translated_text: Then that one of innately pure being, even in that state, his mind free from ignoble despondency, wretchedness, and agitation, addressed the hunter:

children.text: amogho yad ayaṃ bāṇas tvayā tāta samudyataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Since this arrow raised by you, dear one, should not go to waste —

children.text: mayi prahara niḥśaṅkaṃ mā kārṣīr mṛtamārikām || GoKī_36 ||
children.translated_text: strike me without hesitation; do not cause death to my mother! // GoKī 36 //

children.text: atha sā vṛddhā vānarī taṃ bodhisattvasyātiduṣkaraṃ hṛdayasaṃtāpakaraṃ vyavasāyam avetya pāṇibhyāṃ hṛdayam abhighnantī sāśrukaṇṭhā gadgadāyamānavacanā bodhisattvam āha |
children.translated_text: Then that old she-monkey, perceiving the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s exceedingly difficult and heart-rending resolve, striking her chest with her hands, her throat choked with tears, her words faltering, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

children.text: putra mā sāhasaṃ kārṣīr mayy eva praharatv ayam |
children.translated_text: 'Son, do not act rashly! Let him strike me instead;

children.text: mṛtayāpi mayā kiṃ syāj jarayāpītasārayā || GoKī_37 ||
children.translated_text: what use is there even in me alive — old, with all vitality drained by age? // GoKī 37 //

children.text: yad ahaṃ tāta jīvāmi durmanā duḥkhabhāginī |
children.translated_text: 'That I live, O child, sorrowful and sharing in suffering,

children.text: tvatsaṅgamasukhābhyāsaṃ rasāgraṃ na varaṃ hi tat || GoKī_38 ||
children.translated_text: clinging to the supreme essence of the joy of your company — is that really worthwhile? // GoKī 38 //

children.text: tvayi jīvati jīvanti bahavo dharmajīvinaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'While you live, many who live by <s>dharma</s> live;

children.text: nimīlite tvayi vyaktaṃ diśaḥ sarvā nimīlitāḥ || GoKī_39 ||
children.translated_text: if your eyes close, clearly all directions are closed. // GoKī 39 //

children.text: jarājanitasaṃvegā viproṣitavilocanā |
children.translated_text: 'Filled with urgency born of old age, my sight having departed,

children.text: mṛtyum evābhikāṅkṣāmi niśvāsaikaparāyaṇā || GoKī_40 ||
children.translated_text: I long only for death, my sole refuge being my sighs. // GoKī 40 //

children.text: tvaṃ me hṛdayasarvasvaṃ putrakocchvasimi tvayā |
children.translated_text: 'You are the entire treasure of my heart, my son — I breathe through you;

children.text: tvayi jīvati jīvantīṃ mām avehi mṛtām api || GoKī_41 ||
children.translated_text: know me as dead even while living, if you live. // GoKī 41 //

children.text: upāyāsi prapannāyā jarākāntāram āyatam |
children.translated_text: 'For me who has entered upon the vast wilderness of old age, without protection,

children.text: viśrambhasthānavan mṛtyur bhāgyenaiva mamāgataḥ || GoKī_42 ||
children.translated_text: death has come, by good fortune, as a place of trust. // GoKī 42 //

children.text: atha bodhisattvo 'bhipraṇamyānuneṣyann anukampāśītalair api nirdahann iva vacobhir jananīṃ praty āha |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, bowing down and about to console [her], with words cool with compassion yet as if burning [her heart], said to his mother:

children.text: kṣudrajantor api kṛte jahyāṃ dehaśatāny api |
children.translated_text: 'Even for the sake of the lowliest creature, I would give up a hundred bodies;

children.text: mātur arthe tyajed deham itaro 'pi gatavyathaḥ || GoKī_43 ||
children.translated_text: for a mother's sake, even another [person] would abandon his body without distress. // GoKī 43 //

children.text: kāyavraṇam imaṃ tīvravyasanāpātakātaram |
children.translated_text: 'This body-wound, trembling at the sudden blow of calamity —

children.text: tavaiva paricaryāyai mātaḥ pariharāmy aham || GoKī_44 ||
children.translated_text: I preserve it, O mother, for the sole purpose of serving you. // GoKī 44 //

children.text: na ca me kāyikaṃ duḥkhaṃ tathā janayati vyathām |
children.translated_text: 'Physical suffering does not cause me such anguish

children.text: mānasenaiva duḥkhena yathā pīḍye vidāhinā || GoKī_45 ||
children.translated_text: as the burning mental suffering by which I am tormented. // GoKī 45 //

children.text: svakāyaparirakṣārtham adhyupekṣya vadhaṃ tava |
children.translated_text: 'If, for the sake of protecting my own body, I overlook your slaughter,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ manomayaṃ soḍhuṃ kathaṃ śakṣyāmi duḥsaham || GoKī_46 ||
children.translated_text: how shall I be able to endure the unbearable mental suffering? // GoKī 46 //

children.text: api cāmba |
children.translated_text: 'And moreover, O mother:

children.text: ucchrāyā vinipātinaḥ priyajanaśleṣā visaṃyoginaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Elevations end in falls; unions with loved ones end in separation;

children.text: sarve saṃnicayāḥ kṣayāntavirasā dīpāḥ prabhāteṣv iva |
children.translated_text: all accumulations end in loss, insipid — like lamps at dawn;

children.text: mṛtyor aprativāryavīryamahataḥ krīḍāmṛgāḥ prāṇinaḥ
children.translated_text: living beings are the playthings of death, whose power is irresistible;

children.text: saṃsārādhvani dehināṃ vicaratāṃ dharmānukṛtyaṃ param || GoKī_47 ||
children.translated_text: for embodied beings wandering on the road of <s>saṃsāra</s>, <s>dharma</s> alone is the supreme guide.' // GoKī 47 //

children.text: atha sā bodhisattvajananī śītair ananyasattvasadṛśaiḥ karuṇāniṣyandabhūtaiḥ snehātiśayodgāribhiḥ svajīvitanirapekṣair aparimlāyamānagauravaprasādapeśalais tadvacobhiḥ sutarām ākleditahṛdayā vyāpinā svareṇa tad vanam āpūrayantī sakaruṇaṃ virurāva |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother, her heart all the more melted by those words — cool, unmatched in character, born of the flow of compassion, overflowing with excess of love, heedless of her own life, unfading in their gravity and graceful clarity — filling that forest with her voice spreading everywhere, cried out piteously:

children.text: amūni tava vākyāni śītāny api dahanti mām |
children.translated_text: 'These words of yours, though cool, burn me

children.text: himāpātā iva latāṃ pākapāṇḍupalāśinīm || GoKī_48 ||
children.translated_text: like snowfalls upon a creeper whose leaves have yellowed from [over-]ripening. // GoKī 48 //

children.text: hā mātṛvatsala ripuṣv api maitracitta
children.translated_text: 'Alas, O you who are devoted to your mother, friendly-minded even toward enemies,

children.text: kṣudreṣv api prakṛtibhadra mṛdusvabhāva |
children.translated_text: innately good even toward the lowly, gentle by nature!

children.text: putrāpahāya kṛpaṇāṃ kva nu yāsyasi tvaṃ
children.translated_text: Where will you go, abandoning me — wretched one —

children.text: mām adya duḥkhaśatabāṇaśaravyabhūtām || GoKī_49 ||
children.translated_text: who today has become the target of hundreds of arrows of sorrow? // GoKī 49 //

children.text: hā hā hatāsmi kṛpaṇā cyutabhāgadheyā daivena sādhujananirdayapauruṣeṇa |
children.translated_text: 'Alas, alas! I am slain — wretched, fallen from my share of fortune — by fate, whose valor is merciless toward good people!

children.text: saṃrakṣa māṃ suciram ekapade jahāsi kiṃ putrakādya nanu saiva tavāsmi mātā || GoKī_50 ||
children.translated_text: Protect me for long — why do you abandon me in a single step, my son? Am I not still that very mother of yours? // GoKī 50 //

children.text: yātāḥ kva te 'dya munayo jvalitaprabhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Where have they gone today, those sages blazing with splendor?

children.text: sakhyaḥ kva tāḥ pratigatā vanadevatās te |
children.translated_text: Where have they gone, those forest deities who are your friends?

children.text: dharmāya rakṣati jagat kila dharmajīvī
children.translated_text: 'One who lives by <s>dharma</s> protects the world for <s>dharma</s>'s sake,' [they say] —

children.text: kasmāj jagan mama nimīlati putraśūnyam || GoKī_51 ||
children.translated_text: then why does the world shut its eyes on me, bereft of my son? // GoKī 51 //

children.text: śailā nirjhariṇaḥ kadambakakubhaśreṇīniruddhātapā
children.translated_text: 'May the mountains with their cascades, with rows of <s>kadamba</s> trees blocking the heat,

children.text: nadyaś ca sphuṭapadmareṇuharitakṣāmormimālādharāḥ |
children.translated_text: and the rivers bearing garlands of waves tinged green with the pollen of blossoming lotuses,

children.text: saṃśāntā vanarājayaś ca śikhinā sudyotitāś candrakair
children.translated_text: and the serene royal forests illuminated by the radiant peacock tail-moons,

children.text: bhānor aṃśukarālitāś ca divasā rakṣantu me putrakam || GoKī_52 ||
children.translated_text: and the days blazing with the sun's fierce rays — may they all protect my child! // GoKī 52 //

children.text: acetanānām api pādapānāṃ babhūva kampo ruditena tena |
children.translated_text: Even the insensate trees trembled at that weeping;

children.text: mṛdūkṛtaṃ tasya na nāma ceto manāg api krūramanorathasya || GoKī_53 ||
children.translated_text: but the heart of that one of cruel desires was not softened even a little. // GoKī 53 //

children.text: atha sa durātmā tadvākyaśravaṇajvalitakopānalādīptahṛdayaḥ kathāparyavasānam avigaṇayyaiva bodhisattvaṃ tīkṣṇena bāṇena marmadeśe 'bhihatya prāṇair viyojayāṃ babhūva |
children.translated_text: Then that evil-souled one, his heart set ablaze by the fire of anger kindled by hearing those words, without waiting for the end of the speech, having struck the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with a sharp arrow in a vital spot, deprived him of life.

children.text: śivāvirutajarjarā iva diśo 'bhavaṃs tatkṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: The directions seemed shattered by the howling of jackals at that instant;

children.text: tatāna bahalaṃ tamo dviradayūthanīlaṃ jagat |
children.translated_text: thick darkness, dark as a herd of elephants, spread over the world;

children.text: bhayād iva cakampire vilulitopalāḥ parvatāḥ
children.translated_text: the mountains trembled as if in fear, their boulders dislodged;

children.text: papāta śalabhāvalīvalayapiṅgalaṃ khād rajaḥ || GoKī_54 ||
children.translated_text: dust fell from the sky, tawny with a wreath of moth-swarms. // GoKī 54 //

children.text: viśuṣkajalabhairavāḥ pradaragahvarāḥ sindhavo
children.translated_text: The rivers at that instant, with their waters dried up, became terrifying with gaping chasms,

children.text: dvitīya iva bhāskare samudite 'bhavaṃs tatkṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: as if a second sun had risen;

children.text: papāta rudhiraṃ divo ghaṭamukhair ivāvarjitaṃ
children.translated_text: blood rained from the sky, as if poured from the mouths of pots,

children.text: hate kapigaṇādhipe sucaritaikaratnākare || GoKī_55 ||
children.translated_text: when the lord of the monkey-host, that sole treasury of good conduct, was slain. // GoKī 55 //

children.text: atha sa dasyus tad atidāruṇaṃ karma kṛtvā sadyas tadvipākacihnākulīkṛtahṛdayaḥ svam āvāsam abhipratasthe | tatra ca tatkarmāparādhena bhairavo niṣpratīkārarabhasajvālāmālākulo mahadagniḥ prajajvāla |
children.translated_text: Then that bandit, having committed that exceedingly terrible deed, his heart immediately troubled by signs of its consequence, set off for his dwelling. And there, by the very transgression of that deed, a dreadful great fire blazed up, seething with garlands of fierce, irresistible flames.

children.text: dūrād eva tam āpatantam anilapreṅkholanācañcalaiḥ
children.translated_text: From afar, the fire embraced him as he came rushing, with its long flame-arms swaying in the wind's rocking —

children.text: sadyo 'gniḥ pariṣaṣvaje priyam iva jvālābhujair āyataiḥ |
children.translated_text: instantly — as if [embracing] a beloved, with its extended flame-arms.

children.text: karma kṣetraviśeṣabṛṃhitaphalaṃ karmāntarāvyāhataṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s>, whose fruit is nurtured by the particular field, unimpeded by other <s>karmas</s>,

children.text: nikṣepaṃ vapuṣo vipākacapalaṃ nodīkṣate prāṇinām || GoKī_56 ||
children.translated_text: fickle in its ripening, does not regard the deposit of [good deeds in] the bodies of living beings. // GoKī 56 //

children.text: saṃśuṣkakakṣāntavisarpiṇībhir jvālābhir agneḥ pavanoddhatābhiḥ |
children.translated_text: With flames of fire spreading through the dried undergrowth, fanned by the wind,

children.text: āliṅgito 'sau kaṭhināntarātmā mumoha hā heti ca saṃrurāva || GoKī_57 ||
children.translated_text: that hard-hearted one, embraced [by them], fainted and cried out 'Alas, alas!' // GoKī 57 //

children.text: anilākulitānalāvalīḍhaḥ kaṭudhūmaughaniruddhakaṇṭhatāluḥ |
children.translated_text: Licked by rows of flames agitated by the wind, his throat and palate blocked by clouds of acrid smoke,

children.text: nipapāta samutpapāta cāsāv asakṛn mīna ivāturas tapasvī || GoKī_58 ||
children.translated_text: that wretched one fell and rose again and again — like a suffering fish [out of water]. // GoKī 58 //

children.text: tasyāsthiśeṣam api kāpuruṣasya dagdhvā
children.translated_text: Having burnt even the bone-remains of that coward,

children.text: vahniḥ saroṣa iva naiva śaśāma śīghram |
children.translated_text: the fire, as if still angry, did not quickly subside;

children.text: taddūṣitāṃ vasumatīm api dagdhukāmo
children.translated_text: wishing to burn even the earth defiled by him,

children.text: jajvāla dhūmakapiśārcir ⏑ – ⏑ antaḥ || GoKī_59 ||
children.translated_text: it blazed with smoke-tawny flames [lacuna] within. // GoKī 59 //

children.text: jvālānāṃ gaganatalāvalambinīnāṃ saṃtānāḥ kusumitakarṇikāragaurāḥ |
children.translated_text: The streams of flames reaching the surface of the sky, pale gold like blossoming <s>karṇikāra</s> flowers —

children.text: rejus te pralayavilīyamānasānor niryāsāḥ kanakagirer iva sravantaḥ || GoKī_60 ||
children.translated_text: They shone — the exudations of the golden mountain streaming forth, as from a mountain dissolving at the end of the world. // GoKī 60 //

children.text: dagdho duścaritāgnibhiḥ sa paruṣair dagdhaḥ punaḥ pāvakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Burned by the fires of his own evil deeds, then burned again by harsh [actual] flames,

children.text: pāpātmā sakalatraputravibhavaḥ śuṣko yathā pādapaḥ |
children.translated_text: that sinful one, with his wife, sons, and wealth, was like a dried-up tree;

children.text: taṃ bhūyo 'pi dadāha dāruṇataraḥ karmendhano nārako
children.translated_text: him the hellish fire burned yet again, even more terrible, fueled by <s>karma</s>,

children.text: vahnir dhūmakalākalaṅkitamukhajvālākalāpaś ciram || GoKī_61 ||
children.translated_text: with garlands of flames from its smoke-and-streak-stained mouth, for a long time. // GoKī 61 //

children.text: avetya pāpakarmaṇām idaṃ vipākavaiśasaṃ
children.translated_text: Understanding this terrible ripening of sinful deeds,

children.text: vivarjayed asatkriyāṃ bhujaṅgamāṅganām iva |
children.translated_text: one should shun evil actions as one would a female serpent;

children.text: prasādayec ca mānasaṃ prasādanīyakarmasu
children.translated_text: and one should make the mind serene through actions that bring serenity —

children.text: jinauraseṣv akāraṇaprajāhitābhiyogiṣu || GoKī_62 ||
children.translated_text: [devotion to] the sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), who are devoted to the welfare of beings without cause. // GoKī 62 //

children.text: || iti śrīkapīśvarajātakaṃ navatriṃśattamam ||
children.translated_text: || Thus ends the thirty-ninth [tale], the <s>Kapīśvara-jātaka</s> (the birth-story of the Lord of Monkeys). ||

children.text: 5. Maitrakanyaka
children.translated_text: 5. <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>

children.text: mātary apakāriṇaḥ prāṇina ihaiva vyasanaprapātapātālāvalambino bhavantīti satatasamupajāyamānapremaprasādabahumānamānasaiḥ satpuruṣair mātaraḥ śuśrūṣaṇīyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Since creatures who harm their mothers fall, even in this very life, into the abyss of calamity — therefore mothers should be served with devotion by virtuous persons whose minds are constantly filled with love, serenity, and high esteem.

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate
children.translated_text: As the tradition relates —

children.text: vikasitasitakumudendukundakusumāvalīguṇagaṇavibhūṣitaḥ pūrvajanmāntaropāttāprameyānavadyavipulasakalasaṃbhāro dhanadasamānaratnāśrayaḥ svajanakṛpaṇavanīpakabhujyamānodāravibhavasāranicayo mitro nāma sārthavāho babhūva |
children.translated_text: There was a caravan-leader named <s>Mitra</s>, adorned with the clusters of virtues [resembling] garlands of blooming white night-lotuses, moon, and <s>kunda</s> flowers; endowed with immeasurable, faultless, vast, and complete provisions accumulated in former births; a repository of jewels equal to <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>); whose abundant and excellent store of wealth was enjoyed by his own people and the poor like trees [enjoyed by all].

children.text: paropakāraikarasābhirāmā vibhūtayaḥ sphītatarā babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: His abundant riches, delightful in their sole essence of benefiting others, flourished

children.text: tasyāryasattvasya nabhasy anabhre karā ivendoḥ kumudāvadātāḥ || GoMk_1 ||
children.translated_text: like the rays of the moon, white as water-lilies, in a cloudless sky — [the riches] of that noble-souled one. // GoMk 1 //

children.text: tṛṣṇānalaiḥ śokaśikhāpracaṇḍaiś cittāni dagdhāni bahuprakāram |
children.translated_text: The minds of the hopeful, burned in many ways by the fires of craving with fierce flames of grief,

children.text: āśāvatāṃ sapraṇayābhirāmair dānāmbusekaiḥ śamayāṃ babhūva || GoMk_2 ||
children.translated_text: he would cool with the sprinkling of gifts, affectionately delightful. // GoMk 2 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā lokam imaṃ dhanakṣayabhayāt saṃtyaktadānotsavaṃ
children.translated_text: Seeing this world, which had abandoned the festival of giving out of fear of losing wealth,

children.text: lobhakleśapiśācikāvaśatayā saṃdūṣitādhyāśayam |
children.translated_text: whose inner disposition was corrupted by the dominion of the she-demon of greed and affliction —

children.text: kāruṇyāt sa dadāv anāthakṛpaṇaklībāturebhyo dhanaṃ
children.translated_text: out of compassion, he gave wealth to the helpless, wretched, impotent, and afflicted,

children.text: matvā vāyuhatārṇavormicapalaṃ svaṃ jīvitaṃ bhūyasā || GoMk_3 ||
children.translated_text: considering his own life to be as fleeting as ocean waves struck by the wind. // GoMk 3 //

children.text: yeṣu vyāsajya ceto bhujagavaravadhūbhogabhīmeṣu lubdhā
children.translated_text: Those riches — upon which the greedy, having fixed their minds, plunge into the pit of sin

children.text: gāhante pāpagartaṃ sphuṭadahanaśikhābhīmaparyantarandhram |
children.translated_text: with its terrifying edges of blazing fire-flames, fearsome as the coils of a great serpent-queen —

children.text: vātāghātapranṛttapravaranaravadhūnetrapakṣmāgralolāṃs
children.translated_text: those riches, restless as the tips of the eyelashes of excellent women dancing in the wind-blasts,

children.text: tān arthān arthiduḥkhavyupaśamapaṭubhiḥ protsasarja pradānaiḥ || GoMk_4 ||
children.translated_text: he released through generous gifts, skilled at alleviating the suffering of supplicants. // GoMk 4 //

children.text: tasyāputradhanatvāt putrābhilāṣiṇo yadā manorathaśatair asakṛd unmiṣitonmiṣitāḥ putraśriyaḥ prasahya sphītataravairabhārendhanavahnineva vigatanikhilapratīkāradāruṇaprabhāvamahatāśu kṛtāntālayaikaparāyaṇāḥ kriyante sma tadāsau lokapravādamātrayāpi panthānaṃ samavatīrya dhanadavaruṇakuberaśaṃkarajanārdanapitāmahādīn devatāviśeṣān putrārthaṃ yācitum ārebhe |
children.translated_text: Since he was without a son and wealth [heir], and since his desires for a son, though kindled again and again by hundreds of wishes, were forcibly destroyed — as if by a fire fueled by the firewood of an ever-increasing, terrible, and irresistible enemy, made utterly subject to the abode of Death — he descended on the path [of supplication] guided merely by popular custom, and began to beseech the specific deities <s>Dhanada</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), and <s>Pitāmaha</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) for a son.

children.text: yasmin yasmiṃs tanayasarasi svacchapuṇyāmbupūrṇe
children.translated_text: In whichever pond of offspring, filled with clear meritorious waters,

children.text: vavre vṛddhiṃ samuditamahāvaṃśalakṣmyambujanma |
children.translated_text: the lotus-born fortune of a great and flourishing lineage sought growth —

children.text: tat tat tasya prabālavirasāṃ yāti tīkṣṇāṃśumālaiḥ
children.translated_text: in each of those, it withered, rendered barren of sprouts; [the sun of] destiny

children.text: śoṣaṃ ninye ravir iva jalaṃ bhāgadheyārkabimbam || GoMk_5 ||
children.translated_text: dried it up like the sun dries water, with its garlands of fierce rays. // GoMk 5 //

children.text: rudraṃ naikakapālaśekharadharaṃ cakrāyudhaṃ vajriṇaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, wearer of many skulls as crown; the discus-armed one (<s>Viṣṇu</s>); the thunderbolt-bearer (<s>Indra</s>);

children.text: sraṣṭāraṃ makaradhvajaṃ girisutāputraṃ mayūrāsanam |
children.translated_text: the Creator (<s>Brahmā</s>); the fish-bannered one (<s>Kāma</s>); the son of the Mountain's daughter (<s>Kārttikeya</s>); the peacock-seated one (<s>Kārttikeya</s>);

children.text: gaṅgāṃ śaṅkhadalāvadātasalilāṃ tāṃ tāṃś ca devān asau
children.translated_text: the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with waters white as conch-shell petals; and those various gods —

children.text: putrārthī śaraṇaṃ yayau bahu punar dānaṃ dvijebhyo dadau || GoMk_6 ||
children.translated_text: desiring a son, he went to them for refuge, and also gave much in gifts to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // GoMk 6 //

children.text: yad yaj jano maṅgaladeśanābhir vratopavāsādhigataiś ca duḥkhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever people [seek] through auspicious rites and through the hardships of vows and fasting —
[lacuna] // GoMk 7 //
[lacuna]

children.text: putrārthasaṃsiddhinimagnabuddhir vikṣipya khedaṃ sa cakāra tāṃs tān || GoMk_8 ||
children.translated_text: With his mind immersed in the longing for the success of [obtaining] a son, casting aside despondency, he performed those various [rites]. // GoMk 8 //

children.text: evam anekaprakāraṃ kāyacetassor āyāsakāribhir api vratopavāsamaṅgalair yadā naiva kadā cit kāle 'sya putrā jīvino babhūvus tadaivam ativipule pragāḍhaśokāpagāmbhasi nimajjantaṃ kaś cit sādhupuruṣo 'bravīt |
children.translated_text: Thus, when through many kinds of vows, fasting, and auspicious rites — even though they wearied body and mind — no sons were ever born to him alive, then, as he was sinking in the vast and deep flood of grief, a certain virtuous man said to him:

children.text: karmāṇy evāvalambanti dehināṃ sarvasaṃpadaḥ |
children.translated_text: It is <s>karma</s> alone that supports all the fortunes of embodied beings;

children.text: bhūtānāṃ tuṅgaśṛṅgāc ca vinipāto na bhūtaye || GoMk_9 ||
children.translated_text: and the fall from a lofty peak does not lead to prosperity for creatures. // GoMk 9 //

children.text: saṃkleśaṃ bahavaḥ prāptāḥ putratṛṣṇārtabuddhinā [!] |
children.translated_text: Many have reached misery through a mind tormented by the thirst for a son;

children.text: na ca te 'dyāpi jīvanti tatra kiṃ parikhidyase || GoMk_10 ||
children.translated_text: yet they do not live even now — so why do you grieve over this? // GoMk 10 //

children.text: karmāṇi nirmucya kathaṃ bhavebhyaḥ svargaukasas tuṣṭivaśād iheyuḥ |
children.translated_text: How could heavenly beings, freed from their <s>karmas</s>, come here from their existences out of satisfaction?

children.text: ye yair vinā nātmabhavaṃ labhante te tair vinā janma kathaṃ bhajeran || GoMk_11 ||
children.translated_text: Those without whom they cannot obtain their own existence — how could they take birth without them? // GoMk 11 //

children.text: ye sāṃsārikanaikaduḥkhadahanajvālālatāliṅgitās
children.translated_text: Those who are embraced by the creepers of the flames of manifold sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) —

children.text: te vāñchanti narāmaroragasukhaṃ prāyeṇa dānādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: they desire the happiness of humans, immortals, and serpents, mostly through gifts and similar [merits];

children.text: tvaṃ kenāpi viḍambyase jaḍamatiḥ putrāśayonmattako
children.translated_text: but you, dull-witted, are being mocked by some [trickster], maddened by the desire for a son —

children.text: yas tvaṃ dyām adhigantum icchasi bṛhatsopānamālāśrayāt || GoMk_12 ||
children.translated_text: you who wish to ascend to heaven by means of a great series of stairways! // GoMk 12 //

children.text: vidhim aparam ahaṃ te bodhayāmi prasiddhyai
children.translated_text: I shall teach you another method for success;

children.text: tvam api ca kuru tāvat saṃprasiddhyai kadā cit |
children.translated_text: and you too should do it at some point for fulfillment:

children.text: yadi bhavati sutas te kanyakānāma tasya
children.translated_text: if a son is born to you, name him <s>Kanyakā</s> ("Maiden"),

children.text: sakalajanapade 'smin khyāpayasva prasiddhyai || GoMk_13 ||
children.translated_text: and proclaim it throughout this entire land for [its] establishment. // GoMk 13 //

children.text: atha tasya kālāntare gaganatalam aṃśumālīva svakiraṇanikarair virājamānaṃ svavaṃśalakṣmīḥ putraṃ janayāṃ babhūva | sa ca
children.translated_text: Then, after some time, his lineage-fortune produced a son, illuminating his family like the sun illuminating the sky with its multitude of rays. And he —

children.text: nirvāntāmalahemaśailaśikharapracchedagauradyutiḥ
children.translated_text: had a golden luster like the ridgecrest of a stainless gold mountain after cooling,

children.text: saṃpūrṇāmalacandramaṇḍalasamacchattrorubhāsvacchirāḥ |
children.translated_text: with a large, brilliant head like the canopy of a full, spotless moon-disc,

children.text: mattairāvaṇacārupuṣkarakaravyālambabāhudvayo
children.translated_text: with two arms dangling like the beautiful trunk of the intoxicated <s>Airāvaṇa</s> elephant,

children.text: bhinnendīvaraphullapattranicayaśyāmāruṇāntekṣaṇaḥ || GoMk_14 ||
children.translated_text: with eyes dark-reddish at the corners, like a mass of blooming split blue-lotus petals. // GoMk 14 //

children.text: bhūyaḥ kalpasahasrasaṃcitamahāpuṇyaprabhāvodbhavaiḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, with delightful auspicious marks, born from the power of great merit accumulated over thousands of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: pravyaktasphuritendracāparuciraiḥ prahlādibhir lakṣaṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: beautiful as brightly shining rainbows,

children.text: mūrtis tasya rarāja meruśikharād dhemaṃ yathā bhūcyutaṃ
children.translated_text: his body blazed like gold fallen from the peak of <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: prodgīrṇasvamayūkhajālajaṭilai ratnāṅkurair veṣṭitam || GoMk_15 ||
children.translated_text: encrusted with jewel-buds bristling with their own radiated nets of rays. // GoMk 15 //

children.text: bhramaracamarapaṅktiśyāmakeśābhirāmaṃ
children.translated_text: Charming with hair dark as rows of swarming black bees,
