children.text: samavipulalalāṭaṃ śrīmaduttuṅganāsam |
children.translated_text: with a smooth, broad forehead and a splendid, prominent nose —

children.text: tanayam uditacetā maitrakanyābhidhānaṃ
children.translated_text: his joyous father proclaimed his son, named <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>,

children.text: daśadivasapareṇa khyāpayām āsa loke || GoMk_16 ||
children.translated_text: to the world after ten days. // GoMk 16 //

children.text: śarīriṇāṃ vṛddhikaraiḥ samṛddhair viśeṣayuktair vividhānnapānaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With abundant, excellent, and special varieties of food and drink that nourish the body,

children.text: sudhāvadātaiḥ sphuṭacandrapādaiḥ payodhiveleva yayau samṛddhim || GoMk_17 ||
children.translated_text: white as ambrosia and bright as clear moonbeams, he grew in prosperity like the ocean-shore. // GoMk 17 //

children.text: dhātrībhiḥ sa samunnītaḥ kṣīraiś ca sarpimaṇḍakaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Raised by his nurses, nourished with milk and clarified butter,

children.text: pupoṣa sundaraṃ dehaṃ hradastham iva paṅkajam || GoMk_18 ||
children.translated_text: he grew a beautiful body, like a lotus in a pond. // GoMk 18 //

children.text: atha tasya pitā mitraḥ sārthavāho vaṇigjanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then his father <s>Mitra</s>, the caravan-leader, with merchant folk,

children.text: dravyair vahanam āropya jagāhe toyadhiṃ mudā || GoMk_19 ||
children.translated_text: loading goods onto a vessel, joyfully entered the ocean. // GoMk 19 //

children.text: timiṅgilakṣobhavivardhitormimahodadhau mīnavipannapātre |
children.translated_text: When his father perished in the great ocean, whose waves were swollen by the thrashing of <s>timiṅgila</s> (great sea-monsters), his ship lost to the fish —

children.text: pitur vyatīte jananīṃ jagāda cakāra kiṃ karma pitā mameti || GoMk_20 ||
children.translated_text: he asked his mother: "What trade did my father practice?" // GoMk 20 //

children.text: tato 'sya jananī pativiyogaśokaglapitahṛdayā cintām āpede |
children.translated_text: Then his mother, her heart withered by grief at being separated from her husband, fell into anxiety:

children.text: āśāpāśaśatākṛṣṭo jano mṛtyuṃ na paśyati |
children.translated_text: "Dragged by hundreds of nooses of hope, people do not see death,

children.text: viṣayāsvādakṛpaṇo vāraṇa iva bandhanam || GoMk_21 ||
children.translated_text: wretched in their tasting of sensual pleasures, like an elephant [not seeing] its trap. // GoMk 21 //

children.text: yady api kathayiṣyāmi pitaraṃ yānapātrikam |
children.translated_text: Even if I tell him that his father was a ship-owner,

children.text: eṣo 'pi mama mandāyā nāśam eṣyati toyadhau || GoMk_22 ||
children.translated_text: this [son] of wretched me will also meet his end in the ocean. // GoMk 22 //

children.text: yāvac cāyaṃ janapadam imaṃ tasya vṛttiṃ na bhūtāṃ
children.translated_text: As long as this [son of mine] does not ask anyone in this land about his [father's] true occupation,

children.text: pṛcchaty asmai kathayati na vā sarva evaiṣa lokaḥ |
children.translated_text: and as long as no one in this world tells him —

children.text: tāvad yuktaṃ mama sutam imaṃ mṛtyuvaktrāntarālaṃ
children.translated_text: so long is it proper for me to prevent this son of mine from [entering] the jaws of death,

children.text: nānāduḥkhavyasanagahanaṃ vyādhisaktaṃ niṣeddhum || GoMk_23 ||
children.translated_text: that thicket of manifold sufferings and calamities, caught by disease. // GoMk 23 //

children.text: paro 'pi yaḥ sādhujanānujuṣṭaṃ vihāya mārgaṃ śrayate vimārgam |
children.translated_text: Even a stranger who abandons the path followed by the virtuous and resorts to a wrong path

children.text: nivāraṇīyaḥ sa matāj janena prayatnataḥ kiṃ punar eva putraḥ || GoMk_24 ||
children.translated_text: should be restrained carefully by a wise person — how much more so one's own son! // GoMk 24 //"

children.text: tato janāni kathayāṃ cakre |
children.translated_text: Then she told the people [of the city]:

children.text: putrakaukarikatvena pitā te mām apūpuṣat |
children.translated_text: "Your father maintained me through the trade of a confectioner;

children.text: yady ahaṃ sukhitā kāryā kārayaukarikāpaṇam || GoMk_25 ||
children.translated_text: if I am to be made happy, let him set up a confectioner's shop." // GoMk 25 //

children.text: atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvo mātur vacanaṃ kusumamālām iva śirasā samabhivadyānyasminn ahani [!] aukarikāpaṇaṃ prasasāra |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, honoring his mother's words like a garland of flowers placed upon his head, on the very next day set up a confectioner's shop.

children.text: puṇyasaṃbhāramahatas tasya sattvadayāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: For that great-souled one, possessed of immense accumulated merit and compassion for beings,

children.text: prathame 'hani saṃpannaṃ catuṣkārṣāpaṇaṃ dhanam ||
children.translated_text: on the very first day, a wealth of four <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> was earned.

children.text: svagarbhasaṃdhāraṇaduḥkhitāyai dadau sa tasyai mudito jananyai |
children.translated_text: He joyfully gave it to that mother of his, who had suffered in bearing him in her womb,

children.text: daridraduḥkhavyasanacchidāyai dhanaṃ mahābhogaphalaprasūtyai || GoMk_27 ||
children.translated_text: wealth productive of great enjoyment, to cut through the misery of poverty and destitution. // GoMk 27 //

children.text: atha ye tasmin puravare ciraṃtanā aukarikās te tasya tam abhivardhamānaṃ krayavikrayalokam aviṣamavyavahāranītyā prakṛtipremapeśalatayā cāvarjitamanasaṃ tasmin mahāsattve vyavahārārtham āpatantam avalokya taṃ tasmāt karmaṇo vinivartanārtham āhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Now the long-established confectioners of that finest city, seeing that great-souled one rushing toward their trade with a growing market of buying and selling, his mind won over by his naturally fair and equitable business practices and his innate charm of affection — in order to turn him away from that occupation, they said to him:

children.text: gāndhikāpaṇikaḥ śreṣṭhī pitā te 'smin pure purā |
children.translated_text: "Your father was a perfumer and merchant, a <s>śreṣṭhin</s> (guild-chief) in this city formerly;

children.text: sa tvaṃ tāṃ vṛttim ujjhitvā śrayase 'nyāṃ kayā dhiyā || GoMk_28 ||
children.translated_text: abandoning that occupation, by what reasoning do you resort to another?" // GoMk 28 //

children.text: atha bodhisattvas tām api jīvikām apahāya gāndhikāpaṇaṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, abandoning even that livelihood, set up a perfumer's shop.

children.text: yasminn eva dine cakre sa sādhur gāndhikāpaṇam |
children.translated_text: On the very day that virtuous one set up the perfumer's shop,

children.text: kārṣāpaṇāṣṭakaṃ tasya tasminn evopapadyate || GoMk_29 ||
children.translated_text: eight <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> came to him on that very day. // GoMk 29 //

children.text: tam [!] api mātre pratipāditavān | atha gāndhikāpaṇikāḥ puruṣāḥ sametyāgatya ca taṃ mahāsattvaṃ vicchandayām āsuḥ |
children.translated_text: He gave those too to his mother. Then the perfumer-merchants, coming together and approaching, sought to dissuade that great-souled one:

children.text: gāndhāpaṇaṃ klībajanābhipannaṃ pitā na vaimadyapure cakāra |
children.translated_text: "Your father did not practice perfume-selling, [a trade] resorted to by timid people, in the city of <s>Vaimadya</s>;

children.text: tatraiva hairaṇyikatāṃ sa kṛtvā dhanāni bhūyāṃsi samāpa sādho || GoMk_30 ||
children.translated_text: rather, practicing the goldsmith's trade there, he acquired much greater wealth, O virtuous one." // GoMk 30 //

children.text: atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvas tām api jīvikām apahāya hairaṇyikāpaṇaṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, abandoning even that livelihood, set up a goldsmith's shop.

children.text: tayāpi tasmin vyavahāranītyā hairaṇyikāṃs tān abhibhūya sarvān |
children.translated_text: By that business practice too, surpassing all those goldsmiths,

children.text: lebhe dine sa prathame mahārhaḥ kārṣāpaṇān ṣoḍaśa tān dadau ca || GoMk_31 ||
children.translated_text: on the first day that worthy one earned sixteen <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> and gave them [to his mother]. // GoMk 31 //

children.text: dine dvitīye dvātriṃśatkārṣāpaṇān upārjya saḥ |
children.translated_text: On the second day, having earned thirty-two <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>,

children.text: dakṣiṇīyaviśeṣāya [!] mātre tān api dattavān || GoMk_32 ||
children.translated_text: he gave those too to his mother, as a special offering of merit. // GoMk 32 //

children.text: atha hairaṇyikāpaṇikāḥ puruṣāḥ sametyāgatya ca taṃ tasmāt karmaṇo vinivartanārtham āhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the goldsmith-merchants, coming together and approaching, in order to turn him away from that occupation, said to him:

children.text: śaraccandrāṃśudhavale labdhvā janma kule katham |
children.translated_text: "Having been born in a family white as autumn moonbeams, how

children.text: kṛpaṇāṃ jīvikāhetor vṛttim āśrayate bhavān || GoMk_33 ||
children.translated_text: can you resort to a wretched livelihood for the sake of a living?" // GoMk 33 //

children.text: parbhañjanoddhūtaśikhākarāle hutāśane visphuritasphuliṅge |
children.translated_text: "In a fire terrible with crests fanned by storms, with sparks flying —

children.text: vivartitaṃ ślāghyam ativa puṃsāṃ na tu svavṛtteś cyavanaṃ pravṛttam || GoMk_34 ||
children.translated_text: being steadfast is indeed praiseworthy for men, but falling from one's [proper] conduct is not commendable. // GoMk 34 //

children.text: mahoragaśvāsavighūrṇitograis taraṅgabhaṅgair viṣamān payodhīn |
children.translated_text: Your father, plunging into dangerous oceans with terrible waves churned by the breath of great sea-serpents,

children.text: agādhapātālavilagnamūlān pitā vigāhyārjitavān dhanaṃ te || GoMk_35 ||
children.translated_text: whose foundations were rooted in the fathomless netherworld, earned your wealth. // GoMk 35 //

children.text: yad āśritaṃ karma janānuvartinā tvayā vidagdhena dhanepsunādhunā |
children.translated_text: Having resorted to the trade of a people-following [merchant], you who are clever and desirous of wealth now —

children.text: kathaṃ na saṃprāpsyasi bhāgyasaṃpadaṃ pitur vyatīte 'pi viśālinīṃ śriyam || GoMk_36 ||
children.translated_text: how shall you not attain the fortune of destiny, the expansive prosperity, even though your father has passed away? // GoMk 36 //

children.text: vitteśvaro 'py arthavibhūtivistarair nāsāsadarthā vibabhāra yasya |
children.translated_text: He whose spreading abundance of wealth even <s>Kubera</s>, the lord of riches, could not match in its purposes —

children.text: tasyā [!] mahendrāmalatulyakīrteḥ sūnuḥ kathaṃ tvaṃ na bibharṣi lajjām || GoMk_37 ||
children.translated_text: being the son of that one, whose fame was pure as great <s>Indra</s>'s — how do you not feel shame?" // GoMk 37 //

children.text: ye mṛtyuṃ gaṇayanti naiva vipadi grāmaṃ bhajante na ye
children.translated_text: "Those who do not reckon death even in calamity, who do not cling to home,

children.text: gehe bandhuṣu sūnuṣu vyapagatasnehātmanodyoginaḥ |
children.translated_text: who are free from attachment to kin and sons, self-reliant and enterprising —

children.text: te tīrtvā jaladhīn agādhasalilān āvartabhīmān budhāḥ
children.translated_text: those wise ones, having crossed the oceans of fathomless waters, fearsome with whirlpools,

children.text: prāpyārthān gajadantabhaṅgasitayā cinvanti kīrtyā jagat || GoMk_38 ||
children.translated_text: having obtained wealth, they gather fame throughout the world, white as the breaking of an elephant's tusk. [GoMk 38]

children.text: atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvas tebhyo 'py tathānuguṇinīṃ kathām avadhārya samudrāvataraṇakṛtavyavasāyo mātaram upasṛtyovāca | amba sārthavāhaḥ kilāsmākaṃ pitā purā tad anujñāṃ prayaccha yad aham api mahāsamudram avatariṣyāmīti | sā pūrvam eva bhartṛmaraṇaduḥkhena vigatajīvitāśā svasya tanayasya tenāsaṃlakṣitadāruṇena viyogaśokaśastreṇa bhṛśataraṃ pravidāryamāṇahṛdayā svatanayam āha |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, having heard from them too a discourse suited [to his purpose], resolved to venture upon the ocean, and approaching his mother, said: "Mother, our father was a caravan-leader, they say. Therefore, grant me permission, for I too shall descend into the great ocean." She, who had already lost her will to live due to the grief of her husband's death, her heart being pierced all the more by the weapon of separation-grief — unperceived as cruel by her son — said to her son:

children.text: vatsa kena tavākhyātaṃ vinākāraṇaśatruṇā |
children.translated_text: "Child, who has told you — [some] causeless enemy?

children.text: jīvitaṃ kasya te 'niṣṭaṃ tvayā krīḍāṃ karoti kaḥ || GoMk_39 ||
children.translated_text: Whose life does not displease you? Who is playing games with you? [GoMk 39]

children.text: daivāt kathaṃ cit saṃprāptaṃ cakṣur ekaṃ tvam adya me |
children.translated_text: By fate, somehow obtained, you are now my single eye.

children.text: putraka kleśabhāginyā mṛtyunā hriyase 'dhunā || GoMk_40 ||
children.translated_text: Little son, you are now being seized by Death from me, a partner in affliction. [GoMk 40]

children.text: na yāvad ekaṃ mama duḥkhaśalyaṃ prayāti nāśaṃ pravidārya śokam |
children.translated_text: Before even one thorn of my grief reaches its end, tearing open my sorrow,

children.text: kathaṃ nu tasyopari me dvitīyaṃ nipātyate pāpamayair amitraiḥ || GoMk_41 ||
children.translated_text: how is a second one cast upon it by my wicked enemies? [GoMk 41]

children.text: yeṣāṃ ceto vividhavirasāyāsaduḥkhāprakampyaṃ
children.translated_text: Those whose hearts are unshaken by the varied, unpleasant hardships and sufferings,

children.text: yaiḥ saṃtyaktaṃ kṛpaṇahṛdayair jīvitaṃ bhogalubdhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: who, with pitiable hearts and greedy for enjoyments, have abandoned [even] life —

children.text: te saṃtyaktvā [!] nayanagalitāśrupravāhārdravaktrān
children.translated_text: those fools, abandoning their kinsmen whose faces are wet with streaming tears flowing from their eyes,

children.text: bandhūn ajñā makaranilaye mṛtyave yānti nāśam || GoMk_42 ||
children.translated_text: go to destruction in the abode of sea-monsters, to Death. [GoMk 42]

children.text: tan mām anāthāṃ pratipālanīyāṃ tvajjīvitāśaikanibandhajīvām |
children.translated_text: How can you be resolved to depart, abandoning me — helpless, deserving protection,

children.text: saṃtyajya yātuṃ katham udyamas te mā sā kathā mānavaro madīyam || GoMk_43 ||
children.translated_text: living only by the bond of hope in your life? Let not that be spoken of, O best of men, my [dear]! [GoMk 43]

children.text: svaprāṇasaṃdehakarīm avasthāṃ praviśya naikāntasukhaṃ prasādhyam |
children.translated_text: Having entered a situation that endangers one's own life, the prosperity of merchants, which is not exclusively pleasurable,

children.text: saṃpattayo yena vaṇigjanasya tato 'ham evaṃ suta vārayāmi || GoMk_44 ||
children.translated_text: is the reason why I thus restrain you, O son. [GoMk 44]

children.text: sa tasyā hitārthaṃ madhurāṇy api vacanakusumāni tṛṇam ivāvadhūya sapragalbhatayā samavalambitavikatthāśobhaṃ kiṃ cid īdṛśaṃ pratyāha |
children.translated_text: He, shaking off her sweet flower-words as if they were grass, with a boldness that bore the beauty of boasting, replied something like this:

children.text: varaṃ naiva tu jāyeran ye jātā nirdhanā janāḥ |
children.translated_text: "Better that those people who are born destitute should never have been born at all.

children.text: jātasya yadi duḥkhāni varaṃ mṛtyur na jīvitam || GoMk_45 ||
children.translated_text: If suffering [comes] to one who is born, death is better than life. [GoMk 45]

children.text: āśayā gṛham āgatya dīnadīnās tapasvinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Coming to my home with hope, the wretched, utterly wretched, pitiable [people],

children.text: arthino mama pāpasya yānti niśvasya durmanāḥ [!] || GoMk_46 ||
children.translated_text: the needy — they depart from me, the sinful one, sighing and downcast. [GoMk 46]

children.text: ye śaktihīnā vibhavārjanādau te dehino duḥkhaśataṃ sahante |
children.translated_text: Those beings who lack the power to earn wealth endure a hundred sufferings.

children.text: lokaṃ punar duḥkhaśatopataptaṃ draṣṭuṃ na śaknomi cirāyamāṇaḥ || GoMk_47 ||
children.translated_text: And I cannot bear to see the world, afflicted with a hundred sufferings, for a long time. [GoMk 47]

children.text: tasmād vilaṅghāmi vacas tavedaṃ yāsyāmi taṃ tvaṃ prajahīhi śokam |
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall transgress this word of yours — I shall go. You, put aside your grief!

children.text: tatraiva yāyāṃ nidhanaṃ samudre chinnaṃ mayā vā vyasanaṃ janasya || GoMk_48 ||
children.translated_text: Either I shall meet my end in that very ocean, or I shall cut through the misery of the people." [GoMk 48]

children.text: atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvo mātaram apramāṇīkṛtya nirgatya gṛhād vārāṇasyāṃ puryām ātmānaṃ sārthavāham ity udghoṣayām āsa |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, disregarding his mother, went forth from the house and in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> proclaimed himself as a caravan-leader:

children.text: asyām eva purā puraṃdarapurīpraspardhipuryāṃ vaṇiṅ
children.translated_text: "In this very city, formerly rivaling the city of <s>Purandara</s> (Indra), there was a merchant

children.text: mitro nāma babhūva yaḥ suranaraprakhyātakīrtidhvajaḥ |
children.translated_text: named <s>Mitra</s>, whose banner of fame was renowned among gods and men.

children.text: putras tasya mahāsamudram acirād yāsyaty amuṣmin dine
children.translated_text: His son will soon descend into the great ocean on this very day.

children.text: yātuṃ ye vaṇijaḥ kṛtopakaraṇās te santu sajjā iti || GoMk_49 ||
children.translated_text: Those merchants who have prepared their equipment and wish to go — let them be ready!" [GoMk 49]

children.text: atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvo vividhopakaraṇasaṃbhārasādhanānāṃ samāgṛhītapuṇyāhaprasthānabhadrāṇām upahṛtamaṅgalavidhānānāṃ vaṇijāṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ kṛtaparivāraḥ prasasāra | mātā cainaṃ gacchatīti śrutvāha | mamaikaputraka kva yāsyasīti karuṇakaruṇākranditamātraparāyaṇā komalavimalakamalavilāsālasābhyāṃ pāṇikamalābhyāṃ rucirakanakaghaṭitaghaṭavikaṭapayodharavarorubhāsuram uraḥ pragāḍham abhitāḍayati | bāṣpasaliladhārāparaṃparodbhavoparudhyamānakaṇṭhī [!] anilabalākulitagalitasajalajaladapaṭalāvalīmalinakeśapāśā satvaratvaram abhigamya maitrakanyakasya bodhisattvasya pādayoḥ pariṣvajyaivam āha | mā māṃ putraka parityajya yāsīti |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, accompanied by five hundred merchants who had gathered various provisions and supplies, who had received the auspicious rites of departure on a day declared propitious, and for whom auspicious ceremonies had been performed, set forth. And his mother, hearing that he was departing, said: "My only son, where will you go?" — devoted solely to piteous, piteous wailing, with her pair of lotus-hands, delicate, pure, and languidly graceful like lotuses, she struck hard upon her chest, beautiful and radiant with breasts like shapely pots set with lovely gold. Her throat choked by the succession of streaming tear-waters, her mass of hair disheveled and darkened like a row of cloud-curtains loosened and set drifting by the force of the wind, she swiftly, hastily approached and, embracing the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, spoke thus: "Do not go, abandoning me, little son!"

children.text: anartharāgagrahamūḍhabuddhayo narā hi paśyanti na kevalaṃ hitam |
children.translated_text: "People whose minds are deluded by the grip of passion for harmful things do not see what is truly beneficial.

children.text: satāṃ hitādhānavidhānacetasāṃ giro 'pi śṛṇvanti na bhūtavādinām || GoMk_50 ||
children.translated_text: They do not even hear the words of the virtuous, who speak the truth and whose minds are intent upon establishing what is beneficial." [GoMk 50]

children.text: maitrakanyako 'pi
children.translated_text: And <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>,

children.text: dharaṇi
tala
nimagnāṃ mātaraṃ śokavaśyāṃ
children.translated_text: [seeing] his mother fallen to the ground, overcome by grief,

children.text: śirasi kupitacittaḥ pādavajreṇa hatvā |
children.translated_text: struck her on the head with his foot-thunderbolt, his mind enraged.

children.text: muhur upacitaśokaḥ karmaṇā preryamāṇas
children.translated_text: Repeatedly accumulating grief, driven by <s>karma</s>,

children.text: tvaritamatir abhūt – saṃprayātuṃ vaṇigbhiḥ || GoMk_51 ||
children.translated_text: with hastened mind, he departed with the merchants. [GoMk 51]
upon the ground

children.text: tataḥ sā mātā samutthāyāha | putraka
children.translated_text: Then that mother, rising up, said: "Little son —

children.text: mayi gamananivṛttiṃ kartum abhyudyatāyāṃ
children.translated_text: when I endeavored to prevent your going,

children.text: yad upacitam apuṇyaṃ macchirastāḍanāt te |
children.translated_text: the demerit that you have accumulated by striking my head —

children.text: vyasanaphalam anantaṃ mā tu bhūt karmaṇo 'sya
children.translated_text: may the fruit of endless misery not come from this deed of yours!

children.text: punar api guruvākyaṃ mātigāḥ svapnato 'pi || GoMk_52 ||
children.translated_text: And never again, even in a dream, transgress the word of an elder!" [GoMk 52]

children.text: atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvo vividhavihārāyatanaparvatopavanagahvarasarittaḍāgārāmaramaṇīyatarān anekanagaranigamakarvaṭagrāmādīn anuvicaran krameṇa samudratīraṃ saṃprāpya sajjīkṛtayānapātro bhujagapativadanavisṛtaśvasanacapalānilabalavilulitavipulavimalasalilam aruṇataruṇakiraṇanikararucirapadmarāgapuñjaprabhārāgarañjitormimālājalam asurasvarasamasurasureśvarakarodarasphuritahutavahaśikhāvalīkarālavajrapatanabhayanilīnadharaṇīdharaśikharaparāhatajaloddhatottuṅgataraṅgabhaṅgaraudraṃ samudram avatatāra |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, traveling through various charming monasteries, mountain retreat-groves, caves, rivers, lakes, gardens, and numerous cities, towns, hamlets, and villages, gradually reached the seashore. Having prepared his vessel, he entered the great ocean — whose vast, pure waters were made restless by the swift wind of the breath released from the mouth of the serpent-king, whose garland of waves was colored by the radiance of heaps of ruby-lustre, beautiful with clusters of ruddy young rays, [an ocean] terrifying with the raging crash of towering wave-crests, dashed against the peaks of submerged mountains that had hidden themselves in fear of the fall of thunderbolts flickering with rows of fire-flames shooting from the belly of the hand of the lord of gods and demons, whose sound was like that of demons and gods —

children.text: mahānilotkṣiptataraṅgabhaṅgaiḥ samullasadbhiḥ kham ivotpatantam |
children.translated_text: Rising as if flying into the sky with the crests of waves tossed up by the great wind,

children.text: saritsahasrāmburayapravāhair bhujair vilāsair iva gṛhyamāṇam || GoMk_53 ||
children.translated_text: as if being embraced with playful arms by the streams of a thousand rivers' waters. [GoMk 53]

children.text: prakṣubdhaśīrṣoragabhīmabhogavyāvartitodvartitatoyarāśim |
children.translated_text: A mass of water churned and thrown upward by the terrible coils of serpents with agitated hoods,

children.text: tanmurdhni ratnodgataraśmipuñjaṃ jvālākalāpocchuritormicakram || GoMk_54 ||
children.translated_text: with a circle of waves erupting in clusters of flame-crests from the rays of gems [emerging] from their heads. [GoMk 54]

children.text: ahipativadanād vimuktatīvrajvalitaviṣānaladāhabhīmaśaṅkham |
children.translated_text: With conchs made fearsome by the suspicion of the burning of fierce blazing poison-fire released from the mouth of the serpent-king,

children.text: timinakhakuliśāgradāritādriṃ tadacalapādahatāmbumīnavṛndam || GoMk_55 ||
children.translated_text: with mountains split by the points of the diamond-claws of the <s>timingila</s> fish, with schools of fish struck by the feet of that immovable [ocean]. [GoMk 55]

children.text: tuṅgataraṅgasamudgatatīraṃ tīranilīnakalasvanahaṃsam |
children.translated_text: Its shore emerging from towering waves, with melodious swans sheltering at the shore,

children.text: haṃsanakhakṣatadāruṇamīnaṃ mīnavivartitakampitavelam || GoMk_56 ||
children.translated_text: with fish terribly wounded by the claws of swans, with the coastline trembling from the turning of fish. [GoMk 56]

children.text: ratnalatāvṛtabhāsuraśaṅkhaṃ śaṅkhasitendugabhastivivṛddham |
children.translated_text: With radiant conches wreathed in gem-creepers, swelling with the white moonbeam-rays of conches,

children.text: vṛddhabhujaṃgamahāhavaraudraṃ raudramahāmakarāhatacakram || GoMk_57 ||
children.translated_text: terrible with the great battle of aged serpents, its expanse struck by great, terrifying crocodiles. [GoMk 57]

children.text: khagapatisavilāsapāṇivajraṃ prahatavipāṭitadṛṣṭimūlarandhram |
children.translated_text: With the playful hand-thunderbolt of <s>Khagapati</s> (Garuḍa) splitting the cavities at the root of [serpents'] eyes,

children.text: pramuditajaladantidantakoṭipramathitanaikavilāsakalpavṛkṣam || GoMk_58 ||
children.translated_text: with the tips of the tusks of delighted cloud-elephants churning the many playful wish-fulfilling trees. [GoMk 58]

children.text: tad eva sa saṃlakṣya tīraparyantarekhaṃ prakaṭavikaṭāvartagartodarabhramadbhramitajhaṣabhujagakulamaṇḍalaṃ naikavicitrādbhutāścaryam atiśayam ambhasām ālayam atikramatas tasya dharaṇīdharaśikharavipulātmabhāvasya makarakaripater vivartamānasya samutthitair urvīdharākāradāruṇaiḥ pramuktakalakalārāvaraudrair mahadbhiḥ salilanivahair utpīḍyamānaṃ tad yānapātraṃ maraṇabhayaviṣādabhraśyamānagātrair dīnaruditākranditamātraparāyaṇaiḥ saṃyānapātrakaiḥ saha sahasaiva salilanidher adhaḥ praveṣṭum ārabdham |
children.translated_text: Observing that very [ocean] up to the line of the shore — with circles of fish and serpent families spinning and whirling in the belly of the manifest, gaping vortex-pits — that marvelous, wonderful, extraordinary abode of waters — as he was crossing it, from a whale-elephant-lord turning about with a nature as vast as a mountain peak, there arose waves terrible like mountains, releasing a tumultuous roar, great volumes of water that began to crush the vessel. Together with the fellow travelers whose limbs were trembling with the despair and fear of death, devoted solely to piteous crying and wailing, the vessel suddenly began to sink below the surface of the ocean.

children.text: urvīdharākārataraṅgatuṅgair ugrair yugāntānilacaṇḍavegaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By fierce waves towering like mountains, with the furious velocity of end-of-age winds,

children.text: tad yānapātraṃ jaladher jalaughair āsphālyamānaṃ vidadāra madhye || GoMk_59 ||
children.translated_text: the vessel, battered by the water-floods of the ocean, split apart in the middle. [GoMk 59]

children.text: daṃṣṭrākarāle jhaṣavaktrarandhre kaś cin mamārārtaravas tapasvī |
children.translated_text: Some wretched ones died with cries of anguish in the jaws of fish, gaping like fangs.

children.text: ke cij jalodgāraniruddhakaṇṭhā jagmur nirucchvāsagiro vyasutvam || GoMk_60 ||
children.translated_text: Some, their throats blocked by the gushing water, met their death breathless and voiceless. [GoMk 60]

children.text: gatvāpi ke cit phalakair mahadbhir ambhonidhes tīram avekṣamāṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Some, though reaching great planks, gazing toward the shore of the ocean,

children.text: dūrāmbusaṃtānapariśramārtās trāsākulā nedur udīrṇanādāḥ || GoMk_61 ||
children.translated_text: exhausted by the effort of [swimming through] the far-stretching water, cried out in loud voices, overwhelmed with terror. [GoMk 61]

children.text: atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvas tena mahatā vyasanopanipātenāpy anāpatitabhayaviṣādadainyāyāsamanāḥ samavalambya mahad dhairyaparākramaṃ sasaṃbhramaṃ phalakam ādāya prasasāra |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, even by that great onset of calamity, his mind unassailed by fear, despair, wretchedness, or weariness, having seized upon great courage and valor, hastily took hold of a plank and set forth.

children.text: tato 'sau samapavanagamanajavajanitasavilāsagatibhiḥ salilaplavair itas tataḥ samākṣipyamāṇo nirāhāratayā ca parimlāyamānanayanavadanakamalaś cānyair bahubhir ahorātrair yathā kathaṃ cit tasya duravagāhasalilasya mahārṇavasya dakṣiṇaṃ tīradeśam āsasāda |
children.translated_text: Then, being tossed here and there by the waves of the water, moving with the speed of a level wind with playful gait, and with the lotus of his face and eyes wilting from lack of food, after many more days and nights, he somehow reached the southern shore of that great ocean of unfathomable waters.

children.text: tīrtvā tam ambhonidhim apragādham āsādya tīraṃ phalakaṃ mumoca |
children.translated_text: Having crossed that fathomless ocean and reached the shore, he released the plank.

children.text: saṃsmṛtya mātur vacanaṃ sa pāṇau vyāsajya mūrdhānam idaṃ jagāda || GoMk_62 ||
children.translated_text: Remembering his mother's words, placing his hand upon his head, he spoke thus: [GoMk 62]

children.text: śṛṇvanti ye nātmahitaṃ gurūṇāṃ vākyaṃ hitārthodayakāryabhadram |
children.translated_text: "Those who do not hear the beneficial words of their elders — words that are blessedly productive of welfare —

children.text: teṣām imāni vyasanāni puṃsāṃ māyāvahanti prabhavanti mūrdhni || GoMk_63 ||
children.translated_text: for those men, these calamities arise [and] fall deceptively upon their heads. [GoMk 63]

children.text: tair eva naikavyasanapradasya toyendubimbasthitabhaṅgurasya |
children.translated_text: But by those wise ones who honor the words of their elders,

children.text: prāptaṃ phalaṃ janmataroḥ sudhībhir ye mānayantīha giro gurūṇām || GoMk_64 ||
children.translated_text: the fruit of the tree of birth — fragile as the reflection of the moon in water, productive of manifold calamities — has been obtained. [GoMk 64]

children.text: mātur hitāyaiva sadodyatāyāḥ prollaṅghya vākyaṃ mama duṣkṛtasya |
children.translated_text: Having transgressed the words of my mother, who was always striving for my welfare,

children.text: puṣpaṃ yad īdṛg bharapāpadāruṇaṃ prāntaṃ gamiṣyāmi kadā phalasya || GoMk_65 ||
children.translated_text: this terrible flower of my sin, heavy with evil — when shall I reach the end of its fruit? [GoMk 65]

children.text: hutavahahatalekhātyantaparyantaraudraṃ
children.translated_text: Extremely terrible at its uttermost edge with lines of blazing fire,

children.text: gaganaugraṃ vismayatyantavajram |
children.translated_text: fierce in the sky, astonishing with its utter thunderbolt,

children.text: guruśirasi dadhānaḥ pādavajraṃ khalo 'haṃ
children.translated_text: I, the wretch, having placed the thunderbolt of my foot upon my elder's head —

children.text: katham avanividāryaśvabhrarandhre na lagnaḥ || GoMk_66 ||
children.translated_text: how am I not stuck in the pit-hole that splits the earth? [GoMk 66]

children.text: ye santo hitavādināṃ sphuṭadhiyāṃ saṃpādayante giraḥ
children.translated_text: Those good people who fulfill the words of the clear-minded well-wishers

children.text: śreyas te samavāpnuvanti niyataṃ kravyādapuryāṃ yathā |
children.translated_text: surely attain welfare, even in the city of flesh-eaters (hell).

children.text: ye tūtsṛjya mahārthasāradayitāṃ vācaṃ śrayante 'nyathā
children.translated_text: But those who, casting aside the beloved speech rich in great meaning, resort to other ways —

children.text: dustare vyasanodadhau nipatitāḥ śocanti te 'haṃ yathā || GoMk_67 ||
children.translated_text: fallen into the ocean of calamity, hard to cross, they grieve — as I do. [GoMk 67]

children.text: tato 'sau krameṇa khadiravaṭasaralaniculabakulatamālatālanālikeśaradrumavanagahanaṃ pravaravāraṇavarāhacamaraśarabhaśambaramahiṣaviṣāṇakarṣaṇapatitamathitavividhamālutālatājāladuḥsaṃcaraṃ kva cit kṣubhitakesarininādabhayacakitavanacarakulākīrṇacaraṇaṃ kathaṃ cid api śabaramanujajanacaraṇākṣuṇṇaparyantam anucaran kva cit sthitvaivam āha |
children.translated_text: Then he, gradually wandering through dense forests of acacia, banyan, sal, <s>nicula</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>tamāla</s>, palm, coconut, and <s>śara</s> (reed) trees — impassable due to the tangled nets of various <s>mālutā</s> and <s>tālā</s> creepers fallen, broken, and crushed by the rubbing and dragging of the tusks and horns of excellent elephants, boars, yaks, <s>śarabha</s>, <s>śambara</s> (deer), and buffalo — where the feet of forest-dwellers were in disarray, startled by the fearsome roar of agitated lions — [forests] whose edges were barely trodden by the feet of Śabara forest-people — pausing somewhere, he spoke thus:

children.text: ete dāḍimapuṣpalohitamukhāḥ pronmuktakolāhalā
children.translated_text: "These fearless tree-monkeys with faces red as pomegranate flowers, releasing clamor,

children.text: hāsādarśitadantapaṅktivirasāḥ śākhāmṛgā nirbhayāḥ |
children.translated_text: disagreeable with their rows of teeth displayed in laughter,

children.text: sarpān bhīmaviṣānalasphuradurujvālākarālasphuṭān
children.translated_text: having killed serpents blazing with fierce venom-fire, terrible with clearly flickering flames,

children.text: hatvā pāṇitālaiḥ prayānti vivaśāḥ phutkārabhītāḥ punaḥ || GoMk_68 ||
children.translated_text: with slaps of their palms, go forth — yet return again, helpless, frightened by [the serpents'] hissing. [GoMk 68]

children.text: ramye kuṅkumaśākhinām aviralacchāyākuthāśītale
children.translated_text: In the pleasant coolness of the dense shade of saffron trees, like canopies,

children.text: mūle komalanīlaśādvalavati pravyaktapuṣpotkare |
children.translated_text: at the base where there is soft blue-green grass and conspicuous flower-heaps,

children.text: vaṃśais tālaravaiḥ sagītamadhuraiḥ pracchedasaṃpādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: with bamboo sounds and the music of palm-leaf [instruments], sweet with song, producing rhythmic beats —

children.text: saṃgītāhitacetasaḥ pramuditā gāyanty amī kinnarāḥ || GoMk_69 ||
children.translated_text: these <s>Kinnaras</s>, their minds charmed by music, sing joyfully. [GoMk 69]

children.text: tato nātidūram atisṛtya mahīdharavarākāraṃ parvataṃ dadarśa |
children.translated_text: Then, having traveled not too far, he beheld a mountain resembling the best of earth-holders (a great peak).

children.text: kva cid ugrataracārumaṇiprabhayā surabhīkṛtabhīmaguhāvivaram |
children.translated_text: Somewhere, with the radiance of exceedingly beautiful gems, perfuming the openings of its fearsome caves.

children.text: kva cid uddhatakinnaragītaravaṃ pratibuddhasasaṃbhramanāgakulam || GoMk_70 ||
children.translated_text: somewhere resounding with the music of <s>Kinnaras</s>, with clans of <s>Nāgas</s> stirring in alarm. || GoMk 70 ||

children.text: capalānilavellitapuṣpataruṃ tarumandiramūrdhni caladbhramaram |
children.translated_text: With flowering trees swaying in the playful wind, bees moving on the treetop canopies,

children.text: bhramaradhvanipūrṇaguhākuharaṃ kuharasthitaraudrabhujaṃgakulam || GoMk_71 ||
children.translated_text: the hollows of caves filled with the humming of bees, with fierce serpent-families dwelling in the caverns. || GoMk 71 ||

children.text: pakṣivirājitaparvataśṛṅgaṃ śṛṅgaśilātalasaṃsthitasiddham |
children.translated_text: With mountain peaks graced by birds, with <s>Siddhas</s> seated on the rock-terraces of the summits,

children.text: siddhavadhūjanaramyanikuñjaṃ kuñjaniṣevitamattaśakuntam || GoMk_72 ||
children.translated_text: with delightful groves of <s>Siddha</s> women, with intoxicated birds frequenting the bowers. || GoMk 72 ||

children.text: mattaśikhaṇḍikalasvanaramyaṃ ramyaguhāmukhanirgatasiṃham |
children.translated_text: Charming with the sweet cries of intoxicated peacocks, with lions emerging from the mouths of beautiful caves,

children.text: siṃhaninādabhayākulanāgaṃ nāgamadāmbusugandhisamīram || GoMk_73 ||
children.translated_text: with elephants terrified by the roaring of lions, with breezes fragrant from the rut-water of elephants. || GoMk 73 ||

children.text: kva cid upacitavāraṇadantaśikhāśanidāritaśikharataṭaṃ pravirūḍhavilāsaśikhāgaruvṛkṣavanaṃ kva cid uparipayodharabhārataradhvaniñjitaśikhikulavistṛtapicchakalāpavicitritacārutaṭam |
children.translated_text: Somewhere with cliffs split by the thunderbolts of accumulated elephant-tusk tips, with forests of gracefully-crowned aguru trees growing up; somewhere with beautiful slopes variegated with the spread peacock-tail fans of peacock-clans, set in motion by the rumbling weight of clouds above.

children.text: kva cid anilavikampitapuṣpataruṃ skhalitojjvalasurabhijalaṃ kusumaprabalaprativāsitasānuśikhaṃ ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ ⏑ – || GoMk_74 ||
children.translated_text: Somewhere with flower-trees trembling in the wind, with sparkling fragrant water dripping down, with mountain peaks and ridges perfumed by the profusion of blossoms ... [text incomplete] || GoMk 74 ||

children.text: tathāparaṃ dadarśa |
children.translated_text: And then he saw another:

children.text: likhantaṃ karālair nabhaḥ śṛṅgajālaiḥ kṣipantaṃ mayūkhais tamaḥ sāgarāṇām |
children.translated_text: Scratching the sky with its terrible networks of peaks, dispelling the darkness of the oceans with its rays,

children.text: vahantaṃ samudrāmbarām adrigurvīṃ kṣarantaṃ kva cit kāñcanāmbhaḥpravāham || GoMk_75 ||
children.translated_text: bearing the earth-garment of the seas, heavy as a mountain, streaming in some places with a flow of golden water. || GoMk 75 ||

children.text: phalitāmalabhūṣaṇakalpataruṃ tarukhaṇḍavirājitasānuśikham |
children.translated_text: With wish-fulfilling trees adorned with ripe fruits, with ridges and peaks resplendent with groves of trees,

children.text: śikharasthitadevavadhūmithunaṃ mithunair dahatāṃ vayasāṃ madhuram || GoMk_76 ||
children.translated_text: with pairs of divine maidens stationed on the summits — sweet for those burning with the arrows of passion. || GoMk 76 ||

children.text:
kva cid arkamahārathacakranirvātavikhaṇḍitamayūkhakalāpakarālitanaikamahāmaṇipallavasaṃcayamaulibharāvanatonnatabhāsuravajradharaṃ
kva cid indrakarīndravimardataraṅgarayabhramitapracalatkalahaṃsakulāvalihāranabhaḥsaridambuvidhautaśilaṃ |
kva cid aṇḍajarājavilāsasamucchritapakṣamahābhujavajravipāṭitasāgaravāritaloddhṛtapannagabhogadharaṃ
children.translated_text: somewhere bearing the coils of serpents drawn up from the ocean waters, split apart by the great wing-arms of <s>Garuḍa</s>, king of birds, rising in magnificent display;

children.text: kva cid eva surāsurasaṃyugaśastravipannamahāsura-
children.translated_text: somewhere with great circles of waves of the blood of great <s>Asuras</s>

children.text: vaidyutaśoṇitaraṅgamahāvalayam || GoMk_77 ||
children.translated_text: struck down by weapons in the battle of gods and <s>Asuras</s>, like lightning. || GoMk 77 ||

Somewhere blazing with a great diamond-bearer, his crest bowing under the burden of heaps of great jewel-shoots, made fierce by spreading ray-clusters torn apart by the windless orbit of the sun's great chariot-wheel; somewhere with rocks washed by the waters of the celestial river in the sky, with garlands of moving swans disturbed by the waves churned by the sport of <s>Indra</s>'s chief elephant;

children.text: dṛṣṭvaivam āha |
children.translated_text: Having seen this, he said:

children.text: ete parvataśṛṅgacandanatarucchāyāsthalaṃ saṃsṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: These [lions], having resorted to the slopes beneath sandalwood trees on the mountain peaks,

children.text: karṇaprāvaraṇaṃ navāruṇakaracchāyāsamānaśriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: their ears serving as shawls, their glory equal to the hue of the fresh dawn,

children.text: prekṣante madavārilolamadhuliṭprollīḍhagaṇḍasthalaṃ
children.translated_text: they gaze upon the elephant's cheek-area licked by bees wandering wildly in rut-water,

children.text: darpāt kesariṇo balena mahatā pronmathyamānā gajam || GoMk_78 ||
children.translated_text: and with great strength, out of pride, they crush the elephant. || GoMk 78 ||

children.text: ity evam asāv atikāntāradurgaṃ salilaphalāhāramātraparāyaṇaḥ paribhramann ajñānatamaḥpaṭalāvaguṇṭhitam iva jagat saṃsārapaṅke tribhuvanasvāmīvodayad ramaṇakaṃ nāma nagaraṃ dadarśa |
children.translated_text: Thus he, subsisting on mere water and fruits, wandered through exceedingly wild and difficult terrain, and as if the world were enveloped in a veil of darkness of ignorance, like the lord of the three worlds rising from the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s>, he beheld a city named <s>Ramaṇaka</s> (the Delightful).

children.text: samucchritottuṅgacalatpatākaiḥ patatpatatrisvanavāvadūkaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With lofty, towering, fluttering banners, with turrets loud with the calls of alighting birds,

children.text: suvarṇasālair maṇihemaśṛṅgair mahīdharākāragṛhaiḥ suguptaiḥ || GoMk_79 ||
children.translated_text: with golden halls bearing crests of jewels and gold, well-guarded by houses resembling mountains. || GoMk 79 ||

children.text: nilīnapadmālikulālipadmaiḥ samunmiṣatpadmarajaḥpiśaṅgaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With lotuses upon which bee-garlands had settled, with the golden pollen of opening lotuses tinting [all things],

children.text: kalapralāpāṇḍajarāvaramyair mandānilair āvasathīkṛtaṃ sadā || GoMk_80 ||
children.translated_text: with gentle breezes delightful with the murmuring prattle of young geese — forever made into a dwelling-place. || GoMk 80 ||

children.text: surakarikaradaghnakalpavṛkṣair marakataratnatṛṇaiḥ śukāṃśunīlaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With wish-fulfilling trees as tall as the trunk of <s>Indra</s>'s elephant, with grass of emerald gems blue as parrot-wings,

children.text: maṇikanakalatābaddhaśākhaiḥ kva cid urubhis tarubhiḥ prakāmahāri || GoMk_81 ||
children.translated_text: with branches bound by creepers of jewels and gold — somewhere exceedingly captivating with great trees. || GoMk 81 ||

children.text: vikasitanavakarṇikāragauraiḥ kanakagṛhair bahuratnaśṛṅgacitraiḥ |
children.translated_text: With golden houses white as fresh-opened <s>karṇikāra</s> flowers, beautiful with crests of many jewels,

children.text: svakiraṇaruciroruratnasānor acalapateḥ sakalaśriyaṃ dadhānam || GoMk_82 ||
children.translated_text: bearing the complete splendor of the Mountain Lord, from whose jeweled slopes radiance emanated. || GoMk 82 ||

children.text: kva cid amaravilāsinīkarāgraprahatamahāmurajasvanābhirāmam |
children.translated_text: Somewhere delightful with the sound of great drums struck by the fingertips of heavenly courtesans,

children.text: kva cid uparipayodatūryanādapramuditamattaśikhaṇḍivṛndakīrṇam || GoMk_83 ||
children.translated_text: somewhere filled with flocks of intoxicated peacocks, exhilarated by the sounds of cloud-trumpets above. || GoMk 83 ||

children.text: tatas taddarśanāt samutpannajīvitāśo 'sau ramaṇaṃ nagaram upasasarpa | tasmān nagarād viniḥsṛtya catasro 'psaraso dravitanavakanakarasarāgāvadātamūrtayaḥ pravikasitāmbujakusumarucakarucinayanayugalotpalavilāsāḥ kvaṇadruciravividhamaṇimekhalāpabhāramandavilāsagatayaḥ kanakakalaśākārapṛthutarapayodharabharāvanamitatanumadhyā divasakarakarasparśavibodhitāmlānakamalapalāśabhāsurādharakisalayā vividhavibhūṣaṇaśatā nirāmayadarśanāḥ śirasi viracitobhayakamalāñjalayo maitrakanyakasya bodhisattvasya pādayor vinyāsitaśirasaḥ prāhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, his hope of survival revived by that sight, he approached the city of <s>Ramaṇaka</s>. From that city, four <s>Apsarases</s> came forth — their forms radiant like liquid new gold, with eyes having the beauty of the lustre of blooming lotus flowers, their gait languidly graceful with the weight of tinkling varied jeweled girdles, their slender waists bowing under the burden of breasts shaped like golden pitchers, their lower-lip sprouts resplendent like lotus petals awakened by the touch of the sun's rays, adorned with hundreds of various ornaments, a vision of perfect health — with palms joined in lotus-form above their heads, they bowed at the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> and said:

children.text: susvāgataṃ candrasamānanāya nārījanaprītivivardhanāya |
children.translated_text: Welcome to the moon-faced one, the increaser of the joy of womankind,

children.text: kṛpāmṛtāhlāditamānasāya bodhau cirābaddhaviniścayāya || GoMk_84 ||
children.translated_text: whose mind is delighted by the nectar of compassion, who has long held firm resolve toward <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening)! || GoMk 84 ||

children.text: adyaiva duhkhāni śamaṃ gatāni [!] adyaiva no jīvitagātrasāram |
children.translated_text: Today itself our sufferings have come to rest; today itself the essence of our life and limb [is restored];

children.text: niratyayapremaviśeṣabhadrāṇy adyaiva saukhyāni puraḥsthitāni || GoMk_85 ||
children.translated_text: today itself auspicious joys, excellent with immutable special love, stand before us! || GoMk 85 ||

children.text: imāni duḥkhāṅkuśakhaṇḍitāni manāṃsi naḥ śokaparikṣatāni |
children.translated_text: These minds of ours, shattered by the goad of suffering, wounded by grief,

children.text: bhavantam āsādya vasantakāle vanāntarāṇīva vijṛmbhitāni || GoMk_86 ||
children.translated_text: upon reaching you, have blossomed forth like forest-depths in springtime! || GoMk 86 ||

children.text: yāny arjitāny anyabhavāntareṣu karmāṇi śuklāni śubhodayāni |
children.translated_text: The white deeds of auspicious arising, accumulated in other existences —

children.text: teṣāṃ phalaṃ vīkṣaṇam eva te 'laṃ saṅgas tvayā kiṃ punar eva dīrgham || GoMk_87 ||
children.translated_text: the mere sight of you is their sufficient fruit; what more then of long companionship with you! || GoMk 87 ||

children.text: adyaiva mā bandhusuhṛdviyogaśokaṃ kṛthāḥ kasya na santy apāyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Today, do not grieve with the sorrow of separation from kin and friends — for who has no misfortunes?

children.text: dāsyo vayaṃ te 'psaraś catasraś chāyā na te laṅghayituṃ samarthāḥ || GoMk_88 ||
children.translated_text: We are your four servant-<s>Apsarases</s>, unable even to transgress your shadow. || GoMk 88 ||

children.text: ratnāni vāsāṃsi samujjvalāni śayyāśrayāś cārutarā vayaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Jewels, resplendent garments, beds and seats of exquisite beauty, and we ourselves —

children.text: saṃtyaktabhartā surarājayogyā śaktir vidheneha sukhaṃ bhajasva || GoMk_89 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned their [former] lord, fit for the king of gods — by the power of destiny, enjoy happiness here! || GoMk 89 ||

children.text: api ca
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: duḥkhe mahaty apratikāraghore ye vartamānāś ciram udvahanti |
children.translated_text: Those who, existing in great suffering, dreadful and beyond remedy, long endure it,

children.text: te duḥkhabhāropanipātamūḍhās tatraiva śīghraṃ nidhanaṃ prayānti || GoMk_90 ||
children.translated_text: they, bewildered by the onslaught of the burden of suffering, quickly meet their end right there. || GoMk 90 ||

children.text: nitye viyoge maraṇāt puraḥsthite śocanti te daivakṛte viyoge |
children.translated_text: When separation is inevitable and death stands ahead, they grieve at fate-ordained separation,

children.text: saṃsmṛtya rāgopanipātamūḍhāḥ kāmaprahāraṃ viṣamaṃ prapannāḥ || GoMk_91 ||
children.translated_text: bewildered by the onslaught of passion, having fallen into the harsh blows of desire. || GoMk 91 ||

children.text: śabdāyamānavaranūpuramekhalābhir ādiśyamānabhavanaṃ pravarāpsarobhiḥ |
children.translated_text: With finest anklets and girdles tinkling, directed to the palace by the excellent <s>Apsarases</s>,

children.text: haimādriśṛṅgam iva tat puram āviśantaṃ nemuḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭā bahavo 'pi tatra || GoMk_92 ||
children.translated_text: as he entered that city like the golden peak of <s>Meru</s>, many there bowed with joined palms. || GoMk 92 ||

children.text: anyaiś [!] ca punaḥ
children.translated_text: And others again [said]:

children.text: kiṃ dīptaraśmir vinigūḍharaśmiḥ kiṃ puṣpaketuḥ sahasāvatīrṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Is this the radiant sun with hidden rays? Has <s>Puṣpaketu</s> (Kāmadeva) suddenly descended?

children.text: hā kiṃ vinikṣiptaharāgravajro nāthaḥ surāṇām iti tarkito 'bhūt || GoMk_93 ||
children.translated_text: Ah, has the lord of the gods hurled down the diamond from <s>Hara</s>'s (Śiva's) crest? — such were the speculations. || GoMk 93 ||

children.text: timiranikaralekhyā śyāmagopakṣmalekhyāḥ sphuṭitakanakahārā nyastaratnojjvalāṅgyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Their dark eyelash-lines like strokes drawn in darkness, with gold necklaces burst open, their limbs brilliant with set jewels,

children.text: vipulabhavanamālājālavātāyanasthāḥ pramuditamanaso 'nyāś cikṣipuḥ srastakāñcyaḥ || GoMk_94 ||
children.translated_text: standing at the windows of the great rows of palaces, other [women] with delighted hearts threw down their loosened girdles. || GoMk 94 ||

children.text: ratnapradīpaprahatāndhakāraṃ muktāphalapraruciroruharmyam |
children.translated_text: He entered the palace of those <s>Apsarases</s> — its darkness banished by jewel-lamps,

children.text: calatpatākāgravibhinnameghaṃ gehaṃ viveśāpsarasāṃ hi tāsām || GoMk_95 ||
children.translated_text: its upper stories resplendent with pearls, its clouds pierced by the tips of fluttering banners. || GoMk 95 ||

children.text: tāsāṃ vilāsair gamanaiḥ salīlair hāsaiḥ kaṭākṣair madhuraiḥ pralāpaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Sporting with their graceful movements, playful gaits, laughter, sidelong glances, and sweet conversations,

children.text: krīḍan sa kālaṃ na viveda yātaṃ sarvātmanā rāgaparītacetāḥ || GoMk_96 ||
children.translated_text: his mind entirely seized by passion, he did not perceive the passage of time. || GoMk 96 ||

children.text: pratyahaṃ ca dakṣiṇena gamanaṃ vārayanti sma | so 'pi yathā yathā nivāryate tathā tathā tayā diśā gamanāyotsukamanā babhūva |
children.translated_text: And every day they would restrain him from going south. But the more he was restrained, the more eager his mind became to go in that direction.

children.text: yatrāyaṃ vāryate loko janena hitabuddhinā |
children.translated_text: Where the world is restrained by people of benevolent intent,

children.text: viparyastamatis tatra janaḥ sa paridhāvati || GoMk_97 ||
children.translated_text: there, with perverted understanding, the person runs. || GoMk 97 ||

children.text: yadi kuryād ayaṃ loke suhṛdāṃ vacanaṃ hitam |
children.translated_text: If this person in the world would heed the beneficial words of well-wishers,

children.text: paraiti svargaṃ pātālaśvabhre [!] ā svapnato 'pi na || GoMk_98 ||
children.translated_text: he would reach heaven and never, even in dreams, [fall into] the pit of the netherworld. || GoMk 98 ||

children.text: atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvas tāsām apsarasām parijñātagamanaprayojano dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi padavīm āruhya vrajan sadāmattakaṃ nāma nagaraṃ dadarśa | tasmād api nagarād aṣṭāpsarasaḥ sasaṃbhramaṃ niḥsṛtya taṃ mahāsattvaṃ praveśayām āsuḥ | tatrāpy aciraṃ ratim anubhūya pratiṣidhyamānagamanakriyas tenaiva dakṣiṇena pathā gacchan nandanaṃ nāma nagaraṃ dadarśa | tasmād api ṣoḍaśāpsarobhir abhigamya satkṛtya praveśayām āse | tatrāpi ciraṃ krīḍāṃ sevitvā tasmād api brahmottaraṃ nāma nagaraṃ prayayau | tatrāpi dvātriṃśatāpsarobhir bhūyaḥ satkāraṃ viṣayasukham bhuktvā tāḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, having understood the purpose of the <s>Apsarases</s>' [attempts to prevent his] going, took the road southward and walking, beheld a city named <s>Sadāmattaka</s> (the Ever-Intoxicating). From that city too, eight <s>Apsarases</s> hastily came forth and led the great being inside. After enjoying pleasures there for a short time, his going again being forbidden, he went by that same southern path and beheld a city named <s>Nandana</s> (the Joyous). From that too, sixteen <s>Apsarases</s> approached him, honored him, and led him inside. After long sporting there, he proceeded from there to a city named <s>Brahmottara</s> (Supreme Brahma). There too, having been honored by thirty-two <s>Apsarases</s> and enjoyed sensual pleasures, he said to them:

children.text: icchāmi gantum tad ahaṃ bhavantyo [!] mā matkṛte śokahrade śayidhvam |
children.translated_text: I wish to go, ladies; do not lie in the lake of grief on my account;

children.text: saṃpātabhadrāṇi hi kasya nāma viśleṣaduḥkhāni na santi loke || GoMk_99 ||
children.translated_text: for who in this world does not have sorrows of separation, though fortunate in meeting? || GoMk 99 ||

children.text: sthitvāpi yenaiva ciraṃ viyogaḥ śatroḥ kṛtāntād bhavitāntakāle |
children.translated_text: Even having stayed long, the separation from the enemy Death must come at the end of time;

children.text: tenaiva netrāśrujalārdragaṇḍān [!] yuṣmān vihāyādya yiyāsur asmi || GoMk_100 ||
children.translated_text: from that very [Death], I now wish to depart, leaving you with cheeks moist with streams of tears. || GoMk 100 ||

children.text: vātāhatāmbhodhitaraṅgalole ye jīvaloke bahuduḥkhabhīme |
children.translated_text: In the world of the living, rolling with the waves of the wind-tossed ocean, full of many fearful sufferings,

children.text: viśleṣaduḥkhāya ratiṃ prayānti teṣāṃ paro nāsti vimūḍhacetāḥ || GoMk_101 ||
children.translated_text: those who take delight in what leads to the suffering of separation — there is none more deluded than they. || GoMk 101 ||

children.text: athāpsarasas tāḥ samastās tadgamanaviyogaśokaglapitaṛdayāḥ sasaṃbhramāḥ kamalakuvalayakuḍmalavilāsā nalinya iva śirasi viracitobhayakamalāñjalayaḥ prāhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then all those <s>Apsarases</s>, their hearts wilting with the grief of his departure, agitated, their charm like buds of lotuses and blue water-lilies — like lotus-pools — with palms joined in lotus-form above their heads, said:

children.text: asmāsu te kartum aniṣṭam iṣṭaṃ kathaṃ hi bhaktipraṇayārpitāsu |
children.translated_text: How can you wish to do this unwelcome thing to us who have offered our devotion and love?

children.text: so 'nyena ekagrahaṇīyarūpaḥ śarīrakānena vayo grahīte || GoMk_102 ||
children.translated_text: He of incomparably captivating form — with this very body, youth has been seized. || GoMk 102 ||

children.text: gatvā tan nagaratrayaṃ yad api he svāminn ihāpy āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Having visited those three cities, O master, you have now come here too;

children.text: saṃprāptā viṣayopabhogamadhurāḥ saṃpattayas te ciram |
children.translated_text: for a long time you have obtained pleasures sweet with the enjoyment of sense-objects;

children.text: gantavyaṃ na punas tvayā subahunā proktena kiṃ yāsi cet
children.translated_text: you must not go again. What is the use of much speaking? If you do go,

children.text: saṃsmartāsi vipatsamudrapatito vākyaṃ hi no duḥkhitaḥ || GoMk_103 ||
children.translated_text: when fallen into the ocean of misfortune, grieving, you will remember our words. || GoMk 103 ||

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: yad abhyāsavaśān nṛṇām udayasaṃpadaḥ sthirāḥ |
children.translated_text: When through the power of habit, the prosperous attainments of people are firm,

children.text: kathaṃ te nu nivāryeran nivarteran kathaṃ nu vā || GoMk_104 ||
children.translated_text: how indeed can they be restrained? How indeed would they turn back? || GoMk 104 ||

children.text: niyojanīyāḥ suhṛdaḥ suhṛdbhir yasmin hite karmaṇi nityakālam |
children.translated_text: Friends should be encouraged by friends in whatever beneficial action at all times;

children.text: nivāraṇaṃ tatra tu ye prakurvate te śatravo 'mitratayā bhavanti || GoMk_105 ||
children.translated_text: but those who obstruct that — they become enemies, acting in the manner of foes. || GoMk 105 ||

children.text: divyaṃ prāpya sukhaṃ pure ramaṇake saṃcoditaḥ karmaṇā [!]
children.translated_text: Having obtained divine happiness in the city of <s>Ramaṇaka</s>, urged by <s>karma</s>,

children.text: āyāto 'smi niṣevaṇāya paramaṃ saukhyaṃ sadāmattakam |
children.translated_text: I came to enjoy the supreme bliss of <s>Sadāmattaka</s>;

children.text: saṃprāpto 'smi tataḥ svakarmakuśaleneṣṭaṃ puraṃ nandanaṃ
children.translated_text: from there, by the merit of my own <s>karma</s>, I reached the desired city of <s>Nandana</s>;

children.text: tasmād āgatakasya yūyam adhunā pronmūlitā bhūmayaḥ || GoMk_106 ||
children.translated_text: from that point, for one who has arrived here, the foundations have been uprooted for you. || GoMk 106 ||

children.text: tasmād ato me gamanaṃ bhavantyo [!] mā vārayadhvaṃ na hi no 'sty apāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, ladies, do not obstruct my going from here — for there is no misfortune for us;

children.text: asmād viśeṣāṇi sukhāni manye lapsye 'ham ity uccalito 'ham adya || GoMk_107 ||
children.translated_text: I think I shall obtain pleasures superior to these — stirred by that [thought], I depart today. || GoMk 107 ||

children.text: ity atha mitrakanyako bodhisattvas tāsām apsarasāṃ hitam api vākyam ahitam ivāvajñayā tiraskṛtya tenaiva dakṣiṇena pathā gacchan dadarśa mahārgaḍapraṭitaprakaṭapuṭacaturdvāradāruṇaṃ sureśvareṇāpy abhedyottuṅgāyasaviśālaprākārapariveṣṭitam antarbhramaccakramaṇḍalālokapramuktadamadamāśabdagambhīrabhairavam āyasaṃ nagaraṃ tasya ca dvāradeśam upacakrāma |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, disregarding and scorning the words of those <s>Apsarases</s> — which though beneficial seemed unwelcome — went by that very southern path and beheld an iron city, dreadful with four gates whose massive bolts and panels stood open, encircled by high, broad iron walls impenetrable even by the lord of gods, terrifying with the deep and dreadful sounds of 'dam-dam' released from the sight of the turning wheel-circles within; and he approached its gate.

children.text: saṃprāptamātrasya tu tatkṣaṇena dvāraṃ ca visphoṭakapāṭabhāram |
children.translated_text: The very moment he arrived, instantly the door with its heavy bolt-panels

children.text: vajrāgradhārāparibhinnasānor vindhyācalasyeva nitambakukṣiḥ || GoMk_108 ||
children.translated_text: like the flank and hollow of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain whose peak is cleft by a diamond-edged blade. // GoMk 108 //

children.text: tato maitrakanyako bodhisattvo 'tra viveśa |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, entered therein.

children.text: praviṣṭamātrasya tu tatkṣaṇena dvāraṃ parikṣiptakapāṭayantram |
children.translated_text: But the very instant he entered, the door with its bolt-mechanism

children.text: tatkarmavāyuprabhavair mahadbhiḥ kṣaṇād bhujāgrair iva saṃjaghāṭa || GoMk_109 ||
children.translated_text: was slammed shut in a moment by great arms, as it were, arisen from the wind of that [past] <s>karma</s>. // GoMk 109 //

children.text: aśrauṣīc ca pragāḍhavedanāviklavahṛdayapuruṣasyāntaḥprākārāntaratiraskṛtaparamabhīṣaṇanirnādaṃ sakalajanottrāsanam uccarantaṃ śrutvā ca dvāradeśaṃ tvaritamatir lalaṅgha |
children.translated_text: And he heard, from within the inner enclosure wall, the supremely terrifying cry of a man with heart tormented by excruciating pain — a cry that would terrify all people. And hearing it, with quickened mind, he leaped toward the door.

children.text: praviṣṭamātrasya tato dvitīyam āsphālitaṃ dvāram ivoparuddham |
children.translated_text: The very instant he entered, a second door was slammed shut as if blocked,

children.text: paryantakālānilavegaviddhaṃ dvāraṃ surāṇām iva vajrakalpam || GoMk_110 ||
children.translated_text: a door [struck] by the force of wind at the end of time, adamantine like the gate of the gods. // GoMk 110 //

children.text: tato mitrakanyako bodhisattvaḥ praviveśa |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, entered further.

children.text: praviṣṭamātrasya punas tṛtīyaṃ dvāraṃ parikṣiptakapāṭayantram |
children.translated_text: The very instant he entered, a third door with its bolt-mechanism

children.text: kṣaṇād abhūt tan nagaraṃ ca sarvaṃ bhrāntaṃ ca kṛtsnaṃ sa dadarśa bhītaḥ || GoMk_111 ||
children.translated_text: closed in an instant — and the entire city was [seen to be] empty, and he, frightened, saw everything confused. // GoMk 111 //

children.text: tato maitrakanyako bodhisattvaḥ paśyati sma tam atidāruṇākārapramāṇaṃ krūrajvalanamālāliṅgitam udāreṇa paṭupavanavikīryamāṇadhūmapaṭalāndhakāradurdinena sphuratsphuliṅgāvalikarāladarśanenāyasena mahatā bhramatā cakreṇa dārv iva pravidāryamāṇamūrdhānaṃ svaśiraḥpravigalitaśoṇitavasārasāhāramātravidhṛtaprāṇaśeṣaṃ samīpaṃ copagamyainaṃ paryapṛcchat |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, beheld that man — of exceedingly terrible form and size, embraced by garlands of fierce flame, with a terrible appearance of flickering spark-garlands amid the darkness of dense clouds of smoke scattered by a fierce, sharp wind — his skull being split open as if by a great rotating iron wheel, his remaining life sustained solely by the food of blood and fat flowing from his own head. And approaching him, he asked:

children.text: kiṃ nāgo 'si suro 'si kinnaravaro yakṣo 'si kiṃ mānuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Are you a <s>Nāga</s>? A god? A supreme <s>Kinnara</s>? A <s>Yakṣa</s>? A human?

children.text: kiṃ vidyādharasainikaḥ kim asi vā daityaḥ piśāco 'si vā |
children.translated_text: A soldier of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>? Or a <s>Daitya</s>? A <s>Piśāca</s>?

children.text: kiṃ vākāri bhavāntareṣu bhavatā karmātiraudraṃ svayaṃ
children.translated_text: What supremely terrible <s>karma</s> did you yourself perform in former existences

children.text: yasyāstivyasanaṃ duruttaram idaṃ bhujyaṃ phalaṃ krandayat || GoMk_112 ||
children.translated_text: that you must endure this unbearable, weeping-inducing misfortune as its fruit? // GoMk 112 //

children.text: puruṣaḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: The man said:

children.text: nāhaṃ nāgo naiva yakṣo na devo daityo nāhaṃ nāpi gandharvarājā [!] |
children.translated_text: I am not a <s>Nāga</s>, not a <s>Yakṣa</s>, not a god; I am not a <s>Daitya</s>, nor a <s>Gandharva</s> king.

children.text: rakṣo nāhaṃ nāpi vidyādharo 'pi jātis tulyā saṃpratīhi tvayā naḥ || GoMk_113 ||
children.translated_text: I am not a <s>Rākṣasa</s>, nor a <s>Vidyādhara</s>; know our birth to be the same [as yours]. // GoMk 113 //

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text:
kiṃ karma bhramatā tvayā kumatinā saṃsāradurge kṛtaṃ
yenedaṃ jvalitānalaṃ śirasi te cakraṃ bhramaty āyasam |
children.translated_text: What <s>karma</s> did you, of evil mind, wandering in the fortress of <s>saṃsāra</s>, perform, that this blazing iron wheel whirls upon your head?

children.text: puruṣaḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: The man said:

children.text: nānāduṣkarakārikā bhagavatī saṃsārasaṃdarśikā
tatra śreyaḥsukhopapādanaparā matsnehabaddhāśayā || GoMk_114 ||
children.translated_text: who was devoted to producing my welfare and happiness, whose heart was bound by affection for me — // GoMk 114 //
My revered mother, who showed me the way of <s>saṃsāra</s> through various hardships,

children.text: yāṃ loke pravadanti sādhumatayaḥ kṣetraṃ paraṃ prāṇināṃ
children.translated_text: she whom the wise in the world call the supreme field of merit for living beings —

children.text: daivāveśavaśād akāryagurukas tasyāṃ jananyām aham |
children.translated_text: upon that mother, I, overwhelmed by fate and burdened with evil deeds,

children.text: sādho prāskhalayaṃ śiraḥpraharaṇaṃ pādena pāpāśayas
children.translated_text: O virtuous one, stumbled — striking her head with my foot, with sinful intent;

children.text: tenedaṃ jvalitānalaṃ śirasi me cakraṃ bhramaty āyasam || GoMk_115 ||
children.translated_text: therefore this blazing iron wheel whirls upon my head. // GoMk 115 //

children.text: atha bodhisattvas tasya puruṣasya pravacanapratodena saṃcoditahṛdayas tāṃ parajugupsām ātmany anupaśyann āha |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his heart stirred by the goad of that man's words, perceiving in himself that same blame toward others, said:

children.text: anyaṃ jugupsāmy aham alpabuddhir ātmānam evādya nininda ajñaḥ |
children.translated_text: I, of little wisdom, used to despise others — now, ignorant, I condemn myself alone;

children.text: yeṣu svayaṃ doṣagaṇeṣu magnas tair eva lokaṃ katham aṅkayāmi || GoMk_116 ||
children.translated_text: sunk in the very faults [I blamed in others], how can I brand the world with them? // GoMk 116 //

children.text: mayāpi yan mātari dakṣiṇīye [!] kṛto 'parādhaḥ puruṣādhamena |
children.translated_text: The offense I too, lowest of men, committed against my venerable mother —

children.text: tasyaiva pāpasya phalāni bhoktum ullaṅghya toyāvalim āgato 'smi || GoMk_117 ||
children.translated_text: to experience the fruits of that very sin, I have come here, crossing the expanse of waters. // GoMk 117 //

children.text: ity atha tasya vacanānantaram eva prabhinnanavakuvalayadalanirmalān nabhastalāt sajalajaladaninādagambhīradhīrodhvanir uccacāra |
children.translated_text: And then, immediately after his words, from the sky, clear as the petals of a freshly opened blue lotus, there arose a voice, deep and solemn as the rumbling of a rain-bearing cloud:

children.text: kiṃ na paśyati karmāṇi balavanti śarīriṇām |
children.translated_text: Does he not see the mighty <s>karmas</s> of embodied beings?

children.text: lokālokāntarasthāyī pāśeneva vikṛṣyate || GoMk_118 ||
children.translated_text: He who stands between the world and the un-world is dragged as if by a noose. // GoMk 118 //

children.text: ye baddhā viṣayeṇa duḥkhanigaḍe 'nāyāsakarmotkaṭe
children.translated_text: Those who are bound by sense-objects in the fetter of suffering, fierce in effortless deeds of misery,

children.text: ye tyaktvā guruvākyam andhamatayaḥ pāpāśrayaṃ kurvate |
children.translated_text: who, abandoning the words of the guru, with blinded minds take refuge in sin —

children.text: muktāḥ karmabhir eva duḥkhanigaḍapracchedaśūraiḥ śubhair
children.translated_text: freed by those very <s>karmas</s> that are heroic in cutting the fetter of suffering, the wholesome ones,

children.text: mānuṣyaṃ yad avāpya mūḍhamatayo dūre sthitā karmiṇaḥ || GoMk_119 ||
children.translated_text: [yet] having obtained human birth, the deluded, intent on [evil] deeds, stand far [from liberation]. // GoMk 119 //

children.text: atha tasya vacanānantaram eva karmānilavegotkṣiptam iva tac cakraṃ ciṭiciṭāyamānadahanakaṇacayodgāraraudraṃ tasya mūrdhnaḥ samabhyudgamya maitrakanyakasya bodhisattvasya śiraḥ pravidārayaṃ [!] bhramitum ārabdham |
children.translated_text: Then, immediately after those words, that wheel — as if hurled upward by the wind of <s>karma</s>, terrible with showers of crackling fire-sparks — rising from that man's head, began to whirl, splitting open the skull of <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: kṣaṇāt sa reje rudhirapravāhair mūrdhnā [!] cyutaiḥ snātasamastamūrtiḥ |
children.translated_text: In an instant he shone, his entire body bathed in streams of blood flowing from his head,

children.text: prabhinnacakrāgravibhinnamūrdhna airāvaṇasyeva tanuḥ patantī || GoMk_120 ||
children.translated_text: his body falling like that of <s>Airāvaṇa</s> (Indra's elephant) whose skull is split by the tip of the whirling disc. // GoMk 120 //

children.text: tataḥ sa puruṣo hā heti mūrdhnā [!] pravidāhajena tīvreṇa duḥkhena samākramyamāṇaśarīrakaṃ maitrakanyakaṃ bodhisattvam āha |
children.translated_text: Then that man, crying 'Alas!', said to <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whose body was overcome by the excruciating pain of the burning on his head:

children.text: divyāṅganāgītamanoharāṇi cittapramododayasādhanāni |
children.translated_text: Why, having abandoned those divine cities, charming with the songs of celestial women,

children.text: saṃtyajya kasmād u purāṇi tāni prāptas tv idaṃ sthānam anantaduḥkham || GoMk_121 ||
children.translated_text: the means for the arising of delight in the heart, have you come to this place of infinite suffering? // GoMk 121 //

children.text: devālayaṃ divyasukhopabhogaṃ ko nāma saṃprāpya śubhair atulyaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having attained, through incomparable merits, the abode of the gods with its enjoyment of divine pleasures,

children.text: nityajvaladvahniśikhākareṇa saṃprārthayed bhīmam apāyagartam || GoMk_122 ||
children.translated_text: who indeed would desire the terrible pit of lower destinies, with its hands of ever-blazing fire-flames? // GoMk 122 //

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: mattālikolāhalasaṃkulāni vanāni puṣpojjvalamastakāni |
children.translated_text: Elephants, abandoning forests alive with the tumult of intoxicated bees, with treetops blazing with flowers,

children.text: saṃtyajya nāgā vyasanaṃ sahante yayā tayecchālatayāgato 'ham || GoMk_123 ||
children.translated_text: endure misfortune — driven by the same impulse of desire that has brought me here. // GoMk 123 //

children.text: rājyāni vistīrṇadhanojjvalāni vihāya nārīmukhapaṅkajāni |
children.translated_text: Many kings, abandoning kingdoms radiant with vast wealth and the lotus-faces of women,

children.text: yuddhe mriyante bahavo narendrā yayā tayecchālatayāgato 'ham || GoMk_124 ||
children.translated_text: die in battle — driven by the same impulse of desire that has brought me here. // GoMk 124 //

children.text: samutpatattuṅgataraṅgaraudre bhramajjalāvartavimuktanāde |
children.translated_text: In the great ocean, terrible with rising towering waves, resounding with the noise of swirling whirlpools,

children.text: mahodadhau yānti narāḥ praṇāśaṃ yayā tayecchālatayāgato 'ham || GoMk_125 ||
children.translated_text: people go to destruction — driven by the same impulse of desire that has brought me here. // GoMk 125 //

children.text: niratyayātyantikasaukhyasādhanaṃ narāmaraśrīsukhasiddhimārgam |
children.translated_text: The vow of the lord of sages — the path to the perfection of the splendor and happiness of humans and gods, producing ultimate and uninterrupted bliss —

children.text: munīśvarāṇāṃ vratam utsṛjanti yayā tayecchālatayāgato 'ham || GoMk_126 ||
children.translated_text: people abandon it — driven by the same impulse of desire that has brought me here. // GoMk 126 //

children.text: teṣāṃ munīnāṃ vigatavyathānāṃ deyaṃ kathaṃ pādarajo na mūrdhni |
children.translated_text: How can the dust of the feet of those sages, free from suffering, not be placed upon one's head —

children.text: yair laṅghitās tīvraviṣapracaṇḍā āśāprapātā bahuduḥkhabhīmāḥ || GoMk_127 ||
children.translated_text: they who have leaped over the precipices of desire, fierce with sharp poison, terrible with much suffering? // GoMk 127 //

children.text: kiṃ tad bhaved duḥkham atīvatīvraṃ kā vā vipattir bahuduḥkhayoniḥ |
children.translated_text: What suffering could there be, however intense, or what calamity, however much a source of suffering,

children.text: tṛṣṇāviṣāgnikṣatacittavṛtter yā dūrataḥ saṃparivartinī syāt || GoMk_128 ||
children.translated_text: that would keep at a distance one whose mental activity is wounded by the fire-poison of craving? // GoMk 128 //

children.text: api ca he sādho
children.translated_text: And moreover, O virtuous one:

children.text: karmaṇā parikṛṣṭo 'smi vartamāno 'pi dūrataḥ |
children.translated_text: I am dragged by <s>karma</s>, even while existing far away;

children.text: karṣati prāṇinas tatra phalaṃ yatra prayacchati || GoMk_129 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> drags living beings to the place where it delivers its fruit. // GoMk 129 //

children.text: api ca
children.translated_text: And moreover:

children.text: kati varṣasahasrāṇi kati varṣaśatāni ca |
children.translated_text: For how many thousands of years, for how many hundreds of years,

children.text: pradīptam āyasaṃ cakraṃ mama mūrdhni bhramiṣyati || GoMk_130 ||
children.translated_text: will this blazing iron wheel whirl upon my head? // GoMk 130 //

children.text: puruṣaḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: The man said:

children.text: ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭivarṣaśatāni ca |
children.translated_text: For sixty thousand years and sixty hundred years,

children.text: pradīptam āyasaṃ cakraṃ tava mūrdhni bhramiṣyati || GoMk_131 ||
children.translated_text: this blazing iron wheel will whirl upon your head. // GoMk 131 //

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text:
etad bhāsuravahnipiṅgalaśikhājvālākalāpojjvalaṃ
ko 'nyo 'vabhramitaṃ prayāsyati samaṃ chittvā paraḥ caiṣyati |
children.translated_text: This [wheel], blazing with garlands of flames whose tawny tips burn brightly — who else, having worn it, will depart? Will another come, having been cut free?

children.text: puruṣaḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: The man said:

children.text: yo mātary apakārakāryam aparaḥ kṛtvā samāyāsyati
tasyedaṃ śirasi bhramiṣyati punar mūrdhnā [!] tava pracyutaḥ || GoMk_132 ||
children.translated_text: upon his head this will whirl again, having fallen from your head. // GoMk 132 //
He who comes here having committed an offense against his mother —

children.text: atha bodhisattvas tena mūrdhnā [!] pravidāhajena tīvreṇa duḥkhena samākulahṛdayo 'pi sattveṣv ananteṣu samutpāditatīvrakāruṇyāśayas taṃ puruṣam ābabhāṣe |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though his heart was overwhelmed by the excruciating pain of the burning on his head, having generated intense compassion toward infinite beings, addressed that man:

children.text: kṣapitasakalarāgakleśajālāndhakārā gaganatalanilīnā yogino ye namasyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Let the <s>yogins</s>, worthy of homage, who have destroyed the darkness of the entire net of passion and affliction, dwelling in the vault of the sky, hear [this];

children.text: sphuritakaṭakahārāḥ prajvalanmaulayo ye punar amarasamūhās te 'pi śṛṇvantu santaḥ || GoMk_133 ||
children.translated_text: and let those assemblies of immortals too — the virtuous ones — with glistening girdle-necklaces and blazing crowns, listen. // GoMk 133 //

children.text: kṛtvā duścaritaṃ svamātari jagat kṛtsnaṃ yadi prodvahed
children.translated_text: If the entire world should have committed evil against its own mother,

children.text: etatprajvalitāgnirāgakapilaṃ cakraṃ bṛhan mūrdhani |
children.translated_text: may this great wheel, blazing with fire and tawny with passion, [rest] upon my head;

children.text: kalpān kalpasamair ahobhir ayutān voḍhuṃ cirāyotsahe
children.translated_text: for <s>kalpas</s>, for ten thousand days each equal to a <s>kalpa</s>, I am willing to bear it for a long time —

children.text: sattvārthaṃ pratipadya mānava hi me cittaṃ na saṃkhidyate || GoMk_134 ||
children.translated_text: undertaking it for the sake of beings, my mind is not crushed, O mortal. // GoMk 134 //

children.text: atha tasya sarvasattvapriyasya maitrakanyakasya bodhisattvasya vacanānantaram eva mūrdhnā [!] samutpatyotkṣiptam iva tac cakraṃ saptatālocchrayāc cākraṃ nabhastalaṃ samutpatyāvatasthe |
children.translated_text: Then, immediately after those words of <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, beloved of all beings, that wheel — as if hurled upward from his head — rose up to the vault of the sky, to the height of seven palm trees, and remained suspended.

children.text: reje tac capalānilāhatacalajjvālākalāpojjvalaṃ
children.translated_text: That wheel shone, blazing with garlands of flames trembling in the restless wind,

children.text: cakraṃ khe parivartamānam asakṛtpronmuktabhīmasvanam |
children.translated_text: revolving in the sky, repeatedly releasing a terrifying sound,

children.text: udyan [!] bimbam ivāruṇasya sakalaṃ pronmuktaraśmyutkaraṃ
children.translated_text: like the entire rising orb of the sun with its emitted mass of rays,

children.text: ratnādyaiḥ pravilambamānam amalair vaiḍūryabhittyāśrayaiḥ || GoMk_135 ||
children.translated_text: hung with pure gems and beryl-walled supports. // GoMk 135 //

children.text: tataḥ sravannirjharavāricālinaḥ samīraṇollāsitapuṣpaśākhinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the mountains, with their arms of long peaks kissing the sky,

children.text: nabhovicumbyāyataśṛṅgabāhavaś cakampire bhūmibhṛto hatā iva || GoMk_136 ||
children.translated_text: with flower-branches stirred by the wind and streams of flowing waterfalls, trembled as if struck. // GoMk 136 //

children.text: bhujaṃgavikṣobhasamudgatormayaḥ payodharadhvānagabhīranādinaḥ |
children.translated_text: The bodies of water, with waves rising from the agitation of serpents, their roar deep as thunderclouds,

children.text: jalālayā ratnaśikhānivāsinas tadātivelāsalilair lalaṅghire || GoMk_137 ||
children.translated_text: inhabited by jewel-crested [beings], were then flooded by waters beyond their shores. // GoMk 137 //

children.text: pramuktaniḥśeṣamayūkhabhāsuraṃ rarāja khe maṇḍalam aṃśumālinaḥ |
children.translated_text: The disc of the sun shone in the sky, brilliant with all its released rays;

children.text: raver mayūkhāṅkuradanturāntarād diśaḥ samantād dadṛśuḥ sphuṭaśriyaḥ || GoMk_138 ||
children.translated_text: through the gaps bristling with sprouts of the sun's rays, the directions appeared resplendent all around. // GoMk 138 //

children.text: sphurattaḍiddāmavirājitorasaḥ surendracāpapratibaddhakaṅkaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: The clouds, their chests adorned with garlands of flashing lightning, with rainbow-bracelets bound upon them,

children.text: payomucaḥ kiṃcidavāśrutāmbhaso vitānavad vyomani te virejire || GoMk_139 ||
children.translated_text: slightly releasing their waters, shone in the sky like canopies. // GoMk 139 //

children.text: srajo vicitrā vinipetur ambarād vituṣṭuvur harṣatarā divaukasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Colorful garlands fell from the sky; the celestial beings praised with great joy;

children.text: cirapragāḍhavyasanā hatārtayaḥ kṣaṇād abhūvan bahavo nirāmayāḥ || GoMk_140 ||
children.translated_text: those long afflicted with deep misfortune, their pains destroyed, in an instant became free from illness. // GoMk 140 //

children.text: jvalati viṣamacakre prāntadīrṇordhvakāyo
children.translated_text: While the terrible wheel blazed, his body torn at the edges and raised upward,

children.text: galitarudhiradhārāsiktasarvāṅgakāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: his entire body drenched by streams of flowing blood,

children.text: bhagavati guṇarāśau saṃprasādya svacittaṃ
children.translated_text: having composed his mind upon the Blessed One, the treasure of virtues,

children.text: svagṛham iva sa sādhur dyām ayāt tatkṣaṇena || GoMk_141 ||
