children.translated_text: that saint went to heaven in that very instant, as if going home. // GoMk 141 //

children.text: dānodakamahattīrthe śīlaśaucasunirmale |
children.translated_text: At the great ford (<s>tīrtha</s>) of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), beautifully pure with the cleanliness of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>),

children.text: kṣamāsurabhiśītācche vīryāgādhapravāhake || GoMk_142 ||
children.translated_text: cool and clear with the fragrance of patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), with a deep current of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), // GoMk 142 //

children.text: dhyānastimitagambhīre prajñāpadmaprabodhake |
children.translated_text: still and deep with meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), awakening the lotus of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) —

children.text: tasmin bodhimahātīrthe sthitvā bodhipurotsukaḥ || GoMk_143 ||
children.translated_text: having stood at that great ford of <s>Bodhi</s> (enlightenment), eager for enlightenment, // GoMk 143 //

children.text: prakṣālayañ cheṣapāpaṃ tuṣite 'sau yayau mudā |
children.translated_text: washing away the remainder of sin, he went joyfully to <s>Tuṣita</s> [heaven];

children.text: tatrastho 'py aciraṃ reme dṛṣṭvā lokaṃ kṛpānvitaḥ || GoMk_144 ||
children.translated_text: even stationed there, he did not long rejoice — seeing the world, he was filled with compassion. // GoMk 144 //

children.text: tat kim idam upanītam | evaṃ hi mātary apakāriṇaḥ prāṇina ihaiva vyasanaprapātapātālāvalambino bhavantīti satatasamupajāyamānapremaprasādabahumānamānasaiḥ satpuruṣair mātaraḥ śuśrūṣaṇīyā iti ||
children.translated_text: What is the lesson here? Thus, living beings who harm their mother fall even in this life into the abyss of calamity — therefore, mothers should be served with reverence by good people whose minds are ever filled with the arising of love, grace, and respect.

children.text: iti śrīdivyāvadāne maitrakanyakāvadānaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the holy <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Maitrakanyakāvadāna</s> is complete.

children.text: 7. Matsarananda
children.translated_text: 7. <s>Matsarananda</s> (The Story of Miserly Nanda)

children.text: svayaṃkṛtaḥ sarvasukhoparodhī mātsaryatulyo 'sti kalir na loke |
children.translated_text: There is no strife in the world, self-created, that blocks all happiness, equal to envy (<s>mātsarya</s>);

children.text: yatrābhirūḍhā vyasanaughamagnā bhavanti niśvāsaparā manuṣyāḥ || GoMn_1 ||
children.translated_text: those who are mounted upon it, sunk in a flood of misfortune, become people given to sighing. // GoMn 1 //

children.text: evam idam ucyamānam alaṃ saṃvegāya | tadyathānuśrūyate |
children.translated_text: This, thus proclaimed, suffices for spiritual urgency. This is what is heard in tradition:

children.text: śrāvastyāṃ nando nāma sārthavāḥ prativasati sma | tasya janmāntare pātrātiśayapratipāditatvāt taddānabījasyāparimāṇo bhogaskandhaḥ prādur babhūva | mātsaryābhyāsāt tu notsahate sma kiṃ cid api kasmai cit pradātum |
children.translated_text: In <s>Śrāvastī</s>, there dwelt a caravan-leader named <s>Nanda</s>. Because in a former life the seed of his giving had been placed in an exceptional vessel [of merit], an immeasurable mass of wealth manifested for him. But due to the habitual practice of envy (<s>mātsarya</s>), he could not bring himself to give anything at all to anyone.

children.text: tasya kṣetrātiśayapatitaṃ dānabījaṃ purāṇaṃ
children.translated_text: His ancient seed of giving, which had fallen upon an exceptional field [of merit],

children.text: naikākāraṃ vibhavanicayaṃ sphītam āviś cakāra |
children.translated_text: manifested in him an abundant accumulation of wealth of many kinds;

children.text: pūrvaṃ dānākṛtaparicayādhyāśayatvāt tu nāsau
children.translated_text: but because of a disposition unfamiliar with the practice of giving,

children.text: dātuṃ kiṃ cit prabhavati tadā matsarākrāntacetāḥ || GoMn_2 ||
children.translated_text: is able to give anything — his mind seized by jealousy? // GoMn 2 //

children.text: tyāgasyaiva phalānubandhamadhurāṃ citrāṃ vipākaśriyaṃ
children.translated_text: The wondrous splendor of the fruit-laden sweetness that is the result of generosity alone —

children.text: saṃprāpya praharanty anartharucayo mūleṣu ye saṃpadām |
children.translated_text: those who, delighting in misfortune, strike at the very roots of prosperity after having attained it,

children.text: te saṃtyajya nidāghakālasubhagān indoḥ karāñ śīkarān
children.translated_text: they, abandoning the cool, showering moonbeams so pleasant in the hot season,

children.text: hlādāyānupatanti dāvadahanāṃś cañcacchikhāsaṃcayān || GoMn_3 ||
children.translated_text: chase after forest fires for refreshment — with their flickering crests of flame! // GoMn 3 //

children.text: naivātmanāsau bubhuje kadaryo bhogān dadau nāpi suhṛjjanebhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: That miser neither enjoyed his possessions himself nor gave to friends and well-wishers;

children.text: mātsaryabhūtagrahalubdhacetā dravyārjanaṃ kevalam eva cakre || GoMn_4 ||
children.translated_text: his mind covetous, possessed by the demon of jealousy, he merely accumulated wealth. // GoMn 4 //

children.text: praviṣṭapūrvā na gṛhaṃ kadā cid dvijātayas tasya kapālahastāḥ |
children.translated_text: Never did <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with begging bowls in hand enter his house;

children.text: śuśrāva sa pravrajitānanebhyo na dakṣiṇādeśanamaṅgalāni || GoMn_5 ||
children.translated_text: he never heard from the mouths of renunciants the auspicious words of instruction about charitable gifts. // GoMn 5 //

children.text: vanīyakās tasya gṛhājirebhyo vrajanti niśvasya viśuṣkavaktrāḥ |
children.translated_text: Merchants departed from his courtyard sighing, with parched mouths;

children.text: baliṃ na kākā api nāma tasya smaranti sikthaprakaropahāram || GoMn_6 ||
children.translated_text: even the crows do not remember an offering of food-scraps from his <s>bali</s> (ritual offering). // GoMn 6 //

children.text: vivāhakāleṣv api nāma tasya vāditraśabdo na samuccacāra |
children.translated_text: Even at the time of weddings, no sound of musical instruments was heard in his [household];

children.text: āvāhakāleṣv api tasya gehe suhṛjjanā dīnamukhā babhūvuḥ || GoMn_7 ||
children.translated_text: even at the time of welcoming ceremonies, the well-wishers in his home had dejected faces. // GoMn 7 //

children.text: dūrāt śmaśānam iva tasya vivarjya gehaṃ anyena yācakajanas tvaritaṃ jagāma |
children.translated_text: Avoiding his house from afar as if it were a cremation ground, beggars hurried away by another [path];

children.text: nāmāpi tasya parikīrtya kila prabhāte lebhe na kaś cid aśanaṃ divasāvasāne || GoMn_8 ||
children.translated_text: having merely uttered his name in the morning, no one, it is said, obtained food by the end of the day. // GoMn 8 //

children.text: śrutvāpi dānaniyatāṃ sa kathāṃ cakampe dṛṣṭvāpi yācanakam udvijate kadaryaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even hearing a story about giving, that miser trembled; even seeing a beggar, he was distressed;

children.text: tyāgapriyaiḥ saha cakāra na lokayātrāṃ nando jahāsa kila dāyakam īkṣamāṇaḥ || GoMn_9 ||
children.translated_text: he did not conduct worldly dealings with those who loved generosity; <s>Nanda</s>, it is said, laughed when he saw a donor. // GoMn 9 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā parasyāpi sa deyadharmān īrṣyākaṣāyākṣipuṭo babhūva |
children.translated_text: Seeing even another's charitable acts, his eyes became contracted with the bitterness of envy;

children.text: tyāgātmabhiḥ sārdham anāryakarmā cakāra naiva krayavikrayaṃ saḥ || GoMn_10 ||
children.translated_text: that ignoble-acting one never engaged in buying or selling with those of generous nature. // GoMn 10 //

children.text: atha nandaḥ kadā cin niṣpratīkāraparuṣavedanākrāntadeho niyatam ahaṃ mariṣyāmīty utpannabhayaviṣādaśokadainyamānasaḥ putraṃ candanam āhūyābravīt | vatsa candana mayā hi mahatā pariśrameṇa dravyam upārjitaṃ paripālitaṃ ca | tat putra mama priyam anusmaratā na tvayā kasmai kiṃ cid api pradeyam iti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, one day, his body seized by severe and irremediable painful sensations, his mind filled with fear, despair, grief, and wretchedness, [thinking] 'I shall surely die,' summoned his son <s>Candana</s> and said: 'My child <s>Candana</s>, I have earned and guarded wealth with great toil. Therefore, son, remembering my wishes, you must not give anything to anyone.'

children.text: caṇḍālaśālāṃ vrajata pragalbhān paśyāmi yuṣmān na punar yathāham |
children.translated_text: 'I see you — the bold ones — going to the <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) quarter, never to return!' —

children.text: sa yācakān nityasamīkṣyakārī provāca roṣasphuritākṣikośaḥ || GoMn_11 ||
children.translated_text: thus he spoke to the beggars, always watchful, his eye-sockets quivering with rage. // GoMn 11 //

children.text: kṛtvā sa karmāṇi nikṛṣṭakarmā mṛtas tapasvī mṛta eva pūrvam |
children.translated_text: Having performed base deeds, that wretched one of base conduct died — dead even while alive;

children.text: caṇḍālanāryāḥ pratisandhibandhaṃ cakāra kukṣau kṣatalocanāyāḥ || GoMn_12 ||
children.translated_text: he took rebirth (<s>pratisandhihandha</s>) in the womb of a <s>caṇḍāla</s> woman, blind, with damaged eyes. // GoMn 12 //

children.text: sattvānāṃ caritaṃ citram acintyā karmaṇāṃ gatiḥ |
children.translated_text: The conduct of beings is strange; the course of <s>karma</s> is inconceivable;

children.text: malinā bata kāmānāṃ vṛttiḥ paryantadāruṇā || GoMn_13 ||
children.translated_text: the ways of desires are indeed impure, terrible at their culmination. // GoMn 13 //

children.text: andhā vṛddhā daridrā ca caṇḍālī dīrgharogiṇī |
children.translated_text: Blind, old, destitute, a <s>caṇḍāla</s> woman, afflicted with chronic disease —

children.text: saṃrāgāyatanaṃ yātā dhik phalatvaṃ prasaṅginām || GoMn_14 ||
children.translated_text: she became the abode of his passion — fie upon the fruitfulness of those enslaved [by desire]! // GoMn 14 //

children.text: atha sā vṛddhacaṇḍālī krameṇa dārakaṃ prasūtā | tasyā etad abhūt | nūnam ahaṃ devatābhir anukampitā yena me putrako jātaḥ | niyatam ayam āyuṣmān abhivardhamāno mamāndhāyā yaṣṭibhūto bhaviṣyatīti | sā praharṣākṣiptahṛdayā samīpaparivartanīṃ caṇḍālīm abravīt | jñāyatāṃ tāvad bhaginī kīdṛśo 'yaṃ dāraka iti | sā tam ālokyābravīt | īdṛśo mā bhūt kaś cid iti | kathaṃ katham iti ca | tatra paryanuyuktā provāca |
children.translated_text: Then that old <s>caṇḍāla</s> woman in due course gave birth to a child. This was her thought: 'Surely I have been favored by the deities, for a son has been born to me! Certainly this fortunate one, growing up, will become a walking-staff for me who am blind.' She, her heart transported with joy, said to a <s>caṇḍāla</s> woman who was nearby: 'Please see, sister, what this child looks like.' And she, looking at him, said: 'May no one be like this!' 'How so, how so?' And when pressed further, she said:

children.text: niśāntāṅgārasaṃkāśaḥ kubjaś cipiṭanāsikaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Resembling the embers at the end of night, hunchbacked, with a flat nose,

children.text: andhaḥ saṃkucitāṅgaś ca tava putro 'yam īdṛśaḥ || GoMn_15 ||
children.translated_text: blind, with contracted limbs — such is this son of yours.' // GoMn 15 //

children.text:
sā nairāśyopahatasaṃtānā āha | hā hā hatāham adhanyety evaṃ paraṃ vaikalyam
ājagāma | āha ca |
children.translated_text: She, her expectations destroyed, said: 'Alas, alas! I am slain! I am wretched!' — and thus fell into utter distress. And she said:

children.text: na tathānāgatāḥ pīḍāṃ kurvanty arthāḥ śarīriṇām |
children.translated_text: 'Things that have not yet arrived do not cause such pain to embodied beings

children.text: saṃprāptā dhvaṃsamānās tu janayanti yathā vyathām || GoMn_16 ||
children.translated_text: as those which, having arrived, are collapsing — they generate anguish. // GoMn 16 //

children.text: atha sā jarjaracaṇḍālī vyasanavikṛtahṛdayā sasvaraṃ ruroda |
children.translated_text: Then that decrepit <s>caṇḍāla</s> woman, her heart distorted by misfortune, wept aloud:

children.text: patitāham anarthakardame chalitā pūrvakṛtena karmaṇā |
children.translated_text: 'I have fallen into the mire of calamity, tripped by the deeds done in former [lives];

children.text: kim iyaṃ mṛtamāritā kṛtā vidhinā niṣkaruṇena me punaḥ || GoMn_17 ||
children.translated_text: why has fate, merciless, made me killed though already dead? // GoMn 17 //

children.text: vyasanaṃ nirupāyadāruṇaṃ vyasanasyaiva mamopari sthitam |
children.translated_text: 'Calamity, remediless and terrible, is piled upon calamity for me;

children.text: animittakhareva lakṣyate mayi daivasya gatir garīyasī || GoMn_18 ||
children.translated_text: the course of fate — that weighty one — is manifest upon me, like a causeless donkey-kick. // GoMn 18 //

children.text: aham eva khalūrikā kṛtā kṛpaṇā kiṃ nu vipattipattriṇā |
children.translated_text: 'I alone, wretched, have been made a target — by what arrow of misfortune?

children.text: vidhinā kṛpaṇapramāthinā kupiteneva vihīnakarmaṇā || GoMn_19 ||
children.translated_text: By angry fate — that crusher of the wretched — which acts as if devoid of [good] deeds. // GoMn 19 //

children.text: apayuktavilocanāṃ satīm aśanapra
sra
children.translated_text: [lacuna]

children.text: vaṇādivarjitām |
children.translated_text: food and gifts,

children.text: jaratīm upahatya ko guṇo vada māṃ nirghṛṇacitta daiva he || GoMn_20 ||
children.translated_text: an old woman already afflicted — what merit is there in striking me? Tell me, O merciless-hearted fate! // GoMn 20 //
'Me, a woman deprived of sight, lacking even

children.text: evam anyathā ca sā tapasvinī bahuprakāraṃ viruroda |
children.translated_text: Thus and in other ways that wretched woman wept in many fashions.

children.text: atha garbhamalopaliptadehaṃ tanayaṃ taṃ taruṇa
ṃ
children.translated_text: [lacuna]

children.text: vraṇāyamānam |
children.translated_text: festering [with sores] —

children.text: kupiteva khare mahītale sā vinicikṣepa rujāhataṃ rudantam || GoMn_21 ||
children.translated_text: she, as if angered, flung him on the rough ground — wounded and crying. // GoMn 21 //
Then that infant, his body smeared with the filth of the womb,

children.text: karmāṇi tīvraparitāpaphalāni kṛtvā kiṃ rodiṣi tvam adhunā hatabhāgadheya |
children.translated_text: 'Having performed deeds whose fruit is intense torment, why do you cry now, O ill-fated one?

children.text: duḥkhaṃ mayā saha sahasva bahuprakāraṃ tvaṃ putraketi vilalāpa tapasvinī sā || GoMn_22 ||
children.translated_text: Endure with me this manifold suffering, O my child!' — thus that wretched woman lamented. // GoMn 22 //

children.text: mithyāvikalpapariṇāmasukhānupātī sneho vivṛddhim upayāti sukhe sthitānām |
children.translated_text: The affection of those established in happiness — which follows upon the pleasure of false imaginings and their transformations — grows;

children.text: duḥkhopataptamanasāṃ śithilībhavanti pāśās tv amī priyavikalpamayā janānām || GoMn_23 ||
children.translated_text: but for those whose minds are afflicted by suffering, these bonds made of the imagination of loved ones become loosened. // GoMn 23 //

children.text: atha sa tapasvī cāṇḍāladārako garbhamalākledopaliptabībhatsāśrayas tīvrāmagandhaḥ kṛmimakṣikāśatanipānabhūtaḥ pipīlakagaṇāhṛtakaṣṭāvispaṣṭaceṣṭakaracaraṇavadano māṃsapiṇḍa iva pratyagraḥ kṣititalopanikṣipto vāyasair apy abhibhūyamāno nāraka iva svakarmāvadhūtajīvitaśeṣaḥ paraṃ kṛcchram udvahati sma |
children.translated_text: Then that wretched <s>caṇḍāla</s> child — his body disgustingly smeared with the moisture of womb-filth, of intensely putrid smell, a drinking-place for hundreds of worms and flies, his limbs carried away by columns of ants so that his movements of hands, feet, and face were barely discernible, like a fresh lump of flesh — thrown on the ground, overpowered even by crows, like a being in hell whose remaining life was shaken off by his own <s>karma</s> — endured supreme misery.

children.text: tasya karmāparādhena mātuḥ stanyaṃ kṣayaṃ gatam |
children.translated_text: By the fault of his [past] <s>karma</s>, his mother's milk dried up;

children.text: ucitām api sā bhikṣāṃ na lebhe duḥkhabhāginī || GoMn_24 ||
children.translated_text: even the alms she was accustomed to, that partaker of suffering, she did not obtain. // GoMn 24 //

children.text: sā prasūtiparikleśaparikṣāmatarāśrayā |
children.translated_text: She, her body emaciated by the affliction of childbirth,

children.text: jarārujāparikliṣṭā pretīvābhūd bhayaṃkarī || GoMn_25 ||
children.translated_text: tormented by the pains of old age and disease, became terrifying like a <s>pretī</s> (female ghost). // GoMn 25 //

children.text: ācāmamātrām api nāma nāsau lebhe śunām apy anivāraṇīyām |
children.translated_text: She did not obtain even a mouthful of water — which even dogs cannot be denied —

children.text: tasyaiva vā karmabhir ātmajasya svakarmabhir vā pariṇāmatiktaiḥ || GoMn_26 ||
children.translated_text: either because of the <s>karmas</s> of her own son, or because of her own <s>karmas</s>, bitter in their ripening. // GoMn 26 //

children.text: atha sa cāṇḍāladārako daivasāmārthyāt krameṇa yadā caṅkramaṇakṣamaḥ saṃvṛttas tadāsya mātrā daṇḍaḥ khaṇḍamallakaṃ cārpitaṃ gacchedānīm adhanyānubhavāśubhānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākam iti | atha sa caṇḍālaśiśur bhikṣāhetoś candanasyaiva gṛham upajagāma |
children.translated_text: Then, when by the power of fate that <s>caṇḍāla</s> child gradually became capable of walking, his mother gave him a stick and a broken begging bowl, [saying]: 'Go now, O unlucky one, and experience the fruit-ripening of your inauspicious <s>karmas</s>.' Then that <s>caṇḍāla</s> boy went to the very house of <s>Candana</s> to beg.

children.text: pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva jagāmāsau svam ālayam |
children.translated_text: By that very prior habit, he went to his own [former] dwelling;

children.text: karmaivātyartham abhyastaṃ dehināṃ deśikāyate || GoMn_27 ||
children.translated_text: <s>karma</s> alone, when excessively practiced, serves as a guide for embodied beings. // GoMn 27 //

children.text: adrākṣīc candanaḥ sārthavāhas taṃ cāṇḍālakumārakaṃ daṇḍakhaṇḍaśarāvavyagrahastaṃ lālājalapariklinnavadanaṃ bhinibhināyamānamakṣikāśatanipānabhūtam bāhyādhyātmikamalopahatagātraṃ rathyāreṇuvirūkṣitakatipayaśiroruhaṃ prakṛtikharadarbhasaṃstaraparivartanavilikhitatanum akṛtaśaucasaṃskāravidhānaṃ vikṛtanāsikābilāgalitasiṃhāṇakhaṇḍaparyavanaddhabībhatsānanaṃ vīthīmukhāt pravicitya dhānyapulākān romanthāyamānaṃ pūtanārūpam ivātivirūpaṃ mūrtimantaṃ saṃvegaṃ sākṣād iva pāpmānam alakṣmīpuñjam iva saṃpiṇḍitam apūrvam iva piśācanirmāṇaṃ vipākasarvasvam ivāśubhasya karmaṇaḥ samāhāram iva saṃsāraduḥkhānāṃ
rāhumu
children.translated_text: like another <s>Rāhu</s>

children.text: khānyam iva jagaccakṣuṣāṃ rahasyabhūmim ivānādeyatāyā vigrahavantam iva paribhavam upanighātam iva nagarasya pratyādeśam ivāpakāriṇāṃ nilayam ivādhanyatāyāḥ padam iva daurbhāgyasya gṛhadvāraikadeśe niṣaṇṇaṃ daṇḍena kākān nivārayantam | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ pūrvavairānuśayodbodhitakopa iva sarabhaso dauvārikam abravīt | are kāpuruṣa nirvāsayainam amaṅgalam alakṣmīkam aprekṣaṇīyaṃ caṇḍālādhamam | tathā cainaṃ nirbhartsaya yathā na punar ihāgacched iti |
children.translated_text: for the eyes of the world, as if the secret ground of unacceptability, as if humiliation embodied, as if a blow to the city, as if a rebuke to transgressors, as if the abode of wretchedness, as if the very seat of misfortune — seated at a corner of the house-gate, warding off crows with his stick. Seeing him, and as if with anger roused by the recollection of former enmity, he furiously addressed the doorkeeper: 'Ho, you wretch! Drive out this inauspicious, ill-fortuned, unsightly, basest of <s>caṇḍālas</s>! And threaten him so that he never comes here again!'

<s>Candana</s> the merchant saw that <s>caṇḍāla</s> boy — his hands occupied with a stick and a broken earthen bowl, his face drenched with drool, a drinking-place for hundreds of humming flies, his body defiled by external and internal filth, his few strands of hair roughened by street-dust, his body scratched by rolling on the naturally coarse <s>darbha</s> grass-bedding, with no practice of cleansing or ritual purification, his disgusting face bound with pieces of dried mucus dripping from his misshapen nostrils, picking out grain-husks from the street entrance and chewing on them — like a <s>Pūtanā</s> (demoness) in form, supremely ugly, religious dread (<s>saṃvega</s>) made manifest, as if Sin personified, a mass of misfortune compressed, as if an unprecedented creation of <s>piśāca</s> (evil spirits), the entire fruition of inauspicious <s>karma</s>, a compendium as it were of all the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: sa tatheti pratiśrutya taṃ caṇḍālakumārakam |
children.translated_text: He, having agreed 'So be it,' that <s>caṇḍāla</s> boy —

children.text: daṇḍena prerayām āsa paruṣāṃ giram udgiran || GoMn_28 ||
children.translated_text: he drove away with a stick, uttering harsh words. // GoMn 28 //

children.text: yadi tvāṃ punar āyātam iha paśyāmi kaśmala |
children.translated_text: 'If I see you come here again, you wretch,

children.text: asmāt kaṣṭataraṃ te 'haṃ kariṣyāmīti nigraham || GoMn_29 ||
children.translated_text: I shall do to you something worse than this!' — thus the restraint. // GoMn 29 //

children.text: krauryābhyāsāvaliptasya manaso vṛttivaikṛtam |
children.translated_text: The perverted conduct of a mind smeared with the habit of cruelty

children.text: na hi saṃkocam āyāti khalānāṃ kṛpaṇeṣv api || GoMn_30 ||
children.translated_text: does not shrink back even before the wretched, in the case of the wicked. // GoMn 30 //

children.text: papāta bhūmau kṛpaṇaḥ sa bālo daṇḍābhighātakṣatapṛṣṭhavaṃśaḥ |
children.translated_text: That wretched boy fell to the ground, his backbone shattered by the blow of the stick,

children.text: prakāśayan karmaphalaṃ svam eva karmātiraudraṃ narakasya tasya || GoMn_31 ||
children.translated_text: manifesting the very fruit of his own <s>karma</s> — his exceedingly terrible <s>karma</s> of [a former] hell. // GoMn 31 //

children.text: atha sa tapasvī bhagnaśiraḥkapālabhāgo vikuñcitajānumaṇḍalaḥ pāṣāṇaśakalakapālaśarkarāparikṣatakṣāmajaṅghābāhudaṇḍakaḥ samantato vigalitarudhiradhārāvasicyamānavigraho mahīrajaḥkapālāvaruddhavadanavivaro vikṣiptadaṇḍakaḥ saṃcūrṇitamallako dharaṇitalavikīrṇabhikṣāśeṣas tīvravedanābhyāhataśarīro matsya iva prataptasikatāmadhyagataḥ saṃparivartate sma | athāsya mātā cintayām āsa | kiṃ nu me putrakaḥ prapāte patitaḥ syāc chunā vā bhakṣita uta gavā jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ paribhūya vā bāladārakair viheṭhito mārgapranaṣṭo vānyena pathā gataḥ | kiṃ vā nāgacchatīti sā putrasnehākṛṣṭahṛdayā putra putreti krandatī taṃ deśam upajagāma | sa ca bāladārako jananyāḥ svaraṃ pratyabhijñāya bhṛśataraṃ vicukrośa |
children.translated_text: Then that wretched one, with his skull cracked, his kneecaps contracted, his thin shanks and stick-like arms wounded by stone-fragments, potsherd-pieces, and pebbles, his body drenched all around by streams of flowing blood, his mouth-opening blocked by dust and skull-fragments, his stick flung away, his bowl crushed, his remaining alms scattered on the ground, his body struck by intense pain — like a fish cast upon hot sand — rolled about. Then his mother thought: 'Has my child perhaps fallen into a ditch? Or has he been eaten by a dog? Or killed by a cow? Or teased and tormented by young boys? Or has he lost his way and gone by another path? Why does he not come?' She, her heart drawn by love for her son, crying 'Son! Son!' — came to that place. And that young boy, recognizing his mother's voice, cried out all the more intensely.

children.text: samānasukhaduḥkhānāṃ suhṛdām api saṃgame |
children.translated_text: Even for friends who share the same joys and sorrows, at their meeting

children.text: navībhavanti duḥkhāni vyatītāny api dehinām || GoMn_32 ||
children.translated_text: past sufferings become fresh again for embodied beings. // GoMn 32 //

children.text: mātety apūrvam evaitad viśrambhāyatanaṃ bhuvi |
children.translated_text: 'Mother' — this alone is an unprecedented place of trust on earth;

children.text: putra ity eva niṣyandaḥ snehasyāsya duratyayaḥ || GoMn_33 ||
children.translated_text: 'Son' — this is indeed the irresistible outflow of this [natural] affection. // GoMn 33 //

children.text: ambeti dīnāṃ giram īrayantaṃ sā taṃ pariṣvajya tanupralāpam |
children.translated_text: Embracing him as he uttered the piteous word 'Mother!' — with feeble cries,

children.text: ruroda tīvrāyatadīnakaṇṭhā ninādayantī puracatvarāṇi || GoMn_34 ||
children.translated_text: she wept, her throat drawn out long in sharp, piteous tones, making the city-squares resound. // GoMn 34 //

children.text: kasya putra dayā nāsīt tvayi duḥkhaikabhājane |
children.translated_text: 'Who had no compassion for you, O son, who are the sole vessel of suffering?

children.text: garvitaḥ ko nv asau lakṣmyā gajakarṇāgralolayā || GoMn_35 ||
children.translated_text: Who is that one so proud of fortune that wavers like the tip of an elephant's ear? // GoMn 35 //

children.text: prakāśitam idaṃ kena kṛpaṇe tvayi pauruṣam |
children.translated_text: 'Who has displayed this prowess upon you, a wretched one?

children.text: tvayi praharataḥ kasya bhūmau na patitaḥ karaḥ || GoMn_36 ||
children.translated_text: Whose hand did not fall to the ground when striking you? // GoMn 36 //

children.text: hatas tvaṃ kena me vatsa niranukrośacetasā |
children.translated_text: 'By whom, with a merciless heart, have you been struck, my child?

children.text: nihataḥ pūrvakeṇaiva kaṭupākena karmaṇā || GoMn_37 ||
children.translated_text: You are struck by the bitter fruit of <s>karma</s> done in former [lives]. // GoMn 37 //

children.text: idam anāryatācihnaṃ kena tvayi vidarśitam |
children.translated_text: 'By whom has this mark of ignobility been displayed upon you?

children.text: ko nv asau mānuṣākāro rakṣasām anuśikṣyate || GoMn_38 ||
children.translated_text: Who is that one, human in appearance, who follows the ways of <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons)? // GoMn 38 //

children.text: āyasaṃ hṛdayam kasya kasya vajramayaḥ karaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Whose heart is made of iron? Whose hand is made of diamond?

children.text: kasya vāk saviṣā kasya tvayi nāsīd dayālutā || GoMn_39 ||
children.translated_text: Whose speech is poisonous? Who had no tenderness toward you? // GoMn 39 //

children.text: nihīnakulaje bāle suhṛdbandhuvivarjite |
children.translated_text: 'Upon a child of low birth, friendless and kinless,

children.text: jātyandhe parapiṇḍāśe tvayi kiṃ roṣakāraṇam || GoMn_40 ||
children.translated_text: blind from birth, living on others' scraps — upon you, what cause for anger?' // GoMn 40 //

children.text: sa bālabhāvāt kṛpaṇo varākaḥ svabhyastamātsaryatayā tayā ca |
children.translated_text: That wretched, pitiable boy, out of his childish nature and habitual miserliness,

children.text: śuśoca bhaikṣaṃ kṣitiviprakīrṇaṃ na tu kṣaracchoṇitam ātmadeham || GoMn_41 ||
children.translated_text: lamented the alms scattered on the ground, but not his own body streaming with blood. // GoMn 41 //

children.text: atha vṛddhacaṇḍālī taṃ dārakaṃ kṣatavikṣataśarīraṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ pāṇinā parāmṛśantī provāca | kena te putrakeyam avasthā kṛtā nirdayena pāpakarmaṇā puruṣādhameneti | sa prāha | amba āryacandanena puruṣo 'bhihito nirvāsayainam amaṅgalam alakṣmīkam aprekṣaṇīyaṃ caṇḍālādhamam | tenāham evaṃ pīḍita iti | atha sā vṛddhacaṇḍālī dīrgham uṣṇaṃ viniśvasya pañcāṅgulam abhinipīḍayantī kopaparuṣākṣaram ity avocat |
children.translated_text: Then the old <s>caṇḍālī</s> woman, gently touching that boy's wounded and lacerated body with her hand, said: "Who, O child, has brought you to this state — what merciless, evil-acting, worst of men?" He replied: "Mother, a man called Ārya-<s>Candana</s> struck me — "Expel this inauspicious, unfortunate, unsightly, lowest of <s>caṇḍālas</s>!" Thus have I been tormented." Then that old <s>caṇḍālī</s> woman, heaving a long, hot sigh, pressing her five fingers [against her breast], spoke with words harsh with anger:

children.text: alpāyuṣi kutas tasminn āryatā puruṣādhame |
children.translated_text: "Where is nobility in that short-lived, worst of men,

children.text: vyasanopahate bāle tvayīdaṃ yasya vaikṛtam || GoMn_42 ||
children.translated_text: whose cruelty falls upon a calamity-stricken child like you?" // GoMn 42 //

children.text: evaṃ tasyāḥ śokavaśam upagatāyāḥ kṛpaṇāyāḥ samīpe mahājanakāyaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ | atrāntare
children.translated_text: Thus, as that wretched woman had fallen into the power of grief, a great crowd of people gathered near her. At that very moment —

children.text: ākṛṣyamāṇahṛdayaḥ kṛpayā mahatyā vaineyakṛtyam avalambya vināyakāgryaḥ |
children.translated_text: His heart drawn by great compassion, the foremost Guide, relying on the task of [converting] those to be trained,

children.text: prāvikṣad akṣatamanā bhagavān purīṃ tāṃ buddho vibuddhanavapaṅkajasaṃkrameṇa || GoMn_43 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>, with undisturbed mind, entered that city with steps [like] newly opened lotuses. // GoMn 43 //

children.text: cāmīkarādrim iva jaṅgamam āpatantaṃ taṃ tāyinaṃ svakiraṇaiḥ pariviṣṭamūrtim |
children.translated_text: The citizens bowed from afar — with heads inclined in loosened reverence — to that Protector approaching

children.text: paurāḥ prasādaśithilāvanataiḥ śirobhir dūrāt praṇemur upaśāntabhavaprapañcam || GoMn_44 ||
children.translated_text: like a moving golden mountain, his body surrounded by his own rays, in whom the proliferation of worldly existence had been stilled. // GoMn 44 //

children.text: sitabhavanagatās taṃ saṃbhramodbhrāntaceṣṭās taḍita iva sumeroḥ śṛṅgaparyantalagnāḥ |
children.translated_text: Young women on the white buildings, with movements flustered in excitement, like lightning-flashes clinging to the peak of <s>Sumeru</s>,

children.text: upaśamam iva sākṣād āpatantaṃ taruṇyo maṇiguṇakusumaughair arcayām āsur āryam || GoMn_45 ||
children.translated_text: worshipped the Noble One approaching as if Tranquility itself had arrived in person, with streams of jewels, garlands, and flowers. // GoMn 45 //

children.text: apetapāṣāṇakapālaśarkaraḥ samaḥ sa nimnonnatavarjito 'bhavat |
children.translated_text: Free from stones, potsherd-fragments, and gravel, level, devoid of hollows and elevations,

children.text: bhuvaḥ pradeśo haritārdralepanaḥ pramuktapuṣpaprakarottaracchadaḥ || GoMn_46 ||
children.translated_text: the ground became fresh and green-anointed, with a canopy of scattered flowers above. // GoMn 46 //

children.text: nibaddhajīmūtavitānam ambaraṃ samudgatendrāyudhatoraṇaṃ babhau |
children.translated_text: The sky shone with a bound canopy of clouds and with an archway of risen rainbows;

children.text: vavuḥ śanaiḥ sparśasukhāḥ samīraṇāḥ sirindhrikāpuṣparajovikarṣiṇaḥ || GoMn_47 ||
children.translated_text: breezes blew gently, pleasant to the touch, carrying the pollen of <s>sirindhrikā</s> flowers. // GoMn 47 //

children.text: tamālanīlotpalapattravṛṣṭayo nipetur antargatamattaṣaṭpadāḥ |
children.translated_text: Showers of <s>tamāla</s> and dark blue-lotus petals fell, with intoxicated bees within them —

children.text: vipāṭitasyeva vimānakoṭibhir nabhastalasyāvayavās tatas tataḥ || GoMn_48 ||
children.translated_text: fragments, as it were, of the burst vault of heaven from its palace-peaks, falling here and there. // GoMn 48 //

children.text: puṇyaprabhāvajanite bhagavān niṣadya padme sahasradalake rathacakramātre |
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, the supremely compassionate one, having seated himself on a lotus born of the power of merit — a thousand-petalled [lotus] the size of a chariot wheel, releasing fragrance from the unfading ripening of merit —

children.text: amlānapuṇyaparipākavimuktagandhe taṃ candanaṃ paramakāruṇikaḥ śaśāsa || GoMn_49 ||
children.translated_text: admonished that <s>Candana</s>. // GoMn 49 //

children.text: yenārjitaṃ dhanam idaṃ paripālitaṃ ca svedopadigdhavapuṣā kuṭukuñcakena |
children.translated_text: "This wealth that was earned and protected by the hunchback, his body smeared with sweat —

children.text: nandaḥ pitā tava sa eva phalāni bhuṅkte tiktāni matsaraviṣadrumasaṃbhavāni || GoMn_50 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, your father, he alone now enjoys the fruits, bitter ones, born from the poison-tree of miserliness. // GoMn 50 //

children.text: sthānād itaḥ punar ayaṃ kaluṣāntarātmā yāsyaty apāyam anupāyabhayapratiṣṭham |
children.translated_text: From this state, this one of corrupt inner soul shall again go to a realm of woe, founded on the fear of having no recourse,

children.text: arciṣmatā hutabhujā vinikīrṇadehā yasmin vasanti vivaśā bahavaḥ kadaryāḥ || GoMn_51 ||
children.translated_text: where many wretches, their bodies scattered by blazing fire, dwell helplessly. // GoMn 51 //

children.text: etāṃ suhṛjjanaviṣādakarīm avasthām ālokya mohatamasaḥ pratibimbabhūtām |
children.translated_text: Seeing this condition that causes distress to loved ones, a reflection-image, as it were, of the darkness of delusion —

children.text: svāṅgān nikṛtya piśitāny api ko na dadyāt saṃsāravartmani naraḥ parivartamānaḥ || GoMn_52 ||
children.translated_text: what person, revolving on the path of <s>saṃsāra</s>, would not give even flesh cut from his own limbs? // GoMn 52 //

children.text: kleśāndhakāravadanā vikarāladaṃṣṭrā dāvāgnidagdhaśikharā iva śailapādāḥ |
children.translated_text: With mouths [gaping] in the darkness of affliction, with terrifying fangs, like mountain-bases whose peaks are burned by forest-fire —

children.text: āyāsino yad anavāptajalā bhramanti pretāḥ phalaṃ tad api lobhaviṣadrumāṇām || GoMn_53 ||
children.translated_text: that <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), exhausted and unable to find water, wander about — that too is the fruit of the poison-trees of greed. // GoMn 53 //

children.text: tṛṣṇāvidāritamukhāḥ samupetya bālā dūrvāpravālaharitopanitambalekhām |
children.translated_text: Some unfortunate ones, their mouths split open by thirst, approach a stream

children.text: saṃśuṣkapaṅkapaṭalaprakarāntarālāṃ paśyanti ke cid analajvalitāṃ sravantīm || GoMn_54 ||
children.translated_text: whose banks are lined with green <s>dūrvā</s> grass-shoots, yet they see it burning with fire amid expanses of dried mud-layers. // GoMn 54 //

children.text: dehān dahanti dahanā iva candrapādāḥ śītā raver api karā hi samudgiranti |
children.translated_text: Moon-rays burn their bodies like flames; the cool rays of the sun indeed scorch them;

children.text: aṅgāracūrṇaparuṣāś ca bhavanty amīṣāṃ meghāmbuśīkaramuco 'pi kadambavātāḥ || GoMn_55 ||
children.translated_text: and even the gusts of wind that shower rain-cloud droplets become harsh as coal-dust for them. // GoMn 55 //

children.text: āśīviṣair iva nirīkṣitamātraśobhāḥ pretair drumā vimalanīlacalatpalāśāḥ |
children.translated_text: Trees with beautiful, trembling blue leaves, merely gazed upon by <s>pretas</s> as if by venomous serpents,

children.text: sadyo bhavanti pariśuṣkaviśīrṇaparṇāḥ pratyādiśanta iva matsariṇo manuṣyān || GoMn_56 ||
children.translated_text: instantly become withered and shriveled in their leaves — as if dismissing miserly humans. // GoMn 56 //

children.text: pretopapattiniyatā vyasanābhighātā vyaktībhavanti manujeṣv api naikarūpāḥ |
children.translated_text: The afflictions destined for rebirth as <s>pretas</s> manifest in manifold forms even among humans —

children.text: kṣuttarṣaśītaparitāpabhayaprakārās tyāgadviṣāṃ vipad ataḥ parato 'numeyā || GoMn_57 ||
children.translated_text: varieties of hunger, thirst, cold, heat, and fear — therefore the calamity of those who hate generosity can be inferred from what lies beyond. // GoMn 57 //

children.text: pañcopatāpavirasākṣaram apragalbhaṃ dehīti yad vadati durbalamandamandam |
children.translated_text: When a wellborn, virtuous person, made timid by the five distresses, weakly and feebly utters 'Give!' with faltering words —

children.text: vittāvaliptamanasaḥ kulajo 'pi sādhuḥ sā nīcatā vibhavalobhaparājitānām || GoMn_58 ||
children.translated_text: that is the degradation of those defeated by the greed for wealth, [even if they have] minds anointed with riches. // GoMn 58 //

children.text: āśāvighātabhayasaṃkucitaś ca dīno dehīty api prasahate kṛpaṇo na vaktum |
children.translated_text: And the destitute wretch, shrunken with the fear of having his hopes dashed, cannot even bring himself to say 'Give!' [to a wealthy person] —

children.text: yan nirdhano dhanavataḥ puruṣān akāle maunavrataṃ tad api lobhakṛtaṃ narāṇām || GoMn_59 ||
children.translated_text: that a poor man remains silent before wealthy men at the wrong time — that vow of silence too is caused by greed among men. // GoMn 59 //

children.text: na janasya malo 'sti lobhatulyo na ca mātsaryasamaḥ paropaghātaḥ |
children.translated_text: There is no defilement of a person equal to greed; there is no harm to others equal to envy;

children.text: na ca yācakatulyam asti mitraṃ jagatāṃ tyāgasamo na bandhur anyaḥ || GoMn_60 ||
children.translated_text: there is no friend equal to a supplicant; for the world, there is no other kinsman equal to generosity. // GoMn 60 //

children.text: paripākavimuktagandhakośaṃ bhramarāḥ padmam iva prakāmagandham |
children.translated_text: Just as bees resort to a lotus that freely releases its fragrance from the treasure-house of its ripened [petals] —

children.text: apanītaparigrahāvalepaṃ bahavaḥ satpuruṣaṃ bhajanti santaḥ || GoMn_61 ||
children.translated_text: so many virtuous people resort to the good person who has cast off the arrogance of possessions. // GoMn 61 //

children.text: svamadārdraviśeṣakā gajendrā navakārtasvarabaddhapāśakakṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: Great elephants, moist with their own rut-ichor, bound with ropes of newly forged gold,

children.text: anuyānti janaṃ pradānaśīlaṃ javinaś cāmariṇaś ca vājimukhyāḥ || GoMn_62 ||
children.translated_text: follow the person of generous disposition; and so do swift horses of the finest breed, and yak-tail bearers. // GoMn 62 //

children.text: vinayābharaṇāḥ kriyābhiramyāḥ pramadāś citrakalāvidagdhabhāvāḥ |
children.translated_text: Women — adorned with modesty, delightful in their accomplishments, skilled in diverse arts —

children.text: upayānti narasya dāsabhāvaṃ kuśalair eva vaśīkṛtāḥ purāṇaiḥ || GoMn_63 ||
children.translated_text: come into the service of the man who has been won over by his own good <s>karmas</s> of past lives. // GoMn 63 //

children.text: bhavanāni vibhūtimanti meroḥ śikharāṇīva manojñadarśanāni |
children.translated_text: Magnificent dwellings, beautiful to behold, like the peaks of <s>Meru</s> —

children.text: svakṛtānavagītakarmamāyāracitāny eva mudā viśanti santaḥ || GoMn_64 ||
children.translated_text: the virtuous enter them joyfully, [mansions] fashioned by the magic of their own unblamed <s>karmas</s>. // GoMn 64 //

children.text: vinimīlitajātivādadoṣeṣv anapākṛṣṭacaritrabhūṣaṇeṣu |
children.translated_text: In families where the fault of caste-discrimination has been closed and whose ornament of conduct has not been removed —

children.text: upapattir adurlabhā kuleṣu vyapanītāvilamatsarāśrayāṇām || GoMn_65 ||
children.translated_text: rebirth is not difficult to obtain for those who have cast away [the refuge of] hesitation and envy. // GoMn 65 //

children.text: kusumastabakābhirāmaśobhaṃ naranārīnayanadvirephahāri |
children.translated_text: A body charming as clusters of flowers, captivating the bee-like eyes of men and women —

children.text: kuśalasya phalaṃ vapur narāṇāṃ mativīryācapalaprayāmadhīram || GoMn_66 ||
children.translated_text: that is the fruit of merit for humans: a body firm in the play of wisdom, heroism, and conduct. // GoMn 66 //

children.text: vikasatkumudākarātirekaprabhayā yad gaganaṃ sphuranti kīrtyā |
children.translated_text: The radiance with which they make the sky shine with fame surpassing the brilliance of a field of blooming night-lotuses —

children.text: gatalobhamalasya tā narāṇāṃ dyutayas tyāganiśākarasya ramyāḥ || GoMn_67 ||
children.translated_text: those beautiful splendors of the man free from the stain of greed [are like] the moon of generosity. // GoMn 67 //

children.text: viśadāgalitaiḥ śiromaṇīnāṃ kiraṇair yac chalayanti pādapīṭham |
children.translated_text: That the humble dependents of a king embellish his footstool with the clear, streaming rays of their crest-jewels —

children.text: nṛpater anujīvino vinītā madhuraṃ tyāgavanaspateḥ phalaṃ tat || GoMn_68 ||
children.translated_text: that is the sweet fruit of the tree of generosity. // GoMn 68 //

children.text: kṛpaṇāsu bavopabhogamātrāsv atha vā kaiva kathā vināśinīṣu |
children.translated_text: What need to speak of the wretched [pleasures], mere drops of enjoyment, perishable as they are?

children.text: niravadyasukhānubandhi ramyaṃ phalam āpnoti sanātanaṃ pradānāt || GoMn_69 ||
children.translated_text: Through giving, one attains a delightful, eternal fruit linked to faultless happiness. // GoMn 69 //

children.text: avadhūya balaṃ śamadviṣāṃ yaj jaladānām iva maṇḍalaṃ nabhasvān |
children.translated_text: Shaking off the force of the enemies of tranquility — as the wind [shakes off] a mass of rain-clouds —

children.text: padam avyayam āpnuvanti buddhā bhagavantas tad api pradānabijam || GoMn_70 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, attain the imperishable state — and that too has its seed in giving. // GoMn 70 //

children.text: abhibhūya parapravādipūgān paramārthaṃ gamayanti śāsanaṃ svam |
children.translated_text: Overcoming the hosts of rival teachers, the sages, sole rulers of the world, bring their own teaching to the ultimate truth —

children.text: munayo bhuvanaikaśāsitāras tad idaṃ tyāgaparaṃparāvasānam || GoMn_71 ||
children.translated_text: and that is the final culmination of the succession of generosity. // GoMn 71 //"

children.text: atha bhagavān pātrīkṛtādhyāśayaṃ taṃ janam avetya ratnatrayāvicalitaprasādaṃ saṃsāravāsavimukhaṃ bhavaduḥkhopaśamapratisaṃyuktām eva kathāṃ āviś cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, perceiving that the people's minds had been made into [fit] vessels — their devotion to the Three Jewels unwavering, their minds turned away from dwelling in <s>saṃsāra</s> — continued a discourse connected with the calming of the suffering of existence.

children.text: duḥkhāny amūni sati janmani saṃbhavanti kṣīṇe ca janmani na duḥkham upaiti bhūyaḥ |
children.translated_text: "These sufferings arise when there is birth, and when birth is extinguished, one no longer undergoes suffering;

children.text: janmakṣayāya matimān prayateta tasmād yaḥ prāptum icchati na duḥkhaśatābhighātam || GoMn_72 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, the wise person who does not wish to be struck by hundreds of sufferings should strive for the extinction of birth. // GoMn 72 //

children.text: duḥkhaṃ sakāraṇam idaṃ samupaity anādisaṃtānavartibhayaśokaviṣādayoni |
children.translated_text: This suffering, having a cause, arising from the source of fear, grief, and despair that operates in a beginningless continuum —

children.text: tṛṣṇāṃ pratītya viparītasukhābhimānavyāmohanīṃ tribhavanāṭakayogadhūrtāṃ || GoMn_73 ||
children.translated_text: it depends on <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), which deludes through the conceit of pleasure where there is none, the trickster of the drama of the three realms of existence. // GoMn 73 //

children.text: eṣo 'ham ity ucita eva manovidāhī satkāyadarśanamayaḥ puruṣasya kīlaḥ |
children.translated_text: The peg of <s>satkāyadarśana</s> (the view of a real self-body), which appropriately inflames the mind with "This am I" —

children.text: janmādhvani bhramayatīdam anādimadhyaṃ saṃsāracakram aparigraham apraśāntam || GoMn_74 ||
children.translated_text: it causes this wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>, beginningless and without middle, ungrasped and unquiet, to revolve on the road of births. // GoMn 74 //

children.text: sthitvā śīle vigatarajasi prāpya cetaḥ samādhiṃ
children.translated_text: Standing firm in <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline), free from passion, having attained the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) of the mind,

children.text: prajñālokair manasi śayitaṃ dhvāntam ullikhya kṛtsnam |
children.translated_text: scraping away with the light of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) all the darkness lying in the mind,

children.text: janmāmbhodher vyasanamahataḥ kṣemam āsādya pāraṃ
children.translated_text: reaching the safe shore of the great ocean of birth and its calamities,

children.text: saṃśāntātmā na divi bhuvi vā bhikṣur āyāti saṃkhyam || GoMn_75 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), with a stilled self, no longer comes to be reckoned in heaven or on earth. // GoMn 75 //

children.text: yair nirdagdhā matihutabhujā skandhasaṃbandhalakṣyī
children.translated_text: Those by whom <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) — whose bowstring is the arrangement of arrows of manifold calamities, whose target is the connection with the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) — has been burned by the fire of wisdom,

children.text: tṛṣṇā naikavyasanaviśikhāpātasaṃdhānamaurvī |
children.translated_text: [continued]

children.text: te 'smin dhanyā jagati sukhinas te ta evānavadyās
children.translated_text: they are the blessed ones in this world, they are the happy ones, they alone are the blameless,

children.text: teṣāṃ bhadraṃ sthitam abhimukhaṃ te bhayebhyo vimuktāḥ || GoMn_76 ||
children.translated_text: for them the good stands face to face — they are freed from all fears. // GoMn 76 //

children.text: riktākāradravaratirasāsvādaparyastabuddher
children.translated_text: For one whose mind is overturned by tasting the pleasure of desire in its empty appearances,

children.text: leśanāpi vyanusṛtavato jālinīṃ citramāyām |
children.translated_text: who has followed even slightly the net of wondrous illusion (<s>māyā</s>) —

children.text: āyāsinyaḥ śirasi vipadaḥ saṃcaranti pragalbhā
children.translated_text: bold misfortunes roam upon his head,

children.text: janmābhyastaṃ sucaritaphalaṃ vyartham eva prayāti || GoMn_77 ||
children.translated_text: and the fruit of good conduct practiced over lifetimes goes utterly to waste. // GoMn 77 //

children.text: āyāsinīṃ bhavavibhūtim avāptukāmaiḥ śāntiṃ parāṃ ca parataḥ kuśalaṃ praceyam |
children.translated_text: By those who wish to attain supreme peace, let merit be gathered beyond the wearisome splendor of existence; the venomous serpent released to kill the king became, through merits, a necklace white as a bright moon. // GoMn 78 //

children.text: āśīviṣo narapater nidhanāya mukto hāro babhūva kuśalaiḥ sphuṭacandragauraḥ || GoMn_78 ||
children.translated_text: [continued from above]

children.text: kiṃ ca bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: duḥkhadviṣā hṛdi na lobhakalir niṣevyo janmāntaropacitalobhaviṣāśayasya |
children.translated_text: The <s>kali</s> (stain) of greed should not be harbored in the heart by one who hates suffering — [for greed is] one whose disposition is poisoned by greed accumulated over lifetimes;

children.text: śāntātmano 'pi kila nirvivaraṃ babhūva bhaktābhihārasamaye mukham eva bhikṣoḥ || GoMn_79 ||
children.translated_text: even for the one of stilled soul, at the time of the offering of food, the mouth of the <s>bhikṣu</s> became indeed tightly [closed, i.e., the miser's mouth is shut to giving]. // GoMn 79 //

children.text: tasmāt pradānasalilaiḥ snapayantu santo mātsaryapaṅkamalināni manogṛhāṇi |
children.translated_text: Therefore, let the virtuous bathe the houses of their minds, stained with the mud of envy, with the waters of giving;

children.text: lobhānalendhanam idaṃ nidhanaṃ dhanaṃ vo yāvan na yāti vipadagniśikhāvalīḍham || GoMn_80 ||
children.translated_text: [give] before this wealth of yours — fuel for the fire of greed — is licked away by the flame-garlands of the fire of calamity, going to destruction. // GoMn 80 //

children.text: śrutvā vacāṃsi sa jano jagadekabandhor nandasya tāṃ ca vipadaṃ vipulām udīkṣya |
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of the sole kinsman of the world, and beholding that vast calamity of <s>Nanda</s>,

children.text: vikṣipya matsaramayīṃ manasas tamisrāṃ dānādikaṃ sucaritaṃ prathayāṃ babhūva || GoMn_81 ||
children.translated_text: the people, casting off the darkness of envy from their minds, began to spread the practice of giving and other good deeds. // GoMn 81 //

children.text: iti matsaranandāvadānam ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the story of the Envious <s>Nanda</s> (<s>Matsara-Nanda-avadāna</s>). ||

children.text: 8. Megha
children.translated_text: 8. <s>Megha</s>

children.text: puṇyair vitṛptim upayānti na bodhisattvāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> do not reach satiation with merits

children.text: kāmaiḥ pramādina iva pratipattivāmaiḥ |
children.translated_text: as the heedless do with pleasures that are perverse in their attainment;

children.text: rājyāśrayāṇy api sukhāny avadhīrya dhīrāḥ
children.translated_text: steadfast, disdaining even the pleasures that depend on kingship,

children.text: puṇyāya puṇyanidhayaḥ śramam āśrayante || GoMe_1 ||
children.translated_text: those treasuries of merit exert themselves for the sake of merit. // GoMe 1 //

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate
children.translated_text: As the tradition relates —

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila bhagavān prakṛtidakṣiṇo dakṣiṇāpathe rājā babhūva ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, by nature generous, became a king in the <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s> (the southern region).

children.text: saṃtarpayām āsa yataḥ sa lokaṃ dānāmbubhiḥ sasyam ivāmbugarbhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Since he nourished the world with the waters of giving, as a rain-cloud [nourishes] crops with its waters,

children.text: tato mahāmegha iti kṣitīśo yathārthanāmātiśayo babhūva || GoMe_2 ||
children.translated_text: therefore that lord of the earth was surpassingly known by the fitting name <s>Mahāmegha</s> (Great Cloud). // GoMe 2 //

children.text: na tasya rājyadyutivistareṣu vyāsaktadīnaṃ hṛdayaṃ babhūva |
children.translated_text: His heart was not basely attached to the expanses of royal splendor;

children.text: anarthabhūtān sa parārtham arthān drumaḥ phalānīva babhāra sādhuḥ || GoMe_3 ||
children.translated_text: that virtuous one bore his wealth for the benefit of others — [considering it] purposeless [for himself] — as a tree [bears] its fruits. // GoMe 3 //

children.text: babhūva tasmin pitarīva loko viśrambhasaṃbhogasukhapragalbhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The people felt confident in him as in a father, bold in their intimate enjoyment of happiness;

children.text: suteṣv iva premanibaddhabhāvo babhūva so 'pi kṣitipaḥ prajāsu || GoMe_4 ||
children.translated_text: and that king too had a love-bound disposition toward his subjects, as toward his own sons. // GoMe 4 //

children.text: sagauravo 'sau guruṣu prakṛtyā dīneṣu kāruṇyamṛdusvabhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: He was naturally respectful toward his elders, of a nature softened by compassion toward the afflicted,

children.text: kṛtāparādheṣv api maitracittaḥ samantabhadras tu suhṛjjaneṣu || GoMe_5 ||
children.translated_text: friendly-minded even toward offenders, and universally good toward his loved ones. // GoMe 5 //

children.text: babhūva tasya graharājakīrtes tathāgraho na svaparigraheṣu |
children.translated_text: The attachment of that king — whose fame was like the king of planets (the sun) — was not directed toward his own possessions

children.text: yathā tadīyāsu mamatvam āsīj janasya saṃpatsv atiśāyinīṣu || GoMe_6 ||
children.translated_text: in the way that the people felt a sense of "mine" toward his surpassing fortunes. // GoMe 6 //

children.text: jagrāha dānena sa kāṃś cid eva priyābhidhānair aparān vicitraiḥ |
children.translated_text: He won over some through generosity, others through varied and pleasant words,

children.text: tathārthacaryābhir anarthabhīruḥ kāṃś cit samānārthatayārthabhūtaḥ || GoMe_7 ||
children.translated_text: and some through actions beneficial to their interests — fearful of harm, he became a benefactor by sharing equally in their welfare. [GoMe 7]

children.text: naivā
sau svaṃ
children.translated_text: his own

children.text: parahitapratipatprakāro
children.translated_text: [self-interest but] the manner of devotion to the welfare of others

children.text: yan nātmasāc ca naralokapatiś cakāra |
children.translated_text: that the lord of men did not make his own [i.e., he gave away everything].

children.text: ko 'pi tv asau katham api dyutimān kuto 'pi
children.translated_text: Yet somehow, from somewhere, radiant in some [indescribable] way,

children.text: lokeṣv asaṃstutasuhṛd bhagavān babhūva || GoMe_8 ||
children.translated_text: that blessed one became a friend without prior acquaintance to [all] the worlds. [GoMe 8]
It was not

children.text: sa kadā cin mahīpatir amātyagaṇapuraskṛta udaṅmukho dadarśātasīkusumarāśisaṃkāśam ākāśam avagāhya patato bhagavataḥ pratyekabuddhān paramavismitamanā hy amātyān abravīt || paśyantu bhavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One day, that king, accompanied by a retinue of ministers, looking northward, saw the blessed <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> descending through the sky, which resembled a heap of flax-flowers. His mind filled with supreme wonder, he said to the ministers: "Look, sirs!"

children.text: ete kaṣāyaparuṣāmbarasaṃvṛtāṅgā vyomātasīkusumarāśinibhaṃ vigāhya |
children.translated_text: "These beings, their bodies wrapped in coarse, ochre robes, entering the sky which resembles a heap of flax-flowers,

children.text: āyānti ke 'py upaśamastimitapracārā bhūrjadrumā iva marudbhir udastamūlāḥ || GoMe_9 ||
children.translated_text: come from somewhere, moving with the stillness of tranquility — like birch trees uprooted by the wind." [GoMe 9]

children.text: anyatamo 'py amātyaḥ sasaṃbhramo 'bravīt || samyag abhihitaṃ devena kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Another minister, excited, said: "Well spoken by the king! From where indeed?"

children.text: āyānty amī kāñcanarāśigaurā vidhūtakāṣāyapaṭāntabhaṅgāḥ |
children.translated_text: "These [beings] come, golden as heaps of gold, with the folds of their ochre garments fluttering,

children.text: parasparāsliṣṭavikīrṇapakṣāḥ khaṃ cakravākā iva śobhayantaḥ || GoMe_10 ||
children.translated_text: their outspread wings mutually embracing — adorning the sky like <s>cakravāka</s> birds." [GoMe 10]

children.text: aparo 'py āha ||
children.translated_text: Yet another said:

children.text: svacchendranīlopalarāgam ete nabhaḥ samutpatya samāpatanti |
children.translated_text: "These [beings], rising into the sky with the pure hue of sapphire, are descending,

children.text: samīryamāṇāḥ pavanena saṃdhyākalaṅkitāntāḥ śaradīva meghāḥ || GoMe_11 ||
children.translated_text: carried by the wind, their edges tinged by twilight — like clouds in autumn." [GoMe 11]

children.text: anupatati na caitān abhramālī nabhasvān
children.translated_text: "No garland of clouds follows them, nor do they descend with force;

children.text: upaśamaramaṇīye cāpatanti prakṛtyā |
children.translated_text: by nature they alight with the beauty of tranquility.

children.text: caraṇatalanipāto lakṣyate vyomny amīṣāṃ
children.translated_text: The tread of their foot-soles is visible in the sky —

children.text: na ca gaganam asaṅgaṃ pādasaṃcārayogyaṃ || GoMe_12 ||
children.translated_text: yet the unobstructed sky is not suitable for the movement of feet." [GoMe 12]

children.text: yathā yathā te nikaṭī bhavanti vratīśvarāḥ śāntim ivākirantaḥ |
children.translated_text: The closer those lords of ascetics came, as if scattering peace,

children.text: tathā tathā vismayaharṣapūrṇā rājanvatī sā samitiś cakampe || GoMe_13 ||
children.translated_text: the more that royal assembly trembled, filled with wonder and joy. [GoMe 13]

children.text: atṛptā eva te teṣāṃ darśanena mahātmanāṃ |
children.translated_text: Their eyes remained unsatisfied by the sight of those great souls,

children.text: babhūvur atha cātīyus teṣāṃ nayanagocaraṃ || GoMe_14 ||
children.translated_text: and then [the Pratyekabuddhas] passed beyond the range of their vision. [GoMe 14]

children.text: atha sa pārthivas teṣāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ darśanenāvarjitamanās tān amātyān abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then that sovereign, his mind captivated by the sight of those great sages, said to the ministers:

children.text: idam āścāryam ālokya kautūhalasamākulaṃ |
children.translated_text: "Having beheld this marvel, my mind is agitated with curiosity.

children.text: mano mama tad icchāmi śrotum eṣāṃ pravistaraṃ || GoMe_15 ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear about them in detail." [GoMe 15]

children.text: atha teṣāṃ nṛpatisacivānām abhijñātataro 'mātyas taṃ rājānam abravīt || śrūyatāṃ mahārāja ||
children.translated_text: Then the most knowledgeable among those royal ministers said to the king: "Let the great king hear!"

children.text: notpadyante yadā buddhā bhagavantaḥ kṛpātmakāḥ |
children.translated_text: "When the blessed, compassionate <s>Buddhas</s> do not arise,

children.text: apāsya rajasāṃ vṛttiṃ dīrghakālānuśāyinīm || GoMe_16 ||
children.translated_text: having set aside the way of the passions, long-accumulated, [GoMe 16]

children.text: āvṛte tamasā loke samantād aparāyaṇe |
children.translated_text: when the world is enveloped on all sides by darkness, without refuge,

children.text: bhavaty eṣāṃ tadā janma janmaparyantagāmināṃ || GoMe_17 ||
children.translated_text: then the birth of these [beings] occurs — [they] whose [cycle of] births reaches its end. [GoMe 17]

children.text: pratītyotpādagāmbhīryadūrānugatabuddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Their intellects follow far the depth of dependent origination (<s>pratītyotpāda</s>);

children.text: prāptaśayyāsanaratā hīnadīnānukampakāḥ || GoMe_18 ||
children.translated_text: they delight in the attainment of [simple] beds and seats; they have compassion for the lowly and wretched. [GoMe 18]

children.text: saṃsargabhīravo nityaṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvaparāyaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Always fearful of worldly association, devoted to silence,

children.text: vicaranti jagaty ete jaṅgamāḥ puṇyarāśayaḥ || GoMe_19 ||
children.translated_text: these moving heaps of merit wander through the world. [GoMe 19]

children.text: ātmānam ekaṃ praty ete buddhā yasmād ataḥ kila |
children.translated_text: Since they are awakened (<s>buddha</s>) each unto themselves alone, therefore

children.text: pratyekabuddhā ity evaṃ pratimānam upāgatāḥ || GoMe_20 ||
children.translated_text: they have come to be known by the designation '<s>Pratyekabuddha</s>' (Solitary Awakened One). [GoMe 20]

children.text: atha sa rājā sutarāṃ tadguṇākṛṣṭahṛdayaḥ sa tam amātyam abravīt || atha kutrāmī bhagavantaḥ prativasantīti || sa prāha ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, his heart all the more attracted by their qualities, said to that minister: "Where then do these blessed ones dwell?" He replied:

children.text: meghasya rājño vijite jitātman vasanty amī dagdhabhavādhivāsāḥ |
children.translated_text: "These [sages], who have burnt the dwelling of worldly existence, self-controlled,

children.text: himādrikuñjeṣu namannamerupratānasaṃsaktamahīruheṣu || GoMe_21 ||
children.translated_text: dwell in the dominion of King <s>Megha</s>, in the groves of the <s>Himālaya</s>, among great trees entwined with the spreading [branches of] bowing <s>Meru</s>(-like peaks). [GoMe 21]

children.text: rājovāca || asti kaś cid upāyo yenāmī madviṣayāntam āvaseyur ity amātyo 'bravīt || asti mahārāja yadi megharājā prārthyate tadanvabhyarthitāḥ kilāmī tvadviṣayam alaṃ kurvantyaḥ prāpnuvanti ceti || atha bodhisattvaḥ puṇyeṣv ādaropadarśanārtham amātyān āha || tena hi bhavantaḥ sajjīkuruta || tadanurūpamānapātraṃ svayam evāhaṃ gatvā meghaṃ rājānam asminn arthe vijñāpayiṣyāmīty adhvasaṃbhrāntās te puruṣā bodhisattvam āhuḥ || nārhati devo dūtamātrasādhye prayojane khedam āpattum || api ca mahārāja ||
children.translated_text: The king said: "Is there any means by which they might come to dwell in my dominion?" The minister said: "There is, great king. If King <s>Megha</s> is requested, they, being invited through him, would indeed grace your dominion and arrive." Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, wishing to demonstrate zeal in meritorious deeds, said to his ministers: "Then, sirs, make ready! I myself shall go and request King <s>Megha</s> in this matter, taking a vessel of gifts befitting [him]." The men, alarmed at the [proposed] journey, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: "The king should not take trouble over a matter that can be accomplished by a mere envoy. Moreover, great king —"

children.text: ājñāsukharasaṃ rājyam anekāpāyasaṃkaṭaṃ |
children.translated_text: "Kingship, with its sweet taste of command, is beset with the dangers of many calamities.

children.text: pararāṣṭram ato gantuṃ sahasā tava na kṣamaṃ || GoMe_22 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is not fitting for you to go hastily to another's kingdom." [GoMe 22]

children.text: bodhisattvo 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: svahite 'py abhiyuktānāṃ karuṇāvikalātmanāṃ |
children.translated_text: "For those who are devoted even to their own welfare, whose souls are filled with compassion,

children.text: khedaḥ kaḥ puṇyakāmānāṃ bhavādhvaparivartināṃ || GoMe_23 ||
children.translated_text: who desire merit, who revolve on the road of [worldly] existence — what hardship [is there]? [GoMe 23]

children.text: ātmatvenaiva yair eva tad upāttaṃ bhavatrayaṃ |
children.translated_text: For those who have taken upon themselves the three worlds as their very self,

children.text: jagadatyantabandhūnāṃ teṣāṃ khedaḥ kathaṃ bhavet || GoMe_24 ||
children.translated_text: who are the ultimate kinsmen of the world — how could there be weariness for them? [GoMe 24]

children.text: na ca kāryābhiniṣpattir dūtasādhyā garīyasī |
children.translated_text: And the accomplishment of this matter, being of the greatest importance, cannot be achieved by an envoy.

children.text: nāsmād gurutaraṃ cāsti karaṇīyaṃ mama paraṃ || GoMe_25 ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there any duty greater than this that I must perform. [GoMe 25]

children.text: na cājñārabhasārambhe na rājyabhāraṃ vahāmy ahaṃ |
children.translated_text: I do not bear the burden of kingship in a rush of authority.

children.text: jagatāṃ vayam eveha kṛpayā kiṃkarāḥ kṛtāḥ || GoMe_26 ||
children.translated_text: We are made servants of the world by compassion right here. [GoMe 26]

children.text: anekāpāyasaṃrāddhaṃ rājyaṃ yenaiva bhūbhṛtāṃ |
children.translated_text: The very [danger] by which kings' kingdoms are beset with many calamities —

children.text: tenaivāsya kṣamas tyāgaḥ kupitasyeva bhoginaḥ || GoMe_27 ||
children.translated_text: by that same [token] its renunciation is appropriate, like [the renunciation] of an angered serpent. [GoMe 27]

children.text: dharmād eva ca saṃprāpya rājyaśrīsukhasaṃpadaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having obtained the splendor, happiness, and prosperity of kingship through <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) alone,

children.text: audāsīnyaṃ kathaṃ nāma kuryāt tatraiva paṇḍitaḥ || GoMe_28 ||
children.translated_text: how could a wise person show indifference toward that very [dharma]? [GoMe 28]

children.text: api ca bhadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, sirs —

children.text: vinā śramais tuccham asāram adhruvaṃ sukhaṃ na kāmāśrayam apy avāpyate |
children.translated_text: Without exertions, even the trivial, essenceless, unstable pleasure dependent on sense-desires is not obtained.

children.text: aśeṣalokatrayasaṃpadāspadaṃ padaṃ kim aṅgāpratimasvayaṃbhuvāṃ || GoMe_29 ||
children.translated_text: [How much more so] the state of the incomparable Self-Arisen Ones, which is the ground of the prosperity of all three worlds? [GoMe 29]

children.text: niveśya kāmeṣu caleṣu mānasaṃ mudhaiva khinnā vayam anyajanmasu |
children.translated_text: Having fixed our minds on fickle sense-pleasures, we have been wearied in vain in other births.

children.text: jagaddhitāya tv adhunābhivāñchitā bhavantu nas tv antakarāḥ pariśramāḥ || GoMe_30 ||
children.translated_text: But now, let our exertions, desired for the welfare of the world, bring about the end [of suffering]. [GoMe 30]

children.text: kathaṃ nu tasmin na yateta buddhimān nibadhya yasminn abhilāṣamātrakaṃ |
children.translated_text: How could a wise person not strive toward that, by fixing upon which even a mere aspiration,

children.text: asaṃstutānām api caikabandhutāṃ jano janānām upayāti tatkṣaṇāt || GoMe_31 ||
children.translated_text: a person immediately attains the kinship of even those previously unacquainted? [GoMe 31]

children.text: tadatyayāśaṅkibhiś cāmātyaiḥ sa mahātmā punaḥ punaḥ pratibodhyamāno 'pi naiva teṣāṃ vacanaṃ pramāṇayām āsa ||
children.translated_text: And though the ministers, fearing danger on the journey, admonished that great soul again and again, he did not take their words as authoritative.

children.text: tyaktaspṛhatvāt kṣitipasya tasya sarvatra kāruṇyamayī pravṛttiḥ |
children.translated_text: Because of that king's freedom from desire, his conduct was everywhere filled with compassion.

children.text: guṇānurāgāt sa tathāpi teṣāṃ pūjāṃ munīnāṃ prati sādaro 'bhūt || GoMe_32 ||
children.translated_text: Yet, due to his love for [their] qualities, he remained zealous regarding the worship of those sages. [GoMe 32]

children.text: guṇodgatā eva guṇoditeṣu bhavanti pūjāpratipattinamrāḥ |
children.translated_text: Only those who are themselves elevated in virtue become humbly disposed toward honoring those exalted in virtue.

children.text: ya eva ratnātiśayāntarajñās ta eva teṣv atyadhikaṃ yatante || GoMe_33 ||
children.translated_text: Those very ones who know the supreme excellence of gems are the ones who exert themselves most toward them. [GoMe 33]

children.text: phalābhilāṣopahatāntarātmā parīkṣate pātraviśeṣam eva |
children.translated_text: One whose inner self is impaired by desire for reward examines only the special merit of the recipient.

children.text: kṛpālukas tv arthitayaiva tuṣṭaḥ pravartate yācanakeṣu sāraṃ || GoMe_34 ||
children.translated_text: But the compassionate one, pleased by the mere act of being asked, bestows what is essential upon those who request. [GoMe 34]

children.text: vanaspatīnām iva janma yeṣāṃ paropakāraikarasasvabhāvaṃ |
children.translated_text: Those whose birth, like that of trees, is of a nature whose sole essence is service to others —

children.text: labheta teṣāṃ hṛdaye 'vakāśaṃ khalā phalāśā viduṣāṃ kathaṃ ca || GoMe_35 ||
children.translated_text: how could the wickedness of desire for personal reward find a place in the hearts of such wise ones? [GoMe 35]

children.text: atha sa mahāsattvo guṇānuvṛttisthirānurāgeṇa mahatā balena parivṛtaḥ svapuravarād viniryayau || nirgacchantaṃ cainaṃ dūrvāpravālakusumaphalavyagrātyucchritaikapāṇayo dvijavarā jaya jaya mahārājety uccair ānandayām āsuḥ || atha sa mahātmā laukikamaṅgalāpariniṣpattim abhiprakāśayan buddhānām eva ca bhagavatāṃ guṇānuvādaṃ maṅgalaṃ codbhāvayan vyāpinā svareṇa tān amaṅgale maṅgalābhiniveśino viprān abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then that great being, surrounded by a great army whose affection was firm through devotion to his virtues, went forth from his excellent city. As he was departing, excellent <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, with one hand raised high, busy with <s>dūrvā</s>-grass shoots, flowers, and fruits, gladdened him loudly [crying]: "Victory, victory to the great king!" Then that great soul, making manifest the incompleteness of worldly auspicious rites and announcing the virtues of the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> alone as the [true] auspicious rite, with a resonant voice addressed those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who were devoted to auspiciousness in what is inauspicious:

children.text: sarvānarthopasaṃhārapragalbhaiḥ kleśaśatrubhiḥ |
children.translated_text: "For those of feeble minds who have been defeated by the defilement-enemies, bold in bringing about every misfortune —

children.text: parājitānāṃ ko nāma vijayaḥ klībacetasāṃ || GoMe_36 ||
children.translated_text: what victory can there be for them? [GoMe 36]

children.text: durbhedaṃ yo bibheda pravicayakiraṇair dhvāntam antarniviṣṭaṃ
children.translated_text: He who with rays of discernment shattered the hard-to-pierce darkness lodged within,

children.text: tṛṣṇāvallīṃ samūlāṃ bhavataruśikharārohinīṃ yo dadāha |
children.translated_text: who burnt the creeper of craving, root and all, climbing the treetop of worldly existence,

children.text: āgṛhya krodhasarpaṃ hṛdayabilatalāt ko 'pi cikṣepa yo 'sau
children.translated_text: who, seizing the serpent of anger from the cavern of the heart, cast it out — that wondrous one

children.text: lokālokasvabhāvaḥ sa jayati bhagavān bhagnasaṃsāracakraḥ || GoMe_37 ||
children.translated_text: whose nature is the light of the world — that blessed one who has shattered the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> is victorious! [GoMe 37]

children.text: aśrāntaṃ suvidūragocaracaraṃ durnigrahaṃ durgrahaṃ
children.translated_text: Restless, far-roaming, hard to restrain, hard to grasp,

children.text: duṣpūraṃ viṣayābhilāṣakṛpaṇaṃ māyāsvabhāvaṃ calaṃ |
children.translated_text: insatiable, wretched with desire for sense-objects, illusory by nature, fickle,

children.text: ekāntavyavadānamārgavimukhaṃ saṃkleśapakṣonmukhaṃ
children.translated_text: turned away from the path of absolute purification, inclined toward the side of defilement —

children.text: yaś cittaṃ damayāṃ babhūva sa jayatv avyagracetā muniḥ || GoMe_38 ||
children.translated_text: he who tamed [such a] mind — may that sage of undistracted thought be victorious! [GoMe 38]

children.text: antardyotir apāsya yasya tamasām āyāminīṃ vāsanām
children.translated_text: He whose inner light, having dispelled the far-reaching residual impression of darkness,

children.text: akliṣṭām api nirdadhāva nivṛtiṃ kālatrayavyāpinīṃ |
children.translated_text: produced an unafflicted cessation pervading all three times,

children.text: sarvākāraparopakāraviṣayaṃ yasyāparapratyayaṃ
children.translated_text: whose knowledge encompasses the welfare of others in all forms and is not dependent on another —

children.text: prajñānaṃ bhagavān asau vijayate buddho jagacchaṅkaraḥ || GoMe_39 ||
children.translated_text: that blessed one, the <s>Buddha</s>, the benefactor of the world, is victorious! [GoMe 39]

children.text: sa krameṇa vyatītya tālahiṃtālatamālanaktamālaniculabakulakānanopaśobhitaṃ svaviṣayam khadirabadarabilveṅgudaśamīpalāśagahanadurgām aṭavīṃ prapede || tasya khalu mahāsattvasya puṇyatarṣeṇa drutataraṃ vrajataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He, gradually traversing his own domain, adorned with groves of palm, <s>hiṃtāla</s>, <s>tamāla</s>, <s>naktamāla</s>, <s>nicula</s>, and <s>bakula</s> trees, entered a wilderness impassable with dense forests of acacia, jujube, <s>bilva</s>, <s>iṅguda</s>, <s>śamī</s>, and <s>palāśa</s>. And as that great being, driven by his thirst for merit, traveled swiftly —

children.text: rajobhiḥ sainyānāṃ śalabhakulasaṃpātakapilair
children.translated_text: the sky, blocked by the dust of the armies, tawny as the swarming of a locust horde,

children.text: niruddhaṃ khaṃ reje pulinam iva paryastam udadheḥ |
children.translated_text: shone like a sandbank cast up from the ocean.

children.text: kva cit pāṇikṣepair madasurabhiśīkāraśiśirair
children.translated_text: In places, by the tossing of the hands [trunks] of lordly elephants, [there were sprinklings of] water, cool with fragrant musk-spray,

children.text: jalair nāgendrāṇāṃ navatamavanīhārapaṭalaiḥ || GoMe_40 ||
children.translated_text: [forming] fresh, dark curtains of mist upon the earth. [GoMe 40]

children.text: so 'tikramya tām aṭavīm anukrameṇa meghasya rājño viṣayam anuprāptaḥ | tadāgamanasaṃbhrāntaś ca megho mahīpatir viditatadguṇaprabhāvaḥ pratyudgamyainaṃ sabahumānapraharṣavismayavikacalocano mahatā satkāreṇa mānayitvā mahārhāsanopaviṣṭaṃ tat tat priyam avocat ||
children.translated_text: Having crossed that wilderness, he gradually reached the dominion of King <s>Megha</s>. And King <s>Megha</s>, alarmed at his arrival yet aware of his renowned virtues and power, came out to meet him and, with eyes blossoming with great honor, joy, and wonder, having honored him with great ceremony as he was seated on a magnificent throne, spoke various pleasant words:

children.text: susvāgataṃ kṣitīndrāya dhanyam āgamanaṃ tava |
children.translated_text: "Welcome to the lord of the earth! Blessed is your coming.

children.text: subhāṣitam idaṃ loke jīvan bhadrāṇi paśyasi || GoMe_41 ||
children.translated_text: Well said is this [proverb] in the world: 'Living, one sees auspicious things.' [GoMe 41]

children.text: ko nu saṃbhāvayet puṇyāṃ pramodāmṛtapeśalāṃ |
children.translated_text: Who could have imagined this auspicious meeting of ours two,

children.text: āvayoḥ saṃgatim imāṃ himavadvindhyayor iva || GoMe_42 ||
children.translated_text: delightful with the nectar of joy — like that of the <s>Himālaya</s> and the <s>Vindhya</s>? [GoMe 42]

children.text: dṛśyase caritair eva kāmaṃ lokāntacāribhiḥ |
children.translated_text: You are indeed known by your conduct alone, which reaches the ends of the world.

children.text: sākṣād vo darśanaṃ yat tu tan maṅgalyaphalodayaṃ || GoMe_43 ||
children.translated_text: But your direct vision is the fruit of an auspicious [karmic] arising. [GoMe 43]

children.text: pratyakṣam api kalyāṇaṃ manorathavidūragaṃ |
children.translated_text: Even a blessing that is directly present, [yet] far exceeding one's fantasies,

children.text: na śraddhatte janaḥ prāyaḥ prītipreṅkholitāśayaḥ || GoMe_44 ||
children.translated_text: people generally do not believe, their minds swaying with delight. [GoMe 44]

children.text: svapno 'yam uta māyeti niścayaṃ na labhāmahe |
children.translated_text: "Is this a dream or an illusion?" — we cannot reach certainty,

children.text: bhavantam api paśyanto locanānandabāndhavaṃ || GoMe_45 ||
children.translated_text: even while gazing upon you, the kinsman of the eyes' delight. [GoMe 45]

children.text: kac cid aklāntakāyas tvaṃ rājan kac cid anāmayaḥ |
children.translated_text: O king, is your body unwearied? Are you in good health?

children.text: kac cid viśrambhaniḥsaṅgaḥ praṇayābhimukho mayi || GoMe_46 ||
children.translated_text: Are you free from anxiety and inhibition, disposed with affection toward me? [GoMe 46]

children.text: kac cin notkaṇṭhayanti tvāṃ daksiṇāpathacandrikāḥ |
children.translated_text: Do not the moonlight-beauties of the southern land, with their dear ones

children.text: pradhyānastimitātāmraparyantanayanāḥ priyāḥ || GoMe_47 ||
children.translated_text: whose reddish-tinged eyes are still with longing — do they not make you yearn? [GoMe 47]

children.text: anapāyī bhavet kac cid ayatnaḥ satsamāgamaḥ |
children.translated_text: May the effortless association with the virtuous be uninterrupted!

children.text: kac cid atrābhiramase svadeśa iva bhūpate || GoMe_48 ||
children.translated_text: Do you find pleasure here as if in your own land, O sovereign?" [GoMe 48]

children.text: atha bodhisattvas taṃ rājānam amlānapraṇayaśībharair vacobhiḥ samuttejayann abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, encouraging that king with words laden with unfading affection, said:

children.text: dṛṣṭvaiva darśanīyaṃ tvāṃ viśrānto 'haṃ mahīpate |
children.translated_text: "Having seen you, who are worthy of being seen, I am rested, O sovereign.

children.text: anāryasyāpi viśrambhaḥ kasya na syād bhavādṛśe || GoMe_49 ||
children.translated_text: In one such as you, who would not feel at ease, even a man of low birth? [GoMe 49]

children.text: tvayy asaṃstutasadbandhau bāndhave purataḥ sthite |
children.translated_text: With you, a kinsman and friend without prior acquaintance, standing before me,

children.text: kiṃ cānyad vallabhataraṃ mamotkaṇṭhānibandhanaṃ || GoMe_50 ||
children.translated_text: what else could be dearer or the cause of my longing? [GoMe 50]

children.text: viditāś ca mahārāja mama priyasamāgamāḥ |
children.translated_text: And I know, great king, that meetings with the beloved

children.text: vitathālpasukhāsvādavyasanāyāsahetavaḥ || GoMe_51 ||
children.translated_text: are causes of affliction through the addiction to the taste of false, meager happiness. [GoMe 51]

children.text: ye 'rthāḥ svapne 'nubhūyante ye ca nidrāparikṣaye |
children.translated_text: The things experienced in a dream and those [experienced] when sleep has ended —

children.text: tesāṃ nirbhuktimuktānāṃ viśeṣo nopalabhyate || GoMe_52 ||
children.translated_text: between those enjoyed and those released, no distinction is found." [GoMe 52]

children.text: svapnamāyopamāneṣu muhūrtapariṇāmiṣu |
children.translated_text: Therefore, a wise person should not form attachment to fond affections

children.text: prasaṅgaṃ matimān kuryān na priyapraṇayeṣv ataḥ || GoMe_53 ||
children.translated_text: which are like dreams and illusions, transforming in a moment. // GoMe 53 //

children.text: priyo mamety evam anādikālapravṛttam udvṛttam analpagarbhaṃ |
children.translated_text: What has arisen since beginningless time, swollen with great substance, called 'happiness' —

children.text: sukhābhidhānaṃ pravadanti duḥkhaṃ vyatītaduḥkhā munayaḥ purāṇāḥ || GoMe_54 ||
children.translated_text: the ancient sages who have passed beyond suffering declare it to be suffering, [saying] 'this is dear to me.' // GoMe 54 //

children.text: kṛpā kṛpāvastuṣu saṃpratāryate striyaḥ kṛpāvastu viśeṣataḥ satāṃ |
children.translated_text: Compassion is rightly directed toward objects of compassion; women are especially objects of compassion for the virtuous;

children.text: ato matir me karuṇānupātinī priyāsu rājan na tu vibhramāturā || GoMe_55 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O king, my mind follows compassion toward the beloved, but is not agitated by infatuation. // GoMe 55 //

children.text: svabhāvadīnāḥ paratantravṛttayaḥ sadāturā matsaramānamanmathaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By nature wretched, their conduct dependent on others, always tormented by jealousy, pride, and desire,

children.text: pathi prakīrṇā iva māṃsapeśikāḥ kathaṃ nu na syuḥ pramadāḥ kṛpāspadaṃ || GoMe_56 ||
children.translated_text: like pieces of flesh scattered on the road — how could women not be objects of compassion? // GoMe 56 //

children.text: atha sa rājā prasāditamānasas tair bodhisattvavacanakusumaiḥ praṇamyainam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then that king, his mind gladdened by those flower-like words of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, bowing to him, said:

children.text: ājñāpaya mahārāja yatra māṃ manyase kṣamaṃ |
children.translated_text: Command, O great king, where you deem me fit;

children.text: bhavadvidhānāṃ kṛtyeṣu vayam ānamramūrtayaḥ || GoMe_57 ||
children.translated_text: in the tasks of those like yourself, we bow our bodies low. // GoMe 57 //

children.text: prasannamānasaṃ sa cainam avetya bodhisattvaḥ saṃpraharṣayann abravīt ||
children.translated_text: And perceiving his gladdened mind, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, delighting him, said:

children.text: tavaiva saphalaṃ janma sujīvaṃ tvaṃ ca jīvasi |
children.translated_text: Yours alone is a fruitful birth; you live a life well-lived;
