children.text: aiśvaryaṃ tava pātrasthaṃ yathārthā śrīs tavaiva ca || GoMe_58 ||
children.translated_text: your sovereignty rests in a worthy vessel, and your fortune alone is true to its name. // GoMe 58 //

children.text: yas tvam eṣāṃ bhagavatāṃ bhavasaṃbhogavidviṣāṃ |
children.translated_text: You who, under the pretext of honoring these blessed ones, the enemies of worldly enjoyment,

children.text: satkāravyapadeśena tanoṣi yaśasā jagat || GoMe_59 ||
children.translated_text: spread your fame throughout the world. // GoMe 59 //

children.text: suhṛdaḥ saṃvibhajyante dārair api dhanair api |
children.translated_text: Friends share with one another even wives and wealth;

children.text: saṃvibhāgas tu dharmeṇa durlabho bhuvi nāsti vā || GoMe_60 ||
children.translated_text: but sharing in <s>Dharma</s> is rare on earth — or perhaps nonexistent. // GoMe 60 //

children.text: dharmātithyam ato rājan mama tvaṃ kartum arhasi |
children.translated_text: Therefore, O king, you should offer me the hospitality of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: na hi saṃbhāvanā satsu dṛṣṭā vandhyaphalodayā || GoMe_61 ||
children.translated_text: for among the virtuous, generosity has never been seen to bear barren fruit. // GoMe 61 //

children.text: svargo mokṣaḥ sukhāny arthā dharmād eva yaśāṃsi ca |
children.translated_text: Heaven, liberation, pleasures, wealth, and fame — all come from <s>Dharma</s> alone;

children.text: dadhad dharmam ato yuṅkte svargamokṣasukhādibhiḥ || GoMe_62 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, one who upholds <s>Dharma</s> is yoked with heaven, liberation, happiness, and the rest. // GoMe 62 //

children.text: saddharmapraguṇaṃ mitraṃ karaṇīyaṃ balād api |

children.translated_text: Then once, that great soul, stationed in a part of a circle of young trees set in the opposite forest, was spotted by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — a sorcerer possessed of magic suited for attacking serpents with poison. He, astonished in mind by the special attractiveness of the serpent's trustful demeanor and his radiant nature through the observance of special vows, determining that 'no harm comes from this one,' and recognizing that seizing [the serpent] was an adventurous means for his own livelihood, suddenly struck that lord of serpents — who sat with his hood-circle peacefully folded in trust — on the head with a great staff, and filled his eyes with heaps of hot dust, and squeezed him tightly on the neck with a strong cord, and sprinkled his mouth-cavity with phlegm mixed with root-poison, and having pried open his mouth-fold with iron tongs, extracted his fangs. And with his mind turbulent with greed, with a sharp instrument he tore out the crest-jewel whose root was concealed in a dense sheath, and sitting down on his hood-coils as if on a <s>bimba</s>-fruit cushion, he rested.

children.translated_text: Thus and otherwise that worst of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, having tormented the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, placed him in a great basket and wandering here and there, arrived at the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. Then, seeing the beauty of that serpent-lord, the great multitude, their minds supremely astonished, honored that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> with great worship.

children.translated_text: Then a serpent-woman named <s>Sumanā</s>, the foremost of his inner court, not seeing the lord of serpents at the customary time of his arrival, knowing his naturally good nature, and the delight of human hearts in ignoble deeds, suspecting that harm had befallen him, her heart afflicted with the anguish of intense grief, imagining this and that, quickly wept:

children.translated_text: burn my body all the more — burning as I am with the grief of my beloved's absence. || GoNā 26 ||

children.text: pratibhāty apūrvam iva sarvam adya me na ca vedmi kāham iti tena varjitā |
children.translated_text: Everything appears unprecedented to me today; bereft of him, I do not know who I am;

children.text: vyasane sa eva śaraṇaṃ mama priyo virahe tu tasya maraṇaṃ parāyaṇam || GoNā_27 ||
children.translated_text: in misfortune, that beloved alone is my refuge; in separation from him, death is the final recourse. || GoNā 27 ||

children.text: maṇivedikākiraṇapāṭalormayo gṛhadīrghikā na ramayanti me manaḥ |
children.translated_text: The pools of the palace, with waves pinkened by the rays of jeweled platforms,

children.text: priyavipravāsaparitāpaviplutaṃ sphuṭapadmakośamakarandavāsitāḥ || GoNā_28 ||
children.translated_text: fragrant with the nectar of open lotus-buds, do not delight my mind — shattered by the burning grief of my beloved's absence. || GoNā 28 ||

children.text: diśatūttamāni jagaduttamadyutir mama maṅgalāni bhagavān sa eva tu |
children.translated_text: May he of supreme radiance in the world, that very Blessed One, bestow the highest auspiciousness upon me,

children.text: na bhavāntare 'pi viraho yathā bhaved dayitena tena niravadyakarmaṇā || GoNā_29 ||
children.translated_text: that there be no separation even in another existence from that beloved of blameless deeds. || GoNā 29 ||

children.text: virahānubandhavirasāḥ samāgamā jagato 'raparvapariṇāminī sthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Meetings end in the bitterness of separation; the existence of the world changes at every turn' —

children.text: iti yaj jagāda manaso 'tivallabhaḥ samupasthitaṃ tad idam adya vaiśasam || GoNā_30 ||
children.translated_text: that which the most beloved of my heart declared — that calamity has now arrived. // GoNā 30 //

children.text: vikasatsphuliṅgam anilākulārciṣaṃ dahanaṃ viśāmi bahuduḥkhabhāginī |
children.translated_text: 'I shall enter the fire, ablaze with scattering sparks and flames agitated by the wind — I, the partaker of much suffering;

children.text: tanum utsṛjāmi śikharād girer imām avaśiṣyate kim aparaṃ mamāyuṣaḥ || GoNā_31 ||
children.translated_text: I shall cast down this body from the peak of the mountain — what else remains of my life?' // GoNā 31 //

children.text: yadi so 'dya naiti sukhasaumyadarśano mama mūrtimān
a
children.translated_text: [lacuna]

children.text: vikalo manorathaḥ |
children.translated_text: unfulfilled heart's desire —

children.text: svayam eva dhakṣyati mamedam āśrayaṃ hṛdayajvalas tumulaśokadāruṇaḥ || GoNā_32 ||
children.translated_text: this conflagration in my heart, terrible with tumultuous grief, will by itself burn this body of mine.' // GoNā 32 //
'If today he does not come — he of happy, gentle appearance — my embodied

children.text: iti sā rurāva kurarīva viklavā nayanāmbudurdinamukhī tapasvinī |
children.translated_text: Thus she cried out like a distressed <s>kurarī</s> (osprey), that wretched one, her face rainy with the waters of her eyes,

children.text: vasudhātale galitahāramekhalā bhujagāṅganā pativiyogaśaṅkinī || GoNā_33 ||
children.translated_text: her necklace and girdle slipping to the surface of the earth — like a <s>nāga</s> wife apprehending separation from her lord. // GoNā 33 //

children.text: atha sumanā nāma yoṣid bodhisattvam anveṣamānā vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm anuprāptā dadarśa cainaṃ mahāsattvaṃ paramadāruṇām
avasthām
children.translated_text: condition;

children.text: upagataṃ dṛṣṭvā ca tīvraśokāyāsavyathitahṛdayā provāca |
children.translated_text: and seeing him, her heart anguished with intense grief and distress, she spoke:
Then a woman named <s>Sumanā</s>, searching for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, arrived at the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and saw that great being in an extremely terrible

children.text: sphuritakiraṇacchāyāramyāḥ śiromaṇayaḥ kva te
children.translated_text: 'Where are your head-jewels, lovely with the hue of radiant beams?

children.text: kva dayita gatās tās tā daṃṣṭrā bisāṅkuradhūsarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where, O beloved, have those fangs gone, grey as lotus-stalk sprouts?

children.text: vapur upahataṃ daṇḍāghātair navotpalakomalaṃ
children.translated_text: Your body, tender as a fresh blue lotus, is mutilated by blows of a stick —

children.text: vigalitahṛdayā (?) krūreṇaitat kṛpātmaka kena te || GoNā_34 ||
children.translated_text: by whom, O compassionate one, [has this been done] — whose heart has melted?' // GoNā 34 //

children.text: kiṃ dharmo 'stam itaḥ prajāhitakaraḥ kiṃ lokapālā mṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Has <s>Dharma</s>, the benefactor of beings, set? Have the world-protectors (<s>Lokapālas</s>) died?

children.text: tejaḥ kopaviṣātisaṅgarabhasaṃ kiṃ proṣitaṃ bhoginām |
children.translated_text: Has the fiery might of serpent-lords, fierce with the venom of wrath, departed?

children.text: śūnyaṃ kiṃ nu patiprabhābhir adhunā niḥśuklamūlaṃ jagad
children.translated_text: Is the world now empty of the splendor of lords, its very root become white [with destruction],

children.text: yena tvaṃ vyasanaṃ duruttaram idaṃ prāpto vināśāya te || GoNā_35 ||
children.translated_text: that you have reached this calamity, difficult to surmount, leading to your destruction?' // GoNā 35 //

children.text: nāsīt kasya dayā tvayi praharato 'nāryasya śāntātmani
children.translated_text: 'Who had no compassion in striking you — the ignoble one — you of peaceful soul?

children.text: krauryaṃ tvayy api nāma sādhucarite pāpātmanāṃ jāyate |
children.translated_text: Cruelty arises even toward you, O one of saintly conduct, on the part of evil-souled ones!

children.text: tvām āyāsayataḥ kathaṃ na patitau tasya prakoṣṭhāt karau
children.translated_text: How did the hands of the one tormenting you not fall from his wrists?

children.text: nāthānātha ivāpadaṃ katham imāṃ prāptas tvam āyāsinīm || GoNā_36 ||
children.translated_text: How, like one without a protector, have you reached this painful adversity?' // GoNā 36 //

children.text: bodhisattvas tu pratyagrakopaśokakaluṣitādhyāśayātmanām avetya tūṣṇīm eva babhūva || sā punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: But the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving their inner dispositions to be clouded by fresh anger and grief, simply remained silent. She spoke again:

children.text: kasyāpriyaṃ jīvitam ādyajātaṃ kālena kelī
ṃ
children.translated_text: [lacuna]

children.text: saha kaḥ karoti |
children.translated_text: and death?

children.text: tvadapriyāriṣṭaniviṣṭaceṣṭo lokāntaraṃ ko 'bhyanugantukāmaḥ || GoNā_37 ||
children.translated_text: Who, his actions polluted by the ill-omen of your misfortune, would desire to follow to another world?' // GoNā 37 //
'Who does not hold life, the firstborn, dear? Who plays with time

children.text: śītābhilāṣī pravivikṣur agniṃ ko mārutoddhataśikhākalāpam |
children.translated_text: 'Who, desiring coolness, would enter a fire whose crest of flames is fanned by the wind?

children.text: āditsate krūraviṣaṃ bhujaṅgaṃ kaḥ puṣpadāmākṛtivipralabdhaḥ || GoNā_38 ||
children.translated_text: Who, deceived by the appearance of a flower-garland, seizes a serpent of cruel venom?' // GoNā 38 //

children.text:
udadhiparikhām adyaivaināṃ dahāmi vasundharāṃ
sanaganagaragrāmārāmāṃ svadṛṣṭihutāśanaiḥ |
na mama hṛdayaṃ śānti
ṃ
children.translated_text: [lacuna]

children.text: yāti tvadapriyatāḍitaṃ
children.translated_text: peace, struck by [the grief of] your misfortune;

children.text: dahati yadi na krodhāgnir māṃ purā niravagrahaḥ || GoNā_39 ||
children.translated_text: if the unrestrained fire of anger does not burn me first!' // GoNā 39 //
'I shall burn this earth, with its ocean-moats, this very day — with its cities, towns, villages, and groves — with the fires of my gaze! My heart does not attain

children.text: atha bodhisattvas tāṃ tapasvinīm aviṣahyakopāgnipradīptamānasā
ṃ
children.translated_text: [lacuna]

children.text: hlādayann iva tadāmṛtaśiśirābhir vāgbhir ity abravīt ||
children.translated_text: with words as cool as nectar, spoke thus:
Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as if cooling that wretched one — her mind ablaze with the unbearable fire of anger —

children.text: alam alaṃ mā gā bhadre vai kopasya cetovidāhinaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Enough, enough! Do not, O good one, go to anger — that burner of the mind!

children.text: prakṛtiduḥkheṣu ko bhūyaḥ sattveṣu duḥkhāni cintayet || GoNā_40 ||
children.translated_text: In regard to beings who are by nature subject to suffering, who would further contemplate [adding] suffering? // GoNā 40 //

children.text: duḥkhahetau vartamāneṣu śocyeṣu saṃkleśabhāgiṣu kaḥ parākramet || duḥkhāya svahitakramārteṣu dehiṣu na mama daṃṣṭrotpāṭanād duḥkhaṃ na ca daṇḍasaṃpātajā rujāḥ || duḥkhayanti mānasaṃ caṇḍi tvadvākkarkaśās tudanti mām || api ca kānte ||
children.translated_text: 'Who would exert prowess against the pitiable, who exist in the cause of suffering, who share in affliction? Against embodied beings who are pained by the disruption of their own welfare? I feel no suffering from the tearing out of my fangs, nor do the pains born of the blows of the stick afflict me; O fierce one, your harsh words of speech pierce me — what is more, O beloved:'

children.text: bodhisaṃprāptaye cittaṃ yadaivotpāditaṃ purā |
children.translated_text: 'The very moment when the mind was first directed toward the attainment of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),

children.text: vayaṃ tadaiva lokānām ādheyakriyatāṃ gatāḥ || GoNā_41 ||
children.translated_text: at that very moment we became [vessels] for the world's rightful use. // GoNā 41 //

children.text: kopavahnimlāyamānā punaḥ saiva tvam anyeva lakṣyase ||
children.translated_text: 'Wilting with the fire of anger, you appear to be someone other than yourself —

children.text: candralekheva cāmbare vikasadghanadhūmasaṃbādhadhūsare || GoNā_42 ||
children.translated_text: like a crescent moon in the sky made grey with the oppression of spreading cloud-smoke. // GoNā 42 //

children.text: kiṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: 'Furthermore:

children.text: karmāparādhajanitaṃ yadi duḥkham etat kopāvakāśa iha ko nu mama dvijātau |
children.translated_text: 'If this suffering is born of the transgression of [past] <s>karma</s>, what room for anger at this <s>brāhmaṇa</s>?

children.text: karmendhanoddhataśikhāśakalākulebhyaḥ kupyet kathaṃ na matimān narakānalebhyaḥ || GoNā_43 ||
children.translated_text: Would a wise person be angry at the fires of hell, seething with the sparks of fuel that is <s>karma</s>?' // GoNā 43 //

children.text: tad alaṃ kopadainyena tava cetovidāhinā |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, enough of this wretchedness of anger, which burns your mind;

children.text: svagṛhān eva gacchasva saṃtyāgaṃ ca kuruṣva me || GoNā_44 ||
children.translated_text: go to your own home, and take leave of me.' // GoNā 44 //

children.text: sā bhartur abhiprāyaṃ saṃpādayantī tadvacanāpyāyitahṛdayā vigatakopasaṃrambhā babhūva ||
children.translated_text: She, fulfilling her husband's wish, her heart nourished by his words, became free from the agitation of anger.

children.text: kopoparāgavigame vivṛto 'dhimātraḥ snehaḥ priye viṣamavartini nāgavadhvā |
children.translated_text: When the stain of anger was removed, the excessive love of the <s>nāga</s> wife for her beloved, traveling a difficult path, was revealed —

children.text: udghāṭitābhrapaṭalasphuṭadigvibhāge khe niḥsapatna iva candramasaḥ prakāśaḥ || GoNā_45 ||
children.translated_text: like the light of the moon, unopposed, in the sky when the curtain of clouds has been opened, revealing the clear expanse of the directions. // GoNā 45 //

children.text: śokāśrunayanapariplutā ceti bodhisattvam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Her eyes flooded with tears of grief, she addressed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

children.text: kuto me duḥkhabhāginyā gehaṃ ārya tvayā vinā |
children.translated_text: 'Where is home for me, a partaker of suffering, without you, O noble one?

children.text: ihaiva śoṣam eṣyāmi yā gatis tava sā mama || GoNā_46 ||
children.translated_text: I shall wither away right here — whatever is your fate, that is mine. // GoNā 46 //

children.text: viṣamasthaṃ parityajya tvām anātha sukhaidhitam |
children.translated_text: 'Abandoning you, unprotected one, in adversity — you who were nurtured in comfort —

children.text: kānta kena sukhenāhaṃ drakṣyāmi svajanaṃ punaḥ || GoNā_47 ||
children.translated_text: O beloved, with what happiness could I see my own people again? // GoNā 47 //

children.text: sukhe samānatāṃ gatvā duḥkhe jahyāṃ yadi priyam |
children.translated_text: 'If, having shared in happiness equally, I should abandon my beloved in suffering,

children.text: anāryām akṛtajñāṃ māṃ dhārayiṣyati bhūḥ katham || GoNā_48 ||
children.translated_text: how would the earth support me — ignoble, ungrateful? // GoNā 48 //

children.text: pratibhāti jagac chūnyaṃ tvayā virahitaṃ mama |
children.translated_text: 'The world appears empty to me, bereft of you;

children.text: tvaṃ me jīvitasarvasvaṃ tvaṃ bandhus tvaṃ parāyaṇam || GoNā_49 ||
children.translated_text: you are my entire life's treasure; you are my kinsman; you are my final refuge. // GoNā 49 //'

children.text: bodhisattvo 'tha tāṃ sādhvīṃ bahalasnehaviklavām |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, [seeing] that virtuous woman distraught with abundant love,

children.text: anukampāvaśāt sādhur īdṛśaṃ pratyabhāṣata || GoNā_50 ||
children.translated_text: out of compassion, the good one, replied to her thus: // GoNā 50 //

children.text: adṛṣṭapūrvavyasanā sukhasaṃvardhitā priye |
children.translated_text: 'Never having seen adversity before, nurtured in comfort, O beloved —

children.text: parikleśam imaṃ soḍhum akṣamā tvam anindite || GoNā_51 ||
children.translated_text: you are unable to endure this affliction, O blameless one. // GoNā 51 //

children.text: mayi sneho 'sti yadi te duḥkhaṃ me yadi necchasi |
children.translated_text: 'If you have love for me, if you do not wish me suffering,

children.text: adṛṣṭam adya māṃ kṛtvā tad gaccha tvaṃ svam ālayam || GoNā_52 ||
children.translated_text: then, making me unseen today, go to your own dwelling.' // GoNā 52 //

children.text: atha sā tair bodhisattvavaco'dbhir ākleditahṛdayā duḥkhadaurmanasyaparyākulamānasā niśīthe kāśikārājam upetya karuṇākulatarākṣareṇa vacasā kṛtāñjalir avocat ||
children.translated_text: Then she, her heart melted by those waters of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s words, her mind overwhelmed with sorrow and despair, at nightfall, approaching the king of <s>Kāśī</s>, with hands joined in supplication, spoke with words whose syllables were all the more imbued with compassion:

children.text: āpadgatānāṃ vyasanakṣayāya tvaṃ pañcamaḥ pārthiva lokapālaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'For those who have fallen into adversity, for the cessation of their calamity, you, O king, are the fifth world-protector;

children.text: trāyasva mām āpadi vartamānāṃ dīnām anāthāṃ jagadekanātha || GoNā_53 ||
children.translated_text: save me, dwelling in adversity — wretched, without protector, O sole protector of the world!' // GoNā 53 //

children.text: atha sa rājā tad atibhāsuraṃ vapur avalokya kim idaṃ kathaṃ cety utpannajātasaṃbhramaḥ sādaram utthāya paryaṅkapṛṣṭhāt tāṃ nāgayoṣitam etad avocat ||
children.translated_text: Then that king, beholding her exceedingly radiant form and [wondering] 'What is this? How so?' — with rising wonder and agitation, rising respectfully from his couch, addressed that <s>nāga</s> wife thus:

children.text: dhyāmīkṛtya maṇipradīpakiraṇān etad vapus te sthitaṃ
children.translated_text: 'This form of yours stands dimming the rays of gem-lamps;

children.text: vyāhārasphuṭacitravarṇakaraṇo divyaprabhāvaś ca te |
children.translated_text: and your divine power, producing clear and varied colors in speech —

children.text: kā nu tvaṃ karavāṇi kiṃ bhavati te brūhi tvadājñām imāṃ
children.translated_text: who are you? What may I do for you? Speak — this command of yours

children.text: mālāṃ phulladalām ivādya śirasā samyak pratīcchāmy aham || GoNā_54 ||
children.translated_text: I accept today upon my head as fittingly as a garland of blossoming petals.' // GoNā 54 //

children.text: athāsau bhujagavadhūs tena tasya rājño 'bhijātyapeśalena vacasā samānanditamanasā provāca ||
children.translated_text: Then that serpent-wife, her mind gladdened by the well-born, graceful speech of the king, spoke:

children.text: āśāvaśānāṃ naradeva ko 'nyo manorathaṃ pūrayituṃ samarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Who else, O lord of men, is able to fulfill the heart's desire of those at the mercy of hope,

children.text: tyaktvā bhavantaṃ jagato hitāya prajāpater vaṃśam ivāvatīrṇam || GoNā_55 ||
children.translated_text: other than you — descended as if from the lineage of <s>Prajāpati</s> for the welfare of the world?' // GoNā 55 //

children.text:
nāgāṅganāṃ mām avagaccha rājaṃs tvaddeśaparyantakṛtādhivāsām |
āpadgataṃ mānada pannagendraṃ trāyasva kṛtyaṃ mama tad garīya
ḥ
children.translated_text: [lacuna]
// GoNā 56 //

'Know me, O king, as a <s>nāga</s> woman who has made her dwelling at the borders of your realm; save the serpent-lord who has fallen into adversity, O bestower of honor — that would be my greatest [request].'

children.text: rājovāca || bhagini kas tavāsau bhujagavaraḥ || sā provāca ||
children.translated_text: The king said: 'Sister, who is your serpent-lord?' She replied:

children.text: bhartā mama prāṇadhaneśvaro 'sau nyāyopradeṣṭā ca gurur garīyān |
children.translated_text: 'He is my husband, the lord of my life and wealth, the instructor in righteousness, a most venerable teacher;

children.text: piteva nityaṃ hitasaṃvidhātāsukhe ca viśrambhaniratyayaś ca || GoNā_57 ||
children.translated_text: like a father, always providing for [my] welfare, and in happiness, an unfailing place of trust.' // GoNā 57 //

children.text: atha sa bhūpatis tena tasyāḥ svāmyanurāgaśībhareṇa caritenābhiprasāditaḥ || provāca cainām ||
children.translated_text: Then that king, gratified by her conduct, full of the quality of devotion to her husband, spoke to her thus:

children.text: bhaktir bhartari darśitā ghanarasā dākṣiṇyam unmīlitaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Devotion to your husband has been shown — dense with feeling; courtesy has been revealed;

children.text: premodbhāvitam āpadi sthirataraṃ prodghāṭitā bhadratā |
children.translated_text: love has been manifested, all the firmer in adversity; nobility has been displayed.

children.text: dharmo nyāyaparigraheṇa paramāṃ vṛddhiṃ tvayāpādito
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> has been brought to the highest growth by your embrace of righteousness;

children.text: loke sādhupativratatvam iti te khyātiḥ sthitā śāśvatī || GoNā_58 ||
children.translated_text: your fame in the world as a virtuous devoted wife (<s>pativratā</s>) shall stand forever.' // GoNā 58 //

children.text: tyaktvā priyaṃ jīvitam apy ato 'haṃ puṇyaprabhāvopanataṃ ca rājyam |
children.translated_text: 'Abandoning even dear life and also the kingdom bestowed by the power of merit,

children.text: saṃpūrayiṣyāmi manorathaṃ te paśyādya bhadre dayitaṃ vimuktam || GoNā_59 ||
children.translated_text: I shall fulfill your heart's desire — behold today, O good one, your beloved set free!' // GoNā 59 //

children.text: atha sa rājā tasya brāhmaṇasyāntikāt taṃ nāgarājānaṃ mahatā mūlyena niṣkrīya parameṇa .............. sapatnīkaṃ svabhavanaṃ praveśya mahārhasiṃhāsanopaviṣṭam abhyarcayām āsa || atha bodhisattvas tena tasya rājño 'tyadbhutena niṣkāraṇopakārasaṃbhrameṇākṛṣṭamanāḥ provācainam ||
children.translated_text: Then that king, having ransomed that serpent-king from the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> at a great price, with supreme [honor] .............. having brought him along with his wife into his own palace, seated on a magnificent throne, worshipped him. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his mind drawn by the king's most wondrous, causeless, generous solicitude, spoke to him:

children.text: asaṃstute nāma tavāyam ādaro mayi prasādasthirabhaktipeśalaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'This regard of yours toward me — one not even known to you — refined with firm devotion and grace,

children.text: kṛtopakāreṣv api yo na dṛśyate pṛthagjaneṣu sukhānubuddhiṣu || GoNā_60 ||
children.translated_text: is not seen even in ordinary people of comfortable understanding toward those who have done them a service.' // GoNā 60 //

children.text: prakāśiteyaṃ guṇapakṣapātitā prajānurāgo bahulīkṛtas tvayā |
children.translated_text: 'This partiality toward virtue has been displayed by you; affection for the people has been made abundant;

children.text: guṇe vivardhasva tad uttarottarair guṇeṣu bhadraṃ jagatāṃ avasthitam || GoNā_61 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, grow ever further in virtues — the welfare of the world rests in virtues.' // GoNā 61 //

children.text: iti saṃrādhya rājānaṃ tam asau bhujageśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus gratified the king, that lord of serpents,

children.text: anubaddho dayitayā kṛpayeva gṛhān yayau || GoNā_62 ||
children.translated_text: followed by his beloved wife, went to his own abode — as if [accompanied] by compassion [itself]. // GoNā 62 //

children.text: iti śrīnāgajātakaṃ catvāriṃśattamam || ḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Nāga Jātaka</s>, the fortieth.

children.text: 10. Puṇyarāśi
children.translated_text: 10. <s>Puṇyarāśi</s>

children.text: athāśoko mahārāja upaguptaṃ yatiṃ gurum |
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, the great monarch, [approached] the ascetic teacher <s>Upagupta</s>,

children.text: kṛtāñjalipuṭo natvā prārthayac ca tathādarāt || GoPr_1 ||
children.translated_text: and with palms joined, bowing, respectfully made a request: // GoPr 1 //

children.text: bhadanta śrotum icchāmi punar anyat subhāṣitam |
children.translated_text: 'Reverend Sir, I wish to hear yet another well-spoken [teaching];

children.text: tad yathā guruṇādiṣṭaṃ tathādeṣṭuṃ ca me 'rhati || GoPr_2 ||
children.translated_text: may you please instruct me as [your own] teacher instructed you.' // GoPr 2 //

children.text: iti tena narendreṇa prārthite sa jinātmajaḥ |
children.translated_text: When thus requested by the king, that son of the <s>Jina</s> (the Buddha),

children.text: upagupto narendraṃ taṃ samālokyaivam ādiśat || GoPr_3 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Upagupta</s>, regarding the king, instructed him thus: // GoPr 3 //

children.text: śṛṇu sādhu mahārāja yathā me guruṇoditam |
children.translated_text: 'Listen well, O great king, as my teacher told me;

children.text: tathāhaṃ te pravakṣyāmi śrutvā caivaṃ śubhe cara || GoPr_4 ||
children.translated_text: so shall I tell you — and having heard, act accordingly in what is good. // GoPr 4 //

children.text: nāsti vipākaparyanta upakārāpakārayoḥ |
children.translated_text: 'There is no end to the [karmic] ripening of [both] benefit and harm;

children.text: saṃbuddhe sadgurau tasmāt kartavyam upakārakam || GoPr_5 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, one should render service to the Fully Awakened One (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>) and to the true teacher.' // GoPr 5 //

children.text: tad yathāstāṃ mahāsattvau saṃbuddhopāsakau purā |
children.translated_text: 'Once upon a time, there were two great beings, devotees of the Fully Awakened One;

children.text: kadā cit tāv ubhau grāmaṃ gacchantau saṃgatau pathi || GoPr_6 ||
children.translated_text: one day, both of them, going to a village, met upon the road. // GoPr 6 //

children.text: saṃbuddhapratimāṃ tatra puṇyarāśim ivottamām |
children.translated_text: 'An image of the Fully Awakened One there — like a supreme heap of merit —

children.text: tāṃ samīkṣya tayor ekaḥ praṇatvaivaṃ tam abravīt || GoPr_7 ||
children.translated_text: beholding it, one of the two, bowing, spoke thus: // GoPr 7 //

children.text: aho bata mahāpuṇyarāśir ayaṃ virājate |
children.translated_text: '"Ah, how wonderful! This great heap of merit (<s>puṇyarāśi</s>) shines forth!

children.text: bhāgyena dṛśyate 'smābhir adya mitra praṇamyatām || GoPr_8 ||
children.translated_text: By good fortune we behold it today, O friend — let us bow!' // GoPr 8 //

children.text: iti tenoditaṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvāparas tam abravīt |
children.translated_text: 'Hearing what was said by him, the other one, seeing it, said:',

children.text: aho bata mahān mitra pāparāśir ayaṃ nv iti || GoPr_9 ||
children.translated_text: '"Ah, how great, O friend, is this heap of sin (<s>pāparāśi</s>)!" — thus. // GoPr 9 //

children.text: iti tenoditaṃ śrutvā prathamaḥ sa upāsakaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Hearing what was said by him, the first devotee,

children.text: karṇau pidhāya hastābhyāṃ tam evaṃ paryabhāṣata || GoPr_10 ||
children.translated_text: covering his ears with his hands, reproached him thus: // GoPr 10 //

children.text: dhik tvām asadbuddhim asatpralāpinam [!] evaṃ hy api tvaṃ pratibhāṣase 'tra |
children.translated_text: '"Fie upon you, of evil understanding, of evil speech! You speak thus even here?

children.text: kasmān muneḥ śāstur upāsako 'pi saddharmamūrtiṃ pratinindase 'dya || GoPr_11 ||
children.translated_text: Why, being a devotee of the sage and teacher, do you today revile the embodiment of the true <s>dharma</s>?' // GoPr 11 //

children.text: kathaṃ na jihvā patitā tavānanād asatpralāpāpahatā tapasvinī |
children.translated_text: 'How has your tongue not fallen from your mouth — that wretched one, struck by evil speech?

children.text: apuṇyarāśir bhagavān iti bruvan kathaṃ na magnas tvam are rasātale || GoPr_12 ||
children.translated_text: Saying 'The Blessed One is a heap of demerit' — how, O wretch, have you not sunk into the netherworld?' // GoPr 12 //

children.text: dhig apraśastām asatāṃ duratyayāṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ prakṛtiṃ calācalām |
children.translated_text: 'Fie upon the nature of ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjanā</s>) — inauspicious, ignoble, insurmountable, fickle and unstable,

children.text: vimarśam aprāpya yatheṣṭacāriṇī karoti yā lokam apāyagocaram || GoPr_13 ||
children.translated_text: which, acting at will without reflection, leads the world to the realm of woe!' // GoPr 13 //

children.text: sudāruṇair āyudhabhīmadarśanair arātibhiḥ sārdham aho varaṃ gatam |
children.translated_text: 'Better indeed to go with enemies terrible in appearance, armed with fearsome weapons,

children.text: tvayā suhṛcchadmanigūḍhapāpmanā padaṃ na caikaṃ vitathapralāpinā || GoPr_14 ||
children.translated_text: not a single step [should be followed] by you, who conceal evil under the guise of friendship, babbling falsehoods. // GoPr 14 //

children.text: namanti yaṃ brahmavido maharṣayaḥ punāti yo viśvam idaṃ vṛṣāṃśubhiḥ |
children.translated_text: To whom the great sages, knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, bow down; who purifies this entire world with showers of truth —

children.text: apuṇyarāśir yadi sa vratīśvaras tathāgataḥ puṇyanidhiḥ kuto 'paraḥ || GoPr_15 ||
children.translated_text: if that lord of ascetics, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, is a heap of demerit, then what other treasury of merit exists? // GoPr 15 //

children.text: muneḥ paroddhāranimittamātram apy upaiti yasyoddhṛtakalmaṣo 'pi san |
children.translated_text: He whose effort, even if merely for the upliftment of others, the sage undertakes — though he himself has already eradicated all defilements —

children.text: sa yogaparyantavidāṃ dhuri sthito na puṇyarāśir yadi ko nv ihāparaḥ || GoPr_16 ||
children.translated_text: he who stands at the forefront of those who know the culmination of <s>yoga</s> — if he is not a heap of merit, then who in this world is? // GoPr 16 //

children.text: na yasya buddhiḥ pratihanyate kva cin na ca praheyāvayavo 'vaśiṣyate |
children.translated_text: He whose intellect is never obstructed anywhere, in whom no component subject to abandonment remains,

children.text: na cāsti saṅgo jagadarthasādhane sa puṇyarāśir na kathaṃkathāntaśaḥ || GoPr_17 ||
children.translated_text: and who has no attachment in accomplishing the welfare of the world — he is a heap of merit, beyond all doubt. // GoPr 17 //

children.text: taduktaṃ sa samākarṇya dvitīyopāsakas [!] tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having heard those words of his, then the second lay-disciple (<s>upāsaka</s>),

children.text: prāgalbhavacasā bhūya āyuṣmantaṃ tam abravīt || GoPr_18 ||
children.translated_text: with bold speech, spoke again to the venerable one: // GoPr 18 //

children.text: hitakāmyatayā niratyayaṃ vacanaṃ kāmam idaṃ sakhe tava |
children.translated_text: "Out of a desire for your good, this speech of yours, friend, is certainly harmless;

children.text: anuyujya tathāpi śobhate vitathaṃ sādhur udīrayan bhavān || GoPr_19 ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless, when examined, it becomes you to speak the untruth, O virtuous one. // GoPr 19 //

children.text: mama bhaktir udāraśāsane sugate yā paramānukampake |
children.translated_text: My devotion to the noble teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One), the supremely compassionate,

children.text: viditā tava sā tathāpi māṃ sahasā saumya kathaṃ vigarhase || GoPr_20 ||
children.translated_text: is known to you; yet why, friend, do you suddenly censure me? // GoPr 20 //

children.text: āpātālpasukhābhimānarasikaṃ paryantariktāśrayaṃ
children.translated_text: Shame on worldly association — which delights in the conceit of momentary, superficial pleasures, whose basis is ultimately empty,

children.text: sāyāsaṃ sabhayaṃ prasaṅgavirasaṃ dhig laukikaṃ saṃgatam |
children.translated_text: which is laborious, fearful, and distasteful in its consequences —

children.text: yan nāmaivam akāraṇoddhataruṣo mithyāvikalpair hataṃ
children.translated_text: that by causeless, arisen anger, destroyed by false conceptualizations,

children.text: gacchaty ekapade kṣayaṃ paricayaṃ vikṣipya mūrdhno 'ntikam || GoPr_21 ||
children.translated_text: goes to ruin in a single step, casting aside familiarity as if [it were] at the head of death. // GoPr 21 //"

children.text: etat tenoditaṃ śrutvā prathamaḥ sa upāsakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing those words spoken by him, that first lay-disciple,

children.text: anyathā tadvaco matvā manasaivaṃ vyacintayat || GoPr_22 ||
children.translated_text: understanding his words differently, reflected in his mind thus: // GoPr 22 //

children.text: aho hy anyad anenoktam anyan mayā vikalpitam |
children.translated_text: "Alas! Something else was meant by him, but something different was imagined by me" —

children.text: iti cintāviṣaṇṇātmā tasthau lajjāhatāśayaḥ || GoPr_23 ||
children.translated_text: thus, dejected with worry, he stood with his purpose struck down by shame. // GoPr 23 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sa ca sahāyas taṃ lajjāvanamitānanam |
children.translated_text: And his companion, seeing that his face was bowed with shame,

children.text: tadabhiprāyam ājñātuṃ prasahya caivam abravīt || GoPr_24 ||
children.translated_text: pressed him to learn his intention and spoke thus: // GoPr 24 //

children.text: sādho kiṃ manyase hy atra yat te lajjāhataṃ mukham |
children.translated_text: "O good one, what do you think about this, that your face is struck with shame?

children.text: tāvat te yad abhiprāyaṃ tat pracakṣva mamāgrataḥ || GoPr_25 ||
children.translated_text: First tell me your intention openly before me." // GoPr 25 //

children.text: tasyaitad vacanaṃ śrutvā sa āyuṣmān upāsakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of his, that venerable lay-disciple

children.text: tanmano'ntargataṃ sarvam abhiprāyaṃ vyamuñcata || GoPr_26 ||
children.translated_text: released all the intention that lay within his mind: // GoPr 26 //

children.text: cittaṃ yatra prasādya kṣaṇam api manujo 'nuttame dakṣiṇīye
children.translated_text: "He in whom a person, having established faith even for a moment, in that supreme object of worship,

children.text: śrīsaubhāgyaprakarṣaṃ bhavagatiṣu paraṃ prāpya nirdvandvaramyam |
children.translated_text: attains the highest degree of glory and good fortune in the courses of existence — splendid and free from duality —

children.text: paścād ālokya lokaṃ vitathavilapitaṃ pratyayagrāhamātraṃ
children.translated_text: then, looking back at the world, knowing it to be mere false lamentation, a mere grasping at conditions,

children.text: jñātvā prāpnoti śāntaṃ katham iva na mahān puṇyarāśir bhavet saḥ || GoPr_27 ||
children.translated_text: attains peace — how could he not be a great heap of merit? // GoPr 27 //

children.text: dattvā palālaśakalasrajam agrasattve lebhe bhavopaśamaśāntisukhāni nārī |
children.translated_text: A woman, having offered a garland of straw-bits to the foremost being, obtained the bliss of the calming and cessation of existence —

children.text: yasminn acintyacaritātiśayaprabhāve kiṃ puṇyarāśir ayam ity avidagdham etat || GoPr_28 ||
children.translated_text: in him of inconceivable, surpassing power and conduct, to say "Is he a heap of merit?" — that is indeed naive. // GoPr 28 //

children.text: kośātakīkusumam api pradāya stūpe muneḥ paramakāruṇikasya yasya |
children.translated_text: Having offered even a <s>kośātakī</s> (luffa) flower at the <s>stūpa</s> of that supremely compassionate sage,

children.text: bhuktvālaye guṇavibhūtisukhaprakarṣaṃ lebhe 'ṅganāmṛtapurapratipatsamṛddhim || GoPr_29 ||
children.translated_text: [a being], having enjoyed the supreme happiness of the splendor of qualities in a heavenly abode, obtained the prosperity of the attainment of the immortal city of women. // GoPr 29 //

children.text: yasmai pāṃśupradānaṃ prakṛticalamanā bālakaiḥ saṃpradāya
children.translated_text: Children, with naturally fickle minds, having offered merely a gift of dust to him —

children.text: sphītāṃ martyendralakṣmīm anavanatasitacchattrahāsābhirāmām |
children.translated_text: attaining the abundant royal fortune of a human lord, delightful with the laughter of white parasols never lowered —

children.text: saṃprāpyātītacintaṃ padam abhayam asaddāhaparyantaśāntaṃ
children.translated_text: and afterwards obtaining the state beyond thought, fearless, calmed at the edge of [all] wrong views —

children.text: lebhe paścān narendraḥ katham iva sa na bhoḥ puṇyarāśir maharṣiḥ || GoPr_30 ||
children.translated_text: that king — how could that great sage not be a lofty heap of merit? // GoPr 30 //

children.text: prasahya paṅkāṅkam ṛṣer varāhaḥ [!] caitye vapur yasya ciraṃ sa eva |
children.translated_text: A boar [who] by force [soiled with] mud the <s>stūpa</s> of the sage — for a long time that was his very body;

children.text: tasyaiva dharmasya sudharmatāsau yadādhipatyena bhavād vimuktaḥ || GoPr_31 ||
children.translated_text: and through the excellence of precisely that <s>dharma</s>, he was liberated from existence through sovereignty. // GoPr 31 //

children.text: kiyān prasādo jaḍacetanānāṃ sakhe tiraścāṃ guṇaniścayo vā |
children.translated_text: How great is the devotion of the dull-minded, friend, or the discernment of qualities by animals?

children.text: kṣetrasya tasyaiva tu sā vibhūtir yenātra sattvāḥ saphalī bhavanti || GoPr_32 ||
children.translated_text: It is rather the power of that very field [of merit] by which beings here become fruitful. // GoPr 32 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā lokavilocanotsavasukhāṃ saṃśāntasarvoddhavāṃ
children.translated_text: Formerly, seeing the form of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>, which was a festival of joy for the world's eyes, in which all affliction was stilled,

children.text: vyāmābhāpariveṣiṇīṃ bhagavato buddhasya mūrtiṃ purā |
children.translated_text: surrounded by a halo the span of a fathom —

children.text: harṣotkampigalaś cukūja madhuraṃ preṅkhatkalāpaḥ śikhī
children.translated_text: a peacock, his throat trembling with delight, cooed sweetly, his tail-fan swaying;

children.text: taddhetoś ca śamaṃ jagāma sa śikhī dhārāmbusikto yathā || GoPr_33 ||
children.translated_text: and because of that, that peacock attained tranquility, as if sprinkled with a stream of water. // GoPr 33 //

children.text: maṅgalyatvam acintyayogamahatāṃ sarvārthasiddhyāvahaṃ
children.translated_text: The auspiciousness of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s> — those of inconceivable, great yoga — which brings about the accomplishment of all aims,

children.text: buddhānāṃ tad udīkṣyatāṃ bhagavatāṃ saṃmohanidrācchidām |
children.translated_text: which cuts through the sleep of delusion — let that be observed:

children.text: atyantopaśamāvahaṃ bhavati yat tiryaggatānām api
children.translated_text: that which brings about supreme tranquility even for animals —

children.text: prāg evābhimukhāśayasya viduṣaḥ śāstur guṇāmbhonidheḥ || GoPr_34 ||
children.translated_text: how much more for the wise person who faces the Teacher, the ocean of qualities, with devotion! // GoPr 34 //

children.text: manye darśanam eva tad guṇavatāṃ teṣām avandhyodayaṃ
children.translated_text: I think that the very sight of those endowed with qualities brings fruitful results,

children.text: sarvākāraparopakāramadhuraṃ pūrvābhisaṃskārajam |
children.translated_text: sweet with the compassion of universal benevolence in every aspect, born of former spiritual cultivation —

children.text: pradveṣopahatāśayān api janān saṃprāpayaty uttamaṃ
children.translated_text: it causes even people whose minds are corrupted by hatred to attain the supreme

children.text: sthānaṃ sarvabhavopasargavigamād ekāntaśāntaṃ śivam || GoPr_35 ||
children.translated_text: state, solely peaceful and auspicious, through the departure of all afflictions of existence. // GoPr 35 //

children.text: śrutvā nāma tathāgatasya makaraḥ sāṃyātrikebhyaḥ purā
children.translated_text: A sea-monster (<s>makara</s>), having heard the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> from sailors,

children.text: saṃpṛktāsyapuṭo mamāra sugate cetaḥ prasādya kṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: died with its mouth still touching [the water], having established faith in the <s>Sugata</s> for just a moment;

children.text: taddhetoḥ saritāṃ patiṃ parimitaṃ nītvā punar dustaraṃ
children.translated_text: because of that, having carried the lord of rivers across a limited [distance], and then crossing the vast, impassable

children.text: janmāmbhonidhim uttatāra vipulaṃ niḥsṛtya mārge plavam || GoPr_36 ||
children.translated_text: ocean of births, it came out, having found a raft on the path. // GoPr 36 //

children.text: apāyapātālatalāvalambī suro munīndraṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadya |
children.translated_text: A god (<s>sura</s>), clinging to the abyss of the netherworld of evil destinations, having taken refuge in the lord of sages,

children.text: svapuṇyasopānaparamparābhiḥ samārurohāgryataraṃ vimānam || GoPr_37 ||
children.translated_text: ascended by the stairways of his own merit to the highest celestial mansion. // GoPr 37 //

children.text: kṛtvā vyāghrabhayān namo bhagavate buddhāya sarvātmanā
children.translated_text: A man, out of fear of a tiger, having bowed to the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s> with his entire being,

children.text: nāmnaivānupamasya puṇyamahatīm ālokya nāndīṃ pumān |
children.translated_text: seeing the great joy of merit [gained] merely by the name of the incomparable one,

children.text: niḥśeṣavyasanāndhakāragahanapradhvaṃsinīṃ prāptavāñ
children.translated_text: attained some peace that destroys the dense darkness of all calamities without remainder,

children.text: chāntiṃ kām api vāgatītaviṣayāṃ prahlādasaṃvardhanīm || GoPr_38 ||
children.translated_text: beyond the reach of words, increasing delight. // GoPr 38 //

children.text: iti bhuvanamahimnām ākaraṃ śāśvatānāṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, him who is the mine of eternal glories of the world,

children.text: tam anupamaviśeṣācintyacaryārahasyam |
children.translated_text: of incomparable, special, inconceivable, wondrous deeds —

children.text: kim api katham apīśaṃ śaṃkaraṃ prāptum āryaṃ
children.translated_text: something somehow — lord, beneficent, noble —

children.text: padam amaram ahāryaṃ puṇyarāśiṃ vadāmi || GoPr_39 ||
children.translated_text: that immortal, imperishable state — I call him a heap of merit. // GoPr 39 //"

children.text: iti tadgaditaṃ śrutvā sa itara upāsakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having heard those words spoken by him, the other lay-disciple,

children.text: tam āyuṣmantam ālokya punar evaṃ samabravīt || GoPr_40 ||
children.translated_text: looking at that venerable one, spoke again thus: // GoPr 40 //

children.text: samyag abhihitaṃ sādho bhavatātra tathāpi ca |
children.translated_text: "What you have said here, O good one, is perfectly correct; nevertheless,

children.text: mamāpy evam abhiprāyaṃ śrūyatāṃ sāṃprataṃ sakhe || GoPr_41 ||
children.translated_text: hear my intention also, friend, as it stands now: // GoPr 41 //

children.text: kṛtvā cittapradoṣaṃ sakṛd api sugate prāptalokāvasāne
children.translated_text: Having committed even once a mental offence against the <s>Sugata</s> — who has reached the end of the world, in whom the inner fury has been washed by hundreds of water-pots of unbroken loving-kindness —

children.text: yatrāvicchinnamaitrījalakalaśaśatakṣālitāntaḥprakope |
children.translated_text: [continued]

children.text: āsaṃsārāparāntaṃ jvaladanalaśikhāgarbhaparyantarandhraṃ
children.translated_text: the ignorant plunge into <s>Avīci</s> (the deepest hell), with its terrifying caverns edged with blazing fire-flames, until the end of <s>saṃsāra</s> —

children.text: gāhante 'vīcim ajñāḥ katham iva sa jino 'puṇyarāśir na tuṅgaḥ || GoPr_42 ||
children.translated_text: how could that <s>Jina</s> (Victor) not be a lofty heap of demerit [for those who offend him]? // GoPr 42 //

children.text: elāpatram avajñayā kila munau cchitvā pramādātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: Out of contempt, having recklessly cut the <s>elā</s> (cardamom) leaves at the sage's [shrine],

children.text: pārthagjanyaviṣasya vṛttim aśivām udbhāvayan karmaṇā |
children.translated_text: manifesting through that deed the inauspicious course of another being's poison —

children.text: elāpādapapādapāṭitaśiro – – dvamacchoṇito
children.translated_text: with his head split by the foot of the <s>elā</s> tree ... bleeding ...

children.text: nāgendraḥ pṛthubhīmabhogapaṭalo nādyāpi nirmucyate || GoPr_43 ||
children.translated_text: the great <s>nāga</s> (serpent-king), with a broad and fearsome hood, is not freed even to this day. // GoPr 43 //

children.text: sūkṣmo 'py evam anādaro bhagavati prābandhikīṃ vyāpadaṃ
children.translated_text: Even the slightest disrespect toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> draws upon living beings

children.text: yat sarvāyatanopatāpavirasām ākarṣati prāṇinām |
children.translated_text: a perpetual calamity, distasteful in the affliction of all faculties;

children.text: sarvotkarṣadaśāvasānamahatīṃ kām apy anāyāsinīṃ
children.translated_text: [yet] he has attained some great peace — the culmination of all supreme states, free from exertion —

children.text: prāptaḥ śāntim apuṇyarāśir asatāṃ tasmāt sa sattvottamaḥ || GoPr_44 ||
children.translated_text: therefore that best of beings is [indeed] a heap of demerit for the wicked. // GoPr 44 //

children.text: kṛtvā cetaḥpradoṣaṃ kṛpaṇakapuruṣo yatra vīthīmukhasthaḥ
children.translated_text: A wretched, base insect standing at a street-corner, having committed a mental offence against the sage,

children.text: kīṭaḥ kopopadagdho nṛparathacaraṇāghātavicchinnamūrdhā |
children.translated_text: burned by anger, with its head crushed by the blow of a king's chariot-wheel —

children.text: jvālāmālākalāpaṃ vivṛtam iva bhuvo bhīṣaṇaṃ vaktrakośaṃ
children.translated_text: entered from that [instant] a pit — the gaping, terrifying mouth-cavity of the earth, as it were, with its garlands of flames —

children.text: śvabhraṃ tasmād viveśa pratihatatimiro 'puṇyarāśis tato 'sau || GoPr_45 ||
children.translated_text: its darkness dispelled; therefore that one is a heap of demerit. // GoPr 45 //

children.text: evaṃ buddhe bhagavati gatibhrāntyupādānadāha-
children.translated_text: Thus, toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s> — who has attained direct knowledge of the burning of grasping through confusion of the paths —

children.text: prāptābhijñe mṛdur api kṛtaś cetanāsaṃniveśaḥ |
children.translated_text: even a mild mental disposition [of offense]

children.text: saṃtānānān upatatiphalaprāptaye nirbabandha
children.translated_text: binds [the offender] to the obtaining of fruit in successive continua of existence,

children.text: saḥ sarttā [?] – bhavasukhalavāsvādalagnābhilāṣam || GoPr_46 ||
children.translated_text: that [being] ... attached to the craving for tasting the pleasures of existence. // GoPr 46 //

children.text: matvā karmasvakam anuśayasnāyutantrīpraṇeyaṃ
children.translated_text: Knowing that <s>karma</s> is one's own — to be guided by the strings of the tendons of latent impressions,

children.text: lokair duḥkhair viṣayakṛpaṇair indriyair vipralabdham |
children.translated_text: deceived by the sense-organs with their miserable sense-objects and worldly sufferings —

children.text: utpadyante vipadupaśamaprāptaye ye janānāṃ
children.translated_text: those who arise for the calming of the calamities of people —

children.text: mātuṃ teṣu prabhavati pumān ko 'pakāropakārau || GoPr_47 ||
children.translated_text: what person is capable of measuring the harm and benefit [that accrue] toward them? // GoPr 47 //

children.text: hṛtvā dhātudharān* srajo bhagavataḥ sadyo 'bhavad dārako
children.translated_text: Having stolen relic-garlands from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s [shrine], a child instantly became

children.text: visphoṭasphuṭitārdramāṃsaguḍako bībhatsasarvāśrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: a mass of putrid, moist flesh bursting with boils — disgusting in every aspect;

children.text: satkāraṃ pravidhāya tatra ca punaḥ sadyo 'bhavan nirvraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: and upon making proper worship there again, he instantly became free of wounds —

children.text: tat ko nāma na pūjayet sahṛdayaḥ puṇyārṇavaṃ jaṅgamam || GoPr_48 ||
children.translated_text: who then, being compassionate, would not worship that moving ocean of merit? // GoPr 48 //

children.text: tasmāt praduṣṭamanasāṃ bhagavān apuṇyarāśiḥ prasannamanasāṃ tu sa puṇyarāśiḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, for those of corrupt minds, the <s>Bhagavān</s> is a heap of demerit; but for those of serene minds, he is a heap of merit;

children.text: paryāyato vigatasarvasavāsanāntaḥsaṃkleśakilbiṣadaśo viṣayāntadarśī || GoPr_49 ||
children.translated_text: in both ways, he who has abandoned all inner defilements together with their residual impressions, who sees the end of the objects [of existence], is free from the state of guilt. // GoPr 49 //

children.text: kṛtvā bhagnāṃ pra
ti
children.translated_text: [continued]

children.text: kṛtim ṛṣer aṅganā kandukena
children.translated_text: of the sage, a woman playing with a ball

children.text: prakṛīḍantī karakisalayapracyutena pramādāt |
children.translated_text: that had accidentally fallen from her bud-like hand —

children.text: paścāttāpajvaraparigatā pūjayitvāpi buddhaṃ
children.translated_text: afterward, seized by the fever of remorse, even having worshipped the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: kiṃ saṃprāptā na kanakavatī bāhuvicchedaduḥkam || GoPr_50 ||
children.translated_text: did not <s>Kanakavatī</s> still suffer the pain of having her arms severed? // GoPr 50 //
Having broken the image

children.text: udyan darśanam ucchinatti savitā naktaṃcarāṇāṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Just as the rising sun cuts off the sight of night-creatures

children.text: nṝṇāṃ dhvāntam apākaroty aviralaṃ rūpopalabdhyai karaiḥ |
children.translated_text: and removes the dense darkness of people with its rays for the perception of forms —

children.text: doṣas tatra na bhāskarasya bhagavaddviṣtaprasannātmanāṃ
children.translated_text: the fault there is not of the sun; [likewise] for those hostile or serene toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: buddho 'py evam apuṇyapuṇyanicayaḥ sāmānyanātho 'pi san || GoPr_51 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddha</s> too is similarly both a heap of demerit and merit, even though he is the common lord of all. // GoPr 51 //

children.text: iti tāv upāsakau buddhaguṇamāhātmyakīrtanam |
children.translated_text: Thus those two lay-disciples, having performed the praise of the glory of the <s>Buddha</s>'s qualities,

children.text: kṛtvā parasparaṃ sattvaṃ pavitrīkṛtya jagmatuḥ || GoPr_52 ||
children.translated_text: purifying each other's minds, departed. // GoPr 52 //

children.text: evaṃ matvā mahārāja saṃbuddhe sadgurau mudā |
children.translated_text: Knowing this, O great king, toward the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, the true teacher, with joy,

children.text: śraddhayā satkṛtiḥ kāryā nāpakṛtiḥ kathaṃ cana || GoPr_53 ||
children.translated_text: worship should be performed with faith — never an offence in any manner. // GoPr 53 //

children.text: śāstary avajñāmalināśayānāṃ bhūmir vidāraṃ na dadāti sadyaḥ |
children.translated_text: The earth does not immediately open up for those whose minds are stained with contempt for the Teacher;

children.text: buddhaprasādadravacetasāṃ vā na jāyate ratnamayī vicitraṃ || GoPr_54 ||
children.translated_text: nor does a jewelled [lotus] miraculously arise for those whose minds melt with devotion to the <s>Buddha</s>. // GoPr 54 //

children.text: ko 'py eṣa karmāntarasaṃnirodhaḥ puṇyaprabhāvātiśayo vicitraḥ |
children.translated_text: There is some mysterious obstruction by intervening <s>karmas</s>, a wondrous peculiarity of the power of merit,

children.text: karmāṇi yat pātraviśeṣajāni sadyo na nṝṇāṃ phalam udvamanti || GoPr_55 ||
children.translated_text: by which <s>karmas</s> arising from special recipients do not immediately vomit forth their fruit for people. // GoPr 55 //

children.text: tasyaiva kāpīyam ṛṣer acintyā vibhūtir āveṇikayogasādhvī |
children.translated_text: That inconceivable power of that very sage, excellent through his unique <s>yoga</s> —

children.text: yenātra kṛtvāpi manaḥpradoṣaṃ sadyo na pātālatalaṃ viśanti || GoPr_56 ||
children.translated_text: is the reason why, even having committed a mental offence, [beings] do not immediately enter the netherworld. // GoPr 56 //

children.text: tal lokānām amṛtaphalade jaṅgame puṇyavṛkṣe
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), who has conquered his inner rivals — that moving tree of merit which bears the fruit of immortality for the world —

children.text: kāryā bhaktir bhagavati jine nirjitāntaḥsapatne |
children.translated_text: [continued]

children.text: nikṣipyāśāṃ viṣayagahanavrātaviṣvagviṣaktāṃ
children.translated_text: devotion should be established, casting aside the desire entangled in the thickets of sense-objects spreading in all directions,

children.text: yāvan nedaṃ bhavati bhuvanaṃ buddhakāntāraghoram || GoPr_57 ||
children.translated_text: as long as this world does not become terrible as a desert devoid of <s>Buddhas</s>. // GoPr 57 //

children.text: utpadyante jagati na sadā nāpi sarvatra buddhāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhas</s> do not arise always in the world, nor everywhere —

children.text: sarvākārāparatavitathagrāhanidrāprasaṅgāḥ |
children.translated_text: free from all false graspings and the torpor of every kind of delusion;

children.text: kaś cit kalpaḥ prabhavati cirāt puṇyasaṃbhāraramyo
children.translated_text: some [rare] <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), delightful with the accumulation of merit, arises after a long time,

children.text: yatrotpādo bhavati bhuvanasvāmināṃ bhūtabhūtyai || GoPr_58 ||
children.translated_text: in which the birth of the lords of the world occurs for the true prosperity of beings. // GoPr 58 //

children.text: yātasyāpi praśāntiṃ bhavapuraparikhāṃ jālinīṃ śoṣayitvā
children.translated_text: Even after the <s>Buddha</s>-sun has gone to cessation, having dried up the moat of deceptive <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: yāvat saṃbuddhabhānoḥ pravacanakiraṇā lokam udbhāvayanti |
children.translated_text: as long as the rays of his teaching illuminate the world —

children.text: tāvat paśyantu santaḥ samaviṣamavatāṃ durvibhāgaprabhedān
children.translated_text: let the virtuous discern the distinctions of the difficult-to-classify divisions of the equal and unequal [conditions of beings];

children.text: loke durdṛṣṭimeghā vipadaśanimukhā durnivārāḥ sphuranti || GoPr_59 ||
children.translated_text: [for] in the world, clouds of wrong views, with the faces of lightning-bolts of calamity, arise irresistibly. // GoPr 59 //

children.text: evaṃ me guruṇākhyātaṃ tathā te kathyate mayā |
children.translated_text: Thus was it told to me by my teacher, and so it is told to you by me;

children.text: tad evaṃ hi parijñāya kartavyaṃ bhajanaṃ muneḥ || GoPr_60 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, knowing this fully, devotion to the sage should be practiced. // GoPr 60 //

children.text: ye bhajanti sadā buddhaṃ na te gacchanti durgatim |
children.translated_text: Those who always worship the <s>Buddha</s> do not go to evil destinies;

children.text: niḥkleśāḥ sabalān mārāñ jitvā yānti jinālayam || GoPr_61 ||
children.translated_text: free from defilements, having conquered <s>Māra</s> and his forces, they go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). // GoPr 61 //

children.text: ye ca śṛṇvanti saddharmaṃ te 'pi na yānti durgatim |
children.translated_text: And those who hear the true <s>Dharma</s> — they too do not go to a bad destiny.

children.text: sarvadā satsukhaṃ bhuktvā yānti cānte sukhāvatīm || GoPr_62 ||
children.translated_text: Having always enjoyed the happiness of the virtuous, they go finally to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Realm of Bliss). [GoPr 62]

children.text: ye 'rcayanti mudā saṃghān na te 'pi yānti durgatim |
children.translated_text: Those who joyfully honor the <s>Saṃghas</s> (monastic communities) — they too do not go to a bad destiny.

children.text: sarvasattvahitaṃ kṛtvā saṃprayānti śubhālaye || GoPr_63 ||
children.translated_text: Having done what is beneficial for all beings, they proceed to the abode of virtue. [GoPr 63]

children.text: evaṃ matvā mahārāja triratnaśaraṇaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having understood this, great king, having taken refuge in the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>),

children.text: sarvasattvahitaṃ kṛtvā saṃvṛtiṃ saṃpracāraya || GoPr_64 ||
children.translated_text: having done what is beneficial for all beings, practice the conventional [path]. [GoPr 64]

children.text: tena te sarvadā bhadram ihāmutrāpi saṃbhavet |
children.translated_text: By that, may welfare always come to you, both here and hereafter.

children.text: kramād bodhiṃ samāsādya nirvṛtiṃ vā samāpnuyāḥ || GoPr_65 ||
children.translated_text: Gradually reaching <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening), may you attain <s>Nirvṛti</s> (final liberation). [GoPr 65]

children.text: iti śāstrā samādiṣṭaṃ śrutvā sa nṛpatir mudā |
children.translated_text: Having joyfully heard this instruction from the Teacher,

children.text: tatheti saṃpratijñāya prābhyanandat sapārṣadaḥ || GoPr_66 ||
children.translated_text: that king, having assented saying "So be it," rejoiced together with his assembly. [GoPr 66]

children.text: puṇyarāśyavadānaṃ tad idaṃ ye śraddhayā mudā |
children.translated_text: This tale of <s>Puṇyarāśi</s> (the Heap of Merit) — those who, with faith and joy,

children.text: śrāvayanty anumodante śṛṇvanti ca samāhitāḥ || GoPr_67 ||
children.translated_text: recite it, rejoice in it, and hear it with concentration, [GoPr 67]

children.text: sarve 'pi
te
children.translated_text: of them,

children.text: mahāsattvāḥ pariśuddhatrimaṇḍalāḥ |
children.translated_text: great beings, with the three spheres [of agent, action, and object] completely purified,

children.text: saddharmaguṇasaukhyāni bhuktvā yānti jinālayam || GoPr_68 ||
children.translated_text: having enjoyed the virtues and happiness of the true <s>Dharma</s>, go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror). [GoPr 68]
all

children.text: || śrī || iti puṇyarāśyavadānaṃ samāptam || 13 ||
children.translated_text: || Śrī || Thus ends the tale of <s>Puṇyarāśi</s>. || 13 ||

children.text: 11. ṛṣipañcaka
children.translated_text: 11. <s>Ṛṣipañcaka</s> (The Five Sages)

children.text: mūlaṃ malānāṃ pravadanti jātiṃ jātiprapañcopaśamapravīṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who are skilled in the cessation of the elaboration of birth declare birth to be the root of defilements —

children.text: tathāgatāś cāvitathapratijñāḥ saṃbhodhisattvāś ca viśuddhasattvāḥ || GoṚp_1 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of unfailing vow, and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of purified nature. [GoṚp 1]

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate |
children.translated_text: As the story is heard:

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila lokābhimataguṇābhilakṣite mahati brāhmaṇakule janma pratijagrāha |
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, took birth in a great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family distinguished by qualities esteemed by the world.

children.text: kiraṇair iva śuklapakṣacandraḥ svaguṇair eva sahābhivardhamānaḥ |
children.translated_text: Like the moon of the bright fortnight growing with its own rays,

children.text: paramāṃ svakulasya cihnaśobhāṃ prathimānaṃ gamayāṃ babhūva sādhuḥ || GoṚp_2 ||
children.translated_text: the virtuous one, growing along with his own qualities, brought the mark-beauty of his family to the height of renown. [GoṚp 2]

children.text: vayasi prathame 'pi vartamāno viṣayeṣv atibaddhamānaso 'sau |
children.translated_text: Even while in his earliest youth, his mind deeply absorbed in sense-objects,

children.text: atimānuṣaceṣṭitasvabhāvo jagatāṃ smayabhājanaṃ babhūva || GoṚp_3 ||
children.translated_text: he, whose natural conduct was superhuman, became an object of wonder to the world. [GoṚp 3]

children.text: so 'paryavasitakukāryaparyākulam upaśamavirodhiprakṛṣṭopāyāsam arthopārjanapradhānakāmarativyavahārāsārakarmadharmabhūyiṣṭham avinayakalahavairavigrahāyatanam īrṣyāmātsaryacauryādiniketabhūtaṃ śokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsabahulaṃ māyāśāṭhyamadamānagahanaṃ sāhasāvalepādhiṣṭhitam anāryavyavahārānupravṛttijihmasattvabhāvaṃ pramādapadasthānam anekarūpaparibhavopasṛṣṭaṃ saṃnihitadainyam anabhibhūtaviṣādaṃ pratyāsannavighātabhayadaurgatyam aviṣahyopadravasamudraṃ kaṇṭakagarbhādabhraśvabhrapratibhayākaram apāsya gārhasthyam anyatamam aśramapadam abhyalaṃcakāra |
children.translated_text: He renounced household life — full of unfinished wicked deeds creating confusion, with distressing effort contrary to tranquility, chiefly consisting of unsound activities of dharma of commerce and pleasure-seeking, the ground of indiscipline, quarrel, hostility, and conflict, the abode of envy, jealousy, theft, and the like, abundant in grief, lamentation, suffering, despair, and distress, dense with deceit, fraud, pride, and conceit, governed by violence and arrogance, with crooked beings following ignoble conduct, the ground of heedlessness, beset with manifold forms of humiliation, with wretchedness ever-present, with unconquered despair, with ruin, fear, and misfortune close at hand, an ocean of unbearable affliction, fearsome like pits and chasms filled with thorns — and undertook a certain stage of the [renunciant] life.

children.text: bahucchalaṃ so 'tha bahuvyalīkaṃ bahūpasargaṃ bahudoṣaduṣṭam |
children.translated_text: Having renounced household life — the root of misfortune, full of much deception, much falsehood,

children.text: apāsya gārhasthyam anarthamūlaṃ tapovanaṃ śāntam alaṃcakāra || GoṚp_4 ||
children.translated_text: many afflictions, corrupted by many faults — he adorned the peaceful ascetic grove. [GoṚp 4]

children.text: sarobhir unnidrapalāśakoṣakuśeśayendīvaracitratoyaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Adorned with lakes whose waters were variegated with lotuses, <s>kuśeśaya</s>, and blue lotuses with awakened petal-sheaths,

children.text: alaṃkṛtaṃ bālakaśerunīlapratīrasaṃsuptaśarārihaṃsaiḥ || GoṚp_5 ||
children.translated_text: and with <s>śara</s>-reed herons sleeping at the banks, their blue color like that of young <s>kaśeru</s> grass. [GoṚp 5]

children.text: mīnāvalīraśanayā saritopagūḍhaṃ snehād iva praṇayinaṃ priyayā prakāmam |
children.translated_text: Embraced by a river with a girdle of fish-rows, as if by a lover lavishly through affection,

children.text: sarvartupuṣpaphaladaiḥ svajanair ivāntar bālapravālaharitais tarubhir niruddham || GoṚp_6 ||
children.translated_text: enclosed within by trees bearing flowers and fruits of all seasons, like kinsmen, with young sprouts green. [GoṚp 6]

children.text: vyālais tapasvibhir ivākṛtimātrarūkṣaiḥ paryākulam jalatṛṇāṅkuratuṣṭacittaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Inhabited by wild animals — fierce only in appearance, like ascetics — their minds content with water, grass, and shoots.

children.text: taṃ kānanāntam upagamya sa bodhisattvo dharmo 'vatīrṇa iva vigrahavān vyarājat || GoṚp_7 ||
children.translated_text: Having entered that forest hermitage, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> shone like <s>Dharma</s> itself descended in bodily form. [GoṚp 7]

children.text: gṛhasthabhāve 'pe sa vartamāno janmāntarābhyastavivekavāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even while dwelling in the householder state, he, in whom the disposition for seclusion was cultivated through past lives,

children.text: āgāradoṣair aparikṣatātmā viśeṣayām āsa tapovanasthān || GoṚp_8 ||
children.translated_text: his self unharmed by the faults of household life, surpassed even those dwelling in the ascetic grove. [GoṚp 8]

children.text: – – ⏑ – – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ – – pramādināṃ kāpuruṣāśrayāṇām |
children.translated_text: [metrical pattern — text partially corrupt] — those who are heedless, the refuge of base men —

children.text: utkaṇṭhayanti pravivekayogyās ta eva śāntāḥ satataṃ vanāntāḥ || GoṚp_9 ||
children.translated_text: for those fit for seclusion, those same peaceful forest-ends are ever a source of longing. [GoṚp 9]

children.text: abhyastanaiṣkramyasukhotsavānāṃ satāṃ pravāsā iva gehavāsāḥ |
children.translated_text: For the virtuous who are practiced in the festival of happiness of renunciation, dwelling in a house is like living abroad.

children.text: mṛgāṅganākuñcitapallavāni vanāni teṣāṃ bhavanottamāni || GoṚp_10 ||
children.translated_text: Forests, where doe-ladies [rest] with curled sprout-like [legs], are their finest abodes. [GoṚp 10]

children.text: parigraheṣv eva vighātabuddhiḥ saṃtoṣa eva svadhanānurāgaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those whose understanding sees ruin in possessions, whose love of their own wealth is [merely] contentment,

children.text: yeṣāṃ gṛhe cārakavāsasaṃjñā teṣāṃ na citro vanasaṃnivāsaḥ || GoṚp_11 ||
children.translated_text: and who regard dwelling in a house as dwelling in a prison — for them, residence in the forest is not surprising. [GoṚp 11]

children.text: tasya pūrvajanmaparamparābhyāsavāsanāghanasnehagauravaniratyayāś catvāraḥ sahāyā babhūvuḥ vāyasaḥ pārāvato bhujago mṛgaś ca | te tadājñāsaṃpādanaikatānamanasaḥ svayonividhinā dharmakriyāsauṣṭhavena jagaty abhilakṣitā babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: He had four companions — a crow, a pigeon, a serpent, and a deer — whose love, respect, and devotion were unceasing, consolidated through the residual impressions of habitual association over a succession of past lives. They, with minds single-pointedly focused on carrying out his commands, became renowned in the world for the beauty of their virtuous conduct, each according to the ways of its own kind.

children.text: chandopaghātavihateṣv aparāyaṇeṣu tiryakṣu mohabahuleṣv adhikaṃ vihbānti |
children.translated_text: Among animals — whose channels of desire are blocked, who have no refuge, who are mostly [sunk] in delusion —

children.text: dharmānurāgaviśadāḥ pratipattiśobhās tāmisrapakṣarajanīṣv iva dīpamālāḥ || GoṚp_12 ||
children.translated_text: the glories of virtuous conduct, radiant with love for <s>Dharma</s>, shine all the more — like rows of lamps in the dark nights of the waning fortnight. [GoṚp 12]

children.text: vismāpayanti sutarāṃ viguṇāśrayiṇyo dharmakriyāḥ karaṇapāṭavayogaramyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Virtuous deeds that are charming in the skill of their execution astonish all the more when they reside in those of inferior birth —

children.text: grīṣmoṣmadurgamatarāsu vanasthalīṣu prodbhidyamānakamalā iva paṅkajinyaḥ || GoṚp_13 ||
children.translated_text: like lotus-ponds with lotuses blooming forth in the forest grounds that are impassable due to the heat of summer. [GoṚp 13]

children.text: teṣām ekadā snehaniryantraṇaramaṇīyāvasthānapravṛttasaṃkathānām ayaṃ viniścayo babhūva | kiṃ nu khalu bhavanto 'tiśayena duḥkhaṃ manyante | teṣāṃ dakṣatām ivodbhāvayan prathamataraṃ vāyasaḥ provāca | nehāsti kṣudho 'nyat paramaṃ duḥkham | kutaḥ
children.translated_text: One day, as they were engaged in conversation in their delightful abode, unrestricted by affection, this question arose: "What, indeed, do you consider to be the supreme suffering?" The crow, as if displaying his cleverness, spoke first: "There is no supreme suffering other than hunger. For —"

children.text: na vyādhayo na ca jarā na suḥrdviyogo nāniṣṭasaṃgamamayā vyasanaprakārāḥ |
children.translated_text: "Neither diseases, nor old age, nor separation from loved ones, nor the varieties of calamity consisting of contact with the undesirable —

children.text: duḥkhāni tāny upaharanti janasya yāni hrī vipravāsaparitāpakarī jighatsoḥ || GoṚp_14 ||
children.translated_text: [none of] these cause the suffering that the shame of a hungry one does, producing the torment of exile [from dignity]. [GoṚp 14]

children.text: duruttarakṣārataraṅgamālinīm upāgatā vaitaraṇīṃ pramādinaḥ |
children.translated_text: The heedless, having reached the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> river with its garland of hard-to-cross, alkaline waves,

children.text: bubhukṣayā yan nigiranty ayoguḍān tato 'sti na kṣutsadṛśo 'paraḥ kaliḥ || GoṚp_15 ||
children.translated_text: swallow iron balls due to hunger — therefore there is no affliction equal to hunger. [GoṚp 15]

children.text: kaḍevarāvaskaranirjharasravanmalopalepākamanīyadarśanaḥ |
children.translated_text: A baby, its appearance made unlovely by the smearing of impure fluid from the stream flowing as refuse from the body,

children.text: rujā parīto 'pi pipāsati stanaṃ yad arbhakaḥ kṣudvyasanaṃ tato mahat || GoṚp_16 ||
children.translated_text: even though afflicted by pain, desires the breast — therefore the distress of hunger is great. [GoṚp 16]

children.text: vinākṛtaḥ prāṇasamair api priyair gato 'pi śokasya vaśaṃ vidāhinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even when separated from loved ones dear as one's own life, even when fallen under the power of burning grief,

children.text: yad aśrumiśrān kavaḍān niṣevate tato bhayaṃ kṣut paramaṃ jino 'bravīt || GoṚp_17 ||
children.translated_text: one consumes morsels mixed with tears — therefore the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) has declared hunger to be the supreme fear. [GoṚp 17]

children.text: api ca bhadantāḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, sirs —

children.text: jātaḥ kule mahati mānamadāvalipte kṣudvikṣato 'bhyudayakāla iva praharṣāt |
children.translated_text: One born in a great family, puffed up with pride and arrogance, when afflicted by hunger, [is] as if [overcome] with joy at the time of good fortune,

children.text: uccheṣapiṇḍam api nāma nṛpasya bhuṅkte yat sārameya iva kaṣṭataraṃ kim anyat || GoṚp_18 ||
children.translated_text: and eats even the leftover scraps of a king — like a dog. What could be more wretched than that? [GoṚp 18]

children.text: pratyantavāsaratayas tṛṇamātratuṣṭā yat tāpasā iva paravyasanānabhijñāḥ |
children.translated_text: Deer, delighting in dwelling at the borders, content with mere grass, unknowing of others' misfortunes like ascetics,

children.text: lakṣyībhavanti hariṇāḥ paritaḥ śarāṇāṃ kṣudduḥkham atra niyamena paraimi hetum || GoṚp_19 ||
children.translated_text: become targets for arrows from all sides — I am certain that hunger-suffering is the cause here. [GoṚp 19]

children.text: marmacchidāpi pavanena viśasyamānā hikkāsphuradgala
ka
children.translated_text: and

children.text:
kaṇṭhavikāradehāḥ |
āhārayanti picunā
children.translated_text:
neck,
they [still] seek to gather even a scrap of food with a rag —

children.text: pi
children.translated_text: therefore

children.text: yad annaleśān na kṣutsamaṃ vyasanam asti tataḥ prajānām || GoṚp_20 ||
children.translated_text: there is no distress of people equal to hunger. [GoṚp 20]
Even when being cut to pieces by the wind that pierces the vital points, with bodies deformed by hiccupping, spasming throat

children.text: api ca sādhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, good sirs —

children.text: āsannānnabhujo nabhastalacarā devā ivābhāsvarāḥ
children.translated_text: The beings of the first cosmic age, partaking of food that came near [spontaneously], moving through the sky, radiant like the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods,

children.text: sattvāḥ prāthamakalpikāḥ svakiraṇajvālāvalīmālinaḥ |
children.translated_text: wreathed in garlands of their own radiant flame-rays —

children.text: āhārapraṇayaprasaṅgavihatās te tām avasthāṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: they, ruined by the attachment of affection for food, reached that [wretched] state

children.text: yat pretā iva vartayanti kṛpaṇāḥ kṛcchropalabdhāśanāḥ || GoṚp_21 ||
children.translated_text: in which, like <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), the pitiable ones subsist, obtaining food only with difficulty. [GoṚp 21]

children.text: kṣudduḥkhopanipātadīnamanasaḥ śuṣkāni kāṣṭhāny api
children.translated_text: Those whose minds are wretched from the onset of hunger-suffering, devoid of disgust, eat even

children.text: klinnāni krimisaṃkulāni vighṛṇāḥ khādanty amedhyāni ca |
children.translated_text: dry sticks, things sodden and crawling with worms, and refuse.

children.text: kakṣaiḥ ke cana yāpayanti paruṣair lālājalakleditair
children.translated_text: Some sustain themselves on coarse husks moistened with their own saliva-water,

children.text: anye 'sthīni cirojjhitāny adhṛtayaḥ kṣudvikṣatā bhuñjate || GoṚp_22 ||
children.translated_text: others, unrestrained, afflicted by hunger, eat bones long discarded. [GoṚp 22]

children.text: te
children.translated_text: Those

children.text: rājāntararakṣiṇām api śirasy ādhāya pādaṃ khagāḥ
children.translated_text: birds, their fear forgotten from the onset of hunger-suffering, even placing their feet on the heads of the guards between kings,

children.text: kṣudduḥkhopanipātavismṛtabhayā hṛtvāmiṣaṃ bhuñjate |
children.translated_text: seize flesh and eat it.

children.text: vegenābhipatanti śastrakalilaprākāraduḥsaṃcarāñ
children.translated_text: They fly with force into enclosures difficult to traverse, bristling with weapons —

children.text: śūlāmāṃsalavābhilāṣakṛpaṇā gacchanti ke cit kṣayam || GoṚp_23 ||
children.translated_text: some, wretched with desire for a morsel of meat on a stake, meet their destruction. [GoṚp 23]

children.text: vividhāny api bhojanāni bhuktvā bhavane sve maṇihemabhājaneṣu |
children.translated_text: Though she had eaten various foods at home in vessels of gems and gold,

children.text: śitakaṇṭakavikṣatāgrahastā bubhuje sā badarāṇi satyabhāmā || GoṚp_24 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Satyabhāmā</s> ate jujube fruits with hands scratched by their sharp thorns. [GoṚp 24]

children.text: śāpotsargānugrahā
n
children.translated_text: was

children.text: mlānaśaktir dikparyantakhyātakīrtiprakāśaḥ |
children.translated_text: [now] weakened, whose fame once spread to the ends of the quarters —

children.text: viśvāmitro yac cakhāda śvamāṃsaṃ kṣudduḥkhānāṃ tena datto niyogaḥ || GoṚp_25 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāmitra</s> ate dog-flesh — by that, the supremacy of hunger-sufferings is established. [GoṚp 25]
[<s>Viśvāmitra</s>,] whose power to grant and withdraw curses

children.text: bālaḥ putraḥ premasarvasvabhūto yat kāntāre khādito dampatibhyām |
children.translated_text: A young son, the entirety of [parental] love, who was eaten in the wilderness by both husband and wife —

children.text: kṣudduḥkhebhyo nāsti duḥkhaṃ tato 'nyaj janmāṭavyāṃ dhāvatāṃ krūrarūpam || GoṚp_26 ||
children.translated_text: there is no other suffering more cruel than hunger-sufferings for those running through the forest of births. [GoṚp 26]

children.text: yācñādainyān mlānavaktraprasādā dehīty evaṃ vyāharanty apragalbham |
children.translated_text: Standing at the door of enemies, craving food due to hunger, with the grace of their faces withered by the wretchedness of begging,

children.text: dvāri sthitvā vidviṣāṃ kṣudvilolāḥ kiṃ manyadhve duḥkham asmād balīyaḥ || GoṚp_27 ||
children.translated_text: uttering 'Give!' feebly — do you think there is any suffering stronger than this? [GoṚp 27]

children.text: athaiṣāṃ pārāvataḥ provāca | satyaṃ balavat kṣudduḥkham | api tu mamābhiprāyaḥ śrūyatām |
children.translated_text: Then the pigeon among them spoke: "It is true that hunger-suffering is powerful. But hear my view:"

children.text: rāga eva mahad duḥkham iti me niścitā matiḥ |
children.translated_text: "Passion (<s>rāga</s>) itself is the great suffering — this is my firm conviction.

children.text: kṣut kariṣyati kiṃ yasmād bhasmanāpi nivāryate || GoṚp_28 ||
children.translated_text: For what can hunger do, since it is warded off even by ashes? [GoṚp 28]

children.text: api ca
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: vāyvambujīrṇataruparṇabhujo 'pi nāma dīrghopavāsaparikarśitagātrayantrāḥ |
children.translated_text: Sages who feed on wind, water, withered tree-leaves, whose bodily mechanisms are emaciated by long fasting,

children.text: andhībhavanti munayaḥ skhalitaprabhāvā rāgena duḥpratividhānasamudbhavena || GoṚp_29 ||
children.translated_text: become blind, their powers faltering, due to passion of irremediable origin. [GoṚp 29]

children.text: amlānacandrakiraṇāsv api yāminīṣu protphālitābhravivareṣv api vā dineṣu |
children.translated_text: Even in nights when the moonbeams are unfading, even on days when the cloud-breaks are wide open,

children.text: andho 'dhamo bhavati rāgaparājitātmā tasmān na rāgasadṛśaḥ kalir asti loke || GoṚp_30 ||
children.translated_text: the lowest [of beings] becomes blind when conquered by passion — therefore there is no affliction in the world equal to passion. [GoṚp 30]

children.text: lajjāṃ nimīlayati sarvaguṇāgrabhūtāṃ kīrtiṃ kalaṅkayati nirvikalaprasādām |
children.translated_text: It closes the eyes of shame, foremost among all virtues; it stains fame, whose purity is beyond question;

children.text: dharmātmanām api ca nāma tiraskaroti śreyāṃsi meruśikharapratimāni rāgaḥ || GoṚp_31 ||
children.translated_text: passion puts to shame even the spiritual virtues of the righteous, [virtues] towering like the peak of <s>Meru</s>. [GoṚp 31]

children.text: nāyaṃ vayas tulayati pragataṃ narāṇāṃ nāpekṣate kulaviśuddhimayīṃ vyavasthām |
children.translated_text: It does not consider the advanced age of men; it does not regard the propriety [born of] purity of family.

children.text: lokāpavādagahanāny api laṅghayitvā saṃkalparāgaturagaḥ svamatena yāti || GoṚp_32 ||
children.translated_text: Having leapt over even the dense [thickets of] worldly censure, the horse of desire-passion goes by its own will. [GoṚp 32]

children.text: saṃmūrchitaḥ kusumahāsiṣu mallikānāṃ gulmeṣu vārikaṇakaṇṭakito nabhasvān |
children.translated_text: The wind, swelling among the flower-smiling <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) bushes, sprinkled with water-drops,

children.text: saṃtāpayaty anupaśāntavikalparāgaṃ ceto narasya sutarām aparīkṣakasya || GoṚp_33 ||
children.translated_text: greatly torments the mind of a man lacking in discernment, in whom the passion of imagination is unquelled. [GoṚp 33]

children.text: sūkṣmāṇi saṃdhigahanāny api cāvagāhya svapratyayā bahuvidhāni matāntarāṇi |
children.translated_text: Even penetrating the subtle and dense jointures, and the manifold doctrines of other schools relying on their own authority —

children.text: medhāvino 'pi nanu rāgapiśācavaśyāḥ saṃprāpnuvanti paramaṃ smṛtivipralopam || GoṚp_34 ||
children.translated_text: do not even the wise, when mastered by the demon of passion, attain the supreme loss of mindfulness? [GoṚp 34]
