children.text: hatvāpi rāgaviṣabījavijṛṃbhitāni svabhyastayogapadavīsthirabuddhayo 'pi |
children.translated_text: Even those of firm understanding, established on the path of yoga mastered through practice, having killed [the seeds of passion] —

children.text: yoṣinmukhāny alakapallavitāny udīkṣya bhraṣṭā bhavanti tapasaḥ paśubhiḥ samānāḥ || GoṚp_35 ||
children.translated_text: upon gazing at women's faces adorned with curling locks, they fall from their austerity, becoming equal to animals. [GoṚp 35]

children.text: dṛṅmārgaheyam avahatya balaṃ malānām ekāvaśiṣṭabhavabandhanatantavo 'pi |
children.translated_text: Even noble ones who have abandoned on the path of sight the power of defilements, who have only a single thread of the bond of existence remaining,

children.text: āryā manaḥsthitibhidānugatāḥ smareṇa lajjālavo 'py anubhavanti daśām anāryām || GoṚp_36 ||
children.translated_text: pursued by <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) who pierces the stability of the mind — even they, with only a trace of modesty, experience an ignoble condition. [GoṚp 36]

children.text: uccaiḥ śiro vahati tāvad ayaṃ prajāsu yāvan na kāmakalidurlalitāny upāste |
children.translated_text: A person carries his head high among people only so long as he does not indulge in the wanton play of passion-affliction.

children.text: āliṅgitaś ca puruṣo madanajvareṇa śvā saṃkaṭasthita iva prakhalīkṛtaś ca || GoṚp_37 ||
children.translated_text: But when a man is embraced by the fever of desire, he is debased like a dog standing in a narrow place. [GoṚp 37]

children.text: api ca bhadramukhāḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, good sirs —

children.text:
kaṇṭhopāntavirodhagadgadataraṃ kūjañ chanaiḥ pṛṣṭhato
rāgād raktatarekṣaṇaḥ sacakitaṃ nirbha
r
children.translated_text: with

children.text:
tsyamāno muhuḥ |
śyenāyātam asaṃpradhārya dayitām anveti pārāvato
children.translated_text: fervor, without discerning that a hawk has come — the pigeon follows his beloved —

children.text: rāgābhyāsakalaṅkitasya manasaḥ kā vañcanā dūrataḥ || GoṚp_38 ||
children.translated_text: what deception is distant for a mind stained by the habit of passion? // GoṚp 38 //
Cooing softly from behind, with a stammering sound blocked in the vicinity of the throat, eyes reddened with passion, repeatedly bowing

children.text: ye naikāṅgulitarjanām api guroḥ soḍhuṃ samarthā narāḥ
children.translated_text: Those men who cannot endure even a single finger's rebuke from a teacher,

children.text: mānātyunnatamānasāś ca sakalaṃ paśyanty adhastāj jagat |
children.translated_text: whose minds are exceedingly elevated with pride, who look down upon the entire world —

children.text: te rāgena kadarthitā dhṛtibhidā pādair hatā yoṣitām
children.translated_text: they, humiliated by passion, their fortitude shattered, struck by the feet of women,

children.text: ājñā mūrdhabhir udvahanti kṛpaṇā mālām ivāmlāyinīm || GoṚp_39 ||
children.translated_text: carry their commands on their heads, wretched, like a wilting garland. // GoṚp 39 //

children.text:
jitvārātīn samaravijayakhyātaśauryāvalepān
āyāminyo jagati vitatā
ḥ
children.translated_text: throughout

children.text:
kīrtayo yaiḥ samantāt |
bhinnās te 'pi prakṛticapalair aṅganāvākyabāṇair
children.translated_text: the world in all directions — they too are pierced by the arrow-words of women, naturally fickle,

children.text: nirmaryādāḥ punar ayaśasā jīvalokaṃ sphuranti || GoṚp_40 ||
children.translated_text: and, transgressing all bounds, they flash across the world of the living with infamy. // GoṚp 40 //
Those who, having conquered enemies, with fame for valor well-known from battlefield victories, have their extended glories spread

children.text: paricitam api śrutvā vādyadhvaniṃ rajanīkṣaye
children.translated_text: Those women who, hearing the familiar sound of musical instruments at dawn,

children.text: bhavati sahasā yāsāṃ trāso gṛheṣu savepathuḥ |
children.translated_text: suddenly become frightened in their homes, trembling —

children.text: madanavihatās tā gacchanti kṣapāsv abhisārikā
children.translated_text: they, struck by passion, go as nocturnal lovers (<s>abhisārikā</s>) in the nights

children.text: bahalatimiracchannān deśāñ chivārutabhīṣaṇān || GoṚp_41 ||
children.translated_text: to places covered in dense darkness, terrifying with the cries of jackals. // GoṚp 41 //

children.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ salīlaṃ sakusumanikare harmyapṛṣthe vivikte
children.translated_text: Those young women who, on a secluded terrace strewn with flowers, slowly and gracefully

children.text: khidyante saṃcarantyaḥ priyavidhṛtakarāmbhoruhā yās taruṇyaḥ |
children.translated_text: wander about, growing weary, their lotus-hands held by their beloved —

children.text: rāgāveśāvatantrā bahumahiṣakhurakṣuṇṇapaṅkāṅkadurgān
children.translated_text: overpowered by the force of passion, they cross in the rainy nights

children.text: mārgān prāvṛḍniśāsu drutapadarabhasaṃ tā vyatikramya yānti || GoṚp_42 ||
children.translated_text: with rapid rushing steps paths made treacherous with mud churned by many buffalo hooves. // GoṚp 42 //

children.text:
vepante navavāricūrṇaśiśiraiḥ spṛṣṭāḥ kadambānilair
bālā jālagavākṣapakṣavisṛtair yā ramyaharmyāśritāḥ |
dhārāpātaviśīrṇapuṣparacanā
ḥ
children.translated_text: the

children.text: sāraṅgaparyākulās
children.translated_text: downpour, agitated by the <s>sāraṅga</s> birds —

children.text: tā paṅkāṅkitamūkanūpuraravā rātrau vrajanty adhvanā || GoṚp_43 ||
children.translated_text: they walk along the road at night, their anklets muffled and silenced by mud. // GoṚp 43 //

Those girls, sheltered in lovely mansions, who tremble when touched by breezes cool with fresh raindrops and fragrant with <s>kadamba</s>, entering through latticed windows — their flower arrangements scattered by

children.text: śastrāpātā kuvalayadalasparśakalpā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Sword-blows become like the touch of blue-lotus petals,

children.text: jvālāś cāgner gataghanaśaraccandrikāśleṣaśītāḥ |
children.translated_text: and flames of fire become cool as the embrace of autumn moonlight with dissipated clouds;

children.text: kāmān prāpya śvasanacapalā mūrtayaḥ pannagānāṃ
children.translated_text: upon attaining desire, the bodies of serpents, restless with breathing,

children.text: sāmyaṃ yānti bhramaravirutair dāmabhir mālatīnām || GoṚp_44 ||
children.translated_text: become equal to garlands of jasmine with the humming of bees. // GoṚp 44 //

children.text: sarvāyatanonmāthī tasmād rāgo mahad duḥkham ity ukte bhujago 'bravīt | nanu khalu duḥkham rāgaś cittaviparyāsakṛd durācāraḥ | krodhaṃ tu duḥkhataram ity avaimi cetojvalaṃ tu mūlam | kutaḥ
children.translated_text: Since passion churns all the senses, therefore passion is great suffering — thus having been said, the serpent spoke: 'Indeed, passion is suffering, it distorts the mind, and causes misconduct. But I consider anger to be even more painful — it is the burning root of the mind. Why?'

children.text: vikṣiptāmbudasāndracandrakiraṇaprakṣālitāṭṭālake
children.translated_text: In a house charming with the sweet singing of women accompanying

children.text: vīṇāveṇuravānubaddhamadhurastrīgitaramye gṛhe |
children.translated_text: the sounds of <s>vīṇā</s> and flute, in a mansion washed by the scattered moonbeams of clouds parting [in the sky] —

children.text: viddhaḥ krodhaśilīmukhena puruṣo nāpnoti nidrāṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: a man pierced by the arrow of anger does not obtain sleep;

children.text: krodhād duḥkhataraṃ na duḥkham aparaṃ kiṃ cit tato vidyate || GoṚp_45 ||
children.translated_text: therefore no suffering more painful than anger exists. // GoṚp 45 //

children.text: yogābhyāsaviśeṣaśāntamatibhir vāyvambumūlāśanair
children.translated_text: Sages whose minds are pacified by the excellence of <s>yoga</s> practice, who subsist on wind, water, and roots,

children.text: viśrambhāyatanatvam abhyupagataiḥ prāyas tiraścām api |
children.translated_text: who have become objects of trust for even animals, generally —

children.text: dagdhāḥ krodhahutāśanair janapadāḥ krūrair ivāśīviṣair
children.translated_text: have burned entire countries with the fires of anger, like fierce venomous serpents;

children.text: yan mohād ṛṣibhir na duḥkham aparaṃ krodhāt tato vidyate || GoṚp_46 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, no suffering greater than anger — born of delusion in sages — exists. // GoṚp 46 //

children.text: trāsāyāsaviśeṣalolanayanastrībāṣpaparyākulaṃ
children.translated_text: The city filled with the tear-blurred eyes of women, their gaze unsteady with particular fear and distress,

children.text: bālaiś ca stanacūcukārpitamukhaiḥ sāvegam unnāditam |
children.translated_text: crying out in alarm with infants whose mouths were pressed to the nipples of breasts —

children.text: saṃrambhasphuritekṣaṇatrayaśikhijvālāpiśaṅgānano
children.translated_text: that fierce <s>Rudra</s> (Śiva), his face tawny with the three-eyed flame flickering in his fury,

children.text: rudro yat tripuram dadāha vighṛṇaḥ krodhasya tad vaikṛtam || GoṚp_47 ||
children.translated_text: without compassion burned the triple city (<s>Tripura</s>) — that is the work of anger. // GoṚp 47 //

children.text: tīvrātaṅkavilolamūlavalayā naivāñjalipragrahāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither joined palms, their base-bracelets trembling with intense agitation,

children.text: strīṇāṃ bāṣpakaṇāḥ karālataralā no pakṣmalā dṛṣṭayaḥ |
children.translated_text: nor the tear-drops of women, terribly trembling, nor their glances, heavy with lashes,

children.text: kurvanty āvaraṇaṃ lalāṭapaṭalavyāvartamānabhruvāṃ
children.translated_text: create a barrier — for the minds of kings, [minds] that are poison-serpents of wrath with brows knitted on the forehead —

children.text: rājñāṃ krodhaviṣāśivasya manasaḥ kiṃ nāma duḥkhaṃ tataḥ || GoṚp_48 ||
children.translated_text: what suffering, then, [is greater] than that? // GoṚp 48 //

children.text:
garbhādhāraṇayantraṇām avigaṇayyāpāyikāṃ mātaraṃ
satkārātiśayakṣamaṃ ca pitaraṃ snehadravādhyāśayam |
yad viśrambhaniratyayāṃ
ś ca
suhṛdo ghnanti kṣatādhyāśayāḥ
children.translated_text: and friends, and even a father worthy of the highest honor, whose heart overflows with affection —

children.text: krodhasyaiva vipākadāruṇatarās tā vṛttayaḥ sādhavaḥ || GoṚp_49 ||
children.translated_text: those are the workings of anger, more terrible in their ripening, O saints. // GoṚp 49 //
When those of wounded disposition kill a mother — who endured the torment of bearing the womb, whose devoted care was one of unfailing trust

children.text: utpadyante paramamatayaḥ śuddhaye ye prajānāṃ
children.translated_text: Those who arise as supreme intellects for the purification of beings

children.text: duḥśodhānām avikalamalālīḍhagūḍhāśayānām |
children.translated_text: whose hard-to-cleanse hearts are smeared with complete impurities hidden deep within —

children.text: tān apy āryān parahitasukhaprakriyāmātrahāryān
children.translated_text: even those noble ones, whose only motive is the benefit and happiness of others,

children.text: krodhāviṣṭā vacanaviśikhaiḥ saṃmukhaṃ ghnanty anāryāḥ || GoṚp_50 ||
children.translated_text: the ignoble, possessed by anger, strike face-to-face with arrow-words. // GoṚp 50 //

children.text: krodhāghrāto bhavati puruṣo dagdhalāvaṇyavaktro
children.translated_text: A man merely touched by anger becomes one whose face's beauty is burned;

children.text: jvālācakrakrakacakalilān krodhano yāty apāyān |
children.translated_text: the angry one goes to lower realms filled with wheel-flames and saws;

children.text: tebhyo bhraṣṭo bhavati jagato locanātaṅkabhūtaḥ
children.translated_text: fallen from those, he becomes a painful sight to the world's eyes —

children.text: śrīvidveṣo na ripur aparaḥ krodhatulyo 'sti yasmāt || GoṚp_51 ||
children.translated_text: since no enemy equal to anger, the hater of prosperity, exists. // GoṚp 51 //

children.text:
yasmin rakto bhavati puruṣas tatra kuryāt priyāṇi
dviṣṭo yasmai tadadhikatarāṇy apriyāṇy eva dhatte |
alpāvadye 'vigatarajasā tena roṣa
ḥ
children.translated_text: entered

children.text: praviṣṭaḥ
krodhaṃ krodhopaśamakuśalā vadyayoniṃ vadanti || GoṚp_52 ||
children.translated_text: those skilled in pacifying anger declare anger to be the cause of death. // GoṚp 52 //
To one he is attached to, a person does favors; to one he dislikes, he inflicts even greater displeasure. When, against a minor fault, by one not free from passion, anger has

children.text: trāsotphullamukhīṃ mṛgīm iva vane lajjālasabhrūlatāṃ
children.translated_text: A doe with face upturned in terror in the forest, her vine-brows languid with shame,

children.text: saṃrambhāpahṛtottarīyavasanāṃ vicchinnakaṇṭheguṇām |
children.translated_text: her upper garment torn away in fury, her necklace broken —

children.text: cikleśa pracurāṅganām iva satīṃ duḥśāsano draupadīṃ
children.translated_text: thus <s>Duḥśāsana</s> tormented <s>Draupadī</s>, the virtuous one, like a common woman before the full assembly —

children.text: sphīte yat sadasi prakāmacapalāḥ krodhasya tā vipluṣaḥ || GoṚp_53 ||
children.translated_text: those are the sparks of anger, freely reckless. // GoṚp 53 //

children.text: śāntātmā vijane vane prativasan nikṣiptadaṇḍo 'pi san
children.translated_text: A sage of peaceful soul, dwelling in a secluded forest, having laid down his staff,

children.text: lokānām animittapeśalarasaḥ snehārthakārī suhṛt |
children.translated_text: a friend of causeless, gracious sweetness to the people, acting from pure affection —

children.text: khaḍgenārdra iva drumaḥ śakalito yat kṣāntivādī munī
children.translated_text: that he, the advocate of patience, was split like a tree with a wet axe —

children.text: rājñā durjanavallabhasya nikaṣaṃ krodhasya tat prāhṛtam || GoṚp_54 ||
children.translated_text: that was the blow of anger dealt by a king dear to the wicked. // GoṚp 54 //

children.text: anekādīnavamayo vinipātī manojvalaḥ |
children.translated_text: Fraught with manifold evils, causing downfall, blazing in the mind —

children.text: ity evaṃ sarvaduḥkhānāṃ krodhārir dhuri vartate || GoṚp_55 ||
children.translated_text: thus anger, enemy of all, stands foremost among all sufferings. // GoṚp 55 //

children.text: mṛgo 'bravīt | samyag vaktum etad bhujagapate krodhavaiśasaṃ tīvram | maraṇabhayād adhikataraṃ duḥkham ahaṃ nāvagacchāmi | kutaḥ
children.translated_text: The deer said: 'You have spoken well, O serpent-lord, about the terrible violence of anger. But I know no suffering greater than the fear of death. Why?'

children.text:
maraṇopanipātakātarāṇāṃ kamanīyāny api mārabandhanāni |
na mano ramayanti yaj janānāṃ
na
children.translated_text: therefore I know

children.text: ⏑ – duḥkham ataḥ paraṃ paraimi || GoṚp_56 ||
children.translated_text: no suffering beyond this. // GoṚp 56 //
The bonds of <s>Māra</s> (Death), even though charming, do not delight the minds of people who are terror-stricken by the approach of death;

children.text: suhṛdāṃ vadanāni vīkṣamāṇo ghanabāṣpāmbutaraṅgadurdināni |
children.translated_text: The misfortune one encounters at the hour of death, gazing upon the faces of friends

children.text: labhate vyasanaṃ yad antakāle na tato duḥkham avaimi kaṣṭam anyat || GoṚp_57 ||
children.translated_text: overcast with floods of dense tears — I know no other suffering more terrible than that. // GoṚp 57 //

children.text: pavanair avidheyaduḥkhaśīlaiḥ karapatrair iva pāṭyamānadehāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those whose bodies are being cut as if by saws — by winds of ungovernable, painful character —

children.text: paralokamahāprapātaśaṅkāḥ kṛpaṇā duḥkham avāpnuvanti tīvram || GoṚp_58 ||
children.translated_text: fearful of the great precipice of the next world, the wretched ones suffer intensely. // GoṚp 58 //

children.text: paripāṇḍukapolamaṇḍalāni śvasanamlānavipāṭalādharāṇi |
children.translated_text: The pallid cheek-circles, the lips faded to dull pink from labored breathing —

children.text: dayitāvadanāni nānukampāṃ janayanty antakadantavikṣatānām || GoṚp_59 ||
children.translated_text: the faces of the beloved do not produce compassion in those bitten by the teeth of Death. // GoṚp 59 //

children.text: jananī malapaṅkadigdhaveṇī sutaviśrambhaniratyayopacārā |
children.translated_text: A mother, her braided hair smeared with dirt, whose devoted care for her son was one of unfailing trust,

children.text: upamṛtyum udīkṣya śokapaṅke vinimajjaty aparāyaṇā rudantī || GoṚp_60 ||
children.translated_text: seeing him near death, sinks weeping into the mud of grief, without refuge. // GoṚp 60 //

children.text: calatāṃ tṛṇaparṇapallavānāṃ dhvanim ākarṇya vane mṛgā vasantaḥ |
children.translated_text: We deer, dwelling in the forest, hearing the sound of stirring grass, leaves, and twigs,

children.text: anapekṣya parasparaṃ dravāmaḥ svasutān apy avadhūya mṛtyubhītāḥ || GoṚp_61 ||
children.translated_text: run without looking at each other, shaking off even our own fawns, terrified of death. // GoṚp 61 //

children.text: kaṭhinopalaśarkarākarāleṣv analapluṣṭatṛṇācaladrumeṣu |
children.translated_text: In mountain fortresses with hard stones and pebbles, with trees and grasses scorched by fire,

children.text: maraṇāśanisaṃnipātabhītāḥ giridurgeṣv aparāyaṇā vasāmaḥ || GoṚp_62 ||
children.translated_text: we dwell without refuge, terrified by the thunderbolt-stroke of death. // GoṚp 62 //

children.text: rajasāpi virūkṣitātmabhāvāḥ paruṣaiś copahatā gadaprahāraiḥ |
children.translated_text: With our very being roughened by dust, struck by harsh blows of disease,

children.text: mahatīm api yātanāṃ vahante vacanatrāsajaḍā bhavanti mṛtyoḥ || GoṚp_63 ||
children.translated_text: though bearing even great torment, [all beings] become paralyzed with fear at the word of Death. // GoṚp 63 //

children.text: hariṇo hariṇeva bandhumadhyād abhibhūya prasabhaṃ vikṛṣyamāṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Like a deer [seized] by a lion, forcibly seized from the midst of its kin,

children.text: avikhaṇḍitapauruṣeṇa mṛtyudviṣatā duḥkham ayaṃ paraiti lokaḥ || GoṚp_64 ||
children.translated_text: by the enemy Death of unbroken might — this world goes to suffering. // GoṚp 64 //

children.text: pariśuṣkagalāntarālanāḍāḥ saritāṃ prāpya taṭāny udanvatīnām |
children.translated_text: With the veins inside our throats dried up, reaching the banks of rivers,

children.text: anavāptajalā mṛgāribhītā vayam utplutya diśo diśaṃ vrajāmaḥ || GoṚp_65 ||
children.translated_text: unable to obtain water, terrified of predators, we leap from direction to direction. // GoṚp 65 //

children.text: deśe deśe vayam aśaraṇā vyādham udvīkṣya hiṃsraṃ
children.translated_text: In every region, shelterless, seeing the violent hunter,

children.text: śaṣpodbhedapracayaharitān saṃparityajya dāvān |
children.translated_text: abandoning the forests green with fresh grass-shoots,

children.text: vindhyāṭavyām ajagaradarīdāruṇāyām anāthāḥ
children.translated_text: in the terrible <s>Vindhya</s> wilderness with its dreadful python-caves, orphaned,

children.text: śārdūlānāṃ nakhamukhaśikhālakṣyabhāvaṃ vrajāmaḥ || GoṚp_66 ||
children.translated_text: we become targets for the claw-tips of tigers. // GoṚp 66 //

children.text: tṛṇapuruṣakān apy ālokya dravanti manāṃsi no
na
children.translated_text: neither

children.text:
niśi na divā mṛtyor bhītāḥ sukhāni labhāmahe |
vitatadhanuṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā vyādhaṃ kṛtāntam ivāparaṃ
children.translated_text: by night nor by day do we, terrified of death, obtain pleasures; seeing a hunter with outstretched bow, like another god of Death,

children.text: na bhavati bhayatrastāṅgānāṃ manāg api bhojanam || GoṚp_67 ||
children.translated_text: there is not the slightest food for those whose limbs are paralyzed with fear. // GoṚp 67 //
Even at the sight of grass-scarecrows our minds flee;

children.text: tarupallavāharitapāṭalādharāḥ kṣitireṇudhūsaritaromarājikāḥ |
children.translated_text: Doe-women, with lips rosy from nibbling tree-shoots, with rows of hair greyed by earth-dust,

children.text: hariṇāṅganā na ramayanti no mano maraṇāturaṃ prakṛticañcalekṣaṇāḥ || GoṚp_68 ||
children.translated_text: with naturally restless eyes — they do not delight our death-stricken minds. // GoṚp 68 //

children.text: sthalīvāse tuṣṭā navajalatṛṇāsvādapaṭavaḥ
children.translated_text: Content with dwelling on the plains, skilled in tasting fresh water and grass,

children.text: salīlaṃ kāntābhiḥ saha gamanavinyāsacaturāḥ |
children.translated_text: graceful in their gait alongside their mates,

children.text: na lokadveṣṭāro na ca na cakitā nāpi bhayadāḥ
children.translated_text: neither hating the world, nor not startled, nor causing fear —

children.text: prayatnād vadhyante tad api hariṇā raudramatibhiḥ || GoṚp_69 ||
children.translated_text: yet even deer are hunted with effort by those of cruel minds. // GoṚp 69 //

children.text: aṭatām aṭavīṣv avāritānāṃ tṛṇaśaṣpāṅkuramātrabhojanānām |
children.translated_text: Tell me, seeing what enmity do people become enemies

children.text: vada kaṃ nu samīkṣya vairibhāvaṃ hariṇānām api vidviṣo bhavanti || GoṚp_70 ||
children.translated_text: of deer who roam the forests unrestrained, whose food is only grass and sprouts? // GoṚp 70 //

children.text: ṛjuṣūttānacitteṣu tṛṇatoyopajīviṣu |
children.translated_text: Toward deer who are straightforward and guileless in heart,

children.text: hariṇeṣu kathaṃ krūrāḥ praharanti mṛgadviṣaḥ || GoṚp_71 ||
children.translated_text: who subsist on grass and water — how do the cruel deer-hunters strike? // GoṚp 71 //

children.text: sarvaduḥkhapratikruṣṭaṃ sarvabhūtabhayaṃkaram |
children.translated_text: Death cries out against all suffering, is terrifying to all beings —

children.text: avaimi maraṇaṃ tasmād upasargaduruttaram || GoṚp_72 ||
children.translated_text: therefore I know death to be a calamity impossible to overcome. // GoṚp 72 //

children.text: yataś ca te mahāsattvāḥ svaṃ svaṃ vādam abhiniviṣṭā na kathāparyavasānam āsādayanti tato bodhisattvam upetya nyāyataḥ praṇamyemam artham ūcuḥ | bhagavan kṣudrāgakrodhamaraṇabhayānāṃ kiṃ nu duḥkham | kasya vāsmākaṃ subhāṣitam ity athainān sa munivaryo 'bravīt |
children.translated_text: Since those great beings, each absorbed in their own argument, could not reach a conclusion to their debate, they approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, bowed properly, and stated the matter: 'Blessed one, among petty desire, anger, and the fear of death — which is [the greatest] suffering? And whose argument among us is well-spoken?' Then that best of sages said to them:

children.text: subhāṣitaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca suniścitam |
children.translated_text: All have spoken well, and all have well-established [arguments];

children.text: sarvāṇy etāni duḥkhāni rujanti bhuvanatrayam || GoṚp_73 ||
children.translated_text: all these sufferings torment the three worlds. // GoṚp 73 //

children.text: api ca bhadramukhā mamāpy abhiprāyaḥ śrūyatām |
children.translated_text: And moreover, O fair-faced ones, hear my own view:

children.text: abhīkṣṇasamudācāro dharme yo yasya bādhate |
children.translated_text: That habitual disposition which obstructs a person's practice of <s>Dharma</s> —

children.text: āśramaṃ manaso duḥkham ity avaimi bravīmi ca || GoṚp_74 ||
children.translated_text: that is the abode of suffering for the mind — this I know and declare. // GoṚp 74 //

children.text: spardhamānā ivānyonyam upaghnanti vidāhinaḥ |
children.translated_text: As if competing with one another, the impurities associated with birth

children.text: lokān eva nirālokāñ janmasaṃbandhino malāḥ || GoṚp_75 ||
children.translated_text: strike down the worlds themselves — the blind worlds — burning. // GoṚp 75 //

children.text: kṣudduḥkhopahatātmānaḥ kiṃ na kuryuḥ śarīriṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: What will embodied beings, with their very selves afflicted by the suffering of hunger, not do —

children.text: apāyaphalasaṃdhānadāruṇaṃ karmavaiśasam || GoṚp_76 ||
children.translated_text: the terrible violence of <s>karma</s> that leads to the fruit of lower rebirths? // GoṚp 76 //

children.text: vyatikrāntāryamaryādā rāgopakliṣṭacetasaḥ |
children.translated_text: People who have transgressed the bounds of noble conduct, with minds stained by passion,

children.text: bhavanti karuṇāpātraṃ puruṣās tattvadarśinām || GoṚp_77 ||
children.translated_text: become objects of compassion for those who see the truth. // GoṚp 77 //

children.text: sphuṭabhrūbhaṅgavikṣepabhramadvikṛtalocanāḥ |
children.translated_text: With eyebrows split in frowning, glancing about with distorted, rolling eyes,

children.text: kṣaṇenānya ivābhānti puruṣāḥ paruṣā ruṣā || GoṚp_78 ||
children.translated_text: in an instant people appear as if someone else, harsh with anger. // GoṚp 78 //

children.text: sarvasattvair vinābhāvapravāso dīrghakālikaḥ |
children.translated_text: The prolonged journey of separation from all beings —

children.text: bhayam ātyantikaṃ hīdaṃ maraṇaṃ sarvadehinām || GoṚp_79 ||
children.translated_text: this is the ultimate fear: death, for all embodied beings. // GoṚp 79 //

children.text: ete cānye ca ye duḥkhaprakārā romaharṣaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: These and other kinds of suffering, which make the hair stand on end,

children.text: te jātim anuvartante karuṇām iva sādhavaḥ || GoṚp_80 ||
children.translated_text: follow birth, just as the virtuous follow compassion. // GoṚp 80 //

children.text: mātāpitror vipratipattiṃ ................ |
children.translated_text: The disagreement with mother and father ................ ;

children.text: ................. kiṃ nāma tataḥ paraṃ duḥkham || GoṚp_81 ||
children.translated_text: what suffering, then, is greater than that? // GoṚp 81 //

children.text: kiṃ nāma tataḥ paraṃ duḥkham || GoṚp_82 ||
children.translated_text: what suffering, then, is greater than that? // GoṚp 82 //

children.text: ruddhocchvāsasya bhṛśaṃ kṛmer ivāmedhyapaṅkamagnasya |
children.translated_text: The state of one in the womb, whose breathing is choked, submerged in impure mud like a worm —

children.text: yā garbhasthasya daśā kiṃ nāma tataḥ paraṃ duḥkham || GoṚp_83 ||
children.translated_text: what suffering, then, is greater than that? // GoṚp 83 //

children.text: kāyāvaskaranirjharavivare niṣpiṣyamāṇadehasya |
children.translated_text: The state of one being born, his body crushed in the cascading cavity of the body's mechanism —

children.text: yā prasavasthasya daśā kiṃ nāma tataḥ paraṃ duḥkham || GoṚp_84 ||
children.translated_text: what suffering, then, is greater than that? // GoṚp 84 //

children.text: tasmāj jātiṃ duḥkhaṃ jātijarāvyādhimaraṇanirmuktāḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, birth is suffering — thus proclaim the supreme narrators, the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), freed from birth, old age, disease, and death,

children.text: kathayanti kathikavarā jinā jitakathaṃkathābījāḥ || GoṚp_85 ||
children.translated_text: who have conquered the seed of doubt. // GoṚp 85 //

children.text: api cāyuṣmantaḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, O long-lived ones:

children.text: rāgo 'naikavidho jarā paribhavo bhogārjanā rakṣaṇā
children.translated_text: Passion of many kinds, old age, humiliation, the toil of acquiring, guarding,

children.text: pradhvaṃsavyasanaṃ mahātyayam asatsaṃparkajaṃ vaikṛtam |
children.translated_text: and the calamity of losing wealth, the great danger, and the distortion born of association with the wicked,

children.text: iṣṭāniṣṭaviyogayogasulabhās te te manoviplavā
children.translated_text: those various agitations of mind that easily arise from the union with the undesired and separation from the desired —

children.text: jātiṃ prāpya yato bhavanti jagataḥ saiveha duḥkhaṃ tataḥ || GoṚp_86 ||
children.translated_text: since these occur upon obtaining birth, birth itself is therefore suffering here. || GoṚp 86 ||

children.text: ātmārthapratiyoginī bhagavatāṃ yeṣāṃ kriyā sarvadā
children.translated_text: Those whose every action of the Blessed Ones is always contrary to self-interest,

children.text: sarvākāraparopakāramadhurā yeṣāṃ samutpattayaḥ |
children.translated_text: those whose arisings are sweet with benefit to others in every aspect —

children.text: ślāghyā jātir acintyayogamahatāṃ teṣāṃ jagaccakṣuṣāṃ
children.translated_text: praiseworthy is the birth of those great ones of inconceivable spiritual attainment, the eyes of the world;

children.text: janma svārthaparasya tu kṣaṇikam apy āpāyikī viplutiḥ || GoṚp_87 ||
children.translated_text: but for one devoted to self-interest, even a momentary birth is a calamitous destruction. || GoṚp 87 ||

children.text: tasmād brūmahe |
children.translated_text: Therefore we say:

children.text: saṃbodhaye kuruta vā sthiram apramādaṃ tūrṇaṃ ghaṭadhvam atha vā bhavasaṃkṣayāya |
children.translated_text: Either fix firm vigilance upon supreme <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening), or quickly strive for the destruction of [cyclic] existence;

children.text: etad dvayaṃ tu virahayya viśanty akāmā bhīmāny apāyavaḍavāmukhagahvarāṇi || GoṚp_88 ||
children.translated_text: but those who abandon both of these enter unwillingly the terrible cavern-mouths of the mare-fire of the lower realms. || GoṚp 88 ||

children.text: yatnena ced ubhayam etad avāpnuvanti yatnaḥ phale mahati yuktataro mato me |
children.translated_text: If through effort one attains both of these, effort directed toward the greater fruit is considered more fitting by me;

children.text: chidraṃ varāṭakam avāpya sudhāpi kiṃ syāc cintāmaṇer adhigamāya varaṃ śramo 'pi || GoṚp_89 ||
children.translated_text: what use is gaining even nectar if one obtains [only] a broken cowrie? Better even the toil of acquiring the wish-fulfilling gem. || GoṚp 89 ||

children.text: māṃ praty ataś ca viphalo 'pi varaṃ prayāsaḥ sādhor mahājanahitāvahitāśayasya |
children.translated_text: And for me therefore, even fruitless effort is better — effort of the good person whose intention is devoted to the welfare of the great multitude;

children.text: icchāviśeṣaviṣayasya parākramasya prasthānam eva mahatīṃ ratim ādadhāti || GoṚp_90 ||
children.translated_text: the very setting forth of heroism directed at a special object of aspiration bestows great delight. || GoṚp 90 ||

children.text: sādhāraṇāni dayitaiḥ saha pelavāni āmodayanti sutarāṃ hṛdayaṃ sukhāni |
children.translated_text: The pleasures shared together with loved ones, delicate, gladden the heart greatly;

children.text: pīḍākarāṇi mahatāṃ samupasthitāni prākarṣikāny api sukhāni tu yautakāni || GoṚp_91 ||
children.translated_text: but the pleasures that come as dowry [of merit], though they bring suffering upon the great when encountered, are yet attractive. || GoṚp 91 ||

children.text: khadyotānāṃ janayati yathā dehasadbhāvamātraṃ
children.translated_text: Just as the glow of fireflies produces merely the semblance of bodily existence,

children.text: dīptir nāsau sphurati jagatāṃ – ⏑ – – ⏑ – – |
children.translated_text: yet that radiance does not shine forth for the worlds ... [text incomplete]

children.text: evaṃ svārthapraṇayamalinajñānaleśāśayānām
children.translated_text: thus for those whose disposition contains merely a trace of knowledge, soiled by attachment to self-interest,

children.text: arthāvāptir vinayanakṛśā nāsti sātulyarūpā || GoṚp_92 ||
children.translated_text: the attainment of their goals, meager through lack of discipline, has no corresponding form. || GoṚp 92 ||

children.text: ājñāṃ śirobhir atha te pratigṛhya tasya mānābhimānamṛdubhir munisattamasya |
children.translated_text: Then, receiving upon their heads the command of that best of sages, with minds humbled by modesty and self-respect, soft with reverence,

children.text: dharmaikatānamanasaḥ prathayāṃ babhūvuḥ kīrtiṃ śaratkumudinīdhavalāṃ samantāt || GoṚp_93 ||
children.translated_text: with minds single-pointedly devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, they spread his fame, white as the autumn <s>kumuda</s>-lily field, in all directions. || GoṚp 93 ||

children.text: iti ṛṣipañcakajātakam ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Ṛṣipañcaka Jātaka</s>. ||

children.text: 12. Saptakumārikā
children.translated_text: 12. <s>Saptakumārikā</s> (The Seven Princesses)

children.text: oṃ namo ratnatrayāya ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels!

children.text: vairāgyayuktaṃ ca subhāṣitaṃ ca dharmārthakāmapratibodhanaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: A well-spoken [narrative] imbued with dispassion, awakening to <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>,

children.text: ekāntaramyaṃ bahusajjanānāṃ vakṣyāmi kiṃ cic chṛṇutāvadānam || GoSk_1 ||
children.translated_text: exceedingly delightful for many good people — I shall speak a portion; listen to this <s>avadāna</s>. || GoSk 1 ||

children.text: evam idaṃ bhrājet paripakvakuśalamūlānāṃ mahānto 'pi bhogā yauvanaṃ vā nālam antarāyāyeti |
children.translated_text: Thus it shines: for those whose wholesome roots have fully ripened, neither great luxuries nor youth are an obstacle.

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate |
children.translated_text: This is what is heard in tradition:

children.text: nayavinayādiguṇaśrīsamṛddho rājābhūt kṛkī nāma | sa ca bhagavati kāśyape samyaksaṃbuddhe samupajātaprasādaḥ | tasya rājñaḥ sapta kumāryaḥ pūrvabuddhotpādasaṃniropitābhivṛddhakuśalamūlabalādhānāḥ samupajātasaṃsāravāsanirvedās tāḥ savinayopacāraṃ madhureṇa vacasā praṇipatya pitaram abruvan |
children.translated_text: There was a king named <s>Kṛkī</s>, rich in the splendor of virtues such as statecraft and discipline. He had developed faith in the Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. That king had seven princesses who, through the power of wholesome roots abundantly cultivated in the presence of former Buddhas, had developed weariness with dwelling in <s>saṃsāra</s>. With respectful conduct and in sweet words, bowing, they said to their father:

children.text: toyāntargatacandrabimbataralām ālokya lokasthitiṃ
children.translated_text: Beholding the condition of the world, as unsteady as the reflection of the moon in water,

children.text: kāmān kruddhabhujaṅgabhogapaṭalacchāyopamān vīkṣya ca |
children.translated_text: and seeing that desires are like the coils of an enraged serpent's body,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā duḥkhahutāśanair jagad idaṃ kṛtsnaṃ ca saṃdīpitaṃ
children.translated_text: and having seen this entire world set ablaze by the fires of suffering,

children.text: naiṣkramyābhiratāśayāḥ khalu vayaṃ yāmaḥ śmaśānaṃ nṛpa || GoSk_2 ||
children.translated_text: we, whose hearts are inclined toward renunciation, wish to go to the charnel ground, O king! || GoSk 2 ||

children.text: rājovāca ||
children.translated_text: The king said:

children.text: bālāḥ sukhocitā yūyam akṛtārthamanorathāḥ |
children.translated_text: You are young, accustomed to comfort, with unfulfilled desires;

children.text: kathaṃ śaknomy ahaṃ vaktum āśrayadhvaṃ tapovanam || GoSk_3 ||
children.translated_text: how can I say: 'take refuge in the ascetic grove'? || GoSk 3 ||

children.text: kanyakā ūcuḥ |
children.translated_text: The princesses said:

children.text: jānīmahe kṣitipate bhavato jane 'pi snehārdrapeśalarasābhiniveṣṭitāni |
children.translated_text: We know, O lord of the earth, that even toward your people your [feelings] are immersed in the tender sap of affection and love;

children.text: asmāsu kiṃ punar akāraṇavatsalasya svāṅke vivṛddhim anaghāṃ samupāgatāsu || GoSk_4 ||
children.translated_text: how much more so toward us, objects of causeless tenderness, who have grown up blameless in your own lap? || GoSk 4 ||

children.text: yuṣmadvidhair api sahābhimukho viyogo yenaiva no nṛpa niratyayaśuddhabhāvaiḥ |
children.translated_text: The very [separation] by which separation even from those like you is inevitable — O king, we of pure and imperishable nature —

children.text: tenaiva śāntipadam āptum iyaṃ manīṣā mā bhūt punaḥ punar ayaṃ vyasanopatāpaḥ || GoSk_5 ||
children.translated_text: by that very means is this resolve to attain the state of peace; let there not be this burning of calamity again and again! || GoSk 5 ||

children.text: atha sa rājā snehavaśād vitānībhūtahṛdayo niścalābhitāmranayanayugalaḥ punaḥ punas tāḥ kanyakāḥ samabhivīkṣyovāca ||
children.translated_text: Then that king, his heart canopied by affection, his pair of eyes unmoving and deeply reddened, gazing again and again at those princesses, said:

children.text: āstīrṇakomalavicitrakuthodareṣu svairaṃ vihṛtya bhavaneṣu kathaṃ bhavatyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having sported freely in palaces with floors of soft and variegated carpets, how could you ladies

children.text: sprakṣyanti durjanamanoviṣamāṃ śmaśānabhūmiṃ sitāsthiśakalaprakarottarīyām || GoSk_6 ||
children.translated_text: touch the charnel-ground, harsh to wicked minds, with an upper garment of fragments of white bones? || GoSk 6 ||

children.text: snehonmukhaṃ pitaram ekapade kathaṃ vā śokāśrudurdinamukhīṃ jananīṃ ca hitvā |
children.translated_text: Leaving behind your father, his face turned lovingly toward you, and your mother, her face clouded with tears of grief —

children.text: amlānasauhṛdanirantaramānasāṃś ca tyaktvā kathaṃ nu suhṛdas tapase ramadhvam || GoSk_7 ||
children.translated_text: and leaving friends whose minds are ceaselessly devoted with unfading affection — how could you delight in austerity? || GoSk 7 ||

children.text: atha tāḥ kanyakā niratiśayadhairyāvaṣṭambhagalbhaṃ pitaram ūcuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then those princesses, bold with the support of supreme fortitude, said to their father:

children.text: mātā pitā suhṛd iti vyavahāramātram etat punarbhavanipātavighātabhājām |
children.translated_text: Mother, father, friend — this is merely conventional usage for those who suffer the devastation of repeated rebirth;

children.text: bhūtārthadarśanaparokṣamalīmasānāṃ loko vṛthā narapate parikhedam eti || GoSk_8 ||
children.translated_text: the world, whose vision of true reality is obscured by impurity, endures futile weariness, O lord of men! || GoSk 8 ||

children.text: kenāpy anartharucinā kapaṭaṃ prayuktam etat suhṛtsvajanabandhumayaṃ vicitram |
children.translated_text: This wonderful [web] consisting of friends, kinfolk, and relations has been contrived as deception by some [force] delighting in misfortune;

children.text: kasyātra kaḥ katham iha svajano jano vā svapnendrajālasadṛśaḥ khalu jīvalokaḥ || GoSk_9 ||
children.translated_text: who here is whose kinsman, and how? Indeed the world of the living resembles a dream or a magic illusion. || GoSk 9 ||

children.text: sālokaṃ bhuvanatrayaṃ narapate saddharmavāgaṃśubhir
children.translated_text: As long as the three worlds with their inhabitants [are illuminated] by the rays of the speech of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: yāvad buddhadivākarasya vilasatkīrtiprabhāmālinaḥ |
children.translated_text: of the <s>Buddha</s>-sun whose resplendent fame-garlands shine forth —

children.text: niryātuṃ vyasanāndhakārapaṭalacchannāntarālād bhavāt
children.translated_text: so long is it proper to emerge from existence, whose interior is concealed by the veil of the darkness of calamity;

children.text: tāvan nyāyyam ataḥ purā hy atimahat paryeti ghoraṃ tamaḥ || GoSk_10 ||
children.translated_text: for before [this opportunity passes], a terrible darkness, exceedingly great, returns. || GoSk 10 ||

children.text: vātāsphālanacañcalānalaśikhājvālāvalīḍhād gṛhān
children.translated_text: Just as those who wish for its cessation do not restrain a person exiting from a house

children.text: niryāntaṃ na nivārayanti puruṣaṃ tacchāntikāmā yathā |
children.translated_text: licked by the rows of flames of fire, their tips dancing in the blowing wind —

children.text: evaṃ duḥkhamahāhutāśanaśikhāgrastāt samastād bhavān
children.translated_text: so the good do not obstruct one emerging from the entirety of existence,

children.text: niṣkrāmantam anarthajālapihitāt santo vivṛṇvanti na || GoSk_11 ||
children.translated_text: seized by the flames of the great fire of suffering, covered by the net of misfortune. || GoSk 11 ||

children.text: atha sa pārthivas tāsāṃ tena suhṛtsvajanabandhunirapekṣarūkṣākṣareṇa svakāyajīvitāśāvidhureṇa vacasā sutarāṃ samupajātaśokadainyamānasaḥ punar vyāha ||
children.translated_text: Then that king, his mind increasingly overcome by grief and humility from their words — harsh in their indifference to friends, kinfolk, and relations, devoid of any hope for their own bodies and lives — spoke again:

children.text: tapāṃsy akāleṣv abhivāñchitāni puṣṇanti nārthān manaso 'nukūlān
akālagarbhā iva kanyakānām ajātasārāvayavāṅgaśobhāḥ || GoSk_12 ||
children.translated_text: like untimely pregnancies of maidens, with immature limbs and bodily beauty. || GoSk 12 ||
Austerities desired at the wrong time do not nourish beneficial results pleasing to the mind —

children.text: bhavanty akāle tapasaḥ prayogāś candroparāgā iva sopasargāḥ |
children.translated_text: The practice of austerity at the wrong time is attended by afflictions, like an eclipse of the moon;

children.text: tasmād ito buddhir iyaṃ kumāryo nivartyatām utpathacāriṇīva || GoSk_13 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O princesses, let this resolve be turned back, like one who has strayed from the path. || GoSk 13 ||

children.text: soḍhuṃ na duḥkhāni vapūṃṣi śaktāny adṛṣṭaduḥkhāni sukhocitāni |
children.translated_text: Bodies accustomed to comfort, that have not seen suffering, are not able to endure sufferings —

children.text: dantābhighātā dviradādhipānām abaddhamūlā iva cūtavṛkṣāḥ || GoSk_14 ||
children.translated_text: like mango trees of unestablished roots [when subjected to] the blows of the tusks of the lord of elephants. || GoSk 14 ||

children.text: savahnigarbhair aśivaiḥ śivārutair vināditaṃ bhīṣaṇarāvagahvaram |
children.translated_text: The charnel ground, resounding with inauspicious howls pregnant with fire, a cavern of terrifying cries,

children.text: bhayaṃ bhayasyāpy upasaṃhared bhṛśaṃ śmaśānam ākrandavirāvadāruṇam || GoSk_15 ||
children.translated_text: terrible with wailing and screaming — it would intensely provoke fear even in fear itself! || GoSk 15 ||

children.text: kva vo vapur bālamṛṇālakomalaṃ matiḥ kva ceyaṃ karapattraniṣṭhurā |
children.translated_text: Where is your body, tender as a young lotus-stalk, and where is this resolve, harsh as a saw-blade?

children.text: paropakāravyatiṣaktacetaso vidher aho mayy anapekṣarūkṣatā || GoSk_16 ||
children.translated_text: Alas, the harshness of fate's indifference toward me, whose mind is devoted to the welfare of others! || GoSk 16 ||

children.text: vaiḍūryanīlamṛduśādvalakañcukāni nānāprakārakusumaprakarotkarāṇi |
children.translated_text: These pleasure-gardens of yours — carpeted with soft, green turf blue as <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli),

children.text: etāni vo madakalālikulākulāni krīḍāvanāny abhimatāni bhavantu kanyāḥ || GoSk_17 ||
children.translated_text: abundant with heaps of blossoms of many kinds, abuzz with swarms of intoxicated bees —

children.text: gṛhopavanadīrghikās taṭavilambipuṣpadrumāḥ
children.translated_text: O princesses, let these be your delight! || GoSk 17 ||

children.text: samīraṇacalattaraṅgarucakāvalīmekhalāḥ |
children.translated_text: The garden-pools of the mansion, with flowering trees hanging over their banks,

children.text: vibuddhakamalotpalākaranilīnahaṃsasvanā
children.translated_text: with garlands and girdles of sparkling wave-ripples stirred by the breeze,

children.text: rater upanibandhanaṃ maghavato 'py alaṃ kanyakāḥ || GoSk_18 ||
children.translated_text: with the sounds of geese settled upon opening lotuses and water-lilies —

children.text: upavījitā jalataraṅgalāsakair navamālikākusumagandhagandhibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: they are enough to bind the delight of even <s>Maghavat</s> (<s>Indra</s>), O princesses! || GoSk 18 ||

children.text: pavanair ihaiva gṛhakānane ratiṃ kurutāṅganāḥ parabhṛtopakūjite || GoSk_19 ||
children.translated_text: Fanned by breezes playful with the waves of water, fragrant with the scent of fresh jasmine blossoms,

children.text: ete jālagavākṣapakṣavivaraprodvāntapuṣpāsavā
children.translated_text: take delight right here in the house-garden, with cuckoos cooing, O ladies! || GoSk 19 ||

children.text: nānāmodavidigdhavāsavikasanniḥśvāsavātā iva |
children.translated_text: These palaces, whose latticed windows exhale the nectar of flowers,

children.text: prāsādā valabhīviṭaṅkavalayaprasvasthasuptāṇḍajā
children.translated_text: like breaths of wind infused with various perfumes from unfolding garments,

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ rataye bhavantu vanitāḥ saṃgītatūryasvanāḥ || GoSk_20 ||
children.translated_text: with birds sleeping peacefully on the terrace-ledge brackets —

children.text: atha tāḥ kumāryas tat pitur vacanam amṛṣyamāṇāḥ punar vyāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: O women, let them be for your delight, [along] with the sounds of music and instruments! || GoSk 20 ||

children.text: na hi tat sukham asti kiṃ cid anyan naralokādhipate divi kṣitau vā |
children.translated_text: Then those princesses, unable to bear their father's words, spoke again:

children.text: śataśaś ca sahasradhā ca bhuktaṃ na yad asmābhir anarthapaṇḍitābhiḥ || GoSk_21 ||
children.translated_text: There is no happiness whatsoever, O lord of the world of men, in heaven or on earth,

children.text: viṣayair na hi tṛptir indriyāṇāṃ viṣayābhyāsaviśeṣaghasmarāṇām |
children.translated_text: that has not been enjoyed by us hundreds and thousands of times — we who are scholars of misfortune! || GoSk 21 ||

children.text: bhavatīti vicintya buddhimantaḥ prayatante bhavabandhanakṣayāya || GoSk_22 ||
children.translated_text: For the sense-faculties, voracious through habitual indulgence in sense-objects, are never satisfied by sense-objects;

children.text: capalāny anavasthitasvabhāvāny aniloddhūtataraṅgabhaṅgurāṇi |
children.translated_text: understanding this, the wise strive for the destruction of the bonds of existence. || GoSk 22 ||

children.text: vinivṛttapunarbhavābhilāṣā vijayante yatayaḥ ṣaḍindriyāṇi || GoSk_23 ||
children.translated_text: The six sense-faculties — fickle, unstable by nature, fragile as waves raised by the wind —

children.text: bhavacārakasūkarās tu bālāś chalitāś cittakaler viceṣṭitena |
children.translated_text: the ascetics whose desire for rebirth has ceased conquer them. || GoSk 23 ||

children.text: prapatanti sukhābhilāṣalubdhā vyasaneṣv eva durantabhairaveṣu || GoSk_24 ||
children.translated_text: But the immature, the hogs roaming in existence, deluded by the play of the trickster mind,

children.text: aham ity upajātavibhrameyaṃ janatā prajvalitāstrayantrakalpān |
children.translated_text: greedy for the desire of happiness, fall into calamities that are interminable and terrifying. || GoSk 24 ||

children.text: viṣayān upasevate hatāśā pariṇāmāyatatīvraduḥkhahetūn || GoSk_25 ||
children.translated_text: This deluded humanity, conceiving 'I,' serves sense-objects — like blazing weapon-machines —

children.text: jagad adhruvam etad asvatantraṃ viṣayāśīviṣapūgasaṃniruddham |
children.translated_text: bereft of hope, though they are the causes of severe suffering prolonged in their consequences. || GoSk 25 ||

children.text: avagamya bhaveṣu ye ramante paśavas te naravigrahopanītāḥ || GoSk_26 ||
children.translated_text: Understanding that this world is impermanent, without self-sovereignty, beset by the mass of venomous serpents of sense-objects —

children.text: camarā iva vṛkṣalagnavālā nidhanaṃ kāpuruṣā vrajanti gehe |
children.translated_text: those who delight in existences are animals delivered into human form. || GoSk 26 ||

children.text: viṣayair uparuddhabuddhimārgā vitathasnehalatānibaddhacittāḥ || GoSk_27 ||
children.translated_text: Like <s>camara</s> deer dying with their tails caught in trees, cowards meet their end in the household,

children.text: ratikāraṇam atra jīvaloke vyasanodbhedanirantarāntarāle |
children.translated_text: their path of wisdom blocked by sense-objects, their minds bound by vines of false affection. || GoSk 27 ||

children.text: vada tāta kim asti yena naḥ syād bhavaneṣv eva ratir bahucchaleṣu || GoSk_28 ||
children.translated_text: Tell us, father, in this world of the living — an interval ceaselessly rent by the eruption of calamity —

children.text: bhavaneṣu narendra bhāgadheyāny upayujyāni bhavāntarārjitāni |
children.translated_text: what cause for delight is there by which we should find pleasure in these houses of many deceptions? || GoSk 28 ||

children.text: muṣitā iva hīnadīnacittā bhavakāntāraparāyaṇā bhavanti || GoSk_29 ||
children.translated_text: In houses, O king, the fortunes accumulated in former existences are consumed;

children.text: puruṣāḥ prasamīkṣya kāriṇo 'pi vyavahāreṣu vicakṣaṇāḥ prakṛtyā |
children.translated_text: [people], as if robbed, become low and wretched in spirit, destined for the wilderness of existence. || GoSk 29 ||

children.text: gṛhacārakam etya yānti nāśaṃ nṛpa mīnāḥ kupinīmukhaṃ yathaiva || GoSk_30 ||
children.translated_text: Even men who are observant, active, and naturally discerning in affairs —

children.text: bahubhir naralokapāla yatnair bhavanāni draviṇāni cārjitāni |
children.translated_text: entering the prison of the household, they perish, O king, just as fish [entering] the mouth of a trap. || GoSk 30 ||

children.text: apahāya naraḥ kṣaṇena yāti svakṛtādeśitamārga eka eva || GoSk_31 ||
children.translated_text: With many efforts, O guardian of the world of men, houses and riches are acquired;

children.text: ata eva jagāda lokanātho nṛpa karmasvakam eva jīvalokam |
children.translated_text: yet a person, abandoning [them] in an instant, goes alone on the path appointed by his own <s>karma</s>. || GoSk 31 ||

children.text: maraṇābhimukhaṃ naraṃ svakarma stanapo vatsa ivānuyāti dhenum || GoSk_32 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the Lord of the World declared, O king, that the world of the living has only its own <s>karma</s>;

children.text: tad alaṃ pariṇāmadāruṇais taiḥ priyabandho priyasaṃgamābhilāṣaiḥ |
children.translated_text: one's own <s>karma</s> follows a person facing death, as a nursing calf follows the cow. || GoSk 32 ||

children.text: dhruvam eva hi viprayogaduḥkhaṃ priyasaṃyogaratāśayā labhante || GoSk_33 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, enough of those desires for union with the beloved, which are terrible in their consequences, O bond of affection;

children.text: api cāpariniṣṭhitasvabhāve priyatā kā naravīra jīvaloke |
children.translated_text: for those whose hearts delight in union with the beloved certainly obtain the suffering of separation. || GoSk 33 ||

children.text: paramārthavicārapelavānāṃ priya ity eva hi vibhramo matīnām || GoSk_34 ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, in the world of the living — of unstable nature — what is there to cherish, O hero among men?

children.text: yadi tu priyatāsti kā cid asmāsv anujānīṣva mahīpate tato 'smān |
children.translated_text: For subtle investigators of ultimate truth, 'beloved' is itself a delusion of the mind. || GoSk 34 ||

children.text: anavadyam ahāryam āryajuṣṭaṃ sukham āsvādayituṃ hi no manīṣā || GoSk_35 ||
children.translated_text: But if there is any affection toward us, then permit us, O lord of the earth;

children.text: atha sa rājā sugataśāsanābhiprasanno dharmāntarāyabhīrur jātasnehākrāntahṛdayaḥ svā duhitṝḥ pūrvajanmānusmaraṇāvagamitaprayojanā jātismarāḥ khalv etā iti parivicintya suciraṃ tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ||
children.translated_text: for our resolve is to taste the happiness that is blameless, irremovable, and cherished by the noble. || GoSk 35 ||

children.text: nirbandham iti vijñāya tāsāṃ sa narapuṅgavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then that king, having faith in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>, fearful of obstructing the <s>Dharma</s>, his heart seized by the arising of affection, reflecting that his daughters — whose purpose was understood through the recollection of former births — were indeed those who remembered their past lives, was silent for a long time.

children.text: gacchatety aparivyaktaṃ kathaṃ cid anujajñivān || GoSk_36 ||
children.translated_text: Understanding their firmness, that bull among men somehow vaguely permitted them, saying: 'Go.' || GoSk 36 ||

children.text: atha tā dārikā vyapanītasraganulepanābharaṇāḥ vinayanibhṛtavapuṣaḥ sitasūkṣmapralambāmbaradharāḥ pavanabalacalitasalilaphenāvalīmālinya iva saritaḥ sāndracandracandrikāpaṭāvaguṇṭhitā iva śaranniśāḥ svakiraṇajālottarīyā iva saptarṣitārakāḥ krameṇa viracitacitāgnimadhyavinyastasimisimāyamānocchūnaśavāmagandhabībhatsaṃ niśitagṛdhratuṇḍakhaṇḍitaśiroghaṭīvivaravinirgatavigalitamastiṣkarasaviliptavadananarakaraṅkākrāntaparyantabhīṣaṇaṃ jīrṇaśīrṇavivarṇāsthikaṅkālaśakalanikarakharabhūmibhāgaduḥsaṃcaraṃ mūrtimantam iva nirvedakarmāntam ivāntakasyāratiśokadainyopāyāsāspadabhūtaṃ śmaśānam anuprāptāḥ || bhavati cātra ||
children.translated_text: Then those maidens, having removed their garlands, unguents, and ornaments, with bodies composed in modesty, wearing white, fine, flowing garments — like rivers garlanded with rows of foam-waves blown by the force of the wind, like autumn nights veiled in the curtain of dense, white moonlight, like the stars of the Seven Sages (the Great Bear) draped in garments of their own rays — gradually arrived at the cremation ground, which had a fire kindled amidst the arranged pyre, with a bloated, swollen corpse hissing hideously with putrid stench, with a horrifying periphery strewn with human skeletons whose skulls had their cranial cavities opened by the tips of sharp vulture beaks with brain-matter flowing and smearing the faces, with ground difficult to traverse due to heaps of old, crumbling, discolored bone-fragments — like disgust embodied, like the workshop of Death, a site of displeasure, grief, wretchedness, and distress. And here [it is said]:

children.text: saṃprāptās tāḥ śmaśānaṃ nararudhiravasāvisragandhāndhagṛdhraṃ
children.translated_text: Those women arrived at the cremation ground, where vultures blinded by the putrid smell of human blood and fat [circled],

children.text: vyāluptāntrodarārdrair aratibhayakaraiḥ saṃniruddhaṃ śavāṅgaiḥ |
children.translated_text: blocked by corpse-limbs — moist with torn-out entrails and viscera — causing revulsion and fear,

children.text: kundāpītāvadātair hasad iva satataṃ jarjarāṅgaiḥ kapālair
children.translated_text: as if laughing with pale, crumbling skulls — yellowish-white like <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers,

children.text: jīrṇanyagrodharandhravyavahitavividholūkahūṅkārabhīmam || GoSk_37 ||
children.translated_text: terrifying with the varied hooting of owls concealed in the hollows of old banyan trees. // GoSk 37 //

children.text: savahnikavaloddhatasphuṭaśivārutābhīṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Terrifying with the shrieking of jackals flushed out by the blazing fire,

children.text: kva cit sitakaraṅkajālapariṇaddhaduḥsaṃcaram |
children.translated_text: in places difficult to traverse due to the lattice of white bones,

children.text: sphuratkṛmikulākulapracalanīlanāsādarī-
children.translated_text: with corpse-slopes teeming with hundreds of flies concealed in the dark cavities of noses

children.text: nilīnabahumakṣikāśataśavākulopatyakam || GoSk_38 ||
children.translated_text: where clusters of quivering worms swarmed. // GoSk 38 //

children.text: sitāsthiśakalāruṇaprabalamārutābhyāhata-
children.translated_text: With serpents hiding in the dried tree-roots where pyre-fires sputtered,

children.text: sphuratsphuṭacitāgniśuṣkatarumūlalīnoragam |
children.translated_text: struck by powerful winds amid white bone-fragments and reddish [embers],

children.text: kva cin niśitaśūlabhinnanaravigrahogrāśrayaṃ
children.translated_text: in places with terrible shelters of human bodies pierced by sharp stakes —

children.text: mahānasam ivāntakasya satatapravṛttotsavam || GoSk_39 ||
children.translated_text: like the kitchen of Death with its perpetually ongoing feast. // GoSk 39 //

children.text: kva cin naraśiroghaṭīvivaranirgatāsṛgdharā-
children.translated_text: In places teeming with crowds of ghoulish <s>piśācīs</s>, excited by the putrid transformation of streams of blood and fat

children.text: vasāsavavikāraghasmarapiśācipūgākulam |
children.translated_text: flowing from the cavities of human skulls,

children.text: kva cit simisimāyamānacitikānalāliṅgita-
children.translated_text: in places with intestine-serpents emerging from the bellies of human corpses

children.text: sphurannarakalevarodaravinirgatāntroragam || GoSk_40 ||
children.translated_text: embraced by the sizzling cremation fire. // GoSk 40 //

children.text: saṃvegānaddhahṛdayā vicerus tatra tāḥ striyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Their hearts bound with religious dread (<s>saṃvega</s>), those women wandered there,

children.text: svabhāvaṃ jīvalokasya cintayantyaś calācalam || GoSk_41 ||
children.translated_text: contemplating the fickle, unstable nature of the world of the living. // GoSk 41 //

children.text: vivṛtavikṛtapūtiguhyadeśaṃ dharaṇirajo'ruṇarūkṣakeśapāśam |
children.translated_text: With private parts exposed, disfigured, and putrid, with matted hair reddened and roughened by the dust of the earth,

children.text: khaganakhamukhakhaṇḍitākṣikośaṃ dadṛśur athojjhitam aṅganāyāḥ || GoSk_42 ||
children.translated_text: with eye-sockets torn by the beaks and claws of birds — they then beheld the abandoned [body] of a woman. // GoSk 42 //

children.text: muhur upāgatasādhvasacañcalaiḥ kuvalayāvayavair iva locanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With eyes trembling with intermittent alarm, like pieces of blue lotus,

children.text: tam abhivīkṣya kalevarapañjaraṃ bahuvidhāni vacāṃsi babhāṣire || GoSk_43 ||
children.translated_text: gazing upon that cage of a corpse, they spoke words of many kinds: // GoSk 43 //

children.text: iyam asau sphuṭacandrakarāṅkuracchuritasaudhavimānanivāsinī |
children.translated_text: 'This is she who dwelt in mansions and palaces sparkling with sprouts of bright moonbeams,

children.text: priyatamāṅkapariṣvajanocitā svapiti yā vasudhātalamaṇḍale || GoSk_44 ||
children.translated_text: accustomed to the embrace of her beloved's lap — she now sleeps on the surface of the earth.' // GoSk 44 //

children.text: priyabhujāntarapañjaraśāyikā jaladharastaniteṣv api kātarā |
children.translated_text: 'She who lay in the cage of her beloved's arms, frightened even by the thunder of clouds —

children.text: sadahanād aśivāc ca śivārutāt katham iyaṃ na bibheti tapasvinī || GoSk_45 ||
children.translated_text: how does this wretched one not fear the fire, the inauspicious [jackals], and the jackal's howl?' // GoSk 45 //

children.text: gurunitambabharālasagāminī lalitahāsavilāsavilokinī |
children.translated_text: 'She of slow gait weighed down by the burden of her heavy hips, of playful laughter and graceful glances —

children.text: iyam asau svagṛhāṅganacandrikā gataghṛṇair vihagair avalupyate || GoSk_46 ||
children.translated_text: this moonlight of her own household courtyard is now torn apart by pitiless birds.' // GoSk 46 //

children.text: narakaraṅkaśatākulacatvare pitṛvane bhagini tvam ihojjhitā |
children.translated_text: 'O sister, you have been abandoned here in the ancestral grove, a square crowded with hundreds of human skeletons;

children.text: akaruṇena kathaṃ dayitena he dhig anavasthitahārdam idaṃ jagat || GoSk_47 ||
children.translated_text: how [could you be abandoned] by a merciless beloved? — Fie upon this world of unreliable affections!' // GoSk 47 //

children.text: svajanabandhusuhṛtkamalākarabhramarikā dayitāṅkavivartinī |
children.translated_text: 'She who was a bee [buzzing] in the lotus-pond of kinsmen, relatives, and friends, revolving in her beloved's lap —

children.text: katham iyaṃ kṣaṇadācarabhairave pitṛvane ramate 'dya varākikā || GoSk_48 ||
children.translated_text: how does this wretched one today delight in the ancestral grove, terrifying with its nocturnal activities?' // GoSk 48 //

children.text: saṃrāgāruṇatārakāntamukulakṣībeṇa yā cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: 'She who formerly, with eyes whose inner buds had reddish, passion-tinted pupils,

children.text: kāntaṃ snigdhavidagdhamugdhamadhureṇodīkṣamāṇā purā |
children.translated_text: gazed at her beloved with a look affectionate, clever, innocent, and sweet,

children.text: cakre manmathavāgurāhariṇakaṃ saivādya saṃrāgiṇāṃ
children.translated_text: and made him a deer in the snare of <s>Manmatha</s> (Kāma, the god of love) — that very one today, her eyes carried away by birds,

children.text: saṃtrāsaṃ vihagāpanītanayanā kaṣṭaṃ karoty aṅganā || GoSk_49 ||
children.translated_text: causes terror in the passionate — alas, how cruel is woman['s fate]!' // GoSk 49 //

children.text: antarnigūḍhavividhāśucigātrayaṣṭyā rāgāndhabuddhinayanāś chalitā mayeti |
children.translated_text: 'With her body-staff hiding within various impurities, she deceived those whose eyes and intellect were blinded by passion, saying "I am [beautiful]" —

children.text: saṃrāgiṇo 'pahasatīva khagāvaluptadantacchadena vadanena varāṅganeyam || GoSk_50 ||
children.translated_text: this excellent woman seems to mock the passionate with her mouth whose lips have been torn away by birds.' // GoSk 50 //

children.text: vīṇāveṇudhvanikalaravaiḥ kākalīgītakair yā
children.translated_text: 'She who once slept to the melodious sounds of the <s>vīṇā</s> and flute, to the strains of <s>kākalī</s> songs,

children.text: nidrāṃ bheje priyatamapariṣvaṅgaviśrabdhagarbhām |
children.translated_text: a sleep secure in the embrace of her most beloved,

children.text: saivādyeha svapiti vanitā bhūrajorūkṣitāṅgī
children.translated_text: that very woman now sleeps — her limbs roughened by earth-dust —

children.text: gomāyūnāṃ dhvanitamukharārāvaraudre śmaśāne || GoSk_51 ||
children.translated_text: in a cremation ground made terrible and clamorous by the howling of jackals.' // GoSk 51 //

children.text: vālāgramātram api yatra vicāryamāṇe nekṣāmahe śuci nijāśucigarbharandhre |
children.translated_text: 'When examined even to the tip of a hair, we see nothing pure in the cavity of its inherent impurity;

children.text: tasmin ratiṃ katham amī prakhalā labhante kāyādhame nidhanadharmiṇi roganīḍe || GoSk_52 ||
children.translated_text: in this basest of bodies — subject to destruction, a nest of disease — how do these brazen ones find pleasure?' // GoSk 52 //

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ jagad idaṃ sakalaṃ bhaginyaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Such is this entire world, O sisters —

children.text: svapnendrajālajalacandracalasvabhāvam |
children.translated_text: of the nature of dream, magic, water-moon, and fickleness;

children.text: matvā virāgam upagacchata yāvad etat
children.translated_text: understanding this, attain dispassion while this

children.text: prāṇāvaśeṣam upayāti na vo vināśam || GoSk_53 ||
children.translated_text: remaining life-breath has not reached your destruction.' // GoSk 53 //

children.text: prāṇāntikavyasanakaṇṭakabhinnamarmā kurvīta kiṃ nu kuśalaṃ jalaviplutākṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'With vital points pierced by the thorn of mortal calamity, what good can one do, eyes flooded with tears,

children.text: daṣṭaḥ kṛtāntamakareṇa jarāmukhena mūrdhnā ca śuklapalitotkaradantureṇa || GoSk_54 ||
children.translated_text: when bitten by the crocodile of death with the mouth of old age, with head bristling with prominent white hairs?' // GoSk 54 //

children.text: ghorāndhakāraparalokamahāprapātasaṃpātacūrṇitatanoḥ kuśalābhilāṣam |
children.translated_text: 'The desire for merit of one whose body is pulverized by the fall into the great precipice of the other world — shrouded in terrible darkness —

children.text: āśīviṣāsyapuṭasaṃkaṭasaṃniruddhamaṇḍūkavāsitasamaṃ pravadanti santaḥ || GoSk_55 ||
children.translated_text: the sages declare to be like a frog's dwelling in the narrow cavity of a venomous serpent's mouth.' // GoSk 55 //

children.text: lokaṃ vākyaiḥ kṛtakamadhurair vañcayitvādya maunaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Having deceived the world with artificially sweet words, why do you now maintain silence',

children.text: dhatse kasmāt paruṣapiśunābaddhavādapragalbhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'O you who were bold with harsh, slanderous, and libelous speech?'

children.text: ity ākrośann iva sarabhasaṃ rājadantāgradaṣṭāṃ
children.translated_text: — as if rebuking thus, a bird forcefully carries away

children.text: jihvāpeśīṃ harati vihagas tuṇḍasaṃdaṃśakena || GoSk_56 ||
children.translated_text: the piece of tongue, bitten by its front teeth, with its beak-pincers. // GoSk 56 //

children.text: rāgāndhānāṃ vitathaviṣayābhyāsajihmāśayānāṃ
children.translated_text: 'In that which, when it came within the sight of young men blinded by passion,

children.text: yad bālānāṃ nayanaviṣayaṃ prāpya dhairyaṃ bibheda |
children.translated_text: with crooked intentions from the habit of false sense-objects, shattered their composure —

children.text: tasminn adya vyapagatabhayāś cārubimbe nitambe
children.translated_text: in that very beautiful orb of the buttock, today, vultures, fearless,

children.text: nāryā gṛdhrā nakhamukhapadanyāsapaṅktiṃ likhanti || GoSk_57 ||
children.translated_text: inscribe rows of claw-and-beak marks upon the woman's [body].' // GoSk 57 //

children.text: yābhyāṃ yātā priyakaratalanyastahastāravindā
children.translated_text: 'With those [feet] by which she used to walk, her lotus-hands placed on her beloved's palms,

children.text: bhittau sācīpariṇatamukhī citram udvīkṣamāṇā |
children.translated_text: her face turned sideways, looking curiously at a painting on a wall,

children.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ svabhavanatale muktapuṣpottarīye
children.translated_text: slowly, slowly, on the floor of her own palace, strewn with flower-offerings —

children.text: tāv evādya grasati caraṇau jambuko 'yaṃ yuvatyāḥ || GoSk_58 ||
children.translated_text: those very two feet of the young woman are now being gnawed by this jackal.' // GoSk 58 //

children.text: itthaṃbhūte sahajavividhāmedhyajambālapaṅke
children.translated_text: 'In such a mire of innate, manifold, impure filth —

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭaṃ madanamadirāḥ kṣībacittāḥ patanti |
children.translated_text: alas, alas! — those intoxicated by the wine of <s>Madana</s> (love), with minds inebriated, fall!

children.text: kāyasyemāṃ prakṛtim aśivāṃ vīkṣamāṇās tu yūyaṃ
children.translated_text: But you, beholding this inauspicious nature of the body,

children.text: nirvidyadhvaṃ pracalitataḍidbhaṅgurāj jīvalokāt || GoSk_59 ||
children.translated_text: be disenchanted with this world of the living — as fleeting as a flash of lightning!' // GoSk 59 //

children.text: yaḥ sattvānām aviratarasakleśanāḍīvraṇāntaḥ-
children.translated_text: 'He who, for beings burning within the wound-veins of ceaseless passion and affliction,

children.text: saṃtaptānām adhigatayathābhūtadharmādhirājaḥ |
children.translated_text: the supreme sovereign who has realized the truth of reality (<s>yathābhūtadharma</s>),

children.text: hlādaṃ cakre prakṛtiśiśirair dharmavāgambukumbhaiḥ
children.translated_text: brought refreshment with water-pots of <s>dharma</s>-speech, cool by nature —

children.text: śāstre tasmai paramabhiṣaje sarvakāle namo 'stu || GoSk_60 ||
children.translated_text: to that Teacher, the supreme physician, homage be at all times!' // GoSk 60 //

children.text: durvijñeyaṃ kapaṭam aśivaṃ kleśakarmaprayuktaṃ
children.translated_text: 'That which is called birth — hard to understand, deceptive, inauspicious, driven by defilement and <s>karma</s>,

children.text: sarvākāraṃ vivṛtam akhilaṃ yena janmābhidhānam |
children.translated_text: in all its aspects revealed and laid bare —

children.text: yasmin mūḍho rathacaraṇavad bambhramīty asvatantro
children.translated_text: in which the deluded [being], without autonomy, whirls like a wheel of a chariot,

children.text: lokas tīvravyasanakuliśāghātaniṣpiṣṭamūrtiḥ || GoSk_61 ||
children.translated_text: his body crushed by the thunderbolt-blows of terrible calamity —' // GoSk 61 //

children.text: mātā bālye pratisaravatīṃ veṇikāṃ yatra cakre
children.translated_text: '[That head] on which a mother in childhood made a braided protective thread (<s>pratisara</s>),

children.text: yasmin kānto maṇimakarikāṃ yauvanāgre babandha |
children.translated_text: on which a beloved at the onset of youth tied a jeweled crocodile-ornament,

children.text: vipraiḥ siktaṃ sukusumalavair yac ca śāntyambuleśaiḥ
children.translated_text: which was sprinkled by <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with drops of consecrated water fragrant with fine flowers —

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ dhṛṣṭaḥ spṛśati balibhuk tac chiro 'dyāṅganāyāḥ || GoSk_62 ||
children.translated_text: alas, that very head of the woman today the bold crow (<s>balibhuj</s>) touches!' // GoSk 62 //

children.text: ye vāsitāḥ sukusumena vivāhakāle mātuḥ kareṇa kṛtakautukamaṅgalena |
children.translated_text: 'Those [tresses] which were perfumed with flowers at the time of marriage,

children.text: te 'dya pracaṇḍapavanair avadhūyamānāḥ keśāḥ śmaśānatarucāmaratāṃ prayātāḥ || GoSk_63 ||
children.translated_text: by the mother's hand that performed the auspicious wedding rites —

children.text: prakṛticaturā dṛṣṭiḥ kvāsāv apāṅgavilokinī
children.translated_text: those very hairs today, shaken by fierce winds, have attained the status of fly-whisks for the cremation-ground trees.' // GoSk 63 //

children.text: salalitapadanyāsā kvāsau gatir madavihvalā |
children.translated_text: 'Where is that naturally artful glance, with its sidelong look?

children.text: kva nu khalu gatā hāsās te 'syā radacchadalāsakāḥ
children.translated_text: Where is that gait, with its graceful steps, swaying with intoxication?

children.text: suracitam aho citraṃ māyārahasyam idaṃ kaleḥ || GoSk_64 ||
children.translated_text: Where indeed have gone those smiles of hers, playful on the petals of her teeth?

children.text: hāsāyāsavilolakuṇḍalamaṇicchāyoparāgāruṇe
children.translated_text: Ah, how skillfully composed is this marvelous secret-play of Time!' // GoSk 64 //

children.text: yasmin prāṇasamaś cakāra muditaḥ pattrāṅkuraṃ yatnataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'On that very cheek, reddened by the shadow-play of swaying earring-gems

children.text: bālāmbhoruhapattrakomaladale tatraiva gaṇḍasthale
children.translated_text: glinting with laughter and emotion, where her dearest once carefully painted a leaf-ornament,

children.text: vaktraṃ raktakalaṅkitaṃ nikaṣati sthitvā lalāṭe 'ṇḍajaḥ || GoSk_65 ||
children.translated_text: tender as a young lotus petal —

children.text: muktāhāramarīciphenasalile romāvalīśaivale
children.translated_text: on that very cheek-surface, a bird, perched on the forehead, now rubs its blood-stained beak.' // GoSk 65 //

children.text: vistīrṇastanacakravākayugale vakṣastaḍāgodare |
children.translated_text: 'In the lake-belly of the chest, with its pearl-necklace-ray foam-waters,

children.text: savyājaskhalitāṃśuke vyasanināṃ yatraiva netrālayaḥ
children.translated_text: its body-hair algae, its pair of broad-breast <s>cakravāka</s> birds,

children.text: petus tatra vipūyake 'dya nipatanty āśātikā makṣikāḥ || GoSk_66 ||
children.translated_text: where once the eyes of the passionate found their resting-place when the garment artfully slipped —

children.text: pūrvaṃ candanavāriśīkaramucair yā tālavṛntānilaiḥ
children.translated_text: there today, in that festering [wound], greedy flies of desire swarm.' // GoSk 66 //

children.text: preṣyābhir valayadhvanivyatikaraiḥ saṃvījitā sundarī |
children.translated_text: 'She, that beautiful one, who was formerly fanned in her palace

children.text: harmye candrakaropahāradhavale bimbopadhānāśritā
children.translated_text: by servants with palm-leaf fans mingled with the tinkling of bracelets,

children.text: tām evādya tu vījayanti paruṣaiḥ pakṣānilair vāyasāḥ || GoSk_67 ||
children.translated_text: wafting sandalwood-water spray — reclining on a pillow in a white-moonlit chamber —

children.text: yenāyaṃ kampitaḥ pūrvaṃ śākhāntaravicāriṇā |
children.translated_text: that very one is today fanned by crows with the harsh winds of their wings.' // GoSk 67 //

children.text: kvemaṃ kāyadrumaṃ tyaktvā sa gataś cittamarkaṭaḥ || GoSk_68 ||
children.translated_text: 'That mind-monkey which formerly set this [body] in motion,

children.text: yena niṣkriyam apy etat kriyāvad iva lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: wandering among the branches — where has it gone, abandoning this body-tree?' // GoSk 68 //

children.text: kalevaram anātmīyaṃ kva sa cittavidūṣakaḥ || GoSk_69 ||
children.translated_text: 'That mind-jester which made even this inert [body] appear as if active —

children.text: antarātmānam icchanti yam avidyāndhabuddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: where has it gone, leaving this corpse that is not truly one's own?' // GoSk 69 //

children.text: vijñānadhūrtakaḥ kvāsau gatas tīrthavimohakaḥ || GoSk_70 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which those whose understanding is blinded by ignorance desire as the inner self —

children.text: ciraṃ vyāmohitaṃ yena na tattveṣu pratiṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: where has that consciousness-trickster gone, that deceiver of holy places?' // GoSk 70 //

children.text: jagat kva nu prayāto 'smāc cittacitrendrajālikaḥ || GoSk_71 ||
children.translated_text: 'By which the world was long deluded, not established in the truths —

children.text: na jānanti gatiṃ yasya kapilādyās tapodhanāḥ |
children.translated_text: where has that mind-magician of varied illusions departed from here?' // GoSk 71 //

children.text: cittavidyādharaḥ kvāsau viṣayāmbaragocaraḥ || GoSk_72 ||
children.translated_text: 'Whose course even the <s>Kapila</s>s and other masters of austerity do not know —

children.text: cacāra yo 'sminn aśucau navadvāre calācale |
children.translated_text: where is that consciousness-sorcerer, whose range is the sky of sense-objects?' // GoSk 72 //

children.text: śarīrapañjare so 'dya kva nu cittavihaṅgamaḥ || GoSk_73 ||
children.translated_text: 'That which dwelt in this impure, nine-gated, fickle body-cage —

children.text: yenāviṣṭā bhavajalanidhau kleśasaṃsarpisarpe
children.translated_text: where now is that mind-bird?' // GoSk 73 //

children.text: tīvracchidravyasananivahakṣāravāriprapūrṇe |
children.translated_text: 'Possessed by which, in the ocean of existence — full of the serpent of affliction and passion,

children.text: majjanty ajñā maraṇamakarakṣobhacañcattaraṅge
children.translated_text: filled with salt-waters of multitudes of terrible, piercing calamities —

children.text: yātas tyaktvā kva nu tanum imāṃ cittanaktaṃcaro 'sau || GoSk_74 ||
children.translated_text: the ignorant sink, in waves churned by the crocodile of death;

children.text: adāntatvād yo 'sau kṣipati narake vyārtam avaśam
children.translated_text: where has that mind-night-wanderer gone, abandoning this body?' // GoSk 74 //

children.text: sphuradvahnijvālāvalayakapiladvāravivare |
children.translated_text: 'He who, untamed, casts [the being] helplessly into hell, afflicted,

children.text: yamopāyaṃ yasya vyapagatamado vetti bhagavān
children.translated_text: into the opening of the gate made tawny by the blazing garland of fire's flames;

children.text: kva yāto 'sāv asmāt prakṛticapalaś cittaturagaḥ || GoSk_75 ||
children.translated_text: he whose means of taming the Blessed One alone, free from pride, knows —

children.text: atha kuliśamarīciśyāmapīnaprakoṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: where has that mind-horse gone from here, fickle by nature?' // GoSk 75 //

children.text: savinayam upagamya prītivispanditākṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then [<s>Śakra</s>], with forearms dark and full like lightning-streaks,

children.text: anunayaramaṇīyaṃ sādhu sādhv ity uvāca
children.translated_text: approaching modestly, his eyes trembling with delight,

children.text: prakṛtisubhagavācā vāsavaḥ kanyakās tāḥ || GoSk_76 ||
children.translated_text: spoke — with words naturally pleasant — 'Well done! Well done!'

children.text: navavayasi bhaginyo manmathāvāsabhūte
children.translated_text: to those maidens — [he,] <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>). // GoSk 76 //

children.text: nṛpatikulavibhūtiśrīsukhaṃ paryudasya |
children.translated_text: 'O sisters, in youthful age — which is the abode of <s>Manmatha</s> (love) —

children.text: ṛṣibhir api purāṇair duṣkaraṃ saṃprapannā
children.translated_text: having renounced the happiness, glory, and comfort of royal families,

children.text: vratam idam iti tuṣṭo 'smy adya vaḥ kiṃ vṛṇīdhvam || GoSk_77 ||
children.translated_text: you have undertaken this vow, difficult even for ancient sages to accomplish;

children.text: karatala iva manye kāmadhātvīśvaratvaṃ
children.translated_text: therefore I am pleased today — what boon do you choose?' // GoSk 77 //

children.text: tridaśapatisukhaṃ vā niścayasyāsya vo 'dya |
children.translated_text: 'I consider the sovereignty of the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (realm of desire) to be as if in the palm of the hand,

children.text: laghu vadata bhaginyaḥ kiṃ karomy eṣa vaśyaḥ
children.translated_text: or the happiness of the lord of the thirty [gods] — for this resolve of yours today.',

children.text: sphurati manasi yad vo devarājo 'smi śakraḥ || GoSk_78 ||
children.translated_text: 'Speak quickly, O sisters — what shall I do? I am at your command;

children.text: atha viṣayasukhebhyo niḥspṛhās tāḥ kumāryaḥ
children.translated_text: that which stirs in your minds — I am the king of gods, <s>Śakra</s>.' // GoSk 78 //

children.text: prakṛtirucirabhāvās tiryag ālokya śakram |
children.translated_text: Then those maidens, free from desire for sensory pleasures,

children.text: jagur idam anavadyaṃ suṣṭhu citrārthavācaḥ
children.translated_text: of naturally lovely disposition, glancing sideways at <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: svakuśalaparipākāṅgāradhīrasvabhāvaḥ || GoSk_79 ||
children.translated_text: spoke these faultless [words], of well-composed and wonderful meaning,

children.text:
na vayam amarabandho janmaduḥkhāturatvād
bhavasukhalavalolāt tantusaṃtānaneyāḥ | (?)
vratam idam anubaddhāḥ śokabāṣpāmbuleśaiḥ
kaluṣavadanaśobhān bāndhavān apy apāsya || GoSk_80 ||
children.translated_text: 'We, O kinsman of the immortals, afflicted by the suffering of birth, are not [beings] to be led by the thread of fickleness, eager for the drops of worldly happiness; we have bound ourselves to this vow, casting aside even our kinsmen — though their faces were beautiful with drops of tears of grief —'
with a nature bold as embers from the ripening of their own merits: // GoSk 79 //

children.text: api tu jagad aśeṣaṃ durnayāviddhatīvra-
children.translated_text: 'But rather, the entire world, pierced by the terrible [arrow] of evil conduct —'

children.text: vyasanaśatasahasrāghātanirbhidyamānam |
children.translated_text: shattered by hundreds of thousands of calamities;

children.text: kṛpaṇam abhisamīkṣya kṣīṇadoṣānujātaṃ
children.translated_text: seeing this [world] pitiable, born with diminished faults,

children.text: padam abhayam aśokaṃ prāptum abhyudyatāḥ smaḥ || GoSk_81 ||
children.translated_text: we have resolved to attain the state that is fearless and sorrowless. // GoSk 81 //

children.text: prabhavasi śatamanyo tvaṃ varaṃ saṃpradātuṃ
children.translated_text: If you, O thousand-eyed one, have the power to grant a boon,

children.text: yadi jagadanukampāpeśalādhyāśayatvāt |
children.translated_text: being of a disposition refined by compassion for the world —

children.text: padam ajaram ahāryaṃ brahmaśāntaṃ tadāryaṃ
children.translated_text: then that noble state, ageless, imperishable, of <s>Brahma</s>-peace —

children.text: bhavabhayaparitaptāḥ prāpayāsmān vimokṣam || GoSk_82 ||
