children.translated_text: bring us, who are scorched by the fear of existence, to liberation! // GoSk 82 //

children.text: kāyāvaskaranirjharasrutamalakledopadigdhāśrayo
children.translated_text: Supported by [a body] smeared with the impurities streaming from the waterfall of bodily refuse,

children.text: niryāṇāsthikaṭāhakārpitaśirā mūrcchāturo niṣpatan |
children.translated_text: with a head placed in the skull-like bowl of afterbirth, afflicted by unconsciousness, falling out

children.text: garbhān mātur amedhyapaṅkagahanād yām aprahāyāśnute
children.translated_text: from the mother's womb — from the thicket of impure muck — the suffering one experiences

children.text: duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaparaṃparāṃ ca paratas tāṃ chinddhi jātiṃ hi naḥ || GoSk_83 ||
children.translated_text: and the succession of sufferings beyond that — cut off this birth of ours! // GoSk 83 //

children.text: jagan nirmaryādā daśati śirasi vyāvṛtamukhī
children.translated_text: Old age, the demoness who bites the world without limit, her mouth gaping wide upon the head,

children.text: jarā rakṣoyoṣit palitasitadaṃṣṭrāṅkuravatī |
children.translated_text: with fangs sprouting white as grey hair —

children.text: nṛṇāṃ yāsau vīryasmṛtidhṛtimatiśrīpramathinī
children.translated_text: she who destroys the vigor, memory, steadfastness, intellect, and beauty of men —

children.text: tatas trāyasvāsmān prabhavasi yadi tvaṃ surapate || GoSk_84 ||
children.translated_text: save us from her, if you have the power, O lord of gods! // GoSk 84 //

children.text: śvāsotkṣepacalatkaṭhorajaṭharo vyāpāṇḍurūkṣacchaviḥ
children.translated_text: With a hard belly heaving from the tossing of breath, with skin pallid and rough,

children.text: saṃprāptān api bhoktum apratibalo bhogān vicitrojjvalān |
children.translated_text: unable to enjoy even the brilliant, various pleasures that have arrived —

children.text: yenādaṣṭavapuḥ sureśvara tato rogābhidhānād bhayāt
children.translated_text: from that fear called disease, which bites the body, O lord of gods,

children.text: trātā no bhava mṛtyudūtapuruṣād ditsur varaṃ ced bhavān || GoSk_85 ||
children.translated_text: be our protector from that messenger of death, if you wish to grant a boon! // GoSk 85 //

children.text: pratyāvṛttastimitanayano marmavicchedaduḥkha-
children.translated_text: With gaze turned back and fixed, body shaken by the agitation and pain of the severing of vital points,

children.text: kṣobhāyāsapratihatatanuḥ śītaviṣṭabdhagātraḥ |
children.translated_text: limbs paralyzed by cold,

children.text: paśyan bandhūn nayanasalilasnātagaṇḍādharāntān
children.translated_text: seeing kinsmen with cheeks and lips bathed in tears from their eyes —

children.text: yenāghrāto vrajati vilayaṃ pāhi mṛtyos tato 'smān || GoSk_86 ||
children.translated_text: that by which one is "smelled" [by Death] and goes to dissolution — protect us from death! // GoSk 86 //

children.text: yenāliṅgitamānasaḥ paśur iva vyāpnoti śocyāṃ daśāṃ
children.translated_text: That by which, when it embraces the mind, a person reaches a pitiable state like an animal,

children.text: kāryākāryavibhāgapelavamatir nindāspadaṃ jāyate |
children.translated_text: becomes feeble in discriminating right from wrong, and becomes an object of censure;

children.text: hlādaṃ naiti tamālaśīkaramucāpy āliṅgito vāyunā
children.translated_text: that by which one finds no delight even when embraced by a breeze carrying <s>tamāla</s> pollen —

children.text: tan no rāgahutāśanaṃ varada he nirvāpayāpāyikam || GoSk_87 ||
children.translated_text: that fire of passion (<s>rāga</s>) which leads to ruin — O boon-granter, extinguish it for us! // GoSk 87 //

children.text: yasyāveśāt sphuritanayanā daṣṭadantacchadāntāḥ
children.translated_text: That by whose seizure, with eyes darting, biting their lip-coverings,

children.text: pāpāḥ pāpaṃ narakam aśivaṃ kurvate tatkṣaṇena |
children.translated_text: sinful ones instantly create sinful, inauspicious hell;

children.text: naivotkhāto munibhir api yaḥ śīrṇaparṇāmbubhakṣais
children.translated_text: that which is not uprooted even by sages who eat withered leaves and water —

children.text: tan naḥ śakra vyapanaya manaḥkoṭarāt krodhasarpam || GoSk_88 ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Śakra</s>, remove from the hollow of our minds that serpent of anger! // GoSk 88 //

children.text: yenāvāritalocanaḥ kumatayas tyaktvā śivāṃ vartmanīṃ
children.translated_text: That by which those of impaired vision, abandoning the auspicious path,

children.text: mithyādṛṣṭiviṣopadigdhamanaso mārgāntaraṃ saṃśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: with minds anointed by the poison of wrong views, have resorted to another path;

children.text: hetuṃ yat pravadanti bhinnatimirāḥ sarvāsravotpattaye
children.translated_text: that which those who have dispelled darkness declare to be the cause of the arising of all defilements (<s>āsrava</s>) —

children.text: tan naś chindhi manogṛhāntaracaraṃ mohāndhakāraṃ hare || GoSk_89 ||
children.translated_text: cut off that darkness of delusion (<s>moha</s>) roaming within the house of our minds, O <s>Hari</s>! // GoSk 89 //

children.text: varam evaṃvidhaṃ śakra bhavantaṃ prārthayāmahe |
children.translated_text: Such a boon, O <s>Śakra</s>, we request of you;

children.text: pratijñātārthavidhuraṃ ceṣṭante na hi sādhavaḥ || GoSk_90 ||
children.translated_text: for the virtuous do not act in a manner that violates their pledged purpose. // GoSk 90 //

children.text: atha śakras tena tāsāṃ viṣayaprārthanākārpaṇyānapekṣāsvacchaśobhinā vacasā pravijṛmbhamāṇavismayaḥ prasādasaṃhṛṣitatanūruhaḥ prāha |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, his amazement blossoming at the brilliance of their words — clear, beautiful, and indicating great, profound meaning, heedless of the wretchedness of prayers for worldly objects — his body's hairs standing erect with joy, spoke:

children.text: aśakyam arthaṃ khalu yācyamāno vighātadīnatvam upaiti lokaḥ |
children.translated_text: "When asked for something impossible, the world falls into dejection and distress;

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇīdhvaṃ naradevakanyā yad eva śakyeta mayā pradātum || GoSk_91 ||
children.translated_text: choose a boon, O princesses, that is within my power to grant." // GoSk 91 //

children.text: atha tā dārikās tena tasyāntarnigūḍhaśāṭhyavikalpitena vacasā samupajātasaṃvegāmarṣāḥ śakram ūcuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then those maidens, with indignation and anger newly aroused by his words contrived with inner concealed guile, spoke to the lord of the thirty [gods]:

children.text: upalāpayase kimartham asmān upagamyādya sahasralocanaivam |
children.translated_text: "Why do you flatter us thus, O thousand-eyed one, having approached us now?

children.text: sukhamātrakadurvidagdhabuddhe prakhalās tena vayaṃ na cāpi gamyāḥ || GoSk_92 ||
children.translated_text: You whose mind is [merely] clever about pleasures alone — we are forthright, and not to be so won over! // GoSk 92 //

children.text: vidito bhavato na rājavaṃśaḥ kim asau dikṣu vikīrṇakīrtipuñjaḥ |
children.translated_text: Is the royal lineage not known to you — that one whose heaps of fame are scattered in all directions,

children.text: dhanado 'py ayathārthanāmadheyo dhanasāraṃ samavekṣya yasya nūnam || GoSk_93 ||
children.translated_text: compared to whose essence of wealth even <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>) bears a name not corresponding to reality? // GoSk 93 //

children.text: yam apāsya vayaṃ jarārtimṛtyuvyasanāyāsavighātadainyabhītāḥ |
children.translated_text: That [lineage] which we have renounced — frightened by old age, the pain of death, calamity, exertion, affliction, and wretchedness —

children.text: suranātha daśām imāṃ prapannā na bhayān nāpi ca bālacāpalena || GoSk_94 ||
children.translated_text: we have reached this state, O lord of gods, not out of fear, nor out of childish fickleness. // GoSk 94 //

children.text: kṛtapuṇya viheṭhitābhir arthas tava ko 'smābhir atīva duḥkhitābhiḥ |
children.translated_text: O meritorious one, what business have you with us who have been tormented, who are exceedingly afflicted?

children.text: upajīva sabandhumitrabhṛtyo vibhavan nanda ca śakra dīrgharātram || GoSk_95 ||
children.translated_text: Enjoy your prosperity with your kinsmen, friends, and servants, O <s>Śakra</s>, and be happy for a long time! // GoSk 95 //

children.text: sukṛtojjvalabhāgadheyayogād yadi devādhipatir bhavāṃs tataḥ kim |
children.translated_text: If, through the conjunction of a destiny brilliant with good deeds, you have become the lord of gods — so what?

children.text: na hi saṃpadam āpnuvanti santaḥ paraheṭhākaraṇāya devarāja || GoSk_96 ||
children.translated_text: For the virtuous do not obtain prosperity in order to torment others, O king of gods. // GoSk 96 //"

children.text: atha mahendras tāsāṃ sphuṭavicitramahārthasārasūcakair vacobhir āpyāyitavismayaḥ prasādābhivyajyamānavadanaśobhaḥ punar api bhāvajijñāsur arthāntarātiśayaśuśrūṣayā vācātyuvāca | mā tāvad bhaginyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then great <s>Indra</s>, his amazement nourished by their clear, various words indicating deep meaning, with the beauty of his face expressing serenity, wishing to test their inner disposition further with a desire to hear yet more, spoke: "Do not, O sisters —"

children.text: nāthante darśanasyāpi mama loke tapodhanāḥ |
children.translated_text: "In the world, ascetics rich in austerity do not even desire the sight of me;

children.text: kimartham evaṃ varade mayi yūyaṃ tu niṣṭhurāḥ || GoSk_97 ||
children.translated_text: why then, O boon-granter that I am, are you so harsh toward me?" // GoSk 97 //

children.text: atha tāḥ kumāryaḥ punar abhyadhikatarajanitamanyukopāḥ sāmarṣaṃ rūkṣākṣaraṃ tridaśapatim ūcuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then those maidens, with anger and indignation aroused even more intensely, spoke to the lord of the thirty [gods] with harsh syllables [and] resentment:

children.text: anyathaiva sitāpāṅgamukhasmitavilokitam |
children.translated_text: "The face of <s>Śacī</s> is seen one way, with white-cornered eyes, a smiling glance —

children.text: dṛśyate vadanaṃ śacyā dīyate varam anyathā || GoSk_98 ||
children.translated_text: but the boon is given another way! // GoSk 98 //

children.text: varapradāne yady asti śaktis tava purandara |
children.translated_text: If you have the power to grant a boon, O <s>Purandara</s>,

children.text: jahīhi prakhalāṃ tāvad viṣayāśāpiśācikām || GoSk_99 ||
children.translated_text: then first abandon the bold she-demon of desire for sense-objects! // GoSk 99 //

children.text: athavā dustyajāḥ kāmā mithyāsaṃkalpalolupaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Or rather, pleasures are hard to abandon for those greedy with false fancies;

children.text: ta eva santu te nityāḥ prabhāvo 'sti yadīdṛśaḥ || GoSk_100 ||
children.translated_text: let them be eternally yours, if such is your power! // GoSk 100 //

children.text: adhruveṣu sahasrākṣa kāmeṣv āsaktamānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: O thousand-eyed one, with a mind attached to impermanent pleasures,

children.text: varaṃ vada kathaṃ nāma tvam anyasmai pradāsyasi || GoSk_101 ||
children.translated_text: how can you, pray tell, grant a boon to another? // GoSk 101 //

children.text: uhyamānaḥ kathaṃ nāma saritā bhīmavegayā |
children.translated_text: How can one being swept away by a river of terrible current

children.text: uttārayiṣyasy aparān parikṣāmajaḍāśrayaḥ || GoSk_102 ||
children.translated_text: rescue others — one whose support is emaciated and enfeebled? // GoSk 102 //

children.text: pāṃśukūlāmbaradharā vyapanītaśiroruhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Wearing robes of cast-off rags, with heads shorn of hair,

children.text: araṇyād grāmam eṣyāmaḥ kadā nas tad bhaviṣyati || GoSk_103 ||
children.translated_text: coming from the forest to the village — when will that be for us? // GoSk 103 //

children.text: yugamātravilokinyo mṛtpātravyagrapāṇayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Looking only a yoke's length ahead, with hands busy holding an earthen bowl,

children.text: sāvadhānaṃ kadā bhikṣāṃ cariṣyāmaḥ kulāt kulam || GoSk_104 ||
children.translated_text: when will we go mindfully begging for alms from family to family? // GoSk 104 //

children.text: asaktā lābhasatkārapaṅke saṃkleśasaṃkaṭe |
children.translated_text: Unattached to the mire of gain and honor, that narrow pass of defilement,

children.text: kadā viśodhayiṣyāmo deyadharmānurāgiṇaḥ || GoSk_105 ||
children.translated_text: when will we purify [the world], passionate about the <s>dharma</s> of giving? // GoSk 105 //

children.text: palālapuñjād utthāya nīhāragurucīvarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Rising from a heap of straw, with robes heavy as frost,

children.text: yatheccham annapānārthe yāsyāmo niḥspṛhāḥ kadā || GoSk_106 ||
children.translated_text: when will we go free from craving, at will, for the sake of food and drink? // GoSk 106 //

children.text: taror mūle śukaśyāme mṛduśādvalakañcuke |
children.translated_text: When, sitting at the root of a tree, on soft green grass like a parrot,

children.text: kadā niṣadya prāpsyāmo dṛṣṭadharmasukhotsavam || GoSk_107 ||
children.translated_text: will we attain the festival of happiness of the directly-seen <s>dharma</s>? // GoSk 107 //

children.text: kāyajīvitayos tyaktvā jarattṛṇalaveṣv iva |
children.translated_text: Having abandoned concern for body and life, as for withered blades of grass,

children.text: apekṣāṃ sucirābhyastāḥ kadā lapsyāmahe sukham || GoSk_108 ||
children.translated_text: when, having long practiced, will we obtain happiness? // GoSk 108 //

children.text: kadā sarinnikuñjasthās taraṅgair udayavyayam |
children.translated_text: When, dwelling in a riverside bower, [observing] by the waves the arising and passing away

children.text: ujjhāmo jīvalokasya bhidyamānair muhur muhuḥ || GoSk_109 ||
children.translated_text: of the living world being broken apart, again and again — when will we discern this? // GoSk 109 //

children.text: satkāyadṛṣṭim utpāṭya sarvātmadṛṣṭimātrikām |
children.translated_text: Having uprooted <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (the view of a real self-body), the mother of all self-views,

children.text: niḥspṛhā bhavabhogebhyo bhaviṣyāmaḥ kadā vayam || GoSk_110 ||
children.translated_text: when will we become free from craving for the enjoyments of existence? // GoSk 110 //

children.text: avabhotsyāmahe lokaṃ kadā nu sacarācaram |
children.translated_text: When indeed will we understand this world, both moving and still,

children.text: svapnamāyāmarīcyabhragandharvanagaropamam || GoSk_111 ||
children.translated_text: as comparable to a dream, an illusion, a mirage, a cloud, a city of the <s>gandharvas</s>? // GoSk 111 //

children.text: iti yāsāṃ priyā trātaḥ spṛhā hṛdi vijṛmbhate
vareṇa tāsāṃ ko nv arthaḥ sāmiṣeṇa calena ca || GoSk_112 ||
children.translated_text: what use to them is a boon that is tainted and fleeting?" // GoSk 112 //
Those in whose hearts this dear yearning for a Protector blossoms —

children.text: api ca sureśāna varapradānacittaka |
children.translated_text: Moreover, O lord of gods, you who have a mind set on granting boons —

children.text: mithyāvikalpakṣaṇamātraramyāḥ svabhāvavāmāḥ suranātha kāmāḥ |
children.translated_text: "Pleasures are charming only for the fleeting moment of false fancy, perverse by nature, O lord of gods;

children.text: vivarjitāḥ sadbhir udāracittair mahāprapātā iva sāndhakārāḥ || GoSk_113 ||
children.translated_text: they are abandoned by the virtuous, the noble-minded, like great chasms enveloped in darkness. // GoSk 113 //

children.text: sarvānayopadravahetubhūtāḥ kāmāḥ khalīkārakarā narāṇām |
children.translated_text: Pleasures are the cause of all ruin and calamity, bringing disgrace to men;

children.text: jugupsitāś caiva bhayāvahāś ca purīṣadigdhā iva kṛṣṇasarpāḥ || GoSk_114 ||
children.translated_text: they are loathsome and terrifying, like black serpents smeared with excrement. // GoSk 114 //

children.text: yān sevamānā nidhanaṃ prayātāḥ prayānti yāsyanti ca sattvakāyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Serving which, hosts of beings have perished, are perishing, and will perish —

children.text: tān vadhyaghātapratimān bhajeta ko nāma kāmān aghahetubhūtān || GoSk_115 ||
children.translated_text: who would embrace those pleasures, causes of sin, comparable to the blows of an executioner? // GoSk 115 //

children.text: śakre ca ye pāṃśupiśācake ca surendra tulyaṃ dadhati svabhāvam |
children.translated_text: Those [pleasures] which have the same nature in <s>Śakra</s> and in a lowly dust-demon, O lord of gods,

children.text: asadvikalpapraṇayodbhavatvāt seved dhi kāmān manasāpi kas tān || GoSk_116 ||
children.translated_text: since they arise from the inclination of unreal fancies — who would serve them even in mind? // GoSk 116 //

children.text: vaiḍūryanīlaharitodgataśādvalāni tyaktvā vanāni kusumonmiṣitadrumāṇi |
children.translated_text: Abandoning forests with meadows sprouting green as <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), with trees blossoming with flowers,

children.text: tīkṣṇāṅkuśollikhitajarjarakumbhadeśā bhārān vahanti viṣayaiś chalitā gajendrāḥ || GoSk_117 ||
children.translated_text: great elephants, deceived by sense-objects, carry burdens, their temple-regions scarred by the scratching of sharp goads. // GoSk 117 //

children.text: śūlāntalagnavapuṣaḥ parivījyamānāḥ pakṣānilair nagaravāyasamaṇḍalānām |
children.translated_text: With bodies impaled on stakes, fanned by the wing-winds of the city's birds of prey,

children.text: vyājena mitranayanair abhivīkṣyamāṇā nāśaṃ vrajanti puruṣā viṣayāhidaṣṭāḥ || GoSk_118 ||
children.translated_text: gazed upon by eyes friendly in pretense — people bitten by the serpent of sense-objects go to destruction. // GoSk 118 //

children.text: prajvālya kāmadahanaṃ svayam eva bālā mithyāvikalpapavanaiḥ svamanogṛheṣu |
children.translated_text: The foolish themselves ignite the fire of desire in the houses of their own minds with the winds of false fancies,

children.text: ātmānam eva hi dahanti śaracchatāni saṃgharṣajena dahanena yathaiva vaṃśāḥ || GoSk_119 ||
children.translated_text: and indeed burn only themselves — as bamboos [burn] by fire born of their own friction in hundreds of autumns. // GoSk 119 //

children.text: api ca kuliśapāṇe vaijayante vihṛtya sphuritamaṇimarīciśrīsamunmeṣaramye |
children.translated_text: Moreover, O wielder of the thunderbolt, having sported in <s>Vaijayanta</s> (Indra's palace), delightful with the blooming splendor of flashing jewel-rays,

children.text: jvaladanalakarālāṃ yānti bhūyo 'py avīciṃ yadi viṣayaviṣaktāḥ svasti tasmai sukhāya || GoSk_120 ||
children.translated_text: they again go to <s>Avīci</s> (the deepest hell), terrible with blazing fires — if attached to sense-objects, then farewell to that happiness! // GoSk 120 //

children.text: bhavatu kugatir ante svargavāsasya sā vā
children.translated_text: Let an evil destiny be the end of dwelling in heaven — that too [must come];

children.text: cyavanapatanaduḥkhaklībalolekṣaṇas tu |
children.translated_text: and the one who delights in the world of gods, with eyes made feeble and rolling from the suffering of falling down from death —

children.text: yad anubhavati duḥkhaṃ devalokābhinandī
children.translated_text: the suffering he experiences —

children.text: nanu sukham anubhūtaṃ tena pūrvānubhūtam || GoSk_121 ||
children.translated_text: surely the pleasure previously experienced [was all consumed] by that. // GoSk 121 //

children.text: vikacakanakapadmacchattrasaṃsuptahaṃsyāṃ
children.translated_text: If, having plunged into the celestial lake with jewel-boats, with swans sleeping under canopies of blooming golden lotuses,

children.text: yadi surapuravāpyāṃ ratnanaubhir vigāhya |
children.translated_text: [continued]

children.text: patati punar akāmaḥ karmabhir vaitaraṇyāṃ
children.translated_text: one falls again unwillingly, by force of <s>karma</s>, into the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> (river of hell),

children.text: kvathitanarakaraṅkavyākulāntarjalāyām || GoSk_122 ||
children.translated_text: whose inner waters are turbid with the boiled skeletons of the damned — // GoSk 122 //

children.text: pariṇativirasebhyaḥ svapnamāyopamebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: what yearning, O <s>Śakra</s>, can there be for those heavenly pleasures,

children.text: surabhavanasukhebhyaḥ kā spṛhā śakra tebhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: which are distasteful in their ripening and comparable to dreams and illusions?

children.text: kupitabhujagajihvācañcalaṃ jīvalokaṃ
children.translated_text: Knowing the entire world of the living to be as fickle as the tongue of an enraged serpent,

children.text: sakalam iti viditvā mokṣakāmāḥ sthitāḥ smaḥ || GoSk_123 ||
children.translated_text: we stand resolute, desiring liberation. // GoSk 123 //

children.text: sukham idam iti mithyākalpanāmātram etad
children.translated_text: "This is happiness" — this is merely a false imagination

children.text: bhavagatigahanāntarvartināṃ bāliśānām |
children.translated_text: of the foolish, caught within the thicket of the paths of existence;

children.text: bhavam avitathavādī duḥkham ity āha buddhaḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddha</s>, the speaker of truth, has declared all existence to be suffering,

children.text: sakalam api yato 'smān sarvaduḥkhaprasūtiḥ || GoSk_124 ||
children.translated_text: since it is the source of all suffering. // GoSk 124 //

children.text: prakṛtibahuladuḥkhopaplute jīvaloke
children.translated_text: In this world of the living, naturally overwhelmed by abundant suffering,

children.text: bhavati yad api saukhyaṃ kākatālīyam asmin |
children.translated_text: whatever happiness there is, is accidental (like a crow alighting on a palm tree);

children.text: vrajati tad api nāśaṃ duḥkhajālābhibhūtaṃ
children.translated_text: even that goes to destruction, overwhelmed by a net of suffering,

children.text: salilam iva nadīnāṃ prāpya sāmudram ambhaḥ || GoSk_125 ||
children.translated_text: like the waters of rivers reaching the ocean's water. // GoSk 125 //

children.text: yasmāt strīṇāṃ karakisalayaiḥ padmapattropamānaiḥ
children.translated_text: Because one who is touched by the bud-like fingertips of women — resembling lotus petals,

children.text: kiṃcitsthānaṃ kalitavalayaiś candanāśleṣaśītaiḥ |
children.translated_text: adorned with tinkling bracelets, cool as a sandalwood embrace —

children.text: spṛṣṭaḥ snehaślathamukulitātāmravṛttāṅgulīyair
children.translated_text: with gently half-closed, slightly reddish, rounded-ring fingers, tenderly loosened with affection,

children.text: nidrāṃ prāpya vyajanapavanavyastamālopahāraḥ || GoSk_126 ||
children.translated_text: having obtained sleep, with a fan-breeze offering of <s>tamāla</s> — // GoSk 126 //

children.text:
bhūyaḥ śete klamagurutanur darbhasūcīkarāle
mārge bhasmavyatikarakharair vījyamāno marudbhiḥ |
tasmān matvā kṣaṇasukhalavaṃ cañcalaṃ jīvalokaṃ
tyaktvā kāmān vyasanaphaladān brahmaśāntaṃ bhajeta || GoSk_127 |
children.translated_text: one should abandon pleasures — which bear the fruit of calamity — and embrace the peace of <s>Brahman</s>. // GoSk 127 //

children.text: daśaśatanayano 'tha kanyakānāṃ hṛṣitatanūruhakañcuko vacobhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the thousand-eyed one (<s>Śakra</s>), his body-hairs standing erect as if in an armor of joy at their words,

children.text: vyavasitam abhinandya caiva tāsāṃ tridaśapurābhimukho yayau kṣaṇena || GoSk_128 ||
children.translated_text: applauding the firm resolve of those maidens, departed instantly toward the city of the thirty [gods]. // GoSk 128 //

again lies with body heavy from fatigue, on a path cruel with thorns of <s>darbha</s> grass, fanned by winds harsh with admixtures of ash — therefore, knowing the world of the living to be fleeting, with merely a morsel of momentary pleasure,

children.text: pravrajyām atha samupetya tāḥ kumāryas tattvārthapravicayaśuddhabuddhinetrāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then those princesses, having gone forth into renunciation, with their minds's eye purified by the investigation of ultimate truth,

children.text: utterur madavirasaṃ calattaraṅgaṃ saṃsāravyasanamahārṇavaṃ durantam || GoSk_129 ||
children.translated_text: crossed the endless great ocean of the calamities of <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose waves were fickle and whose intoxication was distasteful. // GoSk 129 //

children.text: sarvārthaprakṛtivibhāganiścitātmā sarvebhyo munir itivṛttakaṃ jagāda |
children.translated_text: The sage, whose self was established in the determination of the essential divisions of all things, told the story

children.text: mohāndhe jagati samantacakṣur ekaṃ sattvebhyo bhavabhayakaṇṭakakṣatebhyaḥ || GoSk_130 ||
children.translated_text: to beings wounded by the thorns of the fear of existence, [he being] the sole universal eye in this world blinded by delusion. // GoSk 130 //

children.text: || iti śrīsaptakumārikāvadānaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: || Thus ends the noble <s>Saptakumārikā-avadāna</s> (the story of the Seven Maidens). ||

children.text: || kṛtir ācāryabhadantagopadattasya ||
children.translated_text: || Composed by the venerable teacher <s>Bhadanta Gopadatta</s>. ||

children.text: 13. Sārthavāha
children.translated_text: 13. <s>Sārthavāha</s>

children.text: jarattṛṇānīva śarīrakāṇy api tyajanti santo na ca līnamānasāḥ |
children.translated_text: The virtuous ones abandon even their bodies, like withered grass, without dejected minds,

children.text: kṛpājalakṣālitadehamatsarā jagadvipattijvalanopaśāntaye || GoSv_1 ||
children.translated_text: their selfishness regarding the body washed away by the water of compassion — for the quenching of the fire of the world's calamity. [GoSv 1]

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate |
children.translated_text: As the story is heard:

children.text: bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kila bhagavān saṃtoṣābhyāsād apagatabhavopabhogaviśeṣābhilāṣaḥ suparijñātasaṃskārasvabhāvatvāt svadehe 'py astamitasnehānubandhas tṛṣṇādoṣapratyakṣajñānatayā tadabhidheyamānaso janmāntarābhyastavividhalābhakuśalatvād upāyāntareṇāpi dhanārjanasamarthaḥ samupacitapuṇyasambhāratayā cābhiprāyamātreṇāpi draviṇavibhūtyākarṣaṇaprabhuḥ prabhūtavittopakaraṇo 'pi san kevalam udadhigatajagadvyasanoparitrāṇāyavia saṃketapracārasāṃyātrikaparivṛto mahāsamudram upajagāma |
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through practice of contentment had become free from desire for the special enjoyments of worldly existence; through having fully understood the nature of [mental] formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), his attachment even to his own body had ceased; through his direct knowledge of the fault of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), his mind was set upon [abandoning] it; through skill in various acquisitions cultivated in past lives, he was capable of earning wealth by other means as well; and through his accumulated store of merit, he was able to attract the magnificence of wealth by mere intention alone. Yet, even though he possessed abundant wealth and resources, solely for the purpose of rescuing the world from the calamity of those who had gone to the ocean, he, accompanied by travelers following the established trade route, approached the great ocean.

children.text: athāvagāḍhāḥ payasāṃ nidhānaṃ gambhīrabhīmāyatapaṅktirandhram |
children.translated_text: Then the merchants gradually entered the abode of waters — deep, fearsome, with rows of vast cavities,

children.text: velācalopaghnaviśīrṇaphenasitāntalekhaṃ vaṇijaḥ krameṇa || GoSv_2 ||
children.translated_text: with a white borderline of foam scattered against the shore-cliffs. [GoSv 2]

children.text: tatkarmabhir vā pariṇāmaraudraiḥ svabhāvato vāmbunidhiḥ kṣaṇena |
children.translated_text: Whether by their deeds of terrible ripening, or by the ocean's own nature — in an instant

children.text: paryādadāno hṛdayāni teṣāṃ saṃvartakālādhikadāruṇo 'bhūt || GoSv_3 ||
children.translated_text: it seized their hearts, becoming more terrible than the time of cosmic dissolution. [GoSv 3]

children.text: kharamakarakarāgracchinnabālapravāladrumarasaparibhogāpāṭalāvartacakram |
children.translated_text: Its circle of whirlpools reddened by the sap of young coral trees, whose tender shoots were severed by the tips of the claws of fierce sea-creatures,

children.text: viyad iva navasaṃdhyārañjitāmbhodajālaṃ salilanidhim udīkṣya trāsamūkās ta āsan || GoSv_4 ||
children.translated_text: [the ocean] like the sky tinged at a fresh twilight with a web of clouds — seeing the ocean, they became mute with terror. [GoSv 4]

children.text: vanam iva kumudānāṃ dhautam indor mayūkhair viṣamitasitaphenacchedavinyāsacitram |
children.translated_text: Like a forest of white lotuses washed by the rays of the moon, variegated with arrangements of scattered white foam-fragments —

children.text: lavaṇasalilarāśiṃ vīkṣamāṇāḥ samantān na ratim upayayus te prāṇasaṃdehakāle || GoSv_5 ||
children.translated_text: gazing at the mass of salt water on all sides, they found no delight, at that time when life was in doubt. [GoSv 5]

children.text: vivṛtadaśanaśaṅkhadhvānavitrastamīno bhujagabhuvanaśṛṅgaprāntabhinnormijālaḥ |
children.translated_text: With fish terrified by the sound of conch-like gaping jaws, with a web of waves broken at the edges of the peaks of the serpent-world —

children.text: hṛdayam udadhir alpasthāma teṣāṃ bibheda sphuritavikṛtanakrākrāntavistīrṇakukṣiḥ || GoSv_6 ||
children.translated_text: the ocean shattered the hearts of those of little strength, its vast belly overrun by writhing, distorted crocodiles. [GoSv 6]

children.text: anilabalavibhaktaiḥ śailatuṅgais taraṅgair nabha iva nigirantaṃ sārkanakṣatracandram |
children.translated_text: With mountain-high waves divided by the force of the wind, seeming to swallow the sky along with its sun, stars, and moon —

children.text: tam udadhim avalokya prāṇasaṃdehadolāṃ kṛpaṇakamanasas te sarva evādhirūḍhāḥ || GoSv_7 ||
children.translated_text: beholding that ocean, they all mounted the swing of doubt for their lives, their minds wretched and pitiable. [GoSv 7]

children.text: bhujagam iva viṣāgnicchedamālākarālaṃ śvasanavikacabhogaṃ kruddham udvīkṣamāṇāḥ | lavaṇajalaniketaṃ taṃ durālokapāraṃ maraṇabhayaviṣaṇṇās te paraṃ moham īyuḥ || GoSv_8 ||
children.translated_text: Gazing at it — terrifying like a serpent with garlands of severed poison-fire flames, with expanded hoods gaping with breath — that abode of salt water, whose far shore was beyond sight, stricken with the fear of death, they fell into utter bewilderment. [GoSv 8]

children.text: nicayam iva ghanānāṃ vāribhārālasānāṃ timiram iva vamantaṃ vīcicūrṇapravegaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having entered the ocean — like a mass of heavy clouds burdened with water, as if vomiting darkness with the force of sprayed wave-fragments —

children.text: jalanidhim avagāḍhās te nirākrandabhīmaṃ muṣitavadanaśobhā bodhisattvaṃ praṇemuḥ || GoSv_9 ||
children.translated_text: terrible with its lack of cries [of help], their facial beauty stolen, they bowed to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. [GoSv 9]

children.text: adṛṣṭapūrvair atha tannimittair bhayaṃkarair ākulitā vicitraiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, agitated by varied, fearsome omens never before seen,

children.text: ity ūcur āgadgadadīnakaṇṭhās taṃ bodhisattvaṃ samudīkṣamāṇāḥ || GoSv_10 ||
children.translated_text: they spoke thus with stammering, pitiable voices, gazing at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: [GoSv 10]

children.text: ayaṃ janas tvatpratibaddhasarvaprayojanāśāvinivṛttaceṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: "This assembly, whose hopes for all purposes are bound to you, has ceased its efforts.

children.text: yad atra kṛtyaṃ kriyatāṃ tad āśu prāṇātyayaḥ saṃprati vartate naḥ || GoSv_11 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever must be done here, let it be done swiftly — death is upon us now. [GoSv 11]

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇasya puro janas te nirudyamo majjati toyarāśau |
children.translated_text: Before your very eyes, these people are sinking in the mass of water, without effort.

children.text: kālātipāto 'tra na yuktarūpaḥ parākramasva svabalena tasmāt || GoSv_12 ||
children.translated_text: Delay here is not fitting — therefore exert yourself with your own strength. [GoSv 12]

children.text: tvatpādamūlānucaro na kaś cit saṃspṛṣṭapūrvo vyasanaiḥ kadā cit |
children.translated_text: No one who walks at the base of your feet has ever been touched by calamity.

children.text: trāyasva tasmād vipadāṃ mukheṣu bhramantam enaṃ naravīra lokam || GoSv_13 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, O hero among men, save this world whirling in the jaws of disaster. [GoSv 13]

children.text: piteva putrān anukampamānas tan no bhayān mṛtyukarodarasthān |
children.translated_text: Like a father compassionate toward his children, from this terror — placed in the belly of Death —

children.text: vimocayāsmān paramāryasattva tvaṃ naḥ paritrāṇam upadravebhyaḥ || GoSv_14 ||
children.translated_text: free us, O being of supreme nobility! You are our protection from afflictions. [GoSv 14]

children.text: na devatānām api bhūmayas tās tava prabhāvā na caranti yāsu |
children.translated_text: There are no realms of even the gods where your powers do not reach.

children.text: tad eṣa kālaḥ kṛpaṇān anāthān asmān paritrātum avandhyaśakte || GoSv_15 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, this is the time to rescue us, the wretched and helpless, O you of unfailing power. [GoSv 15]

children.text: manyāmahe tvaṃ samanusmṛto 'pi trāṇaṃ paraṃ sarvajagadbhayebhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: We believe that even when merely remembered, you are the supreme refuge from all fears of the world.

children.text: prāg eva sākṣād abhivīkṣyamāṇas tat pauruṣaṃ darśaya lokabandho || GoSv_16 ||
children.translated_text: How much more when directly seen! Therefore, show your valor, O kinsman of the world. [GoSv 16]

children.text: amī daṃṣṭrācakrakrakacakalilavyāttavadanā
children.translated_text: These cruel circles of <s>timi</s> fish and sea-monsters, fearsome,

children.text: jighāṃsanti krūrāḥ pṛthuvivaravistīrṇajaṭharāḥ |
children.translated_text: with gaping mouths bristling with saw-like rows of fangs, with broad cavities and vast bellies,

children.text: purāsmān atrāṇāṃs timimakaracakrā bhayamayāḥ
children.translated_text: seek to devour us who are defenseless here —

children.text: paritrāyasvemaṃ nikaṭavinipātaṃ janam ataḥ || GoSv_17 ||
children.translated_text: save this assembly from imminent destruction! [GoSv 17]

children.text: svapucchavicchinnataraṅgasaṃkalā niśātadantāntavilagnaśuktayaḥ |
children.translated_text: O noble one, <s>timiṅgila</s> fish rush [toward us], their wave-chains severed by their own tails,

children.text: abhidravanty ārya purā timiṅgilā janān imāṃs tvaccaraṇāśritān api || GoSv_18 ||
children.translated_text: shells clinging to the tips of their sharp teeth — [they rush] upon these people, even though they have taken refuge at your feet. [GoSv 18]

children.text: vilambituṃ nātha na yujyate 'dhunā viśīryate naur iyam ambutāḍitā |
children.translated_text: Lord, it is not fitting to delay now — this ship is splitting apart, battered by the water.

children.text: sphuranty amī vīra samantato jhaṣāḥ pramṛṣṭaguñjāphalaraktalocanāḥ || GoSv_19 ||
children.translated_text: O hero, these fish are leaping on all sides, their eyes red like polished <s>guñjā</s> berries." [GoSv 19]

children.text: atha sa mahātmā tena durviṣaheṇa paravyasanenopataptamānasaḥ svaprāṇātyayam avigaṇayya niṣpratikāradāruṇāṃ tāṃ mahājanavyāpattim avetya kṛpāparigatātmā prakṛtidhīratayā tadavastho 'py asaṃbhrāntacetās tatkālātiśayadhyāyinā vacasā tān sahāyān āśvāsayann abravīt |
children.translated_text: Then that great soul, his mind scorched by that unbearable suffering of others, disregarding the danger to his own life, perceiving that terrible, irremediable calamity of the multitude, his self embraced by compassion, yet with mind unperturbed due to his innate composure even in that situation, consoling those companions with words that contemplated the extraordinary [measure demanded by] that moment, said:

children.text: mṛtena sārdhaṃ na vasanti sāgarāḥ prasiddhir eṣām iyam eva śāśvatī |
children.translated_text: "Oceans do not harbor the dead — this is their well-known eternal [nature].

children.text: ato mamāśritya mṛtaṃ kaḍevaraṃ tarantu santo 'mbunidhiṃ sudustaram || GoSv_20 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, relying on my dead corpse, let the virtuous cross this ocean, so hard to cross. [GoSv 20]

children.text: saṃyuktasaṃyogam upetya sarve nirākulāḥ projjhya viṣādadainyam |
children.translated_text: All of you, clinging together in a united bond, free from agitation, casting aside the wretchedness of despair,

children.text: ātmānam uttārayituṃ yatadhvaṃ mahārṇavān māṃ ca parārtipaṅkāt || GoSv_21 ||
children.translated_text: strive to save yourselves from this great ocean — and me from the mire of others' suffering. [GoSv 21]

children.text: āpadgatānāṃ suhṛdāṃ priyāṇāṃ cirānubaddhapraṇayāśayānām |
children.translated_text: For dear friends who have come upon calamity, whose disposition of long-cultivated affection [is known] —

children.text: ko 'nyo 'sty upāyo ramaṇīyarūpas tat kārṣṭa mā snehamayaṃ viṣādam || GoSv_22 ||
children.translated_text: what other beautiful means is there? Therefore, do not be [overcome by] this grief born of affection. [GoSv 22]

children.text: śatror api vyāpadam āpatantīṃ svaprāṇamūlyena nivārayeyam |
children.translated_text: I would avert calamity even from an enemy at the cost of my own life —

children.text: prāg eva yuṣmākam analpakālasaṃvardhitasnehaparigrahāṇām || GoSv_23 ||
children.translated_text: how much more for you, whose bonds of affection have been nurtured over no short time. [GoSv 23]

children.text: mamātmabhāvair apavṛttasaukhyaiḥ syāc cet sukhī kuntapipīliko 'pi |
children.translated_text: If even a wretched ant could be made happy by my bodies from which happiness has departed,

children.text: jarattṛṇānīva tathāpi jahyām ahaṃ śarīrāṇi nirastakhedaḥ || GoSv_24 ||
children.translated_text: even so, I would cast off bodies like withered grass, free from grief. [GoSv 24]

children.text: trāṇāśayāyāṃ samupāśritānāṃ guṇaiḥ pavitrīkṛtamānasānām |
children.translated_text: For one who abandons his body for the welfare of those who have taken refuge with the hope of protection,

children.text: hitāya dehaṃ tyajato mamaikaṃ dayāparītaṃ kim ivātra citram || GoSv_25 ||
children.translated_text: whose minds have been purified by [his] virtues — what is wonderful in that, since he is pervaded by compassion? [GoSv 25]

children.text: parārthacaryāviguṇaṃ śarīraṃ vṛthā guruṃ bhāram ivodvahantaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those of purified nature, who have made the living world the spouse of their compassion,

children.text: vrajanti khedaṃ pariśuddhasattvāḥ kṛpākalatrīkṛtajīvalokāḥ || GoSv_26 ||
children.translated_text: carrying in vain this body — a heavy burden, useless for the practice of serving others — become wearied. [GoSv 26]

children.text: evaṃvidhe yadi na kāyam imaṃ prayokṣye puṇyāgame nirupamānasukhānubandhe |
children.translated_text: If I do not employ this body in such [an occasion] — an arrival of merit, a sequel of incomparable happiness —

children.text: ko 'rtho 'munā parihṛtena kaḍevareṇa vātāhatāmbunidhibudbudadurbalena || GoSv_27 ||
children.translated_text: what use is this preserved corpse, as feeble as a bubble on a wind-struck ocean? [GoSv 27]

children.text: tyakṣyāmi nemaṃ yadi pūtikāyaṃ bhavaddhitādhānavidhānakāle |
children.translated_text: If I do not abandon this putrid body at the time of establishing your welfare,

children.text: saṃtyājayiṣyaty abalaṃ balātmā jagadvināśāvahitaḥ kṛtāntaḥ || GoSv_28 ||
children.translated_text: the powerful Death, intent on the world's destruction, will forcibly make the weak abandon it. [GoSv 28]

children.text: tyajāmi yuṣmān kim udīkṣamāṇo yaśo 'tha vā mānagataṃ ca dharmam |
children.translated_text: What am I looking at [i.e., what am I waiting for], abandoning you? Fame? Or pride-bound <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: dehaṃ kalīnāṃ padabandhabhūtaṃ utāvaśo mṛtyukarābhimṛṣṭam || GoSv_29 ||
children.translated_text: Or this body, which is the foothold of afflictions, helplessly groped by the hand of Death? [GoSv 29]

children.text: tad atra śokāya matir na deyā bhavadbhir āsannaparābhavāya |
children.translated_text: Therefore, your minds should not be given to grief — [grief] on the verge of being overcome.

children.text: mama krameṇaiva samāgato 'yaṃ mahotsavaḥ puṇyaviśeṣaramyaḥ || GoSv_30 ||
children.translated_text: This great festival, beautiful with extraordinary merit, has come to me in due course. [GoSv 30]

children.text: bahusukhalavanānātantusaṃtānaneyās tṛṇam iva gataśaṅkā deham ujjhanty asantaḥ |
children.translated_text: The ignoble, suspicion-free, abandon their bodies — like grass — when led by the threads of manifold petty pleasures.

children.text: atisṛjati parārthaṃ kāyam āsannanāśaṃ yadi sucaritapūrvaṃ duṣkaraṃ kiṃ nu tatra || GoSv_31 ||
children.translated_text: If one gives up a body near destruction for the sake of others, preceded by good conduct — what is difficult in that? [GoSv 31]

children.text: atha te puruṣās tena tasyādbhutenābhiprasāritamānasāḥ sutarāṃ tadviyogaśaṅkāvyathitahṛdayā viṣādadainyavidheyāś cintāviṣayātītagocaram aviṣahyam ativismayanīyaṃ ca tatkarma taṃ mahāsattvam aviratāśrudhārāprakṣālitanayanadīnavadanāḥ pādayoḥ saṃpariṣvajya praṇamya ca sarvāṅgair ity avadan |
children.translated_text: Then those men, their minds drawn forth by that wondrous [speech] of his, yet all the more pained at heart by the fear of separation from him, subject to the wretchedness of despair, [seeing] that deed beyond the realm of thought, unbearable yet supremely astonishing — those men, with faces pitiable, their eyes washed by an unceasing stream of tears, embracing his feet and bowing with all their limbs, spoke thus:

children.text: kāmam atraiva nidhanaṃ sarva eva mahodadhau |
children.translated_text: "Let us all meet our end right here in this great ocean,

children.text: yāsyāmo na tu śakyāmaḥ kartum etad anāryakam || GoSv_32 ||
children.translated_text: but we are unable to commit this ignoble [act]. [GoSv 32]

children.text: evaṃvidhasya vyasanāni dṛṣṭvā suhṛdviśeṣasya sudurlabhasya |
children.translated_text: Having seen the calamities of such an extraordinary, most rare dear friend,

children.text: prāṇair dhanair vā kim ihāsti kṛtyaṃ tat sāhasād vāraya dhīracetaḥ || GoSv_33 ||
children.translated_text: what business is there here with lives or wealth? Therefore, restrain [yourself] from this rash act, O steadfast-minded one! [GoSv 33]

children.text: uttīrṇān api toyaughād asmān asmād duruttarāt |
children.translated_text: Even if rescued from this water-flood, so hard to cross,

children.text: magnān duścaritāvarte kaḥ samuttārayiṣyati || GoSv_34 ||
children.translated_text: who will rescue us, sunk in the whirlpool of wicked deeds? [GoSv 34]

children.text: nūnaṃ karmaṇa evāyaṃ vipākaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Surely this is the ripening of [past] <s>karma</s> that has arrived,

children.text: yenāpad iyam āyātā niṣpratīkāradāruṇā || GoSv_35 ||
children.translated_text: by which this calamity has come — terrible, without remedy. [GoSv 35]

children.text: adhyupekṣya suhṛtpīḍām etāṃ pāpānubandhinīm |
children.translated_text: Having overlooked this suffering of our friend — [suffering] accompanied by sin —

children.text: duḥkhāntam upayāsyāmaḥ kair upāyaiḥ punar vayam || GoSv_36 ||
children.translated_text: by what means shall we ever reach the end of suffering? [GoSv 36]

children.text: dayāmṛdukasaṃtānaṃ kuryād antāvasāyinam |
children.translated_text: This heroic tale of your compassion would make [even one who has] reached the final [stage]

children.text: idaṃ karmāvadānaṃ te prāg evārya suhṛjjanam || GoSv_37 ||
children.translated_text: [turn] soft-hearted — how much more the community of friends, O noble one! [GoSv 37]

children.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sutarāṃs tais teṣāṃ saujanyasūcakair vacobhiḥ pravijṛmbhamāṇatīvraprasādapremagauravakāruṇyas samanuneṣyaṃs tān sahāyakān anukampāmṛtavāribhiḥ siñcann iva tṛptivisargair ity abravīt |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, all the more swelling with intense devotion, love, respect, and compassion at those words of theirs indicating their nobility, wishing to persuade those companions, as if sprinkling them with the water-nectar of kindness, with [words like] outpourings of satisfaction, spoke thus:

children.text: bhavadbhir anadhīṣṭo 'haṃ svabhūtyai dehasaṃjñakam |
children.translated_text: "Without being urged by you, I abandon for my own welfare this thing called 'body,' which is

children.text: tyajāmy anarthaṃ tatra syād yuṣmākaṃ kim anāryakam || GoSv_38 ||
children.translated_text: a misfortune — so what ignobility would there be for you? [GoSv 38]

children.text: akāle kaumudī hy eṣā naivaitad vyasanaṃ mama |
children.translated_text: This is indeed a moonrise at an unexpected time — this is not my calamity.

children.text: pratīkāro mayā labdho vipadām eṣa śāśvataḥ || GoSv_39 ||
children.translated_text: I have obtained a remedy for disasters — this is eternal. [GoSv 39]

children.text: sauhārdaviśrambhaniratyayā vo yady asti kā cin mayi cittavṛttiḥ |
children.translated_text: If you have any disposition of mind toward me, [born] of unceasing affection and trust,

children.text: na kartum arhanti tato bhavanto dharmasya kīrtyābharaṇasya vighnam || GoSv_40 ||
children.translated_text: then you should not create an obstacle to <s>dharma</s>, the ornament of fame. [GoSv 40]

children.text: cittaṃ balād api hite viniyojanīyam āryair anāryam ahitāc ca vivecanīyam |
children.translated_text: The mind is to be directed forcibly toward what is beneficial by the noble, and is to be separated from what is harmful and ignoble.

children.text: tasmāt pravṛttim iha karmaṇi sādhujuṣṭe nārhanti vighnayitum aśrumukhā bhavantaḥ || GoSv_41 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, you with tear-stained faces should not create an obstacle to my engagement in this deed favored by the virtuous. [GoSv 41]

children.text: anupādānam evāsya parārthaṃ cāparigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: This [body] is itself non-attachment, and its [surrender] for others' sake is non-possession.

children.text: māṃ saṃpratīkṣate kāyakale randhraprahāriṇaḥ || GoSv_42 ||
children.translated_text: Death, who strikes at vulnerabilities, awaits me through the [instrument] of this body. [GoSv 42]

children.text: upātto 'py ayam asmābhir anādeyo na nīyate |
children.translated_text: Though taken up by me, this [body] — unacceptable — cannot be retained.

children.text: yadi sattvārthasācivyaṃ ko 'nenārthaḥ praṇāśinā || GoSv_43 ||
children.translated_text: If it cannot serve the welfare of beings, what use is this perishable thing? [GoSv 43]

children.text: yadi nābhyuddhariṣyāmi yuṣmān asmād duruttarāt |
children.translated_text: If I cannot rescue you from this [ocean], so hard to cross,

children.text: katham uttārayiṣyāmi lokaṃ saṃsārasāgarāt || GoSv_44 ||
children.translated_text: how shall I ferry the world across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>? [GoSv 44]

children.text: etāni cānyāni ca bodhisattvāḥ kurvanti karmāṇy avipannasattvāḥ |
children.translated_text: These and other deeds are performed by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of unfailing resolve,

children.text: parārthacaryāviṣaye carantaḥ kṛpānubhūtāḥ svasukhānurāgāḥ || GoSv_45 ||
children.translated_text: who walk in the domain of service to others, impelled by compassion, unattached to their own happiness. [GoSv 45]

children.text: anāvṛtadvāram idaṃ niketanaṃ durāvahāṇāṃ bhavaduḥkhapattriṇāṃ |
children.translated_text: This dwelling — the open-doored abode of the arrows of suffering in worldly existence, hard to endure —

children.text: cirāt pramodāyatanī kariṣyate mayā śarīraṃ suhṛdāṃ hitāgame || GoSv_46 ||
children.translated_text: I shall make it, after a long time, a ground of delight, at the arrival of welfare for my friends — [namely,] this body. [GoSv 46]

children.text: bhavatparitrāṇamaye sukhodaye niyojya kāyaṃ niyataṃ mayāpsyate |
children.translated_text: By employing my body in the joyful occasion of your rescue, I shall surely obtain

children.text: abhedyam acchedyam ahāryam avyayaṃ niruttaraṃ dharmaśarīram avraṇam || GoSv_47 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Body of the Dharma) — unbreakable, unpierceable, unassailable, imperishable, unsurpassed, and unwounded. [GoSv 47]

children.text: amitrabhūtaṃ yadi mitrasād imaṃ kaliṃ kariṣyāmi na kāyasaṃjñakam |
children.translated_text: If I do not turn this thing called 'body,' which is an enemy, into a friend's [instrument] —

children.text: vidhakṣyate vipratisāravahninā mano viniśvāsaśikhena me ciram || GoSv_48 ||
children.translated_text: my mind will be burned for a long time by the fire of remorse, whose flame is the [fire of] sighing." [GoSv 48]

children.text: gataviklavā bhavanto madīyam udgataprāṇaṃ śarīraṃ plavam ivālambyānyonyasaṃsaktikayā vārivegavaśena yena vātena vā digbhāgena sthalam upagamya parṇamūlaphalajalādibhir yāpayantaḥ parasparam avipannasauhṛdāḥ karmasvakatāvalambino lokasvabhāvam avekṣamāṇā vinītavivādaśokadainyāḥ kāryāvasānam āgamayata | sukham anubhūya duḥkham apy anubhūyate | saṃpattim apy upāsya vipattir upāsyate | saṃsāracārakāvacarāṇāṃ hi etad eva paryāptaṃ vyasanam ataḥ pratikaṣṭatarāṇy apy atra kṛcchrāṇy āsādyante śrutimanovidāhinī | na hy enam anupatan kaś cit sukhī nāma | prabalānilākulānalajvālākalāpamadhyagatasyānuktasiddhaṃ dāhaduḥkham | tṛṣṇāvidheyamanasāṃ cābhimukhaḥ parābhava utsaṅgagatāni sarvadainyāny āsannavartī paribhavo bhayam upari vyavasthitam abhito vipralambhavaikṛtāni | saṃkṣepataḥ sarvam aśivajālam upagṛhya tṛṣṇā naram upabadhnāti | sa ca madviyogadainyāvakāśo na hṛdi karaṇīyaḥ | īdṛśo hi lokasvabhāvo viyogaduḥkhānugatā eva hi priyajanasaṃyogāḥ |
children.translated_text: Be without agitation, noble ones. Grasping my lifeless body as a raft, clinging to one another, [carried] by the force of the current or whichever wind to whatever direction, reaching dry land, sustaining yourselves with leaves, roots, fruits, water, and such, maintaining unimpaired friendship toward one another, relying on the fact that each owns their <s>karma</s>, observing the nature of the world, with disputes, grief, and despondency calmed — await the conclusion of your task. Having experienced happiness, suffering too is experienced. Having enjoyed prosperity, adversity too must be endured. For this alone is the sufficient misfortune of those who wander in the paths of <s>saṃsāra</s> — and even worse difficulties are encountered here, which burn the ears and mind. For no one following [this path] is truly happy. The burning suffering of one caught in the midst of garlands of flames fanned by powerful winds is self-evident. For those whose minds are subject to craving, defeat is face-to-face, all wretchedness sits in their lap, humiliation is ever near, fear stands above, and on all sides are the distortions of disappointment. In short, craving, having gathered all that is inauspicious, binds a person. And the occasion for despondency at separation from me should not be given place in your hearts. For such is the nature of the world — unions with dear ones are indeed attended by the suffering of separation.

children.text: dīrghakālaparicayād dṛḍhasnehanibaddhāny api sauhṛdāni kṣaṇena viśliṣyanti | prāṇināṃ viparyāsaś caiṣa cetasaḥ priyo 'yaṃ mameti | dṛśyante kāraṇāntaraviparyayāt parivartamānāni priyāpriyāṇi jīvaloke | tasmān na paratantreṣv apariniṣpannasvabhāveṣu prakṛtibhedavartiṣu vipralambhapadasthāneṣu kṣaṇavipariṇāmalolaśīleṣu śokāyāsamayeṣu priyasamāgameṣv abhiniviśyātmā khedayitavyaḥ | tatra sukhaṃ dhairyam eva paruṣāṇām āpatsv avalambo bhavati viṣādam avadhīrayati śokam uparuṇaddhi vighnayati āpadam āpatantīṃ prajñānasahitaṃ ca tad evābhimatam artham ānayati |
children.translated_text: Even friendships bound by firm affection from long acquaintance are severed in an instant. And this is the delusion of the mind of living beings: 'This one is dear to me.' In the world of the living, the pleasant and unpleasant are seen to transform due to the reversal of [their] causes. Therefore, one should not torment oneself by clinging to fond unions that are dependent on others, of unfinished nature, subject to inherent change, stations of disappointment, whose nature is to transform in a moment, and that are occasions for grief and distress. There, steadfastness alone is happiness — it becomes the support of the resolute in calamities, it dismisses despondency, checks grief, obstructs oncoming adversity, and combined with wisdom, it brings the desired goal.

children.text: śokānivṛttis tu niṣprayojanam āśrayaṃ saṃtāpayati kṛtyam antarayati kāntim ācchinatti pratibhānam āyāsayaty āsannasnehaduḥkhaṃ suhṛjjanaṃ .... dharmārthayaśaḥsukhāni copahanti | matkṛtam anupaśyadbhis tu bhavadbhiḥ puṇyeṣv ādaraḥ karaṇīyaḥ | puṇyam eva hi prāṇinām ihāmutra ca niratyayo bandhur āpatsu viṣādī sahāyaḥ pātheyam ayatnavāhyaṃ pradīpas tamasi prapāteṣu saṃkramaṃ bhayasthāneṣv ārakṣā maṅgalam advaidhasiddham atyantikaṃ siddhaṃ sūpacaraḥ svāmī parāyaṇam āpadgatānām āyatanam avipariṇāmināṃ sukhānāṃ kṣetraṃ diśāvidiśāntavyāpināṃ yaśasāṃ ākaraḥ praśaṃsānām anabhibhūtaṃ vaiśāradyam | puṇyāvaṣṭhambhād eva ca puruṣo duravagāhe 'pi sukham avagāhate | paralokakāntāre viṣādapadasthāne 'pi nāma maraṇasamaye na viṣīdanti puṇyakarmāṇaḥ | kaṇṭakapracayakarkaśāny api janmadurgāṇi prāyeṇākṣatāḥ saṃcaranti puṇyabalinaḥ | puṇyair eva cākhilajagaddhitasukhādhyāśayapravṛttivistīrṇām ākarṣayanti sakalabhuvanādhipatyābhiṣekamahatīṃ sarvalokasādhāraṇāṃ tāthāgatīṃ guṇasamṛddhiṃ prāg eva pratanusukhānavakāśādīnavāṃ pracurajanamanovikāriṇīm anantaduḥkhabāṇasaṃnipātadūṣitām āyāsinīm iha paratra ca bāliśānāṃ pratikṣaṇavyayānubandhādūṣitām anekarūpavairakṛtānuṣaṅgadāruṇāṃ bhavabhogamayīm aśivām akhilāṃ viparītasukhābhiniveśakhalāṃ saṃpattisaṃjñāntaritāṃ vipattim akāraṇabhraṃśamanovidāhinīm ity alam iti prasaṅgenātipatati | kāryakālaś caramasaṃdeśo 'yaṃ bhadramukhā ity uktvā bodhisattvo muhūrtam ekāgramano babhūva |
children.translated_text: But indulgence in grief, without purpose, burns its possessor, obstructs duty, diminishes grace, wearies eloquence, causes grief-suffering to friends who are near .... and destroys <s>dharma</s>, wealth, fame, and happiness. But you, seeing what I have done, should cultivate devotion to meritorious deeds. For merit alone is, for living beings, in this world and the next, an unfailing kinsman, a sympathetic companion in misfortune, provisions that need no carrying, a lamp in darkness, a crossing at precipices, a guard at places of danger, an auspicious [sign] of undivided efficacy, an ultimate, proven, easy-to-serve master, a refuge for those in distress, a field of undiminishing happiness, a mine of fame that pervades all quarters and sub-quarters, an unconquerable confidence. And by the support of merit alone, a person happily plunges even into what is hard to fathom. In the wilderness of the next world, at that place of despondency, even at the hour of death, doers of meritorious deeds do not despair. Those mighty in merit generally traverse unharmed even the fortresses of birth, rough with heaps of thorns. And by merits alone, they attract the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s wealth of qualities — that great consecration of universal sovereignty, shared by all worlds, vast with the activity of aspiration for the welfare and happiness of all the world — let alone the prosperity of worldly enjoyment, inauspicious, with its defects of trivial, spaceless happiness, agitating the minds of many, polluted by the rain of arrows of infinite suffering, painful here and hereafter for the foolish, tainted by the sequence of momentary decay, terrible with the attendant enmity of manifold forms, wicked with attachment to perverted happiness, a calamity concealed under the name of prosperity, burning the mind with causeless loss — but enough! This digression goes too far. The time for action [has come]. This is my final message, O fair-faced ones.' Having said this, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> became single-pointed in mind for a moment.

children.text: nivāryamāṇo 'pi śataiḥ suhṛdbhir bāṣpāmbuvisyandivilocanāntaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Though restrained by hundreds of friends, their eyes streaming with tear-water,

children.text: sādhuḥ svadehāśrayaṇīm apekṣāṃ tatyāja lokavyasanopataptaḥ || GoSv_49 ||
children.translated_text: the saint abandoned the concern for dwelling in his own body, burning with the suffering of the world's misfortune. // GoSv 49 //

children.text: ārtasvarair aviratair avibhaktavarṇais teṣāṃ viṣādapariluptamanaḥsthitīnām |
children.translated_text: With the unceasing, inarticulate cries of distress from those whose mental composure was destroyed by despair,

children.text: āpūryamāṇasalilapradarāntarālaḥ saṃcukṣubhe bhṛśataraṃ lavaṇāmburāśiḥ || GoSv_50 ||
children.translated_text: the salt-water ocean, in the intervals between its filling torrents, was greatly agitated. // GoSv 50 //

children.text: bodhisattvo 'pi mahāsattva iti praṇidhim upabṛmhayām āsa śāntaye sarvasattvānām |
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being, strengthened his vow (<s>praṇidhi</s>) for the peace of all beings:

children.text: divyā tāvat prakṛticapalā sopasargā vibhūtiḥ
children.translated_text: Even divine prosperity is fickle by nature and attended by calamity —

children.text: prāg evānyā parimitasukhapratyayapratyapāyā |
children.translated_text: let alone other [prosperity], with its limited causes of happiness and their reversal.

children.text: tasmān nārtho mama ⏑ ⏑ sukhaiḥ svapnamāyopamānaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I have no use for these pleasures, which are like dreams and illusions;

children.text: puṇyād asmān na ca śamasukhaṃ prārthaye projjhya lokān || GoSv_51 ||
children.translated_text: and from this merit, abandoning [desire for all] worlds, I seek only the happiness of peace. // GoSv 51 //

children.text: mohāvarte maraṇamakare mānapāṣāṇagarbhe
children.translated_text: In the ocean of existence, churned by the wind of grief, with the whirlpool of delusion, the crocodile of death,

children.text: tṛṣṇātoye madanakaluṣe krodhasaṃsarpisarpe |
children.translated_text: the boulders of pride, the waters of craving, muddied by passion, the creeping serpent of anger —

children.text: magnaṃ lokaṃ bhavajalanidhau śokavātāvadhūte
children.translated_text: the world is sunk —

children.text: puṇyād asmād aham aśaraṇaṃ kṛtsnam uttārayeyam || GoSv_52 ||
children.translated_text: from this merit, may I rescue it entirely, shelterless as it is. // GoSv 52 //

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā praṇidhim acalaṃ sādrisārasthirātmā
children.translated_text: Thus having made an unshakable vow, his soul firm as <s>Sādri</s> (the steadfast mountain),

children.text: tyaktāpekṣaḥ sucaritaśatopārjite 'pi svadehe |
children.translated_text: without concern even for his own body, acquired through hundreds of good deeds,

children.text: nistriṃśena pramuditamanāḥ pāṭayām āsa kukṣiṃ
children.translated_text: with a joyful mind, he split open his own belly with a sword,

children.text: svāṃ śokārtivyathitahṛdayaḥ prāṇināṃ tāraṇāya || GoSv_53 ||
children.translated_text: his heart aching with grief, for the rescue of living beings. // GoSv 53 //

children.text: atha śuśruvire giraḥ śubhāḥ suravidyādharayakṣarakṣasām |
children.translated_text: Then auspicious words were heard from the gods, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: iti citramanoharāśrayāḥ patitās tasya guṇopasaṃhitāḥ || GoSv_54 ||
children.translated_text: falling upon him, full of wonderful delight, gathered with [praises of] his virtues: // GoSv 54 //

children.text: sattvārthapratipattikauśalam aho hī dhīratā cetasaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Ah, what skill in the practice of benefiting beings! Ah, the fortitude of mind!

children.text: puṇyābhyāsaviśeṣapuṇyamahatām āścaryarūpasthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: The wondrous state of those whose greatness of merit comes from the excellence of meritorious practice!

children.text: sādhūnāṃ svasukhānurāgavigamasvacchā bata prakriyā
children.translated_text: Ah, the transparent conduct of saints, free from the attachment of self-happiness!

children.text: – – – ⏑ ⏑ – ⏑ – bata kṛpā nāpekṣate svāśrayam || GoSv_55 ||
children.translated_text: [...] Ah, compassion does not regard its own support!' // GoSv 55 //

children.text: loko 'yaṃ vinimīlito 'pi viduṣā pronmīlitaḥ sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: 'This world, though closed [in darkness], has been opened on all sides by the wise one,

children.text: kīrtyā candramayūkhadhautakumudacchāyā ⏑ – – ⏑ – |
children.translated_text: with fame [radiant as] the shadow of white lotuses washed by moonbeams [...];

children.text: etenaiva nimajjatāpi bhuvanaṃ magnaṃ samabhyuddhṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: by this very one, though sinking, the world, sunk

children.text: janmāvaskarakardame sphuradurukleśakrimivyākule || GoSv_56 ||
children.translated_text: in the mire of the mechanism of birth, swarming with fierce worms of affliction, has been lifted up.' // GoSv 56 //

children.text: tiryag vikṣipyamānaṃ navajalaśiśirair mandamandair marudbhir
children.translated_text: Scattered sideways by soft, gentle breezes cool with fresh rain,

children.text: divyodyānadrumebhyaḥ kusumam avirataṃ taccharīre papāta |
children.translated_text: flowers from the trees of divine gardens fell continuously upon his body.

children.text: abhyudgamyāmburāśeḥ sphuṭamaṇikiraṇaśrīkarālaiḥ śirobhir
children.translated_text: Rising from the ocean, with heads made radiant by the splendor of brilliant gem-rays,

children.text: vyābhugnopāntamadhyaiḥ kuvalayamṛdubhis taṃ bhujaṅgāḥ praṇemuḥ || GoSv_57 ||
children.translated_text: the serpents, their middles gently bent, bowed to him with [hoods] soft as blue lotuses. // GoSv 57 //

children.text: lakṣmyā samālabdham iva prakāmaṃ pramṛṣṭacāmīkaracāruvarṇam |
children.translated_text: As if fully anointed by <s>Lakṣmī</s>, of beautiful color like polished gold,

children.text: samudgataprāṇam api prasannaṃ rarāja tat tasya vibhoḥ śarīram || GoSv_58 ||
children.translated_text: though the life-breath had departed, that body of the lord shone, serene. // GoSv 58 //

children.text: ālambya plavam iva te 'tha taccharīraṃ bāṣpāmbuvyatikarapāṭalāntanetrāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, grasping his body as a raft, their eyes reddened by the mingling of tears,

children.text: utterur makarakarakṣatormicakraṃ tasyaiva praṇidhibalāśrayāt samudram || GoSv_59 ||
children.translated_text: they crossed the ocean, with its circles of waves scarred by the claws of sea-creatures, by the power of his very vow (<s>praṇidhi</s>). // GoSv 59 //

children.text: tad evam atiduṣkarāṇi bhagavān asau bhūtaye
children.translated_text: Thus that Blessed One performed deeds exceedingly difficult

children.text: cakāra jagatāṃ kṛpāparigatāmalādhyāśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: for the prosperity of the worlds, with pure aspiration encompassed by compassion.

children.text: prasādayata tatra mānasam ato jagadbāndhave
children.translated_text: Therefore, compose your minds upon that friend of the world,

children.text: samagrabhuvanopakārakaraṇaikavīre jine || GoSv_60 ||
children.translated_text: the hero unsurpassed in accomplishing the welfare of the entire universe, the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). // GoSv 60 //

children.text: prasādya ca mano munau sucaritaikaratnākare
children.translated_text: And having composed your minds upon the sage, the sole treasure-mine of good deeds,

children.text: vaco 'vitathavādinaḥ śrutirasāyanaṃ śrūyatām |
children.translated_text: hear the speech that is a rejuvenating elixir for the ears — the words of the truth-speaker.

children.text: tadaśravaṇavañcitaṃ jagad idaṃ bhramaty āturaṃ
children.translated_text: This world, deprived of hearing [his words], wanders afflicted

children.text: bhavādhvani nirāśraye vyasanakaṇṭakāndhācite || GoSv_61 ||
children.translated_text: on the shelterless path of existence, filled with the thorns and darkness of misfortune. // GoSv 61 //

children.text: iti śrīsārthavāhajātakaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the holy <s>Sārthavāhajātaka</s> (Caravan-Leader Birth-Story) is complete.

children.text: 14. Sarvaṃdada
children.translated_text: 14. <s>Sarvaṃdada</s> (The All-Giving King)

children.text: paraduḥkhaduḥkhitāḥ svajīvitam api nāpekṣante sādhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Saints, suffering at the suffering of others, disregard even their own lives.

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate |
children.translated_text: This is what is heard in tradition:

children.text: bodhisattvo 'nyatamaṃ svakulakramāgataṃ mahīmaṇḍalaṃ samanuśaśāsa | tasyārthijanamanoharair aviṣamapravṛttimadhuratarair anatikrāntakālābhilaṣitaiḥ phalāśākārpaṇyopaśamasvacchaśobhair vibhavavisargair lokān saṃtarpayataḥ sarvaṃdada ity evaṃ yathārthaṃ nāma prathitam āsīt |
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> ruled a certain kingdom inherited from his own lineage. As he satisfied the people with distributions of wealth that were alluring to supplicants, sweeter than equitable conduct, whose desires were never belated, pure and beautiful with the pacification of the poverty of fruition and hope — he bore the name '<s>Sarvaṃdada</s>' (All-Giving), true to its meaning.

children.text: jagaddhitādhānasamutsukatvāt sa rājyabhāraṃ bibharāṃ babhūva |
children.translated_text: That lord of the earth bore the burden of kingship, gradually bestowed upon him

children.text: kṣitīśvaraḥ pūrvakṛtānavadyapuṇyaprabhāvopanataṃ krameṇa || GoSd_1 ||
children.translated_text: by the power of previously performed, faultless merit, out of his eagerness to establish the welfare of the world. // GoSd 1 //

children.text: na tasya kiṃpākaphalopamāś calā mano manovibhramamātrabhadrikāḥ |
children.translated_text: For that great soul of noble nature, prosperities — transient like the fruit of the <s>kiṃpāka</s> tree,

children.text: svabhāgadheyopanatā vibhūtayo babandhur āryaprakṛter mahātmanaḥ || GoSd_2 ||
children.translated_text: pleasant only to the delusion of the mind — did not bind him, though they came by his own destiny. // GoSd 2 //

children.text: pariśramas tasya babhūva yautako mahākṛpādhīnamater mahīpateḥ |
children.translated_text: Exertion was his wedding-gift, that king whose mind was subject to great compassion;

children.text: prabhutvam āsīj jagatāṃ tv abādhithaṃ vibhūtisaṃbhogasukheṣu bhūriṣu || GoSd_3 ||
children.translated_text: his sovereignty over the worlds was untroubled amid the many pleasures of the enjoyment of prosperity. // GoSd 3 //

children.text: na tasya mātsaryatamo'vaguṇṭhanaṃ babhūva gātreṣv api mānasaṃ yadā |
children.translated_text: When there was in him not even the slightest mental veiling by the darkness of envy, even in his body,

children.text: tadā kathaivoparatāsukhāgate tṛṇopame śokanibandhane dhane || GoSd_4 ||
children.translated_text: then how much less in wealth — the cause of bondage to grief, comparable to grass, to which un-renounced happiness clings! // GoSd 4 //

children.text: taṃ kila mahātmānam anyatamaḥ pārthivo 'tṛptaḥ svarājyaśriyā parityaktadharmayaśāḥ sukhasādhanopāyadāruṇaḥ svarājyād uccālayitum upacakrame |
children.translated_text: A certain king, unsatisfied with the glory of his own kingdom, having abandoned <s>dharma</s> and fame, terrible in his means of procuring happiness, undertook to dislodge that great soul from his kingdom.

children.text: saṃprāpya bhogān mahato 'py anāryāḥ panthānam āryācaritaṃ vilaṅghya |
children.translated_text: Having obtained great enjoyments, the ignoble ones, leaping over the path of noble conduct,

children.text: tṛṣṇāparītāḥ karuṇātmakeṣu sādhuṣv api krodhaviṣaṃ vamanti || GoSd_5 ||
children.translated_text: possessed by craving, vomit the poison of anger even upon the virtuous, whose very nature is compassion. // GoSd 5 //

children.text: bhaiṣajyavṛkṣā iva ye kadā cit kva cit kathaṃ cij jagato hitāya |
children.translated_text: Those who, like healing trees, arise here or there, now or then, for the welfare of the world —

children.text: bhavanti tān apy upataptacittāḥ krodhāgninā kāpuruṣā dahanti || GoSd_6 ||
children.translated_text: even them, the base, with minds inflamed by anger-fire, burn. // GoSd 6 //

children.text: kurvīta ko nāma manuṣya āryaḥ sacetanas teṣu manaḥpradoṣam |
children.translated_text: What noble, sentient human being would harbor ill-will toward those

children.text: yeṣāṃ yaśobhiḥ kumudāvadātair udbhāsitānīva digantarāṇi || GoSd_7 ||
children.translated_text: whose fame, white as jasmine, has illuminated, as it were, the far quarters? // GoSd 7 //

children.text: atha dharaṇirajobhiḥ śārikākaṇṭhadhūmrais turagakhuranipātaprodgataiś chādayan kham |
children.translated_text: Then that king arrived, covering the sky with dust — grey as the throat of <s>sārikā</s> birds — rising from the impact of horse-hooves,

children.text: sa nṛpatir upatasthe mattamātaṅgasainyair upavanatarupūgān ārujan meghanīlān || GoSd_8 ||
children.translated_text: with armies of maddened elephants, uprooting the groves of garden-trees, dark as clouds. // GoSd 8 //

children.text: udadhir iva yugānte plāvayaṃl lokam antarlulitamakarapucchacchinnacañcattaraṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: Like the ocean at the end of a <s>yuga</s> flooding the world, its churning fish-tails breaking its restless waves —

children.text: sa nṛpabalasamūho nagnanistriṃśapattrasphuritaravimayūkhas tatpuraṃ saṃrurodha || GoSd_9 ||
children.translated_text: that royal army, with the sun's rays flashing on naked sword-blades, besieged his city. // GoSd 9 //

children.text: upanatam api puṇyair vipralambhāvasānaṃ dhig anupaśamakāri śrīsukhaṃ pārthivānām |
children.translated_text: Even when attained through merits — shame on the happiness and splendor of kings that offers no peace, ending in disappointment,

children.text: piśitam iva vipūti kravyabhugmaṇḍalānāṃ yad iha bhavati puṃsāṃ vairavairasya mūlam || GoSd_10 ||
children.translated_text: which, like meat to circles of carrion-eaters, becomes here the root of enmity born of enmity for people! // GoSd 10 //

children.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ prāg eva viditaviṣayadoṣavairavairaḥ saṃrambhavipralabhādyanarthabhūyiṣṭhaṃ rājyam atimanyamānaḥ svasukhasaṃbhogābhiṣvaṅgadainyānupakliṣṭamānasaś cintayāṃ babhūva |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who had long since become hostile to the defects and enmities of sense-objects, regarding kingship — mostly filled with the harm of fury and disappointment — with contempt, his mind unafflicted by the wretchedness of clinging to self-happiness and enjoyment, reflected:

children.text: dhig astv anāryaṃ viṣayāśrayaṃ sukhaṃ samīraṇoddhūtalatāntacañcalam |
children.translated_text: Fie upon this ignoble happiness dependent on sense-objects, flickering like the tips of vines shaken by the wind;

children.text: upāsate yatra nibaddhamānasā narā daśāṃ bandhujanopatāpinīm || GoSd_11 ||
children.translated_text: where people, with minds bound, worship a state that causes suffering to their kinsmen! // GoSd 11 //

children.text: vātoddhūtataraṅgitadhvajaśikhāpratyāhatāmbhodharaṃ
children.translated_text: The enemy army, with clouds repelled by the tips of banner-flags fluttering in the wind,

children.text: dānaprasrutisiktadantamusalakrūradvipendrākulam |
children.translated_text: crowded with terrible, fierce war-elephants, their tusk-pestles wet with streaming ichor —

children.text: śakto 'rātibalaṃ vihantum akhilaṃ bāhudvitīyo 'py ahaṃ
children.translated_text: though I am able single-handedly to crush the entire enemy force,

children.text: rakṣed akṣatacāriṇī yadi kṛpā māteva māṃ nāpadi || GoSd_12 ||
children.translated_text: may compassion, like a mother, protect me from harm — if it travels unbroken. // GoSd 12 //

children.text: yā vā śrīr adhigamyate paravadhavyāsaṅgadagdhātmanā
children.translated_text: What prosperity is gained by one whose soul is burned by involvement in killing others —

children.text: tāṃ vāñched bhramaropagītakusumāṃ ko vadhyamālām iva |
children.translated_text: Who would desire it — like a garland of execution, humming with bees, made of flowers?

children.text: yo 'pi svārhanibandhanapraṇayinā saṃprasthito vartmanā
children.translated_text: I, who have set out on the path that delights in the bond of what is fitting for oneself,

children.text: prāg eva vyasanāturasya jagato yo 'haṃ hitāyodyataḥ || GoSd_13 ||
children.translated_text: all the more [should welcome this] — I who am exerted for the welfare of the world, tormented by calamity. || GoSd 13 ||

children.text: api ca
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: rājye 'paro yadi mama praṇayaṃ karoti pūjyo mayā nanu viśeṣata eva rājā |
children.translated_text: If another has affection for my kingdom, is not a king especially to be honored by me?

children.text: rājyāśrayaṃ khalu parārtham ahaṃ bibharmi saṃkleśabhāram imam āyataduḥkhahetum || GoSd_14 ||
children.translated_text: For I bear this burden of affliction that is the kingdom, dependent on its framework, for the sake of others — the cause of prolonged suffering. || GoSd 14 ||

children.text: atithir iva yato 'yaṃ mānanīyo narendro madupahitavibhūtiprārthanākṛṣṭacetāḥ |
children.translated_text: Since this king is to be honored like a guest — his mind drawn by the desire for the riches I have bestowed —

children.text: upacitakuśalatvāc cānukampāviśeṣāt suta iva vinayārthaṃ ko 'tra kopāvakāśaḥ || GoSd_15 ||
children.translated_text: and since, through accumulated merit and a special compassion, [he is to be treated] like a son, for the purpose of discipline — where here is any occasion for anger? || GoSd 15 ||

children.text: unmocayaty eva balāc ca yo māṃ rājyābhidhānād vyasanapratānāt |
children.translated_text: He who forcibly liberates me from the spreading vine of calamity called kingship —

children.text: yady atra kuryāṃ manasaḥ prakopaṃ pāpo 'paraḥ ko 'tha mayā samaḥ syāt || GoSd_16 ||
children.translated_text: if I were to become angry at this, what other sinner would be my equal? || GoSd 16 ||

children.text: rājyasya doṣāvayave niveśaṃ prakhyāpayan hanti yaśaḥsukhāni |
children.translated_text: The king, proclaiming a dwelling in the defective aspect of kingship, destroys the pleasures of fame;

children.text: mām arthataḥ śikṣayate narendro rājyābhidhāne tamasi bhramantam || GoSd_17 ||
children.translated_text: he in truth instructs me, who wander in the darkness called kingship. || GoSd 17 ||

children.text: tyaktavyam etena ca kāraṇena kṣitīśvaraśrīsukham ātmakāmaiḥ |
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, the happiness and glory of sovereignty should be abandoned by those who seek their own [spiritual] good;

children.text: yad atra saktasya janasya vairabhayaprasaṅgāḥ śirasi sphuranti || GoSd_18 ||
children.translated_text: for upon one attached to it, the occasions of enmity and fear hover over the head. || GoSd 18 ||

children.text: yo vāham utsṛjya tapovanāni nirantarāyāṇy abhitaḥ śivāni |
children.translated_text: Or I who, abandoning the ascetic groves — auspicious on all sides, free from obstacles —

children.text: gṛhābhidhānaṃ bhayam āvasāmi nārhāmi nāhaṃ vyasanāny amūni || GoSd_19 ||
children.translated_text: dwell in the fear called the household — I am not worthy of [escaping] these calamities. || GoSd 19 ||

children.text: tat svastirājyadyutivistarebhyo naikavyalīkāśrayadāruṇebhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, farewell to the splendid displays of royal glory, terrible as the refuge of manifold deceptions;

children.text: yāsyāmi śāntāni vanāny ato 'haṃ vivekajaprītinibandhanāni || GoSd_20 ||
children.translated_text: I shall go from here to the peaceful forests, the basis of the joy born of solitude. || GoSd 20 ||

children.text: kalyāṇamitraṃ yata eva rājā mamādya naiṣkramyasukhodayāya |
children.translated_text: Since this king is my spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) for the arising of the happiness of renunciation today,

children.text: kalyāṇam evāstv anayo 'py ato 'sya sabandhumitrasya śaracchatāni || GoSd_21 ||
children.translated_text: may well-being alone attend him too, along with his kinsmen and friends, for hundreds of autumns — even though this is [technically] misconduct. || GoSd 21 ||

children.text: mā gā garvaṃ mahimnaḥ kṣitipatir aham ity ujjhyatāṃ vipralambhaḥ
children.translated_text: Do not be proud, [thinking] 'I am a king of greatness' — let that delusion be abandoned!

children.text: pratyāsannopatāpām anuvahasi vṛthā bhaṅginīṃ kiṃ nayājñām |
children.translated_text: Why do you bear in vain this royal command — perishable, with imminent suffering?

children.text: rājyaṃ tyaktavyam eva vyasanaparigataṃ nātyajas tvaṃ kimarthaṃ
children.translated_text: The kingdom, encompassed by calamity, must certainly be abandoned — why do you not let go?

children.text: śaṅke daurjanyam itthaṃ mama nṛpatir ayaṃ kṣāpayiṣyaty ayatnaḥ || GoSd_22 ||
children.translated_text: I suspect that this king will effortlessly dispel my wickedness in this way. || GoSd 22 ||

children.text: kadā tyaktvā gehaṃ kukṛtaśatasaṃbādhavirasaṃ
children.translated_text: When shall I abandon this household — repugnant, crowded with hundreds of evil deeds —

children.text: vane vatsyāmīti praśamasukhasaṃbhogasubhage |
children.translated_text: and dwell in the forest, delightful with the enjoyment of the bliss of tranquility?

children.text: vitarkā ye bhūtāḥ suciram anubaddhā mama mateḥ
children.translated_text: Those reflections that were long attached to my mind —

children.text: prasiddhās te diṣṭyā kṣitipatim imaṃ prāpya na cirāt || GoSd_23 ||
children.translated_text: fortunately, they are realized now, not long after encountering this king. || GoSd 23 ||

children.text: iti viniścitya bodhisattvo janmāntarābhyastanaiṣkramyasukhābhyudayaparicayo mṛga iva vāgurāvarodhanirgamopalambhodbhūtapramodaḥ samapanītarājyaśrīsūcakālaṃkāravibhramakāyabhāralaghuviviktavigrahaḥ parair aparijñātatapovanagamanaprayojanaḥ saṃrūḍhapraṇayaviśrambhasnehabahumānaniratyayaṃ ca bandhuvargaṃ svapuṇyabalāvaṣṭambhopanatasukhopabhogyāṃ ca rājalakṣmīṃ paryuṣitopabhogamalinamlānakusumabandhanām iva srajaṃ parityajyānytamad viviktam āśramapadam alaṃcakāra |
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — familiar from former lives with the arising of the happiness of renunciation — like a deer that has found escape from a net-trap and thereby felt great joy, his body lightened by the removal of the weight of the ornaments that signified royal glory, his frame detached and unencumbered, his purpose of going to the ascetic grove unrecognized by others, abandoning his circle of kinsmen — toward whom his tender affection, trust, love, and respect had grown without end — and the royal fortune that was fit for the enjoyment of happiness acquired through the support of his own merit — discarding it like a garland of withered flowers whose enjoyment had staled and become soiled — adorned a certain secluded hermitage.

children.text: āhūyamāna iva pallavināṃ drumāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: As if being called by the branch-arms of flowering trees,

children.text: śākhākaraiḥ svakusumābharaṇābhirāmaiḥ |
children.translated_text: lovely with their own adornments of blossoms,

children.text: śāntaṃ vanāntam upagamya sa bodhisattvaḥ
children.translated_text: that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having reached the peaceful forest's edge,

children.text: prāpto 'mṛtaṃ nṛpasukhair anavāptapūrvam || GoSd_24 ||
