children.translated_text: attained an immortality never before obtained through royal pleasures. || GoSd 24 ||

children.text: yāny eva śokaparidevamukhāni loke kāmātmanām anucitopaśamotsavānām |
children.translated_text: The very things in the world that are occasions for grief and lamentation among those devoted to desires, unaccustomed to the festivals of tranquility —

children.text: tāny eva nāma dadhati praśamapriyāṇāṃ prītiṃ nirāmiṣasukhapraṇayānavadyām || GoSd_25 ||
children.translated_text: those very things bestow upon the lovers of peace a blameless joy, arising from the love of unworldly happiness. || GoSd 25 ||

children.text: puṣpādhivāsaśucibhiḥ sa vanāntavātaiḥ
children.translated_text: Fanned by forest-edge breezes, pure with the fragrance of flowers,

children.text: saṃvījitaḥ prativinodya śarīrakhedam |
children.translated_text: dispelling the weariness of the body,

children.text: dhyātvā pramādamalināṃ manujendralakṣmīṃ
children.translated_text: contemplating the royal fortune soiled by the stain of heedlessness,

children.text: saṃvegam eva manasi kṣitipaḥ pupoṣa || GoSd_26 ||
children.translated_text: the king nourished in his mind only spiritual urgency. || GoSd 26 ||

children.text: kṛtvā namaḥ sa bhuvanatrayaśaṅkarebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions,

children.text: sarvātmanā daśasu dikṣu tathāgatebhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: the causes of trembling for the three worlds, with his entire being,

children.text: amlānaśādvalakuthāparibhogaramye
children.translated_text: upon a delightful carpet of unfading green grass

children.text: mūle taroḥ kṣitipatir niṣasāda madhye || GoSd_27 ||
children.translated_text: the king sat down at the foot of a tree, in the center. || GoSd 27 ||

children.text: sa khedito 'ntaḥpurasundarīṇāṃ saṃkleśapakṣānuguṇair vilāsaiḥ |
children.translated_text: He, who had been wearied by the charms of the inner-palace beauties — charms that followed the side of affliction —

children.text: viviktasaṃbhogasukhāny araṇyāny ālokya viśrānta iva kṣitīśaḥ || GoSd_28 ||
children.translated_text: looking upon the forests — the enjoyment of solitary happiness — rested, as it were, that lord of the earth. || GoSd 28 ||

children.text: parisravannirjharavāridhārāprakṣālitaśyāmaśilātalāni |
children.translated_text: Gazing at the slopes of mountains, with their dark rock-surfaces

children.text: sānūni paśyan sa mahīdharāṇām ayatnaramyāṇi mudaṃ jagāma || GoSd_29 ||
children.translated_text: washed by streams of cascading waterfall-waters, effortlessly beautiful, he felt delight. || GoSd 29 ||

children.text: āliṅgitān puṣpabharālasābhiḥ snehād iva prāṇasamāṃl latābhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Beholding the great trees, blue-green with abundant foliage,

children.text: mahīruhān bhūripalāśanīlān ālokya reme sa mahīmahendraḥ || GoSd_30 ||
children.translated_text: embraced as if in affection by creepers as dear as life, languid with the weight of blossoms — that great sovereign of the earth rejoiced. || GoSd 30 ||

children.text: akarkaśaśyāmakaśerukāṇi bhramaddvirephāhatapuṣkarāṇi |
children.translated_text: Gazing at the lakes, whose <s>śeruka</s> (lotus-stalks) were smooth and dark,

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇaḥ sa nṛpo 'bhireme sarāṃsi pāṭhīnakulākulāni || GoSd_31 ||
children.translated_text: whose lotuses were struck by wandering bees, and teeming with schools of <s>pāṭhīna</s> fish — that king delighted. || GoSd 31 ||

children.text: vivekajaprītisukhānukūlāṃ nisargaramyāṃ sa vanāntabhūmim |
children.translated_text: Looking upon that forest-edge land, naturally lovely,

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇaḥ kṣitipaḥ praharṣaṃ jagāma saṃśāntamanovikāraḥ || GoSd_32 ||
children.translated_text: conducive to the joy-and-happiness born of solitude — that king experienced elation, his mental agitation calmed. || GoSd 32 ||

children.text: udīkṣya saṃsaktaśikhaṇḍikekāmano'bhirāmāṇi sa kānanāni |
children.translated_text: Gazing upon the forest-groves, delightful to the mind, with peacocks dancing and crying out together,

children.text: anekasaṃkleśaviṣopadagdhāṃ nṛpaśriyaṃ bhūmipatir jagarhe || GoSd_33 ||
children.translated_text: the lord of the earth reproached the royal fortune, burnt by the poison of manifold afflictions. || GoSd 33 ||

children.text: kvāsau viparyāsasukhābhimānaprasaṅgajihmā kṣitipālalakṣmīḥ |
children.translated_text: Where is that royal fortune — crooked with the occasion of the conceit of false happiness?

children.text: kva caiva cetovinibandhanāni śāntāny araṇyāśrayiṇāṃ sukhāni || GoSd_34 ||
children.translated_text: And where are the peaceful pleasures of those who dwell in the forest, the bonds of the mind? || GoSd 34 ||

children.text: anartharāgāśrayadūṣitāya namo 'stu tasmai kṣayiṇe sukhāya |
children.translated_text: Homage to that perishable happiness — corrupted by being the refuge of the passion for misfortune;

children.text: viṣajya yasmin manasaḥ pravṛttiṃ kṛpāspadatvaṃ viduṣāṃ vrajanti || GoSd_35 ||
children.translated_text: relying upon which, those who set their minds in motion become objects of compassion for the wise. || GoSd 35 ||

children.text: avanataśikhair vānīrāṇāṃ drumais taṭarohibhiḥ
children.translated_text: With cane-trees along the banks, their tops bowing,

children.text: kṛtaparikaraśrīsaṃbhogāḥ praśāntarayoddhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: enjoying the glory of an ornamental girdle, with peaceful hues,

children.text: haritapulināḥ śaṣpodbhedair jharaiḥ saritaḥ śivāḥ
children.translated_text: rivers — auspicious with green sands sprouting grass, and with cascades —

children.text: kṣititalapatiḥ paśyaṃl lebhe ratiṃ sa nirāmiṣām || GoSd_36 ||
children.translated_text: the lord of the earth, seeing them, found unworldly delight. || GoSd 36 ||

children.text: vitathaviṣayakrodhābhyāsaprayogamalīmasaṃ
children.translated_text: The heart of the wicked — soiled by the practice of false sense-objects and anger —

children.text: hṛdayam asatāṃ śānte 'raṇye ratiṃ katham eṣyati |
children.translated_text: how can it find delight in the peaceful forest?

children.text: sa tu narapatir gotrotkarṣaprabhāvaparigrahād
children.translated_text: But that king, by the power of the embrace of his lineage's excellence,

children.text: viṣayavimukhaḥ prītiṃ bheje parāṃ vijane vane || GoSd_37 ||
children.translated_text: averse to sense-objects, found supreme joy in the secluded forest. || GoSd 37 ||

children.text: prakṛticapalā naikāpāyā nirantaradāruṇā
children.translated_text: Riches — fickle by nature, leading to many downfalls, ceaselessly terrible —

children.text: na khalu hṛdayaṃ no jñānārthaṃ haranti vibhūtayaḥ |
children.translated_text: do not steal the heart, nor [the pursuit of] meaning, for those

children.text: apagatamanaḥsaṃkṣobhāṇāṃ vanāntam upeyuṣāṃ
children.translated_text: who have reached the forest-edge, free from the agitation of mind;

children.text: bhavati tu satāṃ pūrvābhyāsān matiḥ praguṇā śubhe || GoSd_38 ||
children.translated_text: rather, through prior practice, their disposition becomes straight and inclined toward the good. || GoSd 38 ||

children.text: hariṇacaraṇakṣuṇṇopāntāḥ saśādvalanirjharāḥ
children.translated_text: With borders worn by the hooves of deer, with green-grass cascades,

children.text: kusumaśabalair viśvākhātais taraṅgitapādapāḥ |
children.translated_text: with trees set in motion by variegated breezes fragrant with flowers,

children.text: muditavihagaśreṇīcitradhvanipratināditā
children.translated_text: echoing with the colorful sounds of joyful rows of birds —

children.text: manasi na mudaṃ kasyādadhyuḥ śivā vanarājayaḥ || GoSd_39 ||
children.translated_text: in whose mind would these auspicious forest-kingdoms not produce delight? || GoSd 39 ||

children.text: praśamavidhure nityodvegaprade gṛhacārake
children.translated_text: In the household prison — devoid of tranquility, ever producing anxiety,

children.text: viṣayamarutā vyādhūtānāṃ hatopaniṣatsukham |
children.translated_text: the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> happiness of those blown about by the wind of sense-objects is destroyed;

children.text: uparatajanakṣobhāyāsaprakāmasukhe vane
children.translated_text: but in the forest — where the agitation and weariness of people have ceased, where happiness abounds freely —

children.text: vrajati tu manaḥ sadyaḥ śāntiṃ kukāryasamākulam || GoSd_40 ||
children.translated_text: the mind, entangled by evil deeds, immediately attains peace. || GoSd 40 ||

children.text: athānyatamo brāhmaṇo dāridryaduḥkhābhyāhatas tatpratīkāracikīrṣayā mandotsāho 'pi bodhisattvam ekam ārtāyanam avagamya tadviṣayāntam upagacchan mārgaparibhraṃśaparyākulātmā tatas tataḥ paribhraman kṣudduḥkhopaglapitatanur adhvaklamaviklavāvidheyagurutaracaraṇavigrahas tad āśramapadam āsasāda | dṛṣṭvā cainaṃ bodhisattvaś cirābhyāgatasnigdhabāndhavasnehātiriktavātsalyapeśalayā pibann iva dṛṣṭyā pratyudgamyābhivādya ca kṛtapratisaṃmodanam āgamanaprayojanaṃ paryapṛcchat | brāhmaṇo 'bravīt |
children.translated_text: Then a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, struck by the suffering of poverty, wishing to find a remedy for it, though of feeble spirits, having learned that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was a sole refuge for the afflicted, proceeded toward his territory. Wandering here and there with a mind distracted by losing his way, his body wasting from the suffering of hunger, his steps heavy and unsteady from the weariness of travel — he reached that hermitage. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing him, drinking in the sight as it were with a tenderness sweeter than the affection of a kinsman long absent, rising to greet and welcome him and having exchanged pleasantries, asked him the purpose of his coming. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said:

children.text: yaḥ sarvado nāma bhuvi prasiddho yathārthanāmā naralokapālaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is famed on earth as the 'All-Giver' — the guardian of the world of men whose name befits [his nature] —

children.text: kīrtyā samāhūta ivāsmi tasya prāptas tam ārtāyanam īkṣamāṇaḥ || GoSd_41 ||
children.translated_text: summoned as it were by his fame, I have come, seeking that refuge for the afflicted. || GoSd 41 ||

children.text: trātā sa eva vyasanāturāṇāṃ vanīpakānāṃ sa ca bandhur ekaḥ |
children.translated_text: He alone is the savior of those stricken by calamity, he alone is the kinsman of the destitute;

children.text: tam eva caikaṃ vyapadiśya sādhum anyatra maunavratam eti vāṇī || GoSd_42 ||
children.translated_text: pointing to him alone as the good man, speech takes a vow of silence regarding all others. || GoSd 42 ||

children.text: tat tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā sa kṛpāpeśalāśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing those words, he, of compassion-tender disposition,

children.text: ācakampe mahāsattvas tadduḥkhapavanāhataḥ || GoSd_43 ||
children.translated_text: that great being trembled, struck by the wind of that man's suffering. || GoSd 43 ||

children.text: atha sa mahātmā dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niśvasya taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ provāca |
children.translated_text: Then that great soul, having breathed a long, warm sigh, said to that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>:

children.text: upāyaś cintyatām anyo dvija duḥkhopaśāntaye |
children.translated_text: Think of some other means, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, for the alleviation of your suffering;

children.text: bhraṣṭaiśvaryaḥ sa bhūpālas tapase vanam āśritaḥ || GoSd_44 ||
children.translated_text: that king, having lost his sovereignty, has resorted to the forest for austerity. || GoSd 44 ||

children.text: atha sa brāhmaṇaḥ samīhitārthapratyāśāpraṇayabhaṅgadainyākrāntamānasaḥ sahasā pṛthivyāṃ nipapāta paraṃ ca saṃmoham upajagāma |
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, his mind seized by the wretchedness of the breaking of his hope and its affectionate expectation of the desired goal, fell suddenly to the ground and was overcome by a deep swoon.

children.text: āśāparyastadhairyāṇi hṛdayāni prasaṅginām |
children.translated_text: The hearts of those who are attached, their fortitude overthrown by hope,

children.text: dehināṃ moham āyānti hetunā yena kena cit || GoSd_45 ||
children.translated_text: fall into delusion by one cause or another. || GoSd 45 ||

children.text: atha bodhisattvas taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ śītābhir adbhiḥ pariṣiñcya pratilabdhasaṃjñaṃ samāśvāsayann abravīt |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having sprinkled that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> with cool water and reviving his consciousness, consoling him, said:

children.text: asty anyo 'pi pratīkāro bhavadāśāsamṛddhaye |
children.translated_text: There is yet another remedy for the fulfillment of your hope;

children.text: ahaṃ sarvaṃdado rājā mā śucas tvam iha dvija || GoSd_46 ||
children.translated_text: I am King <s>Sarvadada</s> (the All-Giver) — do not grieve here, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || GoSd 46 ||

children.text: sarvaṃdado nāma kathaṃ kadā vā yasya svadehe 'pi manaḥprasaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: How and when will one called 'All-Giver,' who has no attachment even to his own body, [fulfill his name]?

children.text: yathārthanāmā tv adhunā bhaviṣyāmy ahaṃ tvadabhyāgamanotsavena || GoSd_47 ||
children.translated_text: But now I shall become true to my name, by the festive occasion of your arrival. || GoSd 47 ||

children.text: madrājyapraṇayī rājā māṃ samanveṣate kila |
children.translated_text: A king who covets my kingdom is reportedly searching for me;

children.text: baddhvā māṃ dehy atas tasmai sa tvāṃ samtoṣayiṣyati || GoSd_48 ||
children.translated_text: bind me and hand me over to him — he will satisfy you. || GoSd 48 ||

children.text: anekaduḥkhopanipātakātaraś cirasya tāvad bhavadāśrayād ayam |
children.translated_text: Tormented by the onset of many sufferings, after a long time at last — by taking refuge in you —

children.text: mamopayogaṃ guṇapakṣasiddhaye śarīrasaṃjñaḥ kalir adya yāsyati || GoSd_49 ||
children.translated_text: this discord called the body shall today go to its use for me, for the perfection of the side of virtue. || GoSd 49 ||

children.text: jarārujāmṛtyukhalūrikām imāṃ tanuṃ samāśritya sa hanta yo 'dya me |
children.translated_text: Alas, may this body — resorting to this form, a threshing-floor of old age, disease, and death —

children.text: manoratho brāhmaṇamukhya pūryatāṃ tava prabhāvād abhivāñchitaś ciram || GoSd_50 ||
children.translated_text: may that long-cherished wish of mine be fulfilled today, O chief of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, through your power! || GoSd 50 ||

children.text: prītir nṛpasya tava cārthaviśeṣasiddhiḥ saṃpatsyate mama ca pāramitāprakarṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: The king's delight, and the accomplishment of your special purpose, and the excellence of my <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) will all be achieved;

children.text: ekaṃ śarīram atisṛjya vipatparītaṃ paśyotsavātiśayam āpatitaṃ krameṇa || GoSd_51 ||
children.translated_text: by relinquishing this one body, beset by misfortune — behold the surpassing festival that arrives in sequence! || GoSd 51 ||

children.text: evaṃvidhe 'tithijanapraṇayābhidhāne prītyāgame
ca
children.translated_text: -ful

children.text: mama kāryasamṛddhihetau |
children.translated_text: arrival that is the cause of the fulfillment of my purpose,

children.text: dehe kṛtāntamakarāsyapuṭātithau ca naikopasargavihite vidhir asti ko 'nyaḥ || GoSd_52 ||
children.translated_text: and in this body — a guest in the jaws of the crocodile of Death, beset by manifold afflictions — what other course is there? || GoSd 52 ||
In such a declaration of love by a guest, and in the joy-

children.text: kāyād asārād aham adya sāraṃ bhavantam āsādya samujjihīrṣuḥ |
children.translated_text: I, wishing today to extract the essence from this essenceless body, having encountered you —

children.text: manorathaṃ tat saphalaṃ kuruṣva tvam adya me vipra cirānubaddham || GoSd_53 ||
children.translated_text: fulfill this wish of mine, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — long attached [to my mind] — make it fruitful today! || GoSd 53 ||

children.text: evam astv iti pāpātmā pratiśuśrāva sa dvijaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'So be it,' agreed that sinful-souled <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: atikramyāryamaryādāṃ lobhopahatamānasaḥ || GoSd_54 ||
children.translated_text: transgressing the bounds of noble conduct, his mind corrupted by greed. || GoSd 54 ||

children.text: koṭarāntargatavyālaviṣād apy atidāruṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: For those scorched by sense-objects — more terrible even than the venom of a snake hidden in a tree-hollow —

children.text: viṣayair upataptānāṃ pāpaṃ kiṃ nāma duṣkaram || GoSd_55 ||
children.translated_text: what sin is indeed difficult [to commit]? || GoSd 55 ||

children.text: ekaḥ parārthaṃ pradadau svadehaṃ samādade 'nyaḥ param ātmahetoḥ |
children.translated_text: One gave his own body for the sake of others; the other seized another [person] for his own sake;

children.text: aho vikṛṣṭaṃ caritaṃ narāṇāṃ guṇeṣu doṣeṣu ca sādarāṇām || GoSd_56 ||
children.translated_text: ah, how divergent is the conduct of people — devoted respectively to virtues and to vices! || GoSd 56 ||

children.text: taṃ bodhisattvaṃ vinibadhya gāḍhaṃ paścādbhujaṃ cauram iva dvijātiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having bound that <s>Bodhisattva</s> tightly, arms behind his back, as if a thief, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>

children.text: samācakarṣa prakṛtipragalbho nivāryamāṇo vanadevatābhiḥ || GoSd_57 ||
children.translated_text: dragged him off, bold by nature, even though restrained by the forest deities. || GoSd 57 ||

children.text: sākṣād ayaṃ dharma ivāvatīrṇaḥ praśāntavākkāyamanovikāraḥ |
children.translated_text: This one, descended as if <s>Dharma</s> itself in bodily form, with speech, body, and mind-movements pacified —

children.text: dvijādhamenāvinayāvalepakrūreṇa kaṣṭaṃ hriyate maharṣiḥ || GoSd_58 ||
children.translated_text: alas, this great sage is being dragged away by the worst of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, cruel with the arrogance of indiscipline. || GoSd 58 ||

children.text: amī rudantīva vilolapallavāḥ praśastapuṣpāśrumukhā mahīruhāḥ |
children.translated_text: These trees, with trembling leaves, seem to weep, their faces [adorned] with flowers like praiseworthy tears,

children.text: caladdvirephadhvanidīnanisvanā viyujyamānā muninā sumedhasā || GoSd_59 ||
children.translated_text: with sounds made doleful by the buzzing of swaying bees — being separated from the sage <s>Sumedhā</s>. // GoSd 59 //

children.text: sudurlabham darśanam asya sarvathā vilocanaprītikarasya dehinām |
children.translated_text: 'His sight, which gives delight to the eyes of all embodied beings, will be extremely hard to obtain' —

children.text: vilepur ity udgataśokakātarāḥ pragāḍhaśokā munayo vanaukasaḥ || GoSd_60 ||
children.translated_text: thus lamented the sages dwelling in the forest, distressed with arising grief, overwhelmed with deep sorrow. // GoSd 60 //

children.text: ādāya vipro 'tha tam āryasattvaṃ niḥsādhvasānākuladhīraceṣṭam |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, seizing that noble-souled one, whose actions were fearless and composed despite disturbance,

children.text: praveśayām āsa puraṃ sa yasmin mahīpatis tṣṭhati tatsapatnaḥ || GoSd_61 ||
children.translated_text: brought him into the city where the rival king resided. // GoSd 61 //

children.text: yam adrākṣur netraiḥ purayuvatayaḥ snehavikacair
children.translated_text: He whom the young women of the city once beheld with eyes blossoming with affection —

children.text: gajaskandhārūḍhaṃ patim iva surāṇāṃ narapatim |
children.translated_text: riding an elephant's shoulder, like the lord of the gods — that very king,

children.text: tam evāpaśyaṃs tāḥ paravaśagataṃ valkaladharaṃ
children.translated_text: they now saw — gone under another's power, clad in bark-garments —

children.text: mukhaiḥ śokāyāsastimitagurupakṣmāntanayanaiḥ || GoSd_62 ||
children.translated_text: with faces whose heavy-fringed eyes were stilled by the torpor of grief and anguish. // GoSd 62 //

children.text: taṃ mattavāraṇagatiṃ kanakāvadātaṃ
children.translated_text: Him — of the gait of a rutting elephant, golden-bright,

children.text: prāṃśuṃ sumerum iva lakṣaṇaratnacitram |
children.translated_text: tall, like Mount <s>Sumeru</s> studded with the gems of auspicious marks —

children.text: cīrāmbaraṃ vṛjinadīrghajaṭākalāpaṃ
children.translated_text: seeing him in bark-garments, with long matted locks [formed by] penance,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā nṛpo ripur adhīratayā cakampe || GoSd_63 ||
children.translated_text: the rival king trembled with agitation. // GoSd 63 //

children.text: tathābhūtaṃ cainam avekṣya sādhvasākulitamatiś cintayām āsa |
children.translated_text: And seeing him in that state, his mind agitated with alarm, he thought:

children.text: ko nv eṣa kāñcanaśilātalacāruvakṣāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Who is this one, with a chest beautiful as a surface of golden rock,

children.text: kṣāmodaro bhujagabhogavilambibāhuḥ |
children.translated_text: with a lean belly, with arms dangling like the coils of a serpent?

children.text: pratyādiśann iva kukāryasamākulaṃ māṃ
children.translated_text: As if rebuking me, overwhelmed with base deeds,

children.text: prāpto yuvāpi vinayapratipattidhīraḥ || GoSd_64 ||
children.translated_text: he has arrived — a youth, yet steady in the practice of self-discipline.' // GoSd 64 //

children.text:
dharmo 'vatīrṇa iva vigrahavān kuto 'yam
ālambavalkaladharo nayanābhirāmaḥ |
baddhaś ca nāma ca
na
children.translated_text: [he is]

children.text: dainyaviṣādavaśyas
children.translated_text: not subject to the wretchedness and despair;

children.text: tejonidhiḥ praśamam udgiratīva cāyam || GoSd_65 ||
children.translated_text: this treasury of splendor seems to emanate tranquility.' // GoSd 65 //
'Whence has this one come — <s>Dharma</s> descended in bodily form, as it were, wearing bark-cloth, delightful to the eye? Though bound, and though [bearing] a name [of captivity],

children.text: atha sa brāhmaṇādhamas taṃ rājānam abravīt | jayatu jayatu mahārājo diṣṭyā vardhase | yo 'sau tava pratyanīko rājā kenāpi prayojanenāraṇyam anupraviśya tāpasanepathyāvacchādito daurātmyaṃ kim apy ārebhe | sa eṣa mayā balātkāraṃ tvatpriyacikīrṣayā baddhvā mīna iva sphurann ānītas tad atra devaḥ pramāṇam iti | atha sa rājā tat tasya pāpakarmaṇaḥ karmāsaṃbhāvayann avocad enam | mā tāvad bhoḥ |
children.translated_text: Then that vilest of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> addressed the king: 'Victory, victory to the great king! May you prosper! That rival king of yours — having entered the forest for some purpose and disguised in the garb of an ascetic — commenced some villainy. He has been forcibly seized by me, desiring to please you, and brought here, quivering like a fish. Let your majesty decide in this matter.' Then the king, not believing that [this was] the deed of that evil-doer, addressed him: 'Not so, sir!'

children.text: jetuṃ sāgaramekhalāṃ vasumatīṃ bāhudvitīyo 'py ayaṃ
children.translated_text: 'This one is capable of conquering the ocean-girdled earth, with his arms alone as his second,

children.text: śaktaḥ śaktimatāṃ varaḥ karikaravyālambibāhudrumaḥ |
children.translated_text: the best among the mighty, his arm-trees dangling like an elephant's trunk;

children.text: tvaṃ śakto 'sya parābhavaṃ katham are kartuṃ bṛhadvakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: how, O wretch, could you be capable of humiliating this broad-chested one?

children.text: tat tvaṃ brūhi parābhavanti na mṛgāḥ siṃhaṃ sphuratkesaram || GoSd_66 ||
children.translated_text: Tell me then: do deer overpower a lion with bristling mane?' // GoSd 66 //

children.text: sa tasmai rājñe yathābhūtam āviścakāra | dhik tvām iti ca nirbhartsitaḥ kopakaluṣayā dṛṣṭyā tena rājñā parāṃ vrīḍām āpannaḥ | svayam eva vimucya bandhanāni kṣitipaḥ so 'tha yathāsukhaṃ nṛparṣim upaveśya tam āsane mahārhe bahumānānatavigraho jagāda |
children.translated_text: He revealed to the king what had truly happened. Rebuked with 'Shame on you!' and [struck] by the angry gaze of that king, he fell into extreme shame. The king himself then, releasing the bonds, having comfortably seated that royal sage on a magnificent seat, his body bowed with great respect, spoke:

children.text: guṇabhaktitayātimānuṣaṃ te nṛpa karmātiśayāvadānam etat |
children.translated_text: 'This deed of yours, O king, surpassing human [capacity] through devotion to virtue, is most exalted;

children.text: prathayanti surāsurapradhānā bahumānaślatham ānataiḥ śirobhiḥ || GoSd_67 ||
children.translated_text: the foremost among gods and demons proclaim it with heads bowed in reverence.' // GoSd 67 //

children.text: yadi rañjayituṃ prajāḥ samartho nṛpa rājety abhidhānasaṃniveśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'If a king is one who is able to delight his subjects — such is the import of the name "king" (<s>rājan</s>);

children.text: guṇaratnanidhe tvam eva rājā viguṇo rañjayituṃ jagan na śaktaḥ || GoSd_68 ||
children.translated_text: then you alone, O treasury of virtue-gems, are the king — one devoid of virtues cannot delight the world.' // GoSd 68 //

children.text: anuśādhi yathā purā puraṃ svaṃ vayam ājñāpravaṇā bhavadvidhānām |
children.translated_text: 'Rule your own city as before; we are obedient to the commands of those like you;

children.text: vinayād vyasanaṃ ca naḥ kṣamethāḥ skhalati proṣitalocanaḥ same 'pi || GoSd_69 ||
children.translated_text: and by your graciousness, forgive our offense — even on level ground, one whose sight has departed stumbles.' // GoSd 69 //

children.text: jātaprasādam atha taṃ nṛpatiṃ viditvā pātrīkṛtaṃ sucaritasya sa bodhisattvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing that king to have attained grace and become a worthy vessel of good conduct,

children.text: śiṣyaṃ vinītam iva gauravabhāranamraṃ provāca nīlajaladastanayitnughoṣaḥ || GoSd_70 ||
children.translated_text: addressed him — bowed with the weight of reverence like a disciplined student — with a voice deep as the thundering of a dark cloud: // GoSd 70 //

children.text: āyur nṛṇām acirakālavināśi tāvat taptopalodaraniṣikta ivāmbubinduḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The life of mortals is subject to swift destruction — like a water-drop poured on the surface of a heated stone;

children.text: saṅgāḥ priyaiḥ saha sadaiva viyogatiktāḥ saṃpattayo vipariṇāmaviṣāviṣahyāḥ || GoSd_71 ||
children.translated_text: associations with loved ones are always bitter with [the prospect of] separation; prosperities are unbearable with the poison of change.' // GoSd 71 //

children.text: kāmā muhūrtavitathābhiniveśarāmāḥ kiṃpākapādapaphalapratimopabhogāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Pleasures are delightful only in momentary, false attachment, their enjoyment resembling the fruit of the <s>kimpāka</s> (poison tree);

children.text: naikāntarāyavirasaṃ sabhayaṃ savairaṃ rājyaṃ pramādavadhabandhanimittabhūtam || GoSd_72 ||
children.translated_text: kingship, insipid with manifold dangers, fearful, full of enmity, is the cause of heedlessness, killing, and imprisonment.' // GoSd 72 //

children.text: tasmād vipākamadhurāṇi kuruṣva nityaṃ karmāṇi sajjanamanovinibandhanāni |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, always perform deeds whose fruition is sweet, which bind the minds of good people;

children.text: śokāśrukātaramukhās tu vipākakāle yeṣāṃ bhavanti puruṣāḥ prajahīhi tāni || GoSd_73 ||
children.translated_text: and abandon those at whose time of fruition men's faces become anguished with tears of sorrow.' // GoSd 73 //

children.text: nārtho rājyasukhaiḥ punar mama calai riktair anāśvāsikair
children.translated_text: 'I have no need of the pleasures of kingship — fickle, empty, offering no solace,

children.text: vairāyāsaviṣādadainyakalahadvāraiḥ parapratyayaiḥ |
children.translated_text: whose doorways are enmity, distress, despair, wretchedness, and quarrel — dependent on others.',

children.text: utkaṇṭhāṃ janayanti me kṣitidharāḥ saṃsaktadhārādharāḥ
children.translated_text: 'The mountains with their attached streams of rain-clouds,

children.text: puṣpālambakadambapādapavanaśyāmopakaṇṭhāḥ śivāḥ || GoSd_74 ||
children.translated_text: with their vicinity darkened by the groves of flower-laden <s>kadamba</s> trees, auspicious — they awaken longing in me.' // GoSd 74 //

children.text: hariṇakulaviluptasnigdhaśaṣpottarīyā nipatitasitapuṣpā dyaur ivālakṣyatārā |
children.translated_text: 'The forest floor, with its smooth grass-covering browsed upon by herds of deer, with fallen white flowers — like a sky with barely visible stars —

children.text: apaharati balān me mānasaṃ kānanāntakṣitir uparatarājyaprārthanāvipralambham || GoSd_75 ||
children.translated_text: forcibly steals my mind, free from the deception of craving for kingship.' // GoSd 75 //

children.text: sthiravanagamanāśayaṃ viditvā nṛpatir asāv atha taṃ viśuddhasattvam |
children.translated_text: Then the king, perceiving his firm intention to go to the forest, [seeing] that pure-souled one,

children.text: apahṛtahṛdayo guṇais tadiyair vanagamanābhimukhaḥ kilāvatasthe || GoSd_76 ||
children.translated_text: his heart captivated by his virtues — it is said he was on the verge of departing for the forest himself. // GoSd 76 //

children.text: avagamitamanāś ca bodhisattvaḥ kṣitipatinā vinayānatena tena |
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, understanding [the king's] mind — that king bowed low in humility,

children.text: uparataviṣayaspṛho 'pi ceto vanagamanād vinivartayāṃ babhūva || GoSd_77 ||
children.translated_text: though himself free from desire for sense-pleasures — turned his mind away from going to the forest. // GoSd 77 //

children.text: vana iva bhavane 'pi bodhisattvā viṣayasukhavyasanāparītasattvāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, whose being is uncorrupted by the addiction to sensory pleasures,

children.text: munaya iva vanāntavāsanimnāḥ praśamarasaikavihāriṇo bhavanti || GoSd_78 ||
children.translated_text: dwell exclusively in the delight of tranquility — like sages inclined to forest-dwelling — even in a palace as in a forest. // GoSd 78 //

children.text: bhavana iva vane 'pi sādhavas te jagadudayaikanibandhanaprayogāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those good ones, even in the forest as in a palace, whose efforts are solely bound to the welfare of the world,

children.text: svatanum api parārtham utsṛjanti praṇayijanapraṇayaṃ na khaṇḍayanti || GoSd_79 ||
children.translated_text: give up even their own bodies for the sake of others, and do not break the bond of affection with those who are dear. // GoSd 79 //

children.text: ata iha bhavanaṃ vanaṃ ca tulyaṃ jagadupajīvyavibhūtivistarāṇām |
children.translated_text: Therefore, for those whose minds are resolved in the vow of undiminished service to all the worlds,

children.text: avikalabhuvanopakārapārapraṇayakṛtavyavasāyamānasānām || GoSd_80 ||
children.translated_text: palace and forest are equal, as are the broad expanses of their wealth that sustain the world. // GoSd 80 //

children.text: tena dattaṃ samādāya svarājyaṃ lokasārathiḥ |
children.translated_text: The charioteer of the world (<s>lokasārathi</s>), accepting the kingdom given by him,

children.text: dhanaṃ rājā sa viprāya vāñchitātyadhikaṃ dadau || GoSd_81 ||
children.translated_text: the king gave to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> wealth exceeding his desire. // GoSd 81 //

children.text: tasyāścaryam udāradharmasuratiṃ cākarṇya viproditaṃ
children.translated_text: Hearing of that astonishing and noble delight in <s>dharma</s> proclaimed by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: tyaktvā vairavikāraduḥsahataraṃ krodhābhidhānaṃ viṣam |
children.translated_text: abandoning the more unbearable poison called anger — the transformation of enmity —

children.text: dhṛtvā maulim ivonnate ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ – – – ⏑ rājā svayaṃ
children.translated_text: placing [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] as a crown-jewel on his exalted [head] [lacuna] the king himself

children.text: cakre taccaraṇāmbujapraṇayinīm uṣṇīṣamālāṃ kṣaṇāt || GoSd_82 ||
children.translated_text: in an instant made of the garland of his turban a devotee of those lotus-feet. // GoSd 82 //

children.text: tasmin gate nijapuraṃ vinayaprapanne saṃprāpya rājyam arihīnam udārapuṇyaḥ |
children.translated_text: When that one of splendid merit, established in discipline, returned to his own city and obtained the kingdom free of enemies,

children.text: dharmeṇa kīrtidhavalāmbudhiphenamālāvelādukūlalalitāṃ pṛthivīṃ śaśāsa || GoSd_83 ||
children.translated_text: he ruled the earth — lovely in its silken garment of coastline formed by the foam-garland of the ocean of fame whitened by <s>dharma</s> — with righteousness. // GoSd 83 //

children.text: caritam atigatopamānaśobhaṃ na hi vibhavo 'sty anugantum īśvarāṇām |
children.translated_text: The conduct [of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>], whose beauty surpasses all comparison — truly, lords have no power to follow it;

children.text: mama kṛpaṇamates tathāpi caitat kṛtam atisāhasam ātmano hitāya || GoSd_84 ||
children.translated_text: yet this [narration] has been attempted, however presumptuously, by me of meager intellect, for my own benefit. // GoSd 84 //

children.text: kuśalam upacitaṃ kṛpātmakānāṃ caritam idaṃ vinibadhya yan mayādya |
children.translated_text: May the merit accumulated by my composing today this narrative of those whose nature is compassion

children.text: bhavatu bhuvanaśāntaye tad āśu jvalatu tathāgataśāsanaṃ tataś ca || GoSd_85 ||
children.translated_text: swiftly bring about peace for the world, and may the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> blaze forth from it! // GoSd 85 //

children.text: iti sarvaṃdadajātakam ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Sarvaṃdada Jātaka</s>.

children.text: Śvan = GoŚv
children.translated_text: Śvan = GoŚv

children.text:
Ed. Michael Hahn.
Cf. Michael Hahn. Der grosse Legendenkranz Mahajjātakamālā. Wiesbaden 195 (Asiatische Forschungen, 88). No. 8: Somajātakāvadāna

children.text: 16. Śvan
children.translated_text: 16. <s>Śvan</s> (The Dog)

children.text: (247b6) paraduḥkhakātarā devarājyam apy avadhīrayanti sādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The good, distressed by others' suffering, disregard even the sovereignty of the gods.

children.text: tadyathānuśrūyate
children.translated_text: As the story goes —

children.text: bodhisattvabhūtaḥ (248a) kila bhagavān svapuṇyaparipākaviśeṣopanatam amarapurādhipatyam kārayām āsa | naparidyūtahṛdayena sarvalokātiśayināpi mahimnā kevalaṃ puṇyānām avandhyaphalam āviṣkurvann amarapuranivāsināṃ cānugrahāya ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, assumed the lordship of the city of the immortals, which had been bestowed through the ripening of his own special merit. Not with a heart puffed up by [his] supremacy that surpassed the entire world — merely manifesting the unfailing fruit of merits, and also for the benefit of the inhabitants of the city of the immortals.

children.text: jagad dṛṣṭvānantavyasanakuliśāpātavihataṃ
children.translated_text: Having seen the world struck by the thunderbolts of infinite calamities,

children.text: na sa svarge reme prakṛtiramaṇīye 'pi bhagavān |
children.translated_text: the Blessed One did not delight in heaven, though it is naturally delightful;

children.text: tadā hy enaṃ sā dhīr hṛdi tudati niḥsaṅgam aniśaṃ
children.translated_text: for that resolve continually and without attachment pierced his heart —

children.text: parārthaprāgbhārā paramavidhurā svāduvidhurā || GoŚv_1 ||
children.translated_text: [a resolve] weighted toward the welfare of others, supremely compassionate, indifferent to its own pleasure. // GoŚv 1 //

children.text: akṛtakuśalavyāpārānāṃ svabhūtinibandhanaṃ
children.translated_text: Of those who have not engaged in wholesome activities — the cause of their own well-being —

children.text: kṛpaṇamanasāṃ – – yad vā mano bahu manyate |
children.translated_text: of the wretched-minded — [lacuna] — or whatever the mind values highly;

children.text: svacaritapariprāptaiśvaryaṃ jagaddhitakāriṇā
children.translated_text: even when great sovereignty is obtained through one's own [good] conduct, one who acts for the world's welfare

children.text: na viṣayasukheṣv āsthaṃ ceto mahaty api rakṣyate || GoŚv_2 ||
children.translated_text: does not maintain attachment to sensory pleasures in the mind. // GoŚv 2 //

children.text: sa kadā cij jambūdvīpam avalokayan dadarśa [!] evaṃ lokam aśakyapratīkāravyādhiduḥkhopaplutaṃ viṣamavirasakṛtavaidyasāmarthyaṃ samaraṇam āvarjja(?)vyavasāyaviklavaṃ romanthamānam iva piśitāśanair ihaiva narakaduḥkhāny anubhavantaṃ vismṛtasnehabandhumitrasuhṛcchaucācāraprayojanam ||
children.translated_text: Once, surveying <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, he beheld the world thus: afflicted with diseases and sufferings that could not be resisted, with physicians rendered powerless by terrible and repulsive [ailments], [people] facing death, bewildered in their resolve, as if ruminating — experiencing the sufferings of hell right here, being devoured by flesh-eaters — having forgotten the purpose of affection, kinship, friendship, purity, and proper conduct.

children.text: kṛtāntakarmānta iva pravṛttas tadā sa rogāntarakalpatulyaḥ |
children.translated_text: That affliction caused by disease, then active as if it were the workshop of Death,

children.text: aśakyarūpapratikārabhīmo mahātyayo vyādhikṛto vikāraḥ || GoŚv_3 ||
children.translated_text: equal to an apocalyptic plague, terrifying with its incurable manifestations — // GoŚv 3 //

children.text: kṣuttṛṣṇācetanaparigatāḥ sānubandhaṃ stananto
children.translated_text: Seized by hunger, thirst, and loss of consciousness, groaning ceaselessly,

children.text: vikṣiptāṅgāḥ kṣititalarajoguṇṭhitoddhastakeśāḥ |
children.translated_text: with limbs flung about, their disheveled hair matted with the dust of the ground,

children.text: smāraṃ smāraṃ jalakaṇamucāṃ mallikāmālutānāṃ
children.translated_text: remembering again and again the jasmine and <s>mālatī</s> creepers dropping water-drops,

children.text: – – – – madhukaragaṇair mārga āsannapātāḥ || GoŚv_4 ||
children.translated_text: [lacuna] with swarms of bees — [those people were] near the brink of death. // GoŚv 4 //

children.text: śvāsādhmātabṛhatkaṭhorajaṭharavyābhinnanāsāpuṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Their nostrils rent by the great, hardened bellies swollen by labored breathing,

children.text: sṛkkāntapratibaddhaśuṣkavirasaśleṣmānanā bhīṣaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: with dried, tasteless mucus stuck at the corners of their mouths — their faces terrifying;

children.text: rūkṣasthūlaśirāpratānajaṭilatvaksnāyuśeṣāśrayāḥ
children.translated_text: with bodies reduced to mere remnants of rough, thick veins, matted skin, and sinews —

children.text: ke cit pūrvakṛtaṃ ninindur aśubhaṃ karmābhisaṃdhisthiram || GoŚv_5 ||
children.translated_text: some cursed the inauspicious <s>karma</s> done in former [lives], fixed in its intent. // GoŚv 5 //

children.text: kvathitapiśitarandhraprodvamatpūyadhārā malinavikṛtadehāḥ ke cid aprekṣaṇīyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Some, with streams of pus oozing from the holes of boiled [rotting] flesh, their bodies filthy and disfigured — unpresentable,

children.text: krimikulapariluptaprāyabāhūdaroruśravaṇanayananāsāḥ prārthayante sma kālam || GoŚv_6 ||
children.translated_text: their arms, bellies, thighs, ears, eyes, and noses mostly consumed by colonies of worms — they prayed for death. // GoŚv 6 //

children.text: saṃśuṣkādharakaṇṭhatāluvivarās tṛṣṇāgninā dāhinā
children.translated_text: With dried cavities of lower lip, throat, and palate, [consumed] by the burning fire of thirst,

children.text: rūkṣakṣāmavidāritānanapuṭāḥ pretā ivāyāsinaḥ |
children.translated_text: their cracked, emaciated mouth-cavities split open — distressed like <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts),

children.text: āmattālikuloddhatotpalavanacchannāmbuviṣyandināṃ
children.translated_text: gazing at the waters of lakes flowing with water hidden under the lotuses

children.text: vīkṣantaḥ sarasāṃ payāṃsi viviśuḥ ke cit kṛtāntālayam || GoŚv_7 ||
children.translated_text: covered by intoxicated swarms of bees — some entered the abode of Death. // GoŚv 7 //

children.text: dūṣīkāpaṭalaniruddhalocanāntā durgandhā bahalamalopaliptagātrāḥ |
children.translated_text: Others, their eyes blocked by films of cataracts, foul-smelling, their bodies smeared with thick filth,

children.text: anye tu klamaśithilāśrayā rujānām ājagmur nilayanatāṃ prabandhinīnām || GoŚv_8 ||
children.translated_text: their bodies weakened by exhaustion, became the abode of chronic diseases. // GoŚv 8 //

children.text: ke cil lālāsalilavisaraklinnasaṃsaktadīrgha-
children.translated_text: Some, wretched, their long beards matted and sticky with dripping saliva,

children.text: śmaśruvrātāḥ pathiṣu kṛpaṇāḥ klāntakāyāḥ śayānāḥ |
children.translated_text: lying exhausted on the roads,

children.text: krūrārāvaiḥ purabalibhujāṃ maṇḍalaiḥ saṃpatadbhir
children.translated_text: by the circles of town-crows descending with cruel cries,

children.text: vyāvṛttāsyā vipadam avaśāḥ pratyapadyanta tīvrām || GoŚv_9 ||
children.translated_text: their faces turned away — helplessly they met with terrible calamity. // GoŚv 9 //

children.text: tasya tad atidāruṇam ālokya lokavyasanaṃ mahat kāruṇyam udapādi | atha sa mahāsattvas tena sattvopadraveṇa vyathitamanāḥ sutarām abhivardhitānukampākampitaḥ pitevaikaputravyasanam asahamānaś cintām apede ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that exceedingly terrible calamity of the world, great compassion arose in him. Then that great being, his mind pained by that affliction of beings, all the more shaken by swelling compassion — like a father unable to bear the calamity of an only son — fell into reflection:

children.text: itthaṃ gatānāṃ ka ivābhyupāyaḥ syād āmayocchittisukhaḥ prajānām |
children.translated_text: 'What means could there be for the people, leading to the happiness of eradication of disease, [for those] who have come to such a pass?

children.text: apīha lokatrayabāndhavānāṃ tathāgatānām anṛṇo bhaveyam || GoŚv_10 ||
children.translated_text: Could I perhaps become free from debt to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the kinsmen of the three worlds?' // GoŚv 10 //

children.text: api nāma bhaven mama pratijñā sakalā lokahitaprayogasiddhyai |
children.translated_text: 'Would that my vow might be fulfilled for the accomplishment of the work of universal welfare;

children.text: api mānuṣajanmaduḥkhabhājo vyasanebhyaḥ parimokṣam aśnuvīran || GoŚv_11 ||
children.translated_text: would that those who share the suffering of human birth might obtain release from calamities!' // GoŚv 11 //

children.text: api nāma na bodhisattvanāmavyapadeśaṃ vitathaṃ samudvaheyam |
children.translated_text: 'Would that I not bear in vain the designation of the name "<s>Bodhisattva</s>";

children.text: api sarvavidām agarhaṇīyāṃ dadhad ājñām animittavatsalānām || GoŚv_12 ||
children.translated_text: would that I uphold the irreproachable command of the omniscient ones, whose compassion is causeless!' // GoŚv 12 //

children.text: bhavaduḥkhaśilīmukhakṣatānām api mateva piteva ca prajānām |
children.translated_text: I alone shall be the supreme refuge for beings wounded by the arrows of the suffering of existence,

children.text: aham eva parāyaṇaṃ paraṃ syāṃ bhavaduḥkhāmburayapratīrabhūtaḥ || GoŚv_13 ||
children.translated_text: like a mother, like a father — being a ford across the flood of the suffering of existence. // GoŚv 13 //

children.text: yāvad duḥkhābhibhūtaḥ praviśati na jano rogadaṃṣṭrākarālaṃ
children.translated_text: Before people, overwhelmed by suffering, enter the mouth-cavity of the serpent of Death (<s>Kāla</s>), terrible with the fangs of disease,

children.text: kālāher āsyakośaṃ sakalajagadanugrāsasaṃbhogabhīmam |
children.translated_text: fearsome with the devouring and consuming of the entire world —

children.text: tāvad dvandvānurāgaṃ tridaśapurapatiśrīsukhaṃ projjhya ramyaṃ
children.translated_text: until then, abandoning the lovely happiness of the lordship of the celestial city, the delight of paired love,

children.text: prāṇatyāgānurāgaṃ praṇayasukhakaraṃ bhūtabhṛtyai karomi || GoŚv_14 ||
children.translated_text: I shall, with a passion for the sacrifice of life, bring about joy for the service of beings. // GoŚv 14 //

children.text: vyavasāyam iti jñātvā tasyātyadbhutakarmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Knowing this to be the firm resolve of that one of wondrous deeds,

children.text: tadviyogābhiśaṅkārtā vicukruśur athāmarāḥ || GoŚv_15 ||
children.translated_text: the immortals, pained by the apprehension of separation from him, wailed aloud. // GoŚv 15 //

children.text: kṛpālo duḥkhitān asmān parityajya kva yāsyasi |
children.translated_text: "O compassionate one, abandoning us who are afflicted, where will you go?

children.text: viṣamasthān iva pitā vatsalo bālaputrakān || GoŚv_16 ||
children.translated_text: Like a loving father [who would not abandon] his little children in a dangerous situation! // GoŚv 16 //

children.text: saddharmasalilotsekair vardhayan pādapān iva |
children.translated_text: Nourishing us like trees with the sprinkling of the water of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: asmān anāgasas tyaktvā mā yāsīḥ priyadarśana || GoŚv_17 ||
children.translated_text: do not go, O beautiful one, having abandoned us who are without fault! // GoŚv 17 //

children.text: viṣayāsvādacapalair hṛtān indriyavājibhīḥ |
children.translated_text: Us, who are carried away by the sense-horses, fickle with the tasting of sense-objects,

children.text: svāmin māsmān parityākṣīḥ prapātāntānucāriṇaḥ || GoŚv_18 ||
children.translated_text: wandering toward the edge of a precipice — O lord, do not abandon us! // GoŚv 18 //"

children.text: praṇāmalolānatamaulibandhanān pragāḍhaśokopanipātakātarān |
children.translated_text: Then the lord of the winds (<s>Marutpati</s>, i.e., the Bodhisattva as lord of gods), consoling the immortals — whose crown-ties were loosened by their heads bowed in prostration, who were miserable from the onslaught of profound grief, whose eyes were flooded with tears —

children.text: athāmarān aśrupariplutekṣaṇān sa sāntvayann ity avadan marutpatiḥ || GoŚv_19 ||
children.translated_text: spoke thus: // GoŚv 19 //

children.text: na me na yuṣmāsv anurāgapeśalaṃ mano na cāyaṃ svahitodayādaraḥ |
children.translated_text: "My mind is not without tender affection for you, nor is this haste for my own benefit;

children.text: vikāsinīnāṃ vipadāṃ mukhe sthitaṃ jagat paritrātum ayaṃ tu niścayaḥ || GoŚv_20 ||
children.translated_text: rather, this is my firm resolve: to rescue the world, which stands at the mouth of blossoming calamities. // GoŚv 20 //

children.text: tad apramādaḥ kriyatāṃ sa eva vo dhruvaṃ samārtāyanatām upeṣyati |
children.translated_text: Therefore, let heedfulness be practiced by you — it will certainly become a means of deliverance;

children.text: visaṃvadanty eva samāgamāḥ priyair nipātaramyāḥ pariṇāmadāruṇāḥ || GoŚv_21 ||
children.translated_text: for encounters with loved ones are deceptive — pleasant in their onset, terrible in their outcome. // GoŚv 21 //

children.text: sthitvāpi kālam atulaṃ vividhopabhogasaṃbhogavistarasukhais tridaśādhivāse |
children.translated_text: Even after dwelling for an incomparable time in the abode of the thirty [gods], with the happiness of vast, various enjoyments and pleasures,

children.text: karmakṣayād vinipatanti surāḥ smarantaḥ saṃvartakānilahatā iva kalpavṛkṣāḥ || GoŚv_22 ||
children.translated_text: the gods fall through the exhaustion of their <s>karma</s>, remembering [their former state], like wish-fulfilling trees struck by the wind of the world's dissolution. // GoŚv 22 //

children.text: mandākinīm api vigāhya sahāpsarobhir unnidrahemakamalocchuritopakaṇṭhām |
children.translated_text: Even after plunging into the <s>Mandākinī</s> together with <s>Apsarases</s>, its shores raised with alert golden lotuses,

children.text: kṣārodakāṃ jvalanadarbhakukūlakūlāṃ nighnāḥ punar yadi ca vaitaraṇīṃ bhajante || GoŚv_23 ||
children.translated_text: if the helpless ones again resort to the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> — with its salty water, its banks of blazing <s>darbha</s>-grass fire — // GoŚv 23 //

children.text: ko nāma teṣu matimān svamano nidadhyād utkṣepaṇīyakusumāvayavopameṣu |
children.translated_text: what wise person would set his mind upon those pleasures born of heavenly enjoyment, whose components are like flowers to be discarded,

children.text: svargopabhogajaniteṣu sukheṣu yeṣām anteṣv apāyavaḍavāmukhasaṃniveśaḥ || GoŚv_24 ||
children.translated_text: at whose end lies the arrangement of the submarine-fire-mouth of evil destinations? // GoŚv 24 //

children.text: kalpadrumopavanabhūmiṣu naikaratnaprodbhāsyamānatatatalpaśilātalāsu |
children.translated_text: In the grounds of wish-fulfilling tree gardens, on rock-ledges of stone couches illuminated by numerous jewels,

children.text: sākaṃ priyābhir anubhūya sukhāni bhūyas tīkṣṇāsipattravanamadhyagatā bhavanti || GoŚv_25 ||
children.translated_text: having enjoyed pleasures together with their beloveds, they again find themselves in the midst of forests of sharp sword-leaves. // GoŚv 25 //

children.text: saṃbhrāntabālahariṇekṣaṇacañcalāni vibhrāntakālapariṇāmakarāṇi buddheḥ |
children.translated_text: Since the pleasures of the indulgence of dull senses and objects are fleeting like the glances of a startled young fawn,

children.text: yad dhīndriyārthaparibhogasukhāni tasmād yatnaṃ surāḥ kuruta puṇyaparigrahāya || GoŚv_26 ||
children.translated_text: and are subject to the operation of the confused transformation of time — therefore, O gods, make effort for the accumulation of merit! // GoŚv 26 //

children.text: edhobhir agnaya iva praśamaṃ vrajanti kāmāgnayo na viṣayair viṣapānakalpaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Like fires [fueled] by firewood, the fires of desire are not quenched by sense-objects, which are like draughts of poison;

children.text: tasmād upāddhvam anavadyasukhābhirāmāṃ tāthāgatīṃ pratipadaṃ vyasanopaśāntyai || GoŚv_27 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, take up the path of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, delightful with faultless happiness, for the calming of calamities. // GoŚv 27 //

children.text: anāthānāṃ dainyaglapitamanasāṃ duḥkhāśīviṣa-
children.translated_text: For the calming of beings — the helpless, whose minds are withered by wretchedness, who have been "smelled" by hosts of serpents of suffering,

children.text: gaṇopaghrātānāṃ paraśubhir ivotkṛttavapuṣām |
children.translated_text: whose bodies are as if cut by axes —

children.text: praśāntyai bhūtānāṃ vayam api tiraścām anukṛtiṃ
children.translated_text: we too shall take on the likeness of animals,

children.text: kariṣyāmo muktvā surabhavanasaṃbhogavasitām || GoŚv_28 ||
children.translated_text: abandoning the enjoyment of dwelling in the celestial mansions." // GoŚv 28 //

children.text: avicalapratibandho dīrghakālānuṣaṅgī
children.translated_text: "My resolve to benefit the world is of unshakable constancy, adhering through a long time;

children.text: mama jagadupakāraprārthanāsaṃniveśaḥ |
children.translated_text: [continued]

children.text: sucaritaparipākasyeti dṛṣṭvā prasiddhiṃ
children.translated_text: seeing the fulfillment of the ripening of good deeds — the virtuous should not create an obstacle to merit." // GoŚv 29 //

children.text: na khalu kuśalavighnaṃ kartum arhanti santaḥ || GoŚv_29 ||
children.translated_text: [continued from above]

children.text: atimānuṣam apy apāsya citraṃ mahimānaṃ kṛpayā vikṛṣyamāṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having cast aside even the wondrous, superhuman glory, drawn by compassion,

children.text: sa tu duḥkhakaro gatau tiraścāṃ paramāryaḥ pratisaṃdadhe mahātmā || GoŚv_30 ||
children.translated_text: that supremely noble great soul took rebirth in the course of animals, [even though] it would cause suffering. // GoŚv 30 //

children.text: karuṇāmṛtapeśalāśayānāṃ svasukhāsaṅgaviviktamānasānām |
children.translated_text: The arising of the good, whose minds are detached from attachment to their own happiness, whose intentions are refined by the nectar of compassion,

children.text: prabhavā iva kalpapādapānām udayā lokahitāya sajjanānām || GoŚv_31 ||
children.translated_text: is like the emergence of wish-fulfilling trees — for the benefit of the world. // GoŚv 31 //

children.text: vinayānataratnamauliraśmicchuritās taṃ na marudgaṇapraṇāmāḥ |
children.translated_text: The prostrations of the hosts of the <s>Marut</s> gods, whose crown-jewel rays glittered on bowed heads with devotion,

children.text: manujātisukhaṃ samāpatantaṃ sthirasattvaṃ vinivartayāṃ babhūvuḥ || GoŚv_32 ||
children.translated_text: could not turn back that firm-souled one, approaching the happiness of human birth. // GoŚv 32 //

children.text: virahavyasanopatāpadīnair nayanair bāṣpataraṅgadhūsarāntaiḥ |
children.translated_text: His beloveds, gazing at him with pitiful looks — their eyes grey-edged with waves of tears,

children.text: dayitāḥ karuṇaṃ tam īkṣamāṇāḥ śucisattvaṃ na nivartayāṃ babhūvuḥ || GoŚv_33 ||
children.translated_text: wretched from the onslaught of the calamity of separation — could not turn back that pure-souled one. // GoŚv 33 //

children.text: svajaneṣu na tasya sānukampaṃ na mano dakṣiṇa eva sa prakṛtyā |
children.translated_text: His mind was not without compassion toward his kinfolk, nor was he anything but generous by nature;

children.text: avagamya garīyasīṃ tathāpi prakṛtiṃ śvā sa tathā cakāra sādhuḥ || GoŚv_34 ||
children.translated_text: but understanding the weightier [duty], that virtuous one acted accordingly as a dog. // GoŚv 34 //

children.text: sa hitāvahitā rujāturāṇāṃ himavanmerugurur guruḥ prajānām |
children.translated_text: That benefactor of the afflicted, teacher of beings, weighty as <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: puruṣātiśayo guṇaprakarṣān niyataṃ dūrataraṃ samutpapāta || GoŚv_35 ||
children.translated_text: that supremely excellent man, through the pre-eminence of his qualities, was certainly reborn very far [below his station]. // GoŚv 35 //

children.text: tapobhir yāṃ dīrghair yamaniyamasaṃskāragurubhir
children.translated_text: The glory of <s>Indra</s>'s position — which those who subsist on water, fruits, roots, and air

children.text: vyavasyanti prāptuṃ salilaphalamūlānilabhujaḥ |
children.translated_text: aspire to attain through long austerities, weighty with the cultivation of restraint and observances —

children.text: vibhūtiṃ tām aindrīṃ tṛṇam iva parityajya kṛpayā
children.translated_text: abandoning that like a blade of grass, out of compassion,

children.text: tiraścāṃ sābhāgyaṃ sa jagadupakārārtham agamat || GoŚv_36 ||
children.translated_text: he went, through good fortune, into the course of animals, for the sake of benefiting the world. // GoŚv 36 //

children.text: śubhābhyāsād eva kṣapitakukṛtapratyayatayā
children.translated_text: Through the habitual practice of virtue, having attained the mastery of controlling rebirth in the courses of existence —

children.text: tathāgatena prāptā bhavagatisamākṣepavaśitā |
children.translated_text: because of the exhaustion of unwholesome conditions — [that mastery was obtained] by the <s>Tathāgata</s>;

children.text: yathecchaṃ yatrecchaṃ parahitasamādhānaviduṣas
children.translated_text: wherever he wished, whenever he wished, skilled in establishing the welfare of others —

children.text: tathā hy abhūt janmavyasanaśamanāyaiva jagatām || GoŚv_37 ||
children.translated_text: thus indeed his [birth] was solely for the calming of the calamities of birth for the world. // GoŚv 37 //

children.text: svakāmakārānuvidhāyinīm śriyam paṭāntalagnām hutabhukśikhām iva |
children.translated_text: The great ones, whose bond is compassion, cannot tolerate prosperity — which obeys one's own desires like a flame clinging to the edge of a cloth —

children.text: na marṣayanti vyasanāturān janān dṛṣṭvā mahāntaḥ karuṇānibandhanāḥ || GoŚv_38 ||
children.translated_text: when they see people afflicted by calamity. // GoŚv 38 //

children.text: tasyopapattisamakālam athoccacāra lokaṃ sphuran dhvanir iti śravaṇopakārī |
children.translated_text: At the very moment of his birth, a voice arose, shining forth, beneficial to the ear, saying to the world:

children.text: yaḥ pāpy ayaṃ kuru puro bhajanaṃ ca tasya māṃsāsṛjau samupayujya śivaṃ bhajadhvam || GoŚv_39 ||
children.translated_text: "This sinful one [is here] — make devotion to him, and using his flesh and blood, attain welfare!" // GoŚv 39 //

children.text: śrutvātha dhvanim atimānuṣaṃ manuṣyāḥ sāṃhatyasvaritam upetya taṃ pradeśam |
children.translated_text: Then the people, hearing that superhuman sound, uttered in unison, approaching that place,

children.text: ālokya kṣitidharapīvarātmabhāvaṃ taṃ sādhuṃ kṣamiṇam abhīyur udviṣāṇāḥ || GoŚv_40 ||
children.translated_text: and seeing that virtuous, patient one with a body massive as a mountain, came forth with weapons raised. // GoŚv 40 //

children.text: āghūrṇasphuṭitakhaḍganiśātapāṇīn dṛṣṭvā tān abhipatato javena gatvā |
children.translated_text: Seeing them rushing forward with sharp swords drawn and glinting in their hands,

children.text: hāheti sphuṭavirasaṃ vilepur uccaiḥ pratyastapraśithilamaulayaḥ suraughāḥ || GoŚv_41 ||
children.translated_text: the hosts of gods cried out aloud "Alas!" in clear distress, with their crowns thrown back and loosened. // GoŚv 41 //

children.text: māṃ dṛṣṭvā ghanavipulāyatātmabhāvaṃ śrutvā vā surapuravāsināṃ pralāpān |
children.translated_text: "Having seen me with my dense, vast, extended body, or having heard the lamentations of the celestial dwellers,

children.text: na kaś cit pratihatamānaso vasāsṛgmoko 'yaṃ kṣaṇam iti so 'bhavad vikārī || GoŚv_42 ||
children.translated_text: surely not a single one will have a mind unmoved" — but thinking "this release of flesh and blood is only for a moment," he remained undisturbed. // GoŚv 42 //

children.text: tān paurān suhṛda ivāvalokya tasya prītir yā manasi manasvino jṛmbhate |
children.translated_text: The joy that blossomed in the mind of that noble one, seeing those citizens as if they were friends,

children.text: tām eva kṣitidharasāradhīḥ sa mene paryāptaṃ phalam atiduṣkarasya tasya || GoŚv_43 ||
children.translated_text: that alone he considered sufficient fruit of that extremely difficult [act], [he] whose intellect was as firm as a mountain. // GoŚv 43 //

children.text: lokānām abhilaṣitopakāramyaṃ matvāsāv upacitamāṃsam ātmabhavam |
children.translated_text: Considering his own body, with its amassed flesh, to be useful for the desired service of the world,

children.text: ekāntavyasananipātalakṣyabhūte saṃsāre 'py abhiratim ābabandha sādhuḥ || GoŚv_44 ||
children.translated_text: that virtuous one fastened his delight even to <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is a target for the single-aimed fall of calamity. // GoŚv 44 //

children.text: ye dhvastāḥ parahitasaṃvidhānaśūnyās taddehāḥ kṣaṇabhidurā bhavaprabandhe |
children.translated_text: Those bodies in the continuum of existence that are destroyed — empty of the undertaking of others' welfare, fragile as a moment —

children.text: tān manye sa parigaṇayya śailatuṅgān cchuddhyaiva svatanum upādadhe mahātmā || GoŚv_45 ||
children.translated_text: counting them [as worthless], I think that great soul took up his own body solely out of purity, [though it was] mountain-high. // GoŚv 45 //

children.text: taṃ matvā vitatavikāram eva dhairyāt te tīkṣṇais tarum iva cicchiduḥ kuṭhāraiḥ |
children.translated_text: Considering him to be merely a brute creature with deformities, out of boldness

children.text: niḥśaṅkā galitakṛpāśivair manobhiḥ so 'py āsīt tarur iva cāpanītamanyuḥ || GoŚv_46 ||
children.translated_text: they cut him with sharp axes as if a tree, without hesitation, with minds devoid of compassion and merciless; yet he too remained free from anger, like a tree. // GoŚv 46 //

children.text: tadraktavyatirekapāṭalāgrahastās tam khaḍgair araya ivāpare vicakruḥ |
children.translated_text: Others too cut him with swords, their hands reddened by the excess of his blood, like enemies;

children.text: so 'py āsīd abhimatakāryasaṃprasiddhyā prītyaiva sphuṭahṛdayo viśuddhakarmā || GoŚv_47 ||
children.translated_text: yet his heart was wide open with joy at the fulfillment of his desired purpose — that one of purified <s>karma</s>. // GoŚv 47 //

children.text: susrāva kṣatajam athāsya khaḍgadhārāc chedebhyaḥ sphuṭakaradhīrapuṣpatāmram |
children.translated_text: Then blood flowed from the gashes of the sword-blade cuts — copper-colored like bold, blooming flowers,

children.text: saṃprāptaghanasamaye vicitrasānor vindhyādrer jalam iva dhātunirjharebhyaḥ || GoŚv_48 ||
children.translated_text: like water from mineral-cascades of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain with its multicolored ridges at the arrival of the rainy season. // GoŚv 48 //

children.text: cakṣāra vraṇamukhakandarebhyo yat tasya kṣatajam iva kṣatāśayasya |
children.translated_text: The blood that oozed from the cave-like wound-openings of that one whose inner self was free from harm

children.text: tenohur ghanapariṇāhaphenapuñjā viṣṭabdhā vipulasitavīcayaḥ sravantyaḥ || GoŚv_49 ||
children.translated_text: bore piled masses of dense foam — vast white waves flowing forth. // GoŚv 49 //

children.text: tat tasya praṇidhibalāvalambinīnām āśānāṃ katham api pūraṇāt sucetaḥ |
children.translated_text: From the somehow-fulfilled satisfaction of his aspirations supported by the power of his vows, that noble-minded one,

children.text: saṃprāpte 'py amrapure śarīrabhedāt prāmodyaṃ niratiśayopamaṃ babhāra || GoŚv_50 ||
children.translated_text: even upon reaching the city of death through the breaking of his body, bore incomparable, unsurpassed joy. // GoŚv 50 //

children.text: dadhvāna prapatadasṛkkadeharandhre vicchinne paraśutīkṣṇadhārayāsya |
children.translated_text: Holding [steady] as blood cascaded through the openings of his body, when [his limbs] were severed by the axe-sharp edge —

children.text: pratyantajvalanaśikhāvalīḍhasānoḥ kuñjeṣu drutam iva kāncanaṃ sumeroḥ || GoŚv_51 ||
children.translated_text: like gold melting in the groves of <s>Sumeru</s> whose ridges are licked by the flame-garlands at the world's edge. // GoŚv 51 //

children.text: tasyograir yugapad itas tataś ca śastrair niḥśaṅkaṃ śakalitakomalāśrayāṅge |
children.translated_text: When his tender body was simultaneously cut to pieces by fierce weapons from all sides without hesitation,

children.text: vicchinne sahananiviṣṭaśuddhabuddheḥ prītyārdre manasi tirodadhe viṣādaḥ || GoŚv_52 ||
children.translated_text: in the mind of that one of established, pure wisdom and endurance, moist with joy, grief vanished. // GoŚv 52 //

children.text: paricayakṛtamārgās tasya raktapraṇālyo gagaṇaparikhabhūte cchidyamāne śarīre |
children.translated_text: As his body — become like a trench of the sky — was being cut apart, the channels of his blood, their paths made familiar [by the cutting],

children.text: kṣitidharasaridoghā vistarāṇi pracakrur na ca manasi viṣādo nāpi khedo babhūva || GoŚv_53 ||
children.translated_text: spread out like mountain-river floods; yet in his mind there was neither grief nor weariness. // GoŚv 53 //

children.text: apacitataramāṃsāsṛgvasākardamāsu vyapagatabhayaśaṅkās tasya vistāriṇīṣu |
children.translated_text: In those spreading [pools] of his accumulated flesh, blood, and fat-mud,

children.text: tanuvivaratareṣu vyāḍasaṃghā vicerur na ca manasi viṣādo na ca khedo babhūva || GoŚv_54 ||
children.translated_text: packs of wild beasts roamed, free from fear and suspicion, through the ever-widening gaps of his body; yet in his mind there was neither grief nor weariness. // GoŚv 54 //

children.text: yad apahṛtam anāryais tasya māṃsaṃ śarīrād yadi tad apariśeṣaṃ piṇḍitaṃ syāt kathaṃ cit |
children.translated_text: If the flesh carried away from his body by the ignoble ones could somehow be heaped together as a whole,

children.text: girim api sa sumeruṃ laṅghayen māṃsarāśir na ca manasi viṣado na ca khedo babhūva || GoŚv_55 ||
children.translated_text: that mountain of flesh could surpass even <s>Meru</s>; yet in his mind there was neither grief nor weariness. // GoŚv 55 //

children.text: kṣayam upayayur aṅgeṣv eva śastrāṇi tasya prakṛtimṛduṣu sādhor akṣatādhyāśayasya |
children.translated_text: The weapons spent themselves upon the very limbs of that virtuous one, naturally soft, whose inner intention was unwounded,

children.text: abhirucitaparārthaprītisaṃbhogaśānte na ca manasi viṣādo na ca khedo babhūva || GoŚv_56 ||
children.translated_text: whose joy was calmed by the pleasure of savoring the practice of others' welfare; yet in his mind there was neither grief nor weariness. // GoŚv 56 //

children.text: ye cāsya raktair vililepur aṅgā te rejire rogaviṣādamuktāḥ |
children.translated_text: And those who anointed their limbs with his blood shone forth, freed from disease and despair;

children.text: ye cāpi raktāni papuḥ sarogās te sarvalokāḥ pupuṣur virogāḥ || GoŚv_57 ||
children.translated_text: and those who were sick and drank his blood — all those people flourished, free from disease. // GoŚv 57 //

children.text: janam apagatarogaṃ vīkṣamāṇasya harṣo manasi bhuvanabandhor labdhagādho babhūva |
children.translated_text: Seeing the people freed from disease, joy took deep root in the mind of that kinsman of the world;

children.text: piśitam anupayogaṃ vīkṣamāṇasya bhūyo 'py abhavad aratidolaṃ cañcalaṃ tasya cetaḥ || GoŚv_58 ||
children.translated_text: but seeing flesh going unused, his mind again became restless, swinging on the pendulum of dissatisfaction. // GoŚv 58 //

children.text: utkṛttacarmapaṭalasphuṭatāmramāṃso randhrodvamadrudhiraśeṣaviśeṣatāmraḥ |
children.translated_text: With skin-layers cut away, exposed copper-red flesh, copper-colored from the special overflow of blood gushing from the openings,

children.text: kāyaḥ sa tasya vikṛtaḥ kṛtaniścayasya reje javākusumarāśir ivābhracumbī || GoŚv_59 ||
children.translated_text: the deformed body of that one of firm resolve blazed like a sky-touching heap of <s>javā</s> (hibiscus) flowers. // GoŚv 59 //

children.text: vicchidyamānaḥ suniśātaśastrais tad duḥkham ekāśrayam īkṣamāṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Being cut apart by exceedingly sharp weapons, seeing that suffering [existing] in one body alone,

children.text: sukhena duḥkhaṃ sa nirācakāra labdhvā paratrātmani caikamatyam || GoŚv_60 ||
children.translated_text: he happily dispelled that suffering, having attained single-mindedness regarding the self in this world and the next. // GoŚv 60 //

children.text: pariṇāmakharā batādhamāyā gatir ātmābhiniveśavāsanāyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Alas, harsh in its ripening is the course of the base disposition of self-clinging,

children.text: upadigdhadhiyo yayā manuṣyāḥ pitṛbhūteṣv api sādhuṣu skhalanti || GoŚv_61 ||
children.translated_text: by which people, with corrupted minds, stumble even toward the virtuous who have become ancestors. // GoŚv 61 //

children.text: etasya māṃsaṃ bubhuje kṛpālor yo yaḥ sa sa vyādhim apācakāra |
children.translated_text: Whoever ate the flesh of that compassionate one, that person was cured of disease;

children.text: krameṇa kṛcchraṃ jagad uttatāra vipatsamudraṃ tad anena kṛtsnam || GoŚv_62 ||
children.translated_text: gradually, the entire world crossed the ocean of calamity — all of it, through him. // GoŚv 62 //

children.text: atha sarva eva loko vigatanikhilarogopasargas tasmin mahāsattve samupajātapremagauravabahumānaḥ praṇamya śvānaṃ bodhisattvam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then the entire world, freed from the affliction of all diseases, having developed love, reverence, and high esteem for that great being, bowed and said to the dog, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

children.text: aho kṛpābhyāsaviśeṣabhadratā guṇeṣv aho bhaktir apetakalmaṣā |
children.translated_text: "Oh, the excellence of the blessedness of compassion practiced! Oh, the devotion to virtues, freed from defilement!

children.text: aho parārthapratipattipeśalaṃ tavārya karmedam atītamānuṣam || GoŚv_63 ||
children.translated_text: Oh, this deed of yours, O noble one — refined in the practice of others' welfare — is beyond the human!" // GoŚv 63 //

children.text: aho jagacchreṣṭhamahādayārdratā aho svasaukhyavyavasāyaniḥspṛhā |
children.translated_text: "Ah, the great compassion, tender toward the world's best! Ah, the freedom from desire for the pursuit of one's own happiness!

children.text: śubheṣv aho niścayaniścalaṃ mano manasvināṃ bodhipathānupātinām || GoŚv_64 ||
children.translated_text: Ah, the minds of the noble, firm in their resolve toward what is virtuous — those who follow the path to Awakening (<s>Bodhi</s>)! [GoŚv 64]

children.text: aho batācintyam upāyakauśalam aho parārthe 'bhirater udāttatā |
children.translated_text: Ah, the inconceivable skillfulness in means! Ah, the exaltedness of delight in the welfare of others!

children.text: acintyacaryātiśayāya sādhave namo 'stu tubhyaṃ jagadekabandhave || GoŚv_65 ||
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O virtuous one, for the extraordinary excellence of your inconceivable conduct — the sole kinsman of the world! [GoŚv 65]

children.text: tvaṃ naḥ pitā yadi pitā tvam ivārthakāmaḥ śāstā tvam eva yadi dharmagurus tvam eva |
children.translated_text: You are our father — if a father is one who desires our welfare. You are our teacher — if the teacher of <s>Dharma</s> is you yourself.

children.text: tvam daivataṃ yadi na taj janavādamātram ārtāyanaṃ tu jagataḥ paramaṃ tvam eva || GoŚv_66 ||
children.translated_text: You are our deity — if [the word 'deity'] is not mere popular talk. But the supreme refuge of the afflicted world — that you truly are! [GoŚv 66]

children.text: tasmād ājñābhiṣekeṇa pavitrayitum arhasi |
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should deign to purify

children.text: upadigdham imaṃ lokaṃ yuṣmadāyāsacetasā || GoŚv_67 ||
children.translated_text: this world, anointed by the mind of your exertions, with the consecration of your command." [GoŚv 67]

children.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ samupajātaprasādamānasam avagamya tam enam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving that his [audience's] mind had been filled with faith, said to him:

children.text: pīḍā mameyam iti naivam idaṃ pradhāryaṃ sattvārtham eva gaticakracalasya nityam |
children.translated_text: "This is not to be considered as 'my suffering' — for one who is constantly revolving in the wheel of destinies, this is ever for the sake of beings.

children.text: pīḍā mamābhavad udīkṣya vipatparītān yuṣmān nirāmayasukhaṃ tv adhunā mano me || GoŚv_68 ||
children.translated_text: My suffering occurred when I looked upon you, beset by calamity; but now my mind is [filled with] the happiness of well-being. [GoŚv 68]

children.text: kṛtyaṃ na me parahitād aparaṃ garīyaḥ saṃsāracārakanibandhanam etad eva |
children.translated_text: There is no duty for me greater than the welfare of others — this alone is the binding principle of my wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: tasmāt kukāryamalinām atilaṅghya caryāṃ matprītaye satatam ātmahitaṃ kurudhvam || GoŚv_69 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, overstepping conduct stained by wicked deeds, always do what is beneficial for yourselves, for my delight. [GoŚv 69]

children.text: lokān imān svakṛtakarmabhujo viditvā mṛtyor aparvaparuṣasya karodarasthān |
children.translated_text: Knowing these worlds as beings who eat the fruit of their own deeds, placed in the belly of Death whose harsh [hand strikes] without warning,

children.text: pāpāny asahyaparitāpaphalodayāni prāṇātyaye 'pi parivarjayituṃ yatadhvam || GoŚv_70 ||
children.translated_text: strive to avoid sins — whose fruit is the arising of unbearable torment — even at the cost of life. [GoŚv 70]

children.text: svantāny anāśaramaṇīyaphalapradāni janmāṭavīgahanapathyadanopamāni |
children.translated_text: Accumulate merits — which yield beautiful, imperishable fruit, which are like wholesome food on the dense paths of the forest of births —

children.text: puṇyāni saṃcinuta matpratikārabuddhyā kalyāṇamitravacanaṃ hi na laṅghanīyam || GoŚv_71 ||
children.translated_text: with the thought of repaying me; for the word of a virtuous friend should not be transgressed. [GoŚv 71]

children.text: iti samanuśiṣya prāṇinas tān mahātmā niśitaparaśudhārājarjaraklāntadehaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed those living beings, that great soul, his body battered and weary from the edges of sharp axes,

children.text: avasitakaraṇīyaḥ paryudasyātmabhāvaṃ tam ativikṛtarūpaṃ svargam evāruroha || GoŚv_72 ||
children.translated_text: his duty fulfilled, casting off his physical form in that exceedingly disfigured state, ascended directly to heaven. [GoŚv 72]

children.text: iti jagadupajīvyā uttamaśrīsamudrā vipadaśaninipātavyāhatā vyuṣṭiyogāt |
children.translated_text: Thus, those who are the sustenance of the world, oceans of supreme glory, struck by the thunderbolt of calamity, through the power of [their past] dawns [of merit],

children.text: vigatajaladapaṅkavyomaparyantadīrghāḥ śaśina iva mayūkhā lokam uttārayanti || GoŚv_73 ||
children.translated_text: long as the sky cleared of clouds and mud — like the rays of the moon, they deliver the world. [GoŚv 73]

children.text: || iti śrījātakamālāyāṃ śvajātakaṃ tricatvāriṃśattamaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: || Thus, in the illustrious <s>Jātakamālā</s>, the <s>Śvajātaka</s> (Dog Birth-story), the forty-third, is complete. ||
